title: A Conjectural Brouwer Inequality for Higher-Dimensional Laplacian Spectra
problem_statement: In abebe2019conjectural.lean, prove either Abebe2019Conjectural.conjecture_3_brouwer_inequality_for_k_families or refute it by proving its logical negation Abebe2019Conjectural.conjecture_3_brouwer_inequality_for_k_families_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A Conjectural Brouwer Inequality for Higher-Dimensional Laplacian Spectra

Author: Rediet Abebe.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2012](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: R. Abebe, *A conjectural Brouwer inequality for higher-dimensional Laplacian spectra*,
arXiv:1907.07541.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Abebe2019Conjectural

open Matrix
open Finset

/-- A finite pure `k`-family on the labelled vertex set `Fin n`, represented by its `k`-element
facets (after Definition 11). Only the facets are stored; the complex is their downward closure. -/
structure KFamily (n k : ℕ) where
  /-- The facets of the `k`-family. -/
  facets : Finset (Finset (Fin n))
  /-- Each facet has cardinality `k`. -/
  facet_card : ∀ F ∈ facets, #F = k

namespace KFamily

variable {n k : ℕ}

/-- The boundary matrix `∂_{k-1}` from facets to codimension-one faces. Rows and columns range
over all `(k - 1)`- and `k`-subsets of `[n]`, with zero columns at nonfacets and the zero matrix
for `k = 1` (no augmented boundary). -/
def boundaryMatrix (S : KFamily n k) :
    Matrix {R : Finset (Fin n) // R ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1)}
      {F : Finset (Fin n) // F ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard k} ℝ :=
  fun R F ↦
    if h : 1 < k ∧ F.1 ∈ S.facets ∧ R.1 ⊆ F.1 ∧ #F.1 = #R.1 + 1 then
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (#{v ∈ F.1 | v < (F.1 \ R.1).min' (by
        exact Finset.sdiff_nonempty_of_card_lt_card
          (s := R.1) (t := F.1) (by omega))})
    else 0

/-- The source Laplacian matrix `L(S) = ∂_{k-1} ∂ᵀ_{k-1}`. -/
def laplacianMatrix (S : KFamily n k) :
    Matrix {R : Finset (Fin n) // R ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1)}
      {R : Finset (Fin n) // R ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1)} ℝ :=
  S.boundaryMatrix * S.boundaryMatrixᴴ

/-- The `i`th largest Laplacian eigenvalue of the `k`-family. Lean uses `i = 0` for the source's
`λ₁` and pads out-of-range indices by zero. -/
def laplacianEigenvalue (S : KFamily n k) (i : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  letI : Fintype {R : Finset (Fin n) // R ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1)} :=
    Finset.Subtype.fintype (Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1))
  if hi : i < Fintype.card {R : Finset (Fin n) // R ∈ Finset.univ.powersetCard (k - 1)} then
    ((by
      simpa [laplacianMatrix] using
        Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self S.boundaryMatrix :
          S.laplacianMatrix.IsHermitian).eigenvalues₀ ⟨i, hi⟩)
  else 0

end KFamily

/-- **Conjecture 3**. For every pure labelled `k`-family, every partial sum of the Laplacian
spectrum is bounded by `(k - 1) f_{k-1} + binom(t + k - 1, k)`. -/
theorem conjecture_3_brouwer_inequality_for_k_families
    {n k : ℕ} (S : KFamily n k) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.range t, S.laplacianEigenvalue i) ≤
      ((k - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * #S.facets + (Nat.choose (t + k - 1) k : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Abebe2019Conjectural

theorem Abebe2019Conjectural.conjecture_3_brouwer_inequality_for_k_families_neg : ¬ type_of% @Abebe2019Conjectural.conjecture_3_brouwer_inequality_for_k_families := by
  sorry

title: On Gaps in the Closures of Images of Divisor Functions
problem_statement: In achenjang2019gaps.lean, prove either Achenjang2019Gaps.conjecture_7_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Achenjang2019Gaps.conjecture_7_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On Gaps in the Closures of Images of Divisor Functions

Authors: Niven Achenjang and Aaron Berger.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2018](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: N. Achenjang and A. Berger, *On gaps in the closures of images of divisor functions*,
Int. J. Number Theory **15** (2019), no. 5, 1023-1036.
-/

namespace Achenjang2019Gaps

/-- **Conjecture 7.2** (Divisor Function Monotonicity). The number of connected
components of the closure of the negative-power divisor-sum range is nondecreasing
as the real parameter `r > 1` increases. -/
theorem conjecture_7_2 :
    let σ : ℝ → ℕ+ → ℝ := fun r n ↦
      ∑ d ∈ (n : ℕ).divisors, (d : ℝ) ^ (-r)
    MonotoneOn
      (fun r : ℝ ↦ Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (closure (Set.range (σ r)))))
      (Set.Ioi 1) := by
  sorry

end Achenjang2019Gaps

theorem Achenjang2019Gaps.conjecture_7_2_neg : ¬ type_of% @Achenjang2019Gaps.conjecture_7_2 := by
  sorry

title: The Spectrum of the Laplacian on the Pentagasket
problem_statement: In adams2003spectrum.lean, prove either Adams2003Spectrum.primitive_eigenspaces_irreducible or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2003Spectrum.primitive_eigenspaces_irreducible_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Spectrum of the Laplacian on the Pentagasket

Authors: Bryant Adams, S. Alex Smith, Robert S. Strichartz, and Alexander Teplyaev.
Origin: Cornell Mathematics REU.
Reference: B. Adams, S. A. Smith, R. S. Strichartz, and A. Teplyaev, *The spectrum of the
Laplacian on the pentagasket*, in Fractals in Graz 2001, Birkhäuser, 2003, pp. 1-24;
doi:10.1007/978-3-0348-8014-5_1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2003Spectrum

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped Topology

/-- The affine address map for the incidence-corrected pentagasket. -/
def addressMap : ContinuousMap (ℕ → ZMod 5) ℂ :=
  let ρ : ℝ := (3 - √5) / 2
  { toFun := fun a ↦ ∑' n : ℕ,
      ((ρ ^ n * (1 - ρ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * ZMod.stdAddChar (a n)
    continuous_toFun := by
      have hs := Real.sq_sqrt (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 5 by norm_num)
      have hn := Real.sqrt_nonneg (5 : ℝ)
      have hρ₀ : 0 ≤ ρ := by dsimp [ρ]; nlinarith
      have hρ₁ : ρ < 1 := by dsimp [ρ]; nlinarith
      have hsum : Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ ρ ^ n * (1 - ρ)) :=
        (summable_geometric_of_norm_lt_one (by
          simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hρ₀] using hρ₁)).mul_right (1 - ρ)
      apply continuous_tsum (u := fun n : ℕ ↦ ρ ^ n * (1 - ρ))
      · intro n
        exact continuous_const.mul ((continuous_of_discreteTopology :
          Continuous (fun j : ZMod 5 ↦ ZMod.stdAddChar j)).comp (continuous_apply n))
      · exact hsum
      · intro n a
        have hc : 0 ≤ ρ ^ n * (1 - ρ) :=
          mul_nonneg (pow_nonneg hρ₀ n) (by linarith)
        rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hc]
        simp only [ZMod.stdAddChar_apply, Circle.norm_coe, mul_one, le_refl] }

/-- The address of a cell's corner, with the first word letter outermost. -/
def cellCornerAddress {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → ZMod 5) (i : ZMod 5) :
    ℕ → ZMod 5 :=
  fun n ↦ if h : n < m then w (Fin.mk n h) else i

/-- The source renormalized real bilinear energy, retaining every cell incidence. -/
def graphEnergy (m : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ (ContinuousMap (ℕ → ZMod 5) ℝ) :=
  let p : ℝ := (√161 - 7) / 16
  let q : ℝ := 1 / 2 - p
  let r : ℝ := (√161 - 9) / 8
  ∑ w : Fin m → ZMod 5,
    ∑ i : ZMod 5,
      let d₁ := (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
          (cellCornerAddress w i)).toLinearMap -
        (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
          (cellCornerAddress w (i + 1))).toLinearMap
      let d₂ := (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
          (cellCornerAddress w i)).toLinearMap -
        (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
          (cellCornerAddress w (i + 2))).toLinearMap
      ((r ^ m)⁻¹ * p) • LinearMap.BilinForm.linMulLin d₁ d₁ +
        ((r ^ m)⁻¹ * q) • LinearMap.BilinForm.linMulLin d₂ d₂

/-- Continuous geometric pullbacks with bounded diagonal energy at every level. -/
def energyDomain : Submodule ℝ (ContinuousMap (ℕ → ZMod 5) ℝ) where
  carrier := {u | Function.FactorsThrough u addressMap ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ m : ℕ, graphEnergy m u u ≤ C}
  zero_mem' := by
    refine And.intro (by intro a b h; rfl) (Exists.intro 0 ?_)
    intro m
    simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u v hu hv
    refine And.intro ?_ ?_
    · intro a b h
      change u a + v a = u b + v b
      rw [hu.1 h, hv.1 h]
    · obtain ⟨Cu, huC⟩ := hu.2
      obtain ⟨Cv, hvC⟩ := hv.2
      refine Exists.intro (2 * (Cu + Cv)) (fun m ↦ ?_)
      have hpos : ∀ f, 0 ≤ graphEnergy m f f := by
        intro f
        have hs := Real.sq_sqrt (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 161 by norm_num)
        have hn := Real.sqrt_nonneg (161 : ℝ)
        have hp : 0 ≤ (√161 - 7) / 16 := by nlinarith
        have hq : 0 ≤ 1 / 2 - (√161 - 7) / 16 := by nlinarith
        have hr : 0 ≤ (√161 - 9) / 8 := by nlinarith
        simp only [graphEnergy, LinearMap.sum_apply, LinearMap.add_apply,
          LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.BilinForm.linMulLin_apply, smul_eq_mul]
        apply Finset.sum_nonneg
        intro w hw
        apply Finset.sum_nonneg
        intro i hi
        apply add_nonneg
        · have h := mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (pow_nonneg hr m)) hp)
            (sq_nonneg (((ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
              (cellCornerAddress w i)).toLinearMap -
              (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
              (cellCornerAddress w (i + 1))).toLinearMap) f))
          simpa only [pow_two, mul_assoc] using h
        · have h := mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (pow_nonneg hr m)) hq)
            (sq_nonneg (((ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
              (cellCornerAddress w i)).toLinearMap -
              (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
              (cellCornerAddress w (i + 2))).toLinearMap) f))
          simpa only [pow_two, mul_assoc] using h
      have hn := hpos (u - v)
      simp only [map_sub, LinearMap.sub_apply] at hn
      have hsum : graphEnergy m (u + v) (u + v) ≤
          2 * (graphEnergy m u u + graphEnergy m v v) := by
        simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]
        linarith
      exact hsum.trans (by linarith [huC m, hvC m])
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    refine And.intro ?_ ?_
    · intro a b h
      change c * u a = c * u b
      rw [hu.1 h]
    · obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hu.2
      refine Exists.intro (c ^ 2 * C) (fun m ↦ ?_)
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hC m) (sq_nonneg c)
      simpa only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pow_two, mul_assoc] using h

/-- The complete real weak eigenspace for the eigenvalue `r` (the source's `λ`); `true` selects
Dirichlet and `false` Neumann. -/
def weakEigenspace (dirichlet : Bool) (r : ℝ) :
    Submodule ℝ (ContinuousMap (ℕ → ZMod 5) ℝ) :=
  let μ := Measure.infinitePi
    (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod 5)).toMeasure)
  { carrier := {u | u ∈ energyDomain ∧
      (dirichlet = true → ∀ i : ZMod 5, u (fun _ ↦ i) = 0) ∧
      ∀ v ∈ energyDomain,
        (dirichlet = true → ∀ i : ZMod 5, v (fun _ ↦ i) = 0) →
        Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ graphEnergy m u v) atTop
          (𝓝 (r * ∫ a, u a * v a ∂μ))}
    zero_mem' := by
      refine And.intro energyDomain.zero_mem (And.intro (by simp) ?_)
      intro v hv hb
      simp
    add_mem' := by
      intro u w hu hw
      refine And.intro (energyDomain.add_mem hu.1 hw.1) (And.intro ?_ ?_)
      · intro h i
        change u (fun _ ↦ i) + w (fun _ ↦ i) = 0
        rw [hu.2.1 h i, hw.2.1 h i, add_zero]
      · intro v hv hb
        have hiu : Integrable (fun a ↦ u a * v a) μ :=
          (u.continuous.mul v.continuous).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
            (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
        have hiw : Integrable (fun a ↦ w a * v a) μ :=
          (w.continuous.mul v.continuous).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
            (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
        simpa only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, ContinuousMap.add_apply,
          add_mul, integral_add hiu hiw, mul_add] using
          (hu.2.2 v hv hb).add (hw.2.2 v hv hb)
    smul_mem' := by
      intro c u hu
      refine And.intro (energyDomain.smul_mem c hu.1) (And.intro ?_ ?_)
      · intro h i
        change c * u (fun _ ↦ i) = 0
        rw [hu.2.1 h i, mul_zero]
      · intro v hv hb
        simpa only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, ContinuousMap.smul_apply,
          smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, integral_const_mul, mul_left_comm r c] using
          (hu.2.2 v hv hb).const_mul c }

/-- The full complex eigenspace: both real components satisfy the same real weak equation. -/
def complexEigenspace (dirichlet : Bool) (μ : ℝ) :
    Submodule ℂ (ContinuousMap (ℕ → ZMod 5) ℂ) where
  carrier := {u |
    (Complex.reCLM.compLeftContinuous ℝ (ℕ → ZMod 5)) u ∈
      weakEigenspace dirichlet μ ∧
    (Complex.imCLM.compLeftContinuous ℝ (ℕ → ZMod 5)) u ∈
      weakEigenspace dirichlet μ}
  zero_mem' := by simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u v hu hv
    constructor
    · simpa only [map_add] using (weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).add_mem hu.1 hv.1
    · simpa only [map_add] using (weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).add_mem hu.2 hv.2
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    constructor
    · have h := (weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).sub_mem
        ((weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).smul_mem c.re hu.1)
        ((weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).smul_mem c.im hu.2)
      convert h using 1
      ext a
      change (c * u a).re = c.re * (u a).re - c.im * (u a).im
      exact Complex.mul_re c (u a)
    · have h := (weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).add_mem
        ((weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).smul_mem c.re hu.2)
        ((weakEigenspace dirichlet μ).smul_mem c.im hu.1)
      convert h using 1
      ext a
      change (c * u a).im = c.re * (u a).im + c.im * (u a).re
      exact Complex.mul_im c (u a)

/-- The same pentagon symmetry acts on every address digit. -/
def addressSymmetry (g : DihedralGroup 5) :
    Homeomorph (ℕ → ZMod 5) (ℕ → ZMod 5) :=
  Homeomorph.piCongrRight fun _ : ℕ ↦
    Equiv.toHomeomorphOfDiscrete {
      toFun := fun j ↦ match g with
        | .r i => j + i
        | .sr i => -j - i
      invFun := fun j ↦ match g with
        | .r i => j - i
        | .sr i => -j - i
      left_inv := by
        cases g <;> intro j <;> dsimp <;> abel
      right_inv := by
        cases g <;> intro j <;> dsimp <;> abel }

/-- The geometric inverse-pullback action, without conjugating function values. -/
noncomputable def functionRepresentation :
    Representation ℂ (DihedralGroup 5) C(ℕ → ZMod 5, ℂ) where
  toFun g :=
    (ContinuousMap.compCLM ℂ ℂ
      { toFun := addressSymmetry g⁻¹,
        continuous_toFun := (addressSymmetry g⁻¹).continuous }).toLinearMap
  map_one' := by
    ext u a
    change u (addressSymmetry ((1 : DihedralGroup 5)⁻¹) a) = u a
    congr 1
    funext n
    change a n + -(0 : ZMod 5) = a n
    simp
  map_mul' g h := by
    ext u a
    change u (addressSymmetry ((g * h)⁻¹) a) =
      u (addressSymmetry h⁻¹ (addressSymmetry g⁻¹ a))
    congr 1
    funext n
    rcases g with i | i <;> rcases h with j | j
    next =>
      change a n + -(i + j) = (a n + -i) + -j
      abel
    next =>
      change -a n - (j - i) = -(a n + -i) - j
      abel
    next =>
      change -a n - (i + j) = (-a n - i) + -j
      abel
    next =>
      change a n + -(j - i) = -(-a n - i) - j
      abel

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction, p. 5). Every primitive eigenspace is irreducible
under the full complex dihedral action.

Dirichlet and Neumann are treated jointly (pp. 6, 8-9); primitive means absent from both
predecessor spectra. The geometry follows the cell incidence, reading the printed `1 / τ` as
`1 / τ ^ 2`, and the weak operator follows (1.3)-(1.7) rather than the factor in (1.12). -/
theorem primitive_eigenspaces_irreducible (dirichlet : Bool) (μ : ℝ)
    (heigen : complexEigenspace dirichlet μ ≠ ⊥)
    (hdirichlet : complexEigenspace true (μ * ((√161 - 9) / 8) / 5) = ⊥)
    (hneumann : complexEigenspace false (μ * ((√161 - 9) / 8) / 5) = ⊥) :
    ∃ W : Subrepresentation functionRepresentation,
      W.toSubmodule = complexEigenspace dirichlet μ ∧
      Representation.IsIrreducible W.toRepresentation := by
  sorry

end Adams2003Spectrum

theorem Adams2003Spectrum.primitive_eigenspaces_irreducible_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2003Spectrum.primitive_eigenspaces_irreducible := by
  sorry

title: Isoperimetric Regions in Gauss Sectors
problem_statement: In adams2007isoperimetric.lean, prove either Adams2007Isoperimetric.conjecture_3_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2007Isoperimetric.conjecture_3_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Isoperimetric Regions in Gauss Sectors

Authors: Elizabeth Adams, Ivan Corwin, Diana Davis, Michelle Lee, and Regina Visocchi.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2005](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/published.html).
Reference: E. Adams, I. Corwin, D. Davis, M. Lee, and R. Visocchi, *Isoperimetric regions in
Gauss sectors*, Rose-Hulman Undergrad. Math. J. **8** (2007), no. 1, Article 1, 28 pp.;
https://scholar.rose-hulman.edu/rhumj/vol8/iss1/1/.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2007Isoperimetric

open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped ContDiff symmDiff Real ENNReal

/-- The polar interior of the sector, with distinct angular sheets retained (Definition 2.1).
The physical metric is `dr ^ 2 + r ^ 2 dθ ^ 2`, not the coordinate product norm. -/
def sectorInterior (α : ℝ) : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  ⟨Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioo 0 α, isOpen_Ioi.prod isOpen_Ioo⟩

/-- Gaussian area, including the polar Jacobian and the source normalization (Definition 2.1). -/
def sectorMeasure (α : ℝ) : Measure (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  (volume.withDensity (fun x : ℝ × ℝ ↦
    ENNReal.ofReal (x.1 * Real.exp (-(x.1 ^ 2) / 2) / (2 * π)))).restrict
      (sectorInterior α)

/-- The free-boundary weighted perimeter of a measurable region, as a relative BV flux supremum.
Fields use orthonormal polar components bounded in Euclidean L2 (squares, not the sup norm). -/
def sectorPerimeter (α : ℝ) (E : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (F : TestFunction (sectorInterior α) (ℝ × ℝ) 1)
    (_ : ∀ x, (F x).1 ^ 2 + (F x).2 ^ 2 ≤ 1),
    ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x in E ∩ (sectorInterior α : Set (ℝ × ℝ)),
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦
        y.1 * Real.exp (-(y.1 ^ 2) / 2) / (2 * π) * (F y).1) x) (1, 0) +
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦
        Real.exp (-(y.1 ^ 2) / 2) / (2 * π) * (F y).2) x) (0, 1))

/-- A rounded half-edge with real parameter `n = π / α` (Definition 3.2). It is a simple regular
polar arc with signed Definition 2.8 curvature, not the unsigned equation of Proposition 4.1. -/
structure RoundedArc (α : ℝ) where
  angle_pos : 0 < α
  /-- The arc-length parameter interval length of the half-edge. -/
  length : ℝ
  length_pos : 0 < length
  /-- The arc-length parametrisation in polar coordinates (radius, angle). -/
  curve : ℝ → ℝ × ℝ
  smooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ curve
  radius_pos : ∀ s ∈ Icc 0 length, 0 < (curve s).1
  start_angle : (curve 0).2 = 0
  end_angle : (curve length).2 = α
  interior : ∀ s ∈ Ioo 0 length, 0 < (curve s).2 ∧ (curve s).2 < α
  simple : InjOn curve (Icc 0 length)
  radial_monotone : StrictMonoOn (fun s ↦ (curve s).1) (Icc 0 length) ∨
    StrictAntiOn (fun s ↦ (curve s).1) (Icc 0 length)
  orthogonal :
    deriv (fun s ↦ (curve s).1) 0 = 0 ∧
    deriv (fun s ↦ (curve s).1) length = 0
  consecutive : ∀ s ∈ Ioo 0 length,
    deriv (fun t ↦ (curve t).1) s ≠ 0
  reflected_continuation :
    (∀ s, curve (-s) = ((curve s).1, -(curve s).2)) ∧
    (∀ s, curve (2 * length - s) = ((curve s).1, 2 * α - (curve s).2))
  /-- The constant Definition 2.8 Gauss-weighted curvature of the arc. -/
  curvature : ℝ
  geometry :
    let J := Icc 0 length
    let g := fun s ↦ polarCoord.symm (curve s)
    let v := deriv g
    let a := deriv v
    (∀ s ∈ J,
      (v s).1 ^ 2 + (v s).2 ^ 2 = 1 ∧
      0 ≤ (v s).1 * (a s).2 - (v s).2 * (a s).1 ∧
      (v s).1 * (a s).2 - (v s).2 * (a s).1 -
        (g s).1 * (v s).2 + (g s).2 * (v s).1 = curvature) ∧
    (∃ s ∈ Ioo 0 length, 0 < (v s).1 * (a s).2 - (v s).2 * (a s).1)

/-- The vertex-side component cut off by the rounded half-edge. Strict radial monotonicity
places the seed point below every point of the arc. -/
def RoundedArc.vertexSide {α : ℝ} (C : RoundedArc α) :
    TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  ⟨connectedComponentIn
      ((sectorInterior α : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) \ C.curve '' Icc 0 C.length)
      (min (C.curve 0).1 (C.curve C.length).1 / 2, α / 2), by
    apply IsOpen.connectedComponentIn
    exact (sectorInterior α).isOpen.sdiff
      (isCompact_Icc.image C.smooth.continuous).isClosed⟩

/-- **Conjecture 3.3** (pp. 6-7). The full angle-and-mass phase diagram and four-shape
classification of Gaussian free-boundary isoperimetric regions in sectors.

Uniqueness is modulo null sets and sector reflection, with complements at half mass only; ties
assert coexistence, and ray-only phases carry no uniqueness. Approximate numerical thresholds are
existentially quantified. At `α = π / 2`, half-mass circle minimality is asserted without
uniqueness, which is claimed only for `q < a < 1 / 8`. -/
theorem conjecture_3_3 :
    /- The exterior of the centered circular arc (Figure 2, Proposition 3.23). -/
    let circularRegion (α R : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
      {x | x ∈ sectorInterior α ∧ R < x.1}

    /- The cap cut off by a ray perpendicular to the lower edge (Proposition 3.19). Only the
    first-quadrant sheet is used, even when `α > 2 * π`. -/
    let perpendicularRayRegion (α h : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
      {x | x ∈ sectorInterior α ∧ x.2 < π / 2 ∧
        h < x.1 * Real.cos x.2}

    /- The lower-edge subsector cut off by an origin ray of angle `θ` (Proposition 3.15). -/
    let originRayRegion (α θ : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
      {x | x ∈ sectorInterior α ∧ x.2 < θ}
    ∃ β q : ℝ,
      π / 2 < β ∧ β < π ∧ 0 < q ∧ q < 1 / 8 ∧
      ∀ α > (0 : ℝ),
        let U : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := sectorInterior α
        let μ := sectorMeasure α
        let P := sectorPerimeter α
        let M := α / (2 * π)
        let reflect := fun F : Set (ℝ × ℝ) ↦
          {x | x ∈ U ∧ (x.1, α - x.2) ∈ F}
        ∃ c b : ℝ,
          (α < π / 2 → 0 < c ∧ c < M / 2) ∧
          (π / 2 < α ∧ α < β → 0 < b ∧ b < M / 2) ∧
          ∀ A > (0 : ℝ), A < M →
            let a := min A (M - A)
            let fullSide := fun F : Set (ℝ × ℝ) ↦
              if M / 2 < A then U \ F else F
            let minimizing := fun F : Set (ℝ × ℝ) ↦
              NullMeasurableSet F μ ∧ F ⊆ U ∧ μ F = ENNReal.ofReal A ∧
                P F < ⊤ ∧
                ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                  μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A → P F ≤ P E
            let sameShape := fun E F : Set (ℝ × ℝ) ↦
              ∃ reflected complemented : Bool,
                (complemented = true → 2 * A = M) ∧
                μ (E ∆ (if complemented then U \ (if reflected then reflect F else F)
                  else if reflected then reflect F else F)) = 0
            (∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), minimizing E →
              ∃ (F : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (reflected complemented : Bool),
                ((∃ R > (0 : ℝ), F = circularRegion α R) ∨
                  (∃ C : RoundedArc α, F = (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ))) ∨
                  (π / 2 ≤ α ∧ ∃ h ≥ (0 : ℝ),
                    F = perpendicularRayRegion α h) ∨
                  (∃ θ > (0 : ℝ), θ < α ∧
                    F = originRayRegion α θ)) ∧
                μ (E ∆ (if complemented then U \ (if reflected then reflect F else F)
                  else if reflected then reflect F else F)) = 0) ∧
            ∃ R > (0 : ℝ), M * Real.exp (-(R ^ 2) / 2) = a ∧
              μ (circularRegion α R) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
              let circle := fullSide (circularRegion α R)
              if α < π / 2 then
                if a < c then
                  ∃ C : RoundedArc α,
                    μ (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ))) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
                    minimizing (fullSide (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ)))) ∧
                      ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                        μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                          (P E = P (fullSide (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ)))) ↔
                            sameShape E (fullSide (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ)))))
                else if a = c then
                  minimizing circle ∧
                    ∃ C : RoundedArc α,
                      μ (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ))) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
                      minimizing (fullSide (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ)))) ∧
                        P (fullSide (U \ (C.vertexSide : Set (ℝ × ℝ)))) = P circle
                else
                  minimizing circle ∧
                    ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                      μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A → (P E = P circle ↔ sameShape E circle)
              else if α ≤ π then
                ∃ h ≥ (0 : ℝ),
                  (1 / (2 * √(2 * π))) *
                    (∫ t in Ioi h, Real.exp (-(t ^ 2) / 2)) = a ∧
                  μ (perpendicularRayRegion α h) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
                  let ray := fullSide (perpendicularRayRegion α h)
                  if α = π / 2 then
                    if a < q then
                      minimizing ray ∧
                        ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                          μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A → (P E = P ray ↔ sameShape E ray)
                    else if a = q then
                      minimizing circle ∧ minimizing ray ∧ P circle = P ray
                    else
                      minimizing circle ∧
                        (a < 1 / 8 →
                          ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                            μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                              (P E = P circle ↔ sameShape E circle))
                  else if α < β then
                    if a < b then
                      minimizing ray ∧ P ray < P circle
                    else if a = b then
                      minimizing circle ∧ minimizing ray ∧ P circle = P ray
                    else
                      minimizing circle ∧
                        ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                          μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                            (P E = P circle ↔ sameShape E circle)
                  else if α = β then
                    if a = M / 2 then
                      minimizing circle ∧ minimizing ray ∧ P circle = P ray
                    else
                      minimizing ray ∧ P ray < P circle
                  else
                    minimizing ray ∧
                      (α = π →
                        ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                          μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A → (P E = P ray ↔ sameShape E ray))
              else if a ≤ 1 / 4 then
                ∃ h ≥ (0 : ℝ),
                  (1 / (2 * √(2 * π))) *
                    (∫ t in Ioi h, Real.exp (-(t ^ 2) / 2)) = a ∧
                  μ (perpendicularRayRegion α h) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
                  (a = 1 / 4 → h = 0) ∧
                  minimizing (fullSide (perpendicularRayRegion α h))
              else
                μ (originRayRegion α (2 * π * a)) = ENNReal.ofReal a ∧
                  minimizing (fullSide (originRayRegion α (2 * π * a))) ∧
                  (a = M / 2 →
                    ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ U →
                      μ E = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                        (P E = P (fullSide (originRayRegion α (2 * π * a))) ↔
                          sameShape E (fullSide (originRayRegion α (2 * π * a))))) := by
  sorry

end Adams2007Isoperimetric

theorem Adams2007Isoperimetric.conjecture_3_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2007Isoperimetric.conjecture_3_3 := by
  sorry

title: Densities of Hyperbolic Cusp Invariants
source_label: Open question (abstract; expected answer in the introduction)
problem_statement: In adams2017densities.lean, prove either Adams2017Densities.cusp_crossing_density_isLUB or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2017Densities.cusp_crossing_density_isLUB_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Densities of Hyperbolic Cusp Invariants

Authors: Colin Adams, Rose Kaplan-Kelly, Michael Moore, Brandon Shapiro, Shruthi Sridhar, and
Joshua Wakefield.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2016](https://math.williams.edu/small/research-publications/).
Reference: C. Adams, R. Kaplan-Kelly, M. Moore, B. Shapiro, S. Sridhar, and J. Wakefield,
*Densities of hyperbolic cusp invariants of knots and links*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. **146**
(2018), no. 9, 4073-4089; arXiv:1701.03479v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2017Densities

open Set Topology MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

/-- A tame link represented by finitely many disjoint embedded polygonal circles. -/
structure PolygonalLink where
  /-- The number of link components. -/
  components : ℕ
  components_pos : 0 < components
  /-- The number of vertices of each component polygon. -/
  size : Fin components → ℕ
  /-- The closed space polygon forming each component. -/
  polygon : (i : Fin components) → Polygon (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (size i)
  size_ge_three : ∀ i, 3 ≤ size i
  vertices_injective : ∀ i, Function.Injective (polygon i).vertices
  edges_nondegenerate : ∀ i, (polygon i).HasNondegenerateEdges
  simple : ∀ i j k, j ≠ k →
    (polygon i).edgeSet ℝ j ∩ (polygon i).edgeSet ℝ k ⊆
      ({polygon i j, polygon i (finRotate (size i) j)} ∩
        {polygon i k, polygon i (finRotate (size i) k)})
  components_disjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    Disjoint ((polygon i).boundary ℝ) ((polygon j).boundary ℝ)

/-- The geometric link, including every point on its component edges. -/
def PolygonalLink.carrier (L : PolygonalLink) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :=
  ⋃ i, (L.polygon i).boundary ℝ

/-- The link complement in `S³`, modeled by the one-point compactification of `ℝ³`. -/
abbrev PolygonalLink.complement (L : PolygonalLink) :=
  {x : OnePoint (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | x ∉ OnePoint.some '' L.carrier}

/-- A link conformation whose horizontal projection is a regular link diagram. -/
structure LinkDiagram extends PolygonalLink where
  regular :
    let proj : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
      fun x ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 ![x 0, x 1]
    (∀ i j, proj (polygon i j) ≠ proj (polygon i (finRotate (size i) j))) ∧
    (∀ (i k : Fin components) (j : Fin (size i)) (l : Fin (size k)),
      proj (polygon i j) ∈ segment ℝ (proj (polygon k l))
        (proj (polygon k (finRotate (size k) l))) →
      polygon i j = polygon k l ∨ polygon i j = polygon k (finRotate (size k) l)) ∧
    (∀ (i k : Fin components) (j : Fin (size i)) (l : Fin (size k)),
      polygon i j ≠ polygon k l →
      (openSegment ℝ (proj (polygon i j))
        (proj (polygon i (finRotate (size i) j))) ∩
      openSegment ℝ (proj (polygon k l))
        (proj (polygon k (finRotate (size k) l)))).Nonempty →
      LinearIndependent ℝ
        ![proj (polygon i (finRotate (size i) j)) - proj (polygon i j),
          proj (polygon k (finRotate (size k) l)) - proj (polygon k l)]) ∧
    (∀ q, {x | x ∈ toPolygonalLink.carrier ∧ proj x = q}.encard ≤ 2)

/-- The minimal crossing number c(L), over all regular diagrams of its ambient isotopy type. -/
def PolygonalLink.crossingNumber (L : PolygonalLink) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : LinkDiagram,
    ∃ H : unitInterval →
      (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ∧
    H 1 '' L.carrier = D.toPolygonalLink.carrier ∧
    let proj : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
      fun x ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 ![x 0, x 1]
    {q | ∃ x ∈ D.toPolygonalLink.carrier, ∃ y ∈ D.toPolygonalLink.carrier,
      x ≠ y ∧ proj x = q ∧ proj y = q}.encard = n}

/-- The upper-half-space model of hyperbolic three-space used to describe lifted cusps. -/
abbrev upperHalfSpace := {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) | 0 < x 2}

/-- A complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the link complement in `S³`. -/
structure HyperbolicStructure (L : PolygonalLink) where
  /-- The hyperbolic metric on the link complement. -/
  metric : MetricSpace L.complement
  topology_eq : metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace =
    (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace L.complement)
  /-- The universal covering map from upper half-space to the complement. -/
  cover : C(upperHalfSpace, L.complement)
  covering : IsCoveringMap cover
  cover_surjective : Function.Surjective cover
  locally_hyperbolic : ∀ x : upperHalfSpace,
    ∃ U : Set upperHalfSpace, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧
      ∀ y ∈ U, ∀ z ∈ U,
        @dist L.complement metric.toDist (cover y) (cover z) =
          2 * Real.arsinh (dist y.val z.val / (2 * √(y.val 2 * z.val 2)))
  complete : @CompleteSpace L.complement metric.toUniformSpace
  finite_volume :
    @Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure L.complement
      (@MetricSpace.toEMetricSpace L.complement metric)
      (@borel L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace)
      (@BorelSpace.mk L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
        (@borel L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace) rfl)
      3 (univ : Set L.complement) < ⊤

/-- An open torus cusp whose connected lifts are geometric horoballs. -/
structure Cusp {L : PolygonalLink} (H : HyperbolicStructure L) where
  /-- The open cusp region in the link complement. -/
  region : Set L.complement
  isOpen_region : IsOpen region
  torus_end : Nonempty (region ≃ₜ ((Fin 2 → AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) × Ioi (0 : ℝ)))
  horoball_lifts : ∀ x : upperHalfSpace, H.cover x ∈ region →
    (∃ h > (0 : ℝ),
      connectedComponentIn (H.cover ⁻¹' region) x = {p | h < p.val 2}) ∨
    (∃ c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), ∃ r > (0 : ℝ),
      connectedComponentIn (H.cover ⁻¹' region) x =
        {p | dist p.val (WithLp.toLp 2 ![c 0, c 1, r]) < r})

/-- A disjoint cusp neighborhood for every end, with compact complementary core. -/
structure CuspPacking {L : PolygonalLink} (H : HyperbolicStructure L) where
  /-- The cusp assigned to each link component. -/
  cusp : Fin L.components → Cusp H
  disjoint : Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (cusp i).region (cusp j).region)
  compact_core : IsCompact ((⋃ i, (cusp i).region)ᶜ)

/-- The maximal total cusp volume `cv(L)` over all disjoint cusp packings. -/
def HyperbolicStructure.cuspVolume {L : PolygonalLink} (H : HyperbolicStructure L) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ P : CuspPacking H,
    @Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure L.complement
      (@MetricSpace.toEMetricSpace L.complement H.metric)
      (@borel L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace)
      (@BorelSpace.mk L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
        (@borel L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace) rfl)
      3 (⋃ i, (P.cusp i).region)

/-- The cusp-crossing density: maximal total cusp volume divided by crossing number
(Definition 1.4). -/
def HyperbolicStructure.cuspCrossingDensity {L : PolygonalLink}
    (H : HyperbolicStructure L) : ℝ :=
  H.cuspVolume.toReal / L.crossingNumber

/-- **Open question** (abstract; expected answer in the introduction). The number `3` is
the least upper bound of the cusp-crossing densities of all hyperbolic links.

No attainment and no density of values in `[0, 3]` is asserted. -/
theorem cusp_crossing_density_isLUB :
    IsLUB {r : ℝ | ∃ L : PolygonalLink, ∃ H : HyperbolicStructure L,
      r = H.cuspCrossingDensity} 3 := by
  sorry

end Adams2017Densities

theorem Adams2017Densities.cusp_crossing_density_isLUB_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2017Densities.cusp_crossing_density_isLUB := by
  sorry

title: Multi-crossing Number for Knots and the Kauffman Bracket Polynomial
problem_statement: In adams2018multi.lean, prove either Adams2018Multi.crossing_spectrum_monotone or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2018Multi.crossing_spectrum_monotone_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Multi-crossing Number for Knots and the Kauffman Bracket Polynomial

Authors: Colin Adams, Orsola Capovilla-Searle, Jesse Freeman, Daniel Irvine,
Samantha Petti, Daniel Vitek, Ashley Weber, and Sicong Zhang.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU](https://math.williams.edu/small/research-publications/).
Reference: C. Adams, O. Capovilla-Searle, J. Freeman, D. Irvine, S. Petti, D. Vitek, A. Weber,
and S. Zhang, *Multi-crossing number for knots and the Kauffman bracket polynomial*, preprint
(2014); arXiv:1407.4485v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2018Multi

open Finset

/-- A finite simple spatial polygon representing a classical tame knot.
The number of edges is unrestricted, and collinear subdivisions are allowed. -/
structure PolygonalKnot (m : ℕ) extends Polygon (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) m where
  three_le : 3 ≤ m
  vertices_injective : Function.Injective toPolygon.vertices
  nondegenerate_edges : toPolygon.HasNondegenerateEdges
  simple : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    toPolygon.edgeSet ℝ i ∩ toPolygon.edgeSet ℝ j ⊆
      ({toPolygon i, toPolygon (finRotate m i)} ∩
        {toPolygon j, toPolygon (finRotate m j)})

/-- The planar projection of a spatial polygon onto its first two coordinates. Crossing heights
are read from the dropped third coordinate, not from separate labels. -/
def PolygonalKnot.projection {m : ℕ} (K : PolygonalKnot m) :
    Polygon (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) m where
  vertices i := WithLp.toLp 2 ![K.toPolygon i 0, K.toPolygon i 1]

/-- A projection with only transverse `n`-crossings, each in edge interiors. Crossing order comes
from the spatial lift, and subdivisions permit height changes between crossings. -/
structure MultiCrossingDiagram (n m : ℕ) extends PolygonalKnot m where
  projected_vertices_injective : Function.Injective toPolygonalKnot.projection.vertices
  projected_nondegenerate : toPolygonalKnot.projection.HasNondegenerateEdges
  projected_vertices_off_edges : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → i ≠ finRotate m j →
    toPolygonalKnot.projection i ∉ toPolygonalKnot.projection.edgeSet ℝ j
  transverse : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    openSegment ℝ (toPolygonalKnot.projection i)
        (toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m i)) ∩
      openSegment ℝ (toPolygonalKnot.projection j)
        (toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m j)) ≠ ∅ →
    LinearIndependent ℝ
      ![toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m i) - toPolygonalKnot.projection i,
        toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m j) - toPolygonalKnot.projection j]
  crossing_order : ∀ q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
    let branches := {i : Fin m | q ∈ openSegment ℝ (toPolygonalKnot.projection i)
      (toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m i))}
    2 ≤ branches.encard → branches.encard = (n : ℕ∞)

/-- The set of singular planar points of a diagram. -/
def MultiCrossingDiagram.crossingPoints {n m : ℕ} (D : MultiCrossingDiagram n m) :
    Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  {q | ∃ i j : Fin m, i ≠ j ∧
    q ∈ openSegment ℝ (D.toPolygonalKnot.projection i)
      (D.toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m i)) ∧
    q ∈ openSegment ℝ (D.toPolygonalKnot.projection j)
      (D.toPolygonalKnot.projection (finRotate m j))}

/-- The crossing-point set of a diagram is finite. -/
theorem MultiCrossingDiagram.finite_crossingPoints {n m : ℕ}
    (D : MultiCrossingDiagram n m) : D.crossingPoints.Finite := by
  let P := D.toPolygonalKnot.projection
  let A : Fin m → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) := fun i ↦
    openSegment ℝ (P i) (P (finRotate m i))
  have hpair : ∀ i j : Fin m, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite := by
    intro i j hij
    by_cases he : A i ∩ A j = ∅
    · rw [he]
      exact Set.finite_empty
    · have hlin := D.transverse i j hij he
      apply Set.Subsingleton.finite
      intro x hx y hy
      rcases (hx.1 : x ∈ A i) with ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hab, hx₁⟩
      rcases (hx.2 : x ∈ A j) with ⟨c, d, hc, hd, hcd, hx₂⟩
      rcases (hy.1 : y ∈ A i) with ⟨e, f, he, hf, hef, hy₁⟩
      rcases (hy.2 : y ∈ A j) with ⟨g, h, hg, hh, hgh, hy₂⟩
      have ha' : a = 1 - b := by linarith
      have hc' : c = 1 - d := by linarith
      have he' : e = 1 - f := by linarith
      have hg' : g = 1 - h := by linarith
      have hrel : (b - f) • (P (finRotate m i) - P i) +
          (h - d) • (P (finRotate m j) - P j) = 0 := by
        rw [ha'] at hx₁
        rw [hc'] at hx₂
        rw [he'] at hy₁
        rw [hg'] at hy₂
        calc
          (b - f) • (P (finRotate m i) - P i) +
              (h - d) • (P (finRotate m j) - P j) =
            ((1 - b) • P i + b • P (finRotate m i)) -
              ((1 - f) • P i + f • P (finRotate m i)) -
              (((1 - d) • P j + d • P (finRotate m j)) -
                ((1 - h) • P j + h • P (finRotate m j))) := by module
          _ = 0 := by rw [hx₁, hy₁, hx₂, hy₂]; abel
      have hbf := (hlin.eq_zero_of_pair hrel).1
      have bf : b = f := sub_eq_zero.mp hbf
      have ae : a = e := by linarith
      rw [ae, bf] at hx₁
      exact hx₁.symm.trans hy₁
  have hu : (⋃ i : Fin m, ⋃ j : Fin m, ⋃ (_ : i ≠ j), A i ∩ A j).Finite :=
    Set.finite_iUnion fun i ↦ Set.finite_iUnion fun j ↦
      Set.finite_iUnion fun hij ↦ hpair i j hij
  apply hu.subset
  rintro q ⟨i, j, hij, hqi, hqj⟩
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨i, Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j,
    Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨hij, hqi, hqj⟩⟩⟩

/-- The `n`-crossing number: the least number of crossing points over all `n`-diagrams of the
same knot type. The value lies in `ℕ∞`, so it is `⊤` when no diagram exists. -/
def crossingNumber {k : ℕ} (K : PolygonalKnot k) (n : ℕ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {c : ℕ∞ | ∃ m : ℕ, ∃ D : MultiCrossingDiagram n m,
    ∃ H : unitInterval → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ∧
      H 1 '' K.toPolygon.boundary ℝ = D.toPolygonalKnot.toPolygon.boundary ℝ ∧
      c = (#D.finite_crossingPoints.toFinset : ℕ∞)}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 5, pp. 22-23). For every tame knot, including the unknot,
the `n`-crossing number does not increase when `n` increases by one. -/
theorem crossing_spectrum_monotone {k : ℕ} (K : PolygonalKnot k)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : crossingNumber K (n + 1) ≤ crossingNumber K n := by
  sorry

end Adams2018Multi

theorem Adams2018Multi.crossing_spectrum_monotone_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2018Multi.crossing_spectrum_monotone := by
  sorry

title: Vietoris--Rips Complexes of Regular Polygons
problem_statement: In adams2018vietoris.lean, prove either Adams2018Vietoris.conjecture_5_10_star_side_length_extrema or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2018Vietoris.conjecture_5_10_star_side_length_extrema_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Vietoris--Rips Complexes of Regular Polygons

Authors: Henry Adams, Samir Chowdhury, Adam Quinn Jaffe, and Bonginkosi Sibanda.
Origin: [Summer@ICERM 2017](https://icerm.brown.edu/program/summer@icerm/si-17).
Reference: H. Adams, S. Chowdhury, A. Q. Jaffe, and B. Sibanda, *Vietoris--Rips complexes of
regular polygons*, arXiv:1807.10971.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2018Vietoris

open Set
open scoped Real

/-- The normalized counterclockwise boundary coordinate on `P_n` (Section 2). The interval
`[0, 1)` parametrizes the polygon starting at the vertex `1`. -/
abbrev polygonParameter := Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The regular polygon's `k`-th vertex, in the Euclidean complex plane. -/
def regularPolygonVertex (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ℂ :=
  ⟨Real.cos (2 * π * (k : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)),
    Real.sin (2 * π * (k : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))⟩

/-- The parametrization of the polygon by fractional edge count, extended periodically
(Section 2). -/
def polygonPoint (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  let u := (n : ℝ) * Int.fract t
  (1 - Int.fract u) • regularPolygonVertex n ⌊u⌋ +
    Int.fract u • regularPolygonVertex n (⌊u⌋ + 1)

/-- An equilateral `(2l + 1)`-star inscribed in the polygon (Section 4.2). The winding number
`l` is encoded as the sum of counterclockwise advances, each less than half the perimeter. -/
structure InscribedStar (n l : ℕ) (t : polygonParameter) where
  /-- The parameters of the star's `2l + 1` vertices on the polygon. -/
  vertex : Fin (2 * l + 1) → polygonParameter
  base : vertex 0 = t
  distinct : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The common side length of the star. -/
  scale : ℝ
  scale_pos : 0 < scale
  scale_le_cyclic : scale ≤ if Even n then 2 * Real.cos (π / n)
    else 1 + Real.cos (2 * π / n) / Real.cos (π / n)
  equal_sides : ∀ i : Fin (2 * l + 1),
    dist (polygonPoint n (vertex i).1) (polygonPoint n (vertex (i + 1)).1) = scale
  counterclockwise : ∀ i : Fin (2 * l + 1),
    Int.fract ((vertex (i + 1)).1 - (vertex i).1) < 1 / 2
  winding : (∑ i : Fin (2 * l + 1),
    Int.fract ((vertex (i + 1)).1 - (vertex i).1)) = (l : ℝ)

/-- The star side-length function `s_(2l+1)` (Definition 4.13, Section 5.2). The scale set is a
singleton on the conjecture domain; outside it the infimum is a junk value. -/
def starSideLength (n l : ℕ) (t : polygonParameter) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ S : InscribedStar n l t, S.scale = r}

/-- A vertex crossing: the inscribed star contains a polygon vertex (Section 5.2). -/
def IsVertexCrossing (n l : ℕ) (t : polygonParameter) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : InscribedStar n l t, ∃ i : Fin (2 * l + 1), ∃ k : Fin n,
    polygonPoint n (S.vertex i).1 = regularPolygonVertex n k.1

/-- A midpoint crossing: the star contains a polygon edge midpoint (Section 5.2). -/
def IsMidpointCrossing (n l : ℕ) (t : polygonParameter) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : InscribedStar n l t, ∃ i : Fin (2 * l + 1), ∃ k : Fin n,
    polygonPoint n (S.vertex i).1 =
      (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (regularPolygonVertex n k.1 + regularPolygonVertex n (k.1 + 1))

/-- **Conjecture 5.10** (arXiv:1807.10971v1, p. 15). Midpoint and vertex crossings are
alternating global minima and maxima of the star side length, which is strictly monotone on each
intervening counterclockwise arc.

The model uses the source's p. 13 endpoint extension: for `n = 4 * l + 2`, vertex-based stars
have scale `r_n`, since Lemma 5.5's strict-radius exception is erroneous. -/
theorem conjecture_5_10_star_side_length_extrema (n l : ℕ)
    (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hn : 4 * l + 2 ≤ n) :
    let pointAt : ℝ → polygonParameter := fun t ↦
      ⟨Int.fract t, Int.fract_nonneg t, Int.fract_lt_one t⟩
    (∀ t : polygonParameter, IsMidpointCrossing n l t →
      ∀ u : polygonParameter, starSideLength n l t ≤ starSideLength n l u) ∧
    (∀ t : polygonParameter, IsVertexCrossing n l t →
      ∀ u : polygonParameter, starSideLength n l u ≤ starSideLength n l t) ∧
    (∀ t : polygonParameter,
      IsMidpointCrossing n l t ∨ IsVertexCrossing n l t →
      ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), δ < 1 ∧
        (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ε < δ →
          ¬(IsMidpointCrossing n l (pointAt (t.1 + ε)) ∨
            IsVertexCrossing n l (pointAt (t.1 + ε)))) ∧
        ((IsMidpointCrossing n l t ∧
            IsVertexCrossing n l (pointAt (t.1 + δ)) ∧
            StrictMonoOn (fun ε ↦ starSideLength n l (pointAt (t.1 + ε)))
              (Set.Icc 0 δ)) ∨
          (IsVertexCrossing n l t ∧
            IsMidpointCrossing n l (pointAt (t.1 + δ)) ∧
            StrictAntiOn (fun ε ↦ starSideLength n l (pointAt (t.1 + ε)))
              (Set.Icc 0 δ)))) := by
  sorry

end Adams2018Vietoris

theorem Adams2018Vietoris.conjecture_5_10_star_side_length_extrema_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2018Vietoris.conjecture_5_10_star_side_length_extrema := by
  sorry

title: Generalized bipyramids and hyperbolic volumes of alternating k-uniform tiling links
problem_statement: In adams2020generalized.lean, prove either Adams2020Generalized.fixed_genus_maximum or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2020Generalized.fixed_genus_maximum_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Generalized bipyramids and hyperbolic volumes of alternating k-uniform tiling links

Authors: Colin Adams, Aaron Calderon, and Nathaniel Mayer.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2015](https://math.williams.edu/small/).
Reference: C. Adams, A. Calderon, and N. Mayer, *Generalized bipyramids and hyperbolic volumes of
alternating k-uniform tiling links*, Topology Appl. **271** (2020); arXiv:1709.00432v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2020Generalized

open Set Topology MeasureTheory
open scoped Real

universe u

/-- A compact connected Hausdorff second-countable surface without boundary, orientable or not. -/
structure ClosedSurface where
  /-- The underlying topological space of the surface. -/
  carrier : Type u
  [topology : TopologicalSpace carrier]
  [hausdorff : T2Space carrier]
  [secondCountable : SecondCountableTopology carrier]
  [compact : CompactSpace carrier]
  [connected : ConnectedSpace carrier]
  [charts : ChartedSpace (Fin 2 → ℝ) carrier]

attribute [instance] ClosedSurface.topology ClosedSurface.hausdorff
  ClosedSurface.secondCountable ClosedSurface.compact ClosedSurface.connected
  ClosedSurface.charts

/-- The Euler characteristic, computed from singular homology in degrees `0`, `1` and `2` with
coefficients in `ZMod 2`. -/
def ClosedSurface.eulerCharacteristic (S : ClosedSurface.{u}) : ℤ :=
  let H := fun n ↦
    (((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} (ZMod 2)) n).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (ZMod 2) (ULift.{u} (ZMod 2)))).obj (TopCat.of S.carrier))
  (Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (H 0) : ℤ) -
    (Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (H 1) : ℤ) +
    (Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (H 2) : ℤ)

/-- The truncated right-angled symmetric `n`-bipyramid in the Klein ball, with ideal regular
equatorial vertices and two truncated apexes. The source uses only `n ≥ 12`. -/
def rightAngledBipyramid (n : ℕ) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :=
  let a := π / (n : ℝ)
  let equator : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) := fun i ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![Real.cos (2 * a * (i : ℕ)),
      Real.sin (2 * a * (i : ℕ)), 0]
  let top : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) :=
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0, (Real.tan a)⁻¹]
  let bottom : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) :=
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0, -(Real.tan a)⁻¹]
  {x | ‖x‖ < 1} ∩ convexHull ℝ (range equator ∪ {top, bottom}) ∩
    {x | |x 2| ≤ Real.tan a}

/-- A finite locally flat link in the interior of the product of a surface and an interval. -/
structure TameLink (S : Type*) [TopologicalSpace S] where
  /-- The number of link components. -/
  components : ℕ
  /-- The parametrisation of the components as embedded circles in `S × [0, 1]`. -/
  curve : C(Fin components × AddCircle (1 : ℝ), S × unitInterval)
  embedding : IsEmbedding curve
  interior : ∀ t, 0 < (curve t).2.val ∧ (curve t).2.val < 1
  locally_flat : ∀ t,
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph (S × unitInterval) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      curve t ∈ e.source ∧ e (curve t) = 0 ∧
      e '' (e.source ∩ range curve) = e.target ∩ {v | v 1 = 0 ∧ v 2 = 0}

/-- The set of points of the link. -/
def TameLink.carrier {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] (L : TameLink S) : Set (S × unitInterval) :=
  range L.curve

/-- The complement of the link in `S × [0, 1]`, including both boundary surfaces. -/
abbrev TameLink.complement {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] (L : TameLink S) :=
  {x : S × unitInterval | x ∉ L.carrier}

/-- A generic surface diagram: locally embedded branches, only finite transverse double points. -/
structure LinkDiagram (S : Type*) [TopologicalSpace S] extends TameLink S where
  locally_embedded_projection : ∀ t,
    ∃ U : Set (Fin components × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)), IsOpen U ∧ t ∈ U ∧
      IsEmbedding (fun z : U ↦ (curve z.val).1)
  at_most_double : ∀ q : S, {t | (curve t).1 = q}.encard ≤ 2
  finite_crossings : {q : S | ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ (curve a).1 = q ∧ (curve b).1 = q}.Finite
  transverse : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → (curve a).1 = (curve b).1 →
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph S (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      (curve a).1 ∈ e.source ∧ e (curve a).1 = 0 ∧
      ∃ U V : Set (Fin components × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)),
        IsOpen U ∧ IsOpen V ∧ a ∈ U ∧ b ∈ V ∧ Disjoint U V ∧
        IsEmbedding (fun z : U ↦ (curve z.val).1) ∧
        IsEmbedding (fun z : V ↦ (curve z.val).1) ∧
        (fun t ↦ (curve t).1) ⁻¹' e.source = U ∪ V ∧
        (fun t ↦ e (curve t).1) '' U = e.target ∩ {v | v 1 = 0} ∧
        (fun t ↦ e (curve t).1) '' V = e.target ∩ {v | v 0 = 0}

/-- Minimum generic crossing count on the same surface over the link's ambient isotopy class. -/
def TameLink.crossingNumber {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] (L : TameLink S) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : LinkDiagram S,
    ∃ H : unitInterval → ((S × unitInterval) ≃ₜ (S × unitInterval)),
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × (S × unitInterval) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × (S × unitInterval) ↦ (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (S × unitInterval) ∧
      H 1 '' L.carrier = D.toTameLink.carrier ∧
      {q : S | ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ (D.curve a).1 = q ∧ (D.curve b).1 = q}.encard = n}

/-- The closed side of a vertical geodesic plane in the L2 upper-half-space model. -/
abbrev hyperbolicHalfSpace :=
  {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) | 0 < x 2 ∧ 0 ≤ x 0}

/-- A complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure on the link complement with both boundary
surfaces totally geodesic. -/
structure TGHyperbolicStructure {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] (L : TameLink S) where
  /-- The hyperbolic metric on the link complement. -/
  metric : MetricSpace L.complement
  topology_eq : metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace =
    (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace L.complement)
  local_model : ∀ x : L.complement,
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph L.complement hyperbolicHalfSpace,
      x ∈ e.source ∧
      (∀ y ∈ e.source,
        ((y.val.2.val = 0 ∨ y.val.2.val = 1) ↔ (e y).val 0 = 0)) ∧
      (∀ y ∈ e.source, ∀ z ∈ e.source,
        @dist L.complement metric.toDist y z =
          2 * Real.arsinh (dist (e y).val (e z).val /
            (2 * √((e y).val 2 * (e z).val 2))))
  complete : @CompleteSpace L.complement metric.toUniformSpace
  intrinsic :
    letI : TopologicalSpace L.complement := metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
    letI : MetricSpace L.complement := metric
    ∀ x y : L.complement,
      edist x y = ⨅ p : Path x y, eVariationOn p (univ : Set unitInterval)
  finite_volume :
    @Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure L.complement
      (@MetricSpace.toEMetricSpace L.complement metric)
      (@borel L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace)
      (@BorelSpace.mk L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
        (@borel L.complement metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace) rfl)
      3 (univ : Set L.complement) < ⊤

/-- Geometric hyperbolic volume, using Euclidean-normalized three-dimensional Hausdorff measure. -/
def TGHyperbolicStructure.volume {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S]
    {L : TameLink S} (H : TGHyperbolicStructure L) : ℝ :=
  (@Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure L.complement
    (@MetricSpace.toEMetricSpace L.complement H.metric)
    (@borel L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace)
    (@BorelSpace.mk L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
      (@borel L.complement H.metric.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace) rfl)
    3 (univ : Set L.complement)).toReal

/-- The source's volume density, with minimum crossing number on the fixed surface. -/
def TGHyperbolicStructure.volumeDensity {S : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S]
    {L : TameLink S} (H : TGHyperbolicStructure L) : ℝ :=
  H.volume / L.crossingNumber

/-- Klein coordinates on the hyperbolic plane, used to give actual geodesic polygon sides. -/
def kleinCoordinates (z : UpperHalfPlane) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  let d := z.re ^ 2 + z.im ^ 2 + 1
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![2 * z.re / d, (z.re ^ 2 + z.im ^ 2 - 1) / d]

/-- The regular right-angled n-gon in Klein coordinates, with geodesic sides
represented by Euclidean chords. The source range here is `n ≥ 12`. -/
def rightAngledPolygon (n : ℕ) : Polygon (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) n where
  vertices i :=
    let a := π / (n : ℝ)
    let r := √(1 - Real.tan a ^ 2)
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![r * Real.cos (2 * a * (i : ℕ)),
      r * Real.sin (2 * a * (i : ℕ))]

/-- An edge-to-edge regular right-angled hyperbolic polygon tiling and its surface quotient.
The covering and deck group allow orientation-reversing isometries. -/
structure RightAngledTiling (S : Type*) [TopologicalSpace S] (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The tiles of the tiling of the hyperbolic plane. -/
  tiles : Set (Set UpperHalfPlane)
  /-- An isometry placing the standard right-angled `n`-gon onto each tile. -/
  placement : tiles → (UpperHalfPlane ≃ᵢ UpperHalfPlane)
  tile_eq : ∀ P : tiles,
    P.val = placement P ''
      (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' convexHull ℝ (range (rightAngledPolygon n).vertices))
  covers : ⋃₀ tiles = univ
  locally_finite : LocallyFinite (fun P : tiles ↦ P.val)
  disjoint_interiors : tiles.Pairwise (fun P Q ↦ Disjoint (interior P) (interior Q))
  edge_to_edge : ∀ P Q : tiles, P ≠ Q →
    P.val ∩ Q.val = ∅ ∨
    (∃ i j : Fin n,
      P.val ∩ Q.val = placement P ''
        (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' {(rightAngledPolygon n).vertices i}) ∧
      P.val ∩ Q.val = placement Q ''
        (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' {(rightAngledPolygon n).vertices j})) ∨
    (∃ i j : Fin n,
      P.val ∩ Q.val = placement P ''
        (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' (rightAngledPolygon n).edgeSet ℝ i) ∧
      P.val ∩ Q.val = placement Q ''
        (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' (rightAngledPolygon n).edgeSet ℝ j))
  /-- The covering map from the hyperbolic plane to the surface `S`. -/
  quotient : C(UpperHalfPlane, S)
  covering : IsCoveringMap quotient
  surjective : Function.Surjective quotient
  /-- The deck group of the covering, acting by isometries. -/
  deck : Subgroup (UpperHalfPlane ≃ᵢ UpperHalfPlane)
  fibers : ∀ x y, quotient x = quotient y ↔ ∃ g : deck, g.val x = y
  deck_preserves_tiles : ∀ (g : deck) P, P ∈ tiles → g.val '' P ∈ tiles
  finite_tile_orbits : ∃ F : Finset tiles,
    ∀ P : tiles, ∃ Q ∈ F, ∃ g : deck, P.val = g.val '' Q.val

/-- An alternating link whose projection is the edge skeleton of a quotient right-angled tiling. -/
structure TilingLink (S : Type*) [TopologicalSpace S] (n : ℕ) extends LinkDiagram S where
  /-- The right-angled tiling whose quotient edges form the link projection. -/
  tiling : RightAngledTiling S n
  projection_skeleton :
    range (fun t ↦ (curve t).1) = tiling.quotient '' (⋃ P ∈ tiling.tiles, frontier P)
  crossings_vertices :
    {q : S | ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ (curve a).1 = q ∧ (curve b).1 = q} =
      tiling.quotient ''
        (⋃ P : tiling.tiles, tiling.placement P ''
          (kleinCoordinates ⁻¹' range (rightAngledPolygon n).vertices))
  alternating : ∀ (i : Fin components) (a b : ℝ)
      (u v : Fin components × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)),
    a < b → b ≤ a + 1 →
    u ≠ (i, (a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) →
    v ≠ (i, (b : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) →
    (curve u).1 = (curve (i, (a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).1 →
    (curve v).1 = (curve (i, (b : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).1 →
    (∀ c : ℝ, a < c → c < b →
      ∀ t, (curve t).1 = (curve (i, (c : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).1 →
        t = (i, (c : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))) →
    ((curve (i, (a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).2.val < (curve u).2.val ↔
      (curve v).2.val < (curve (i, (b : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).2.val)

/-- **Conjecture 5.6**. At every fixed Euler genus, the sharp hyperbolic volume-density bound for
all links is attained by the stated nonorientable right-angled tiling family.

The index `m` is twice the source genus, including half-integral genera; the universal clause
covers surfaces of both orientation classes. -/
theorem fixed_genus_maximum (m : ℕ) (hm : 4 ≤ m) :
    let β : ℝ :=
      (∫⁻ x in rightAngledBipyramid (4 * m - 4),
        ENNReal.ofReal (((1 - ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ 2)⁻¹)).toReal / ((m : ℝ) - 1)
    (∀ S : ClosedSurface,
      S.eulerCharacteristic = 2 - (m : ℤ) →
      ∀ (L : TameLink S.carrier) (H : TGHyperbolicStructure L),
        H.volumeDensity ≤ β) ∧
    (∃ S : ClosedSurface,
      S.eulerCharacteristic = 2 - (m : ℤ) ∧
      Module.rank ℚ
        ((((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) 2).obj
          (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift ℚ))).obj (TopCat.of S.carrier))) = 0 ∧
      ∃ L : TilingLink S.carrier (4 * m - 4),
      ∃ H : TGHyperbolicStructure L.toTameLink,
        H.volumeDensity = β) := by
  sorry

end Adams2020Generalized

theorem Adams2020Generalized.fixed_genus_maximum_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Adams2020Generalized.fixed_genus_maximum.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: On extending type B parking spaces
problem_statement: In adams2026extending.lean, prove either Adams2026Extending.conjecture_1_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Adams2026Extending.conjecture_1_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On extending type B parking spaces

Authors: Anthony Adams, Joshua Dorsam, Lily Levitsky, and Megan Mann.
Origin: [MathILy-EST 2025](https://mathily.org/mathilyest/past.html).
Reference: A. Adams, J. Dorsam, L. Levitsky, and M. Mann, *On extending type B parking spaces*,
preprint (2026), 14 pp.; arXiv:2601.18090v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adams2026Extending

/-- The signed symmetric group in row-sign coordinates, with the permutation acting on signs by
`s i ↦ s (w.symm i)` (Definition 2.12). -/
abbrev B (n : ℕ) :=
  SemidirectProduct (Fin n → Units ℤ) (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) mulAutArrow

/-- The inclusion fixing the last signed letter: append sign `+1` and extend the permutation by
fixing `Fin.last n` (Introduction). -/
def inclusion (n : ℕ) : MonoidHom (B n) (B (n + 1)) :=
  let signs : MonoidHom (Fin n → Units ℤ) (Fin (n + 1) → Units ℤ) :=
    { toFun := fun s ↦ Fin.lastCases 1 s
      map_one' := by
        funext i
        cases i using Fin.lastCases <;> simp
      map_mul' := by
        intro s t
        funext i
        cases i using Fin.lastCases <;> simp }
  let perms := Equiv.Perm.extendDomainHom (finSuccAboveEquiv (Fin.last n))
  SemidirectProduct.map signs perms fun w ↦ by
    apply MonoidHom.ext
    intro s
    funext i
    change Fin.lastCases (motive := fun _ ↦ Units ℤ) 1 (fun j ↦ s (w.symm j)) i =
      Fin.lastCases (motive := fun _ ↦ Units ℤ) 1 s ((perms w).symm i)
    have hcast (v : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (j : Fin n) :
        perms v j.castSucc = (v j).castSucc := by
      simpa only [perms, Equiv.Perm.extendDomainHom_apply,
        finSuccAboveEquiv_apply, Fin.succAbove_last] using
        v.extendDomain_apply_image (finSuccAboveEquiv (Fin.last n)) j
    have hlast (v : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : perms v (Fin.last n) = Fin.last n := by
      exact v.extendDomain_apply_not_subtype (finSuccAboveEquiv (Fin.last n))
        (by simp)
    change Fin.lastCases (motive := fun _ ↦ Units ℤ) 1 (fun j ↦ s (w.symm j)) i =
      Fin.lastCases (motive := fun _ ↦ Units ℤ) 1 s (perms w.symm i)
    cases i using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => simp only [hlast, Fin.lastCases_last]
    | cast j => simp only [hcast, Fin.lastCases_castSucc]

/-- The signed action on `ZMod m` coordinates, where row sign `s i` multiplies coordinate
`x (w.symm i)` (Definitions 3.1 and 3.3). -/
@[instance_reducible]
def signedAction (m n : ℕ) : MulAction (B n) (Fin n → ZMod m) where
  smul g x i := ((g.left i : ℤ) : ZMod m) * x (g.right.symm i)
  one_smul x := by
    funext i
    change ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod m) * x i = x i
    simp
  mul_smul g h x := by
    funext i
    change (((g.left i * h.left (g.right.symm i) : Units ℤ) : ℤ) : ZMod m) *
        x (h.right.symm (g.right.symm i)) =
      ((g.left i : ℤ) : ZMod m) *
        (((h.left (g.right.symm i) : ℤ) : ZMod m) *
          x (h.right.symm (g.right.symm i)))
    simp only [Units.val_mul, Int.cast_mul, mul_assoc]

/-- **Conjecture 1.1**. For every positive modulus and rank, the complex linearization of the
signed action extends along the last-letter inclusion.

Equality on this canonical space is equivalent, by linear transport, to the source's
isomorphic restriction; the extension need not permute this basis. -/
theorem conjecture_1_1 (m n : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    letI := signedAction m n
    ∃ ρ : Representation ℂ (B (n + 1)) (MonoidAlgebra ℂ (Fin n → ZMod m)),
      ρ.comp (inclusion n) =
        Representation.ofMulAction ℂ (B n) (Fin n → ZMod m) := by
  sorry

end Adams2026Extending

theorem Adams2026Extending.conjecture_1_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adams2026Extending.conjecture_1_1 := by
  sorry

title: Sorting permutations: Games, genomes, and cycles
problem_statement: In adamyk2017sorting.lean, prove either Adamyk2017Sorting.fixed_point_not_np_complete or refute it by proving its logical negation Adamyk2017Sorting.fixed_point_not_np_complete_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Sorting permutations: Games, genomes, and cycles

Authors: K. L. M. Adamyk, E. Holmes, G. R. Mayfield, D. J. Moritz,
M. Scheepers, B. E. Tenner, and H. C. Wauck.
Origin: [Boise State University REU 2012-2013](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.2353v4#page=24).
Reference: K. L. M. Adamyk, E. Holmes, G. R. Mayfield, D. J. Moritz, M. Scheepers, B. E. Tenner,
and H. C. Wauck, *Sorting permutations: games, genomes, and cycles*, Discrete Math. Algorithms
Appl. (2017); doi:10.1142/S179383091750063X; arXiv:1410.2353v4.
-/

namespace Adamyk2017Sorting

/-- A signed permutation in inverse-image notation: each magnitude from `1` to `n` occurs once,
with an independent sign (Section 1). -/
abbrev SignedPermutation (n : ℕ) :=
  {row : List ℤ // (row.map Int.natAbs).Perm (List.range' 1 n)}

/-- A cdr move: reverse and negate the block between opposite pointers (Definition 5.1).
Endpoints use the orientation-aware pointer formulas, not the printed sign-insensitive sentence. -/
def CDR {n : ℕ} (a b : SignedPermutation n) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℤ) (left middle right : List ℤ), 0 < k ∧ k < (n : ℤ) ∧
    ((a.val = left ++ [k] ++ middle ++ [-(k + 1)] ++ right ∧
      b.val = left ++ [k, k + 1] ++ middle.reverse.map (fun x ↦ -x) ++ right) ∨
     (a.val = left ++ [-(k + 1)] ++ middle ++ [k] ++ right ∧
      b.val = left ++ [-(k + 1), -k] ++ middle.reverse.map (fun x ↦ -x) ++ right) ∨
     (a.val = left ++ [k + 1] ++ middle ++ [-k] ++ right ∧
      b.val = left ++ middle.reverse.map (fun x ↦ -x) ++ [-(k + 1), -k] ++ right) ∨
     (a.val = left ++ [-k] ++ middle ++ [k + 1] ++ right ∧
      b.val = left ++ middle.reverse.map (fun x ↦ -x) ++ [k, k + 1] ++ right))

/-- The input decoder for Problem D.5: `n > 1`, then `n` signed initial and `n` signed terminal
entries. Fields are `encodeNat` words ending in `none`, magnitude `m` is coded `2m` (positive) or
`2m + 1` (negative), and malformed inputs decode to `none`. -/
def readInstance (word : List (Option Bool)) :
    Option ((n : ℕ) × SignedPermutation n × SignedPermutation n) := do
  let [] :: reversedFields ← pure (word.splitOn none).reverse | none
  let fields ← reversedFields.reverse.mapM fun field ↦ do
    let bits := field.filterMap id
    let value := Computability.decodeNat bits
    if bits.map some = field ∧ Computability.encodeNat value = bits then
      some value
    else none
  let n :: entries ← pure fields | none
  if 1 < n ∧ entries.length = 2 * n then
    let signed := fun code : ℕ ↦
      if code % 2 = 0 then ((code / 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) else -((code / 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)
    let initial := (entries.take n).map signed
    let terminal := (entries.drop n).map signed
    if hi : (initial.map Int.natAbs).Perm (List.range' 1 n) then
      if ht : (terminal.map Int.natAbs).Perm (List.range' 1 n) then
        some ⟨n, ⟨initial, hi⟩, ⟨terminal, ht⟩⟩
      else none
    else none
  else none

/-- **Open question** (Section 8, p. 23). Deciding whether a specified cdr fixed point
is reachable (Decision Problem D.5) is not NP-complete.

NP-completeness uses Turing machines and polynomial many-one reductions; no membership in P is
claimed. The binary input encoding is a choice, as the source leaves it unspecified, and
zero-step reachability counts. -/
theorem fixed_point_not_np_complete :
    let reachabilityLanguage : Set (List (Option Bool)) := {word |
      ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ initial terminal : SignedPermutation n,
        readInstance word = some ⟨n, initial, terminal⟩ ∧
        (¬∃ next : SignedPermutation n, CDR terminal next) ∧
        Relation.ReflTransGen CDR initial terminal}
    let pairCode := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList (Option Bool))
      (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    let np : Set (List (Option Bool)) → Prop := fun language ↦
      ∃ verifier : (List (Option Bool) × List Bool) → Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime pairCode
          Computability.encodeBool verifier,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ input : List (Option Bool),
          input ∈ language ↔ ∃ certificate : List Bool,
            certificate.length ≤ bound.eval input.length ∧
            verifier (input, certificate) = true
    ¬(np reachabilityLanguage ∧
      ∀ language : Set (List (Option Bool)), np language →
        ∃ reduction : List (Option Bool) → List (Option Bool),
        ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id reduction,
          (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
          ∀ word, word ∈ language ↔ reduction word ∈ reachabilityLanguage) := by
  sorry

end Adamyk2017Sorting

theorem Adamyk2017Sorting.fixed_point_not_np_complete_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adamyk2017Sorting.fixed_point_not_np_complete := by
  sorry

title: Minimizing Closed Geodesics on Polygons and Disks
problem_statement: In adelstein2021minimizing.lean, prove either Adelstein2021Minimizing.conjecture_odd_regular_polygon_corollary_1_2_bound_is_tight or refute it by proving its logical negation Adelstein2021Minimizing.conjecture_odd_regular_polygon_corollary_1_2_bound_is_tight_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Minimizing Closed Geodesics on Polygons and Disks

Authors: Ian Adelstein, Arthur Azvolinsky, Joshua Hinman, and Alexander Schlesinger.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY](https://sumry.yale.edu/pastprojects).
Reference: I. Adelstein, A. Azvolinsky, J. Hinman, and A. Schlesinger, *Minimizing closed
geodesics on polygons and disks*, arXiv:1909.09274.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Adelstein2021Minimizing

open scoped Real

/-- The filled regular polygon with circumradius one. -/
def regularPolygonSet (n : ℕ) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  convexHull ℝ (Set.range fun i : Fin n ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![Real.cos (2 * π * (i : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)),
      Real.sin (2 * π * (i : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))])

/-- The boundary-to-polygon inclusion, with both subtypes carrying the Euclidean metric. -/
def polygonSeamInclusion (n : ℕ)
    (x : frontier (regularPolygonSet n)) : regularPolygonSet n :=
  ⟨x.1, (frontier_subset_iff_isClosed.mpr
    ((Set.finite_range (fun i : Fin n ↦
      WithLp.toLp 2 ![Real.cos (2 * π * (i : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)),
        Real.sin (2 * π * (i : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))])).isClosed_convexHull ℝ)) x.2⟩

/-- The seam inclusion preserves Euclidean distances by the subtype metric. -/
lemma polygonSeamInclusion_isometry (n : ℕ) : Isometry (polygonSeamInclusion n) := by
  intro x y
  rfl

/-- The space `X_n`: two Euclidean copies of the filled polygon glued isometrically along their
common boundary. The nonemptiness of the seam is a hypothesis supplied in the target. -/
abbrev DoubledPolygon (n : ℕ) [Nonempty (frontier (regularPolygonSet n))] :=
  Metric.GlueSpace (polygonSeamInclusion_isometry n) (polygonSeamInclusion_isometry n)

/-- A closed geodesic: a positive-period, unit-speed, locally distance-minimizing map. -/
structure ClosedGeodesic (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] where
  /-- The unit-speed periodic parametrisation. -/
  toFun : ℝ → X
  /-- The period, equal to the length of the geodesic. -/
  length : ℝ
  length_pos : 0 < length
  periodic : Function.Periodic toFun length
  locally_minimizing : ∀ t : ℝ, ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∀ a b : ℝ, |a - t| < ε → |b - t| < ε →
      dist (toFun a) (toFun b) = |b - a|

/-- A `1 / k` geodesic: every subarc of length `L / k` minimizes distance (Section 1). -/
def ClosedGeodesic.IsOneOverK {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]
    (γ : ClosedGeodesic X) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ k ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
    dist (γ.toFun t) (γ.toFun (t + γ.length / (k : ℝ))) = γ.length / (k : ℝ)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (tightness, after Corollary 1.2). The minimizing index of the
doubled odd regular `n`-gon is twice its smallest prime divisor.

Positive-length closed geodesics are the contextual convention; unit speed is a
reparametrization, not an extra geometric restriction. -/
theorem conjecture_odd_regular_polygon_corollary_1_2_bound_is_tight
    (n d : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hn_odd : Odd n)
    (hd_prime : Nat.Prime d) (hd_dvd : d ∣ n)
    (hd_min : ∀ q : ℕ, Nat.Prime q → q ∣ n → d ≤ q) :
    ∃ hseam : Nonempty (frontier (regularPolygonSet n)),
      letI := hseam
      (∃ γ : ClosedGeodesic (DoubledPolygon n), γ.IsOneOverK (2 * d)) ∧
        ∀ k : ℕ, (∃ γ : ClosedGeodesic (DoubledPolygon n), γ.IsOneOverK k) →
          2 * d ≤ k := by
  sorry

end Adelstein2021Minimizing

theorem Adelstein2021Minimizing.conjecture_odd_regular_polygon_corollary_1_2_bound_is_tight_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adelstein2021Minimizing.conjecture_odd_regular_polygon_corollary_1_2_bound_is_tight := by
  sorry

title: Oblivious Points on Translation Surfaces
problem_statement: In adelstein2022oblivious.lean, prove either Adelstein2022Oblivious.question_6_5 or refute it by proving its logical negation Adelstein2022Oblivious.question_6_5_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Oblivious Points on Translation Surfaces

Authors: Ian Adelstein, Krish Desai, Anthony Ji, and Grace Zdeblick.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY 2019](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: I. Adelstein, K. Desai, A. Ji, and G. Zdeblick, *Oblivious points on translation
surfaces*, arXiv:2008.08494v1 (2020).
-/

namespace Adelstein2022Oblivious

/-- The side identifications of `n` unit squares: the right side of square `i` is glued to the
left side of `horizontal i`, and its top side to the bottom side of `vertical i` (Section 2.1). -/
inductive SquareGluing {n : ℕ} (horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    Fin n × unitInterval × unitInterval → Fin n × unitInterval × unitInterval → Prop
  /-- The right side of square `i` is glued to the left side of square `horizontal i`. -/
  | right (i : Fin n) (t : unitInterval) :
      SquareGluing horizontal vertical (i, 1, t) (horizontal i, 0, t)
  /-- The top side of square `i` is glued to the bottom side of square `vertical i`. -/
  | top (i : Fin n) (t : unitInterval) :
      SquareGluing horizontal vertical (i, t, 1) (vertical i, t, 0)

/-- The square-tiled surface glued from these identifications, with the quotient topology
(Section 2.1). -/
abbrev Surface {n : ℕ} (horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Type :=
  Quot (SquareGluing horizontal vertical)

/-- The projection to the square torus, reducing both local coordinates modulo one
(Remark 2.6). -/
def torusProjection {n : ℕ} (horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    C(Surface horizontal vertical, AddCircle (1 : ℝ) × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) where
  toFun := Quot.lift
    (fun p : Fin n × unitInterval × unitInterval ↦
      ((p.2.1.val : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)), (p.2.2.val : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))))
    (by
      intro a b h
      cases h <;> simp [AddCircle.coe_period])
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply continuous_quot_lift
    fun_prop

/-- A regular point of the surface.

Regularity is encoded as the torus projection being a local homeomorphism at the point, so
regular square vertices are included. -/
def IsRegularPoint {n : ℕ} {horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)}
    (p : Surface horizontal vertical) : Prop :=
  IsLocalHomeomorphOn (torusProjection horizontal vertical) {p}

/-- An oblivious point: a regular point through which no closed geodesic passes
(Definition 1.1).

A closed geodesic is encoded as an injective loop on the circle of period one through regular
points whose torus projection is a straight motion with nonzero velocity. -/
def IsObliviousPoint {n : ℕ} {horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)}
    (p : Surface horizontal vertical) : Prop :=
  IsRegularPoint p ∧
    ¬∃ (curve : C(AddCircle (1 : ℝ), Surface horizontal vertical)) (velocity : ℝ × ℝ),
      Function.Injective curve ∧ velocity ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ t, IsRegularPoint (curve t)) ∧
        p ∈ Set.range curve ∧
        ∀ t : ℝ,
          torusProjection horizontal vertical (curve (t : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) =
            torusProjection horizontal vertical (curve 0) +
              (((t * velocity.1 : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)),
                ((t * velocity.2 : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))

/-- **Question 6.5** (Section 6, p. 12). For every sufficiently large `n` there is a connected
square-tiled surface with exactly `n` unit squares and an oblivious point.

Connectedness follows the surfaces of Section 4, and all tiles are unit squares as in
Remark 2.6. -/
theorem question_6_5 :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ horizontal vertical : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ConnectedSpace (Surface horizontal vertical) ∧
        ∃ p : Surface horizontal vertical, IsObliviousPoint p := by
  sorry

end Adelstein2022Oblivious

theorem Adelstein2022Oblivious.question_6_5_neg : ¬ type_of% @Adelstein2022Oblivious.question_6_5 := by
  sorry

title: A conjectural asymptotic formula for multiplicative chaos in number theory
problem_statement: In aggarwal2022conjectural.lean, prove either Aggarwal2022Conjectural.conjecture_1_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Aggarwal2022Conjectural.conjecture_1_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A conjectural asymptotic formula for multiplicative chaos in number theory

Authors: Daksh Aggarwal, Unique Subedi, William Verreault, Asif Zaman, and Chenghui Zheng.
Origin: [Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program
2020](https://www.fields.utoronto.ca/activities/20-21/2020-FUSRP).
Reference: D. Aggarwal, U. Subedi, W. Verreault, A. Zaman, and C. Zheng, *A conjectural
asymptotic formula for multiplicative chaos in number theory*, preprint (2021), 18 pp.;
arXiv:2108.11367v1.
-/

noncomputable section

open scoped Topology
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter

namespace Aggarwal2022Conjectural

/-- The coefficient `A(n)` in (1.1), via the partition expansion (2.1)-(2.2). Coordinate
`i : Fin n` represents `X(i + 1)`. -/
def A (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ p : Nat.Partition n, ∏ i : Fin n,
    (x i / √(i.val + 1)) ^ p.parts.count (i.val + 1) /
      (Nat.factorial (p.parts.count (i.val + 1)) : ℝ)

/-- **Conjecture 1.4**. For both real standard Gaussian and uniform-sign inputs,
`(log N) ^ (1 / 4) E[|A(N)|]` tends to a finite positive law-dependent constant.

The finite product laws model the first `N` coordinates of each iid sequence, and the limit is
along all natural `N`; the complex-Gaussian case (Conjecture 1.1) is not included. -/
theorem conjecture_1_4 :
    ∃ C_R C_S : ℝ, 0 < C_R ∧ 0 < C_S ∧
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
        Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ∫ x : Fin N → ℝ, |A N x|
            ∂(Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N ↦ gaussianReal 0 1)))
        atTop (𝓝 C_R) ∧
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
        Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ∫ x : Fin N → ℝ, |A N x|
            ∂(Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N ↦
              bernoulliMeasure (1 : ℝ) (-1) ⟨(1 : ℝ) / 2, by norm_num⟩)))
        atTop (𝓝 C_S) := by sorry

end Aggarwal2022Conjectural

theorem Aggarwal2022Conjectural.conjecture_1_4_neg : ¬ type_of% @Aggarwal2022Conjectural.conjecture_1_4 := by
  sorry

title: Identifiability of directed-cycle and catenary linear compartmental models
problem_statement: In ahmed2026identifiability.lean, prove either Ahmed2026Identifiability.conjecture_4_6 or refute it by proving its logical negation Ahmed2026Identifiability.conjecture_4_6_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Identifiability of directed-cycle and catenary linear compartmental models

Authors: Saber Ahmed, Natasha Crepeau, Paul R. Dessauer Jr., Alexis Edozie,
Odalys Garcia-Lopez, Tanisha Grimsley, Jordy Lopez Garcia, Viridiana Neri, and Anne Shiu.
Origin: [MSRI-UP 2022](https://people.tamu.edu/~annejls/).
Reference: S. Ahmed, N. Crepeau, P. R. Dessauer Jr., A. Edozie, O. Garcia-Lopez, T. Grimsley,
J. Lopez Garcia, V. Neri, and A. Shiu, *Identifiability of directed-cycle and catenary linear
compartmental models*, preprint (2025); arXiv:2412.05283v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Ahmed2026Identifiability

open MeasureTheory Topology

/-- The parameters of the model: one per cycle edge and one per leak (Definition 2.1). Lean
vertex `i` labels source compartment `i.val + 1`. -/
