abbrev ParameterIndex {n : ℕ} (leaks : Finset (Fin n)) :=
  Fin n ⊕ {i : Fin n // i ∈ leaks}

/-- The compartmental matrix for the directed cycle and its leaks (Definition 2.6). -/
def compartmentalMatrix {n : ℕ} (leaks : Finset (Fin n))
    (k : ParameterIndex leaks → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
  fun i j ↦
    if i = j then -(k (Sum.inl j) + if h : j ∈ leaks then k (Sum.inr ⟨j, h⟩) else 0)
    else if i = finRotate n j then k (Sum.inl j) else 0

/-- The coefficient map for the given input and output `p`, via the adjugate entry for the
signed minor in (3) (Section 2.2). Constant coordinates are retained, as Remark 2.12 permits. -/
def coefficientMap {n : ℕ} (leaks : Finset (Fin n)) (input p : Fin n)
    (k : ParameterIndex leaks → ℝ) : (Fin n → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  let B := (compartmentalMatrix leaks k).charmatrix
  (fun d ↦ B.det.coeff d.val, fun d ↦ (B.adjugate p input).coeff d.val)

/-- **Conjecture 4.6**. For every identifiable directed-cycle model with input in compartment one
and one output, each specified equality between a leaking rate and an earlier nonleaking rate
defines a hyperplane in the singular locus (Definition 4.1). -/
theorem conjecture_4_6 {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (leaks : Finset (Fin n)) (p : Fin n)
    (hidentifiable : ∀ᵐ k : ParameterIndex leaks → ℝ ∂volume,
      ∃ U : Set (ParameterIndex leaks → ℝ), U ∈ 𝓝 k ∧
        Set.InjOn (coefficientMap leaks ⟨0, by omega⟩ p) U)
    (a ℓ : Fin n) (ha : a < p) (hanot : a ∉ leaks)
    (hℓ : ℓ ∈ leaks) (hℓp : ℓ ≤ p)
    (k : ParameterIndex leaks → ℝ)
    (hplane : k (Sum.inl ℓ) + k (Sum.inr ⟨ℓ, hℓ⟩) = k (Sum.inl a)) :
    ¬Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (coefficientMap leaks ⟨0, by omega⟩ p) k) := by
  sorry

end Ahmed2026Identifiability

theorem Ahmed2026Identifiability.conjecture_4_6_neg : ¬ type_of% @Ahmed2026Identifiability.conjecture_4_6 := by
  sorry

title: Connectedness of the Free Uniform Spanning Forest as a function of edge weights
problem_statement: In alexy2022connectedness.lean, prove either Alexy2022Connectedness.conjecture_1_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Alexy2022Connectedness.conjecture_1_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Connectedness of the Free Uniform Spanning Forest as a function of edge weights

Authors: Marcell Alexy, Marton Borbenyi, Andras Imolay, and Adam Timar.
Origin: [Budapest REU Math Program 2020](https://reu.elte.hu/pastworkshops.html).
Reference: M. Alexy, M. Borbenyi, A. Imolay, and A. Timar, *Connectedness of the free uniform
spanning forest as a function of edge weights*, Electron. Commun. Probab. **27** (2022),
paper 13, 1-12; doi:10.1214/22-ECP453; arXiv:2011.12904v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Alexy2022Connectedness

open MeasureTheory Filter SimpleGraph
open scoped Topology ENNReal

/-- The free uniform spanning forest law: the edge-cylinder limit of weighted spanning trees
along every connected finite induced exhaustion. A first clause requires some exhaustion to
exist, so the condition is not vacuous. -/
def IsFreeUniformSpanningForest {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : Sym2 V → ℝ)
    (μ : ProbabilityMeasure (Set (Sym2 V))) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact
    (∃ K : ℕ → Finset V, Monotone K ∧
      (∀ n, (G.induce (K n : Set V)).Connected) ∧ ∀ v, ∃ n, v ∈ K n) ∧
    (∀ᵐ E ∂(μ : Measure (Set (Sym2 V))), E ⊆ G.edgeSet) ∧
    ∀ (K : ℕ → Finset V) (hK : Monotone K)
      (hc : ∀ n, (G.induce (K n : Set V)).Connected)
      (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ n, v ∈ K n) (A B : Finset (Sym2 V)),
      Tendsto (fun n ↦
        let F := G.induce (K n : Set V)
        let trees := ({J | J ≤ F ∧ J.IsTree} : Finset (SimpleGraph (K n)))
        let weight := fun J : SimpleGraph (K n) ↦
          ∏ e ∈ J.edgeFinset, c (Sym2.map Subtype.val e)
        (∑ J ∈ trees,
          if (A : Set (Sym2 V)) ⊆ (J.map Subtype.val).edgeSet ∧
              Disjoint (B : Set (Sym2 V)) (J.map Subtype.val).edgeSet
          then weight J else 0) / (∑ J ∈ trees, weight J))
        atTop (𝓝 ((μ : Measure (Set (Sym2 V))).real
          {E | (A : Set (Sym2 V)) ⊆ E ∧ Disjoint (B : Set (Sym2 V)) E}))

/-- The conductance: `w` inside each finite-factor copy and `1` on edges parallel to the tree
factor. Values on nonedges are unused. -/
def productConductance {V W : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (w : ℝ) :
    Sym2 (V × W) → ℝ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨(fun a b ↦ if a.1 = b.1 then w else 1), by
    intro a b
    simp only [eq_comm]⟩

/-- **Conjecture 1.1**. Both connectivity phases are intervals, and an extended critical
conductance separates one component from infinitely many components.

The finite connected factor is arbitrary (no transitivity or regularity), and the regular tree
includes degree two. Almost-sure assertions hold separately for each weight; nothing is asserted
at the critical weight. -/
theorem conjecture_1_1 {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [Infinite V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) [T.LocallyFinite] (hT : T.IsTree)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : T.IsRegularOfDegree d)
    {n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (hH : H.Connected)
    (μ : {w : ℝ // 0 < w} → ProbabilityMeasure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n))))
    (hμ : ∀ w, IsFreeUniformSpanningForest (T □ H)
      (productConductance w.val) (μ w)) :
    (∀ (a b : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}), a.val < b.val →
      (∀ᵐ E ∂(μ a : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
        (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) →
      (∀ᵐ E ∂(μ b : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
        (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) →
      ∀ (w : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}), a.val ≤ w.val → w.val ≤ b.val →
        ∀ᵐ E ∂(μ w : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
          (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) ∧
    (∀ (a b : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}), a.val < b.val →
      (∀ᵐ E ∂(μ a : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
        ¬(SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) →
      (∀ᵐ E ∂(μ b : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
        ¬(SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) →
      ∀ (w : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}), a.val ≤ w.val → w.val ≤ b.val →
        ∀ᵐ E ∂(μ w : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
          ¬(SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) ∧
    ∃ γ : ℝ≥0∞, ∀ (w : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}),
      (γ < ENNReal.ofReal w.val →
        ∀ᵐ E ∂(μ w : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
          (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).Connected) ∧
      (ENNReal.ofReal w.val < γ →
        ∀ᵐ E ∂(μ w : Measure (Set (Sym2 (V × Fin n)))),
          Infinite (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet E).ConnectedComponent) := by

end Alexy2022Connectedness

title: Non-Archimedean Henon Maps, Attractors, and Horseshoes
problem_statement: In allen2018non.lean, prove either Allen2018Non.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Allen2018Non.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Non-Archimedean Henon Maps, Attractors, and Horseshoes

Authors: Kenneth Allen, David DeMark, and Clayton Petsche.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2016](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/reucv.html).
Reference: K. Allen, D. DeMark, and C. Petsche, *Non-Archimedean Henon maps, attractors, and
horseshoes*, Res. Number Theory **4** (2018), Paper 5; doi:10.1007/s40993-018-0105-2.
-/

namespace Allen2018Non

/-- The quadratic Henon automorphism and its inverse (equations (1) and (2)). -/
def henon {K : Type*} [Field K] (a b : K) (hb : b ≠ 0) : Equiv.Perm (K × K) where
  toFun z := (a + b * z.2 - z.1 ^ 2, z.1)
  invFun z := (z.2, (-a + z.1 + z.2 ^ 2) / b)
  left_inv := by
    rintro ⟨x, y⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · rfl
    · change (-a + (a + b * y - x ^ 2) + x ^ 2) / b = y
      field_simp [hb]
      ring
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨x, y⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · change a + b * ((-a + x + y ^ 2) / b) - y ^ 2 = x
      field_simp [hb]
      ring
    · rfl

/-- The filled Julia set: points with bounded forward and backward orbits (equation (3)). The
product norm is the maximum of the two coordinate norms, as in the source. -/
def filledJulia {K : Type*} [NormedField K] (a b : K) (hb : b ≠ 0) : Set (K × K) :=
  {z | (∃ R : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ,
      ‖((henon a b hb : K × K → K × K)^[n]) z‖ ≤ R) ∧
    (∃ R : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ,
      ‖(((henon a b hb).symm : K × K → K × K)^[n]) z‖ ≤ R)}

/-- **Conjecture 1** (Section 4.2). Every complete, locally compact non-Archimedean field of odd
residue characteristic admits a quadratic Henon map in region `H_II^+` with infinite two-sided
filled Julia set.

Odd residue characteristic is expressed as `‖(2 : K)‖ = 1`, as in Section 2. -/
theorem conjecture_1 (K : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [CompleteSpace K]
    [LocallyCompactSpace K] [IsUltrametricDist K] (hodd : ‖(2 : K)‖ = 1) :
    ∃ (a b : K) (hb : b ≠ 0),
      ‖a‖ ≤ 1 ∧ ‖b‖ < 1 ∧ (filledJulia a b hb).Infinite := by
  sorry

end Allen2018Non

theorem Allen2018Non.conjecture_1_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Allen2018Non.conjecture_1.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Coincidences among skew stable and dual stable Grothendieck polynomials
problem_statement: In alwaise2018coincidences.lean, prove either Alwaise2018Coincidences.conjecture_6_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Alwaise2018Coincidences.conjecture_6_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Coincidences among skew stable and dual stable Grothendieck polynomials

Authors: Ethan Alwaise, Shuli Chen, Alexander Clifton, Rebecca Patrias, Rohil Prasad, Madeline
Shinners, and Albert Zheng.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2016](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: E. Alwaise, S. Chen, A. Clifton, R. Patrias, R. Prasad, M. Shinners, and A. Zheng,
*Coincidences among skew stable and dual stable Grothendieck polynomials*, Involve **11** (2018),
143-167; doi:10.2140/involve.2018.11.143.
-/

namespace Alwaise2018Coincidences

open Finset

/-- The cells of the ribbon with row-length composition `c`, read bottom to top (Section 2).
Rows are numbered upward and consecutive rows overlap in one column. -/
def ribbonCells {n : ℕ} (c : Composition n) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  (Finset.range c.length).biUnion fun r ↦
    (Finset.range (c.blocks.getD r 0)).image fun j ↦
      (r, ((c.blocks.take r).map (fun a ↦ a - 1)).sum + j)

/-- Set-valued tableaux on a diagram with rows numbered upward (Section 2). The alphabet
`1, ..., N` is represented by `Fin N`. -/
abbrev SetValuedTableau (D : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (N : ℕ) :=
  {T : D → Finset (Fin N) //
    (∀ b, (T b).Nonempty) ∧
    (∀ b c, b.val.1 = c.val.1 → b.val.2 < c.val.2 →
      ∀ (i : T b) (j : T c), i.val ≤ j.val) ∧
    (∀ b c, b.val.2 = c.val.2 → b.val.1 < c.val.1 →
      ∀ (i : T b) (j : T c), j.val < i.val)}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The stable Grothendieck polynomial in the first `N` variables: a sum over set-valued
tableaux, signed by the number of entries minus cells (Section 2). -/
noncomputable def stableGrothendieck (D : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (N : ℕ) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin N) ℤ :=
  ∑ T : SetValuedTableau D N,
    MvPolynomial.C ((-1 : ℤ) ^ ((∑ b : D, #(T.val b)) - #D)) *
      ∏ b : D, ∏ i ∈ T.val b, MvPolynomial.X i

/-- **Conjecture 6.1** (p. 166; preprint Conjecture 5.1). Two ribbons have the same stable
Grothendieck series exactly when they coincide or differ by a 180-degree rotation, which reverses
the row composition.

The sign exponent counts skew cells, following the source's prose and Section 4 identity rather
than the outer-partition size printed in Section 2. -/
theorem conjecture_6_1 {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    (a : Composition n) (b : Composition m) :
    (∀ N : ℕ, stableGrothendieck (ribbonCells a) N =
      stableGrothendieck (ribbonCells b) N) ↔
      b.blocks = a.blocks ∨ b.blocks = a.blocks.reverse := by
  sorry

end Alwaise2018Coincidences

theorem Alwaise2018Coincidences.conjecture_6_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Alwaise2018Coincidences.conjecture_6_1 := by
  sorry

title: On the subgraph query problem
problem_statement: In alweiss2021subgraph.lean, prove either Alweiss2021Subgraph.conjecture_16_two_degenerate_query_exponent or refute it by proving its logical negation Alweiss2021Subgraph.conjecture_16_two_degenerate_query_exponent_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the subgraph query problem

Authors: Ryan Alweiss, Chady Ben Hamida, Xiaoyu He, and Alexander Moreira.
Origin: [Stanford SURIM
2019](https://surim.stanford.edu/publications/combinatorics/query-complexity-degenerate-graphs).
Reference: R. Alweiss, C. Ben Hamida, X. He, and A. Moreira, *On the subgraph query problem*,
Combin. Probab. Comput. **30** (2021), 1-16; doi:10.1017/S0963548320000218; arXiv:1911.04413v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Alweiss2021Subgraph

open SimpleGraph
open scoped Topology
open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- A graph is `d`-degenerate when every nonempty induced subgraph has a
vertex of degree at most `d` (Section 1). -/
def IsDegenerate {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset V, S.Nonempty → ∃ v, ∃ hv : v ∈ S,
    (G.induce (fun w ↦ w ∈ S)).degree ⟨v, hv⟩ ≤ d

/-- A `(1,1)`-degenerate partition: an ordered partition into induced trees, each of whose
vertices has at most one neighbor in earlier trees (Section 5). -/
def IsOneDegeneratePartition {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ T : Fin k → Finset V,
    (∀ i, (T i).Nonempty ∧ (G.induce (fun v ↦ v ∈ T i)).IsTree) ∧
    (∀ v : V, ∃ i, v ∈ T i) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin k, i ≠ j → Disjoint (T i) (T j)) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin k, ∀ v ∈ T i,
      #({w | G.Adj v w ∧ ∃ j : Fin k, j < i ∧ w ∈ T j} : Finset V) ≤ 1

/-- Finite adaptive adjacency-query strategies on `N` vertex labels. A bounded strategy on
`G(∞, p)` uses only finitely many labels, so `Fin N` suffices. -/
inductive AdaptiveQueryTree (N : ℕ) where
  | done : AdaptiveQueryTree N
  | query (u v : Fin N) (hne : u ≠ v)
      (absent present : AdaptiveQueryTree N) : AdaptiveQueryTree N

namespace AdaptiveQueryTree

open scoped Classical in
/-- The queried unordered edges along the path selected by `G`. -/
def queriesOn {N : ℕ} : AdaptiveQueryTree N → SimpleGraph (Fin N) →
    Finset (Sym2 (Fin N))
  | done, _ => ∅
  | query u v _ absent present, G =>
      insert s(u, v) (if G.Adj u v then present.queriesOn G else absent.queriesOn G)

/-- The worst-case query budget, including repeated queries if a strategy makes them. -/
def queryCount {N : ℕ} : AdaptiveQueryTree N → ℕ
  | done => 0
  | query _ _ _ absent present => 1 + max absent.queryCount present.queryCount

end AdaptiveQueryTree

/-- The query complexity `f(H, p)`: the least worst-case budget that finds a copy of `H` with
probability at least `1 / 2` (Section 1). A copy must lie in the revealed edges, and the
feasible set is nonempty for `0 < p ≤ 1`. -/
def adaptiveSubgraphQueryCost {V : Type*}
    (H : SimpleGraph V) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p ∧ p ≤ 1) : ℝ :=
  sInf {q : ℝ | ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ T : AdaptiveQueryTree N,
    (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤
      (SimpleGraph.binomialRandom (Fin N) ⟨p, le_of_lt hp.1, hp.2⟩).real
        {G | SimpleGraph.IsContained H
          (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet ((T.queriesOn G : Set (Sym2 (Fin N))) ∩ G.edgeSet))} ∧
      q = (T.queryCount : ℝ)}

/-- **Conjecture 16**. A `2`-degenerate graph which is not `(1,1)`-degenerate has query complexity
`f(H, p) = b ^ (2 - o(1))`, where `b = 1 / p` tends to infinity.

The asymptotic is stated as two-sided exponent bounds. -/
theorem conjecture_16_two_degenerate_query_exponent
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (hdeg : IsDegenerate H 2) (hnot : ¬IsOneDegeneratePartition H)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ b : ℝ in Filter.atTop, 1 < b ∧
      ∀ hp : 0 < b⁻¹ ∧ b⁻¹ ≤ 1,
        b ^ (2 - ε) ≤ adaptiveSubgraphQueryCost H b⁻¹ hp ∧
        adaptiveSubgraphQueryCost H b⁻¹ hp ≤ b ^ (2 + ε) := by
  sorry

end Alweiss2021Subgraph

theorem Alweiss2021Subgraph.conjecture_16_two_degenerate_query_exponent_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Alweiss2021Subgraph.conjecture_16_two_degenerate_query_exponent.{u0} := by
  sorry

/-!
# Spectral properties of the Schreier graphs of the basilica group

Authors: Kyle Ambrose, Noah Dunham, Michael Morris, Luke G. Rogers, and Alexander Teplyaev.
Origin: [University of Connecticut REU
2025](https://mathreu.uconn.edu/2025/06/09/reu-math-uconn-2025/).
Reference: K. Ambrose, N. Dunham, M. Morris, L. G. Rogers, and A. Teplyaev, *Spectral properties
of the Schreier graphs of the basilica group*, preprint (2026); arXiv:2606.07430v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Ambrose2026Spectral

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

/-- The rational functions `ζ_n` with the source's initial data ((4.7)-(4.8)). -/
def zeta : ℕ → RatFunc ℝ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => RatFunc.X - 2
  | 2 => (RatFunc.X ^ 2 - 6 * RatFunc.X + 4) / (RatFunc.X - 2)
  | 3 => (RatFunc.X ^ 4 - 12 * RatFunc.X ^ 3 + 42 * RatFunc.X ^ 2 -
      44 * RatFunc.X + 8) / (RatFunc.X ^ 2 - 6 * RatFunc.X + 4)
  | n + 4 => 2 + (1 + 2 / zeta (n + 3)) * (zeta (n + 2) ^ 2 - 4)

/-- **Conjecture 5.13**. Every gap label of the Basilica KNS measure is dyadic.

The measure is the explicit atomic measure of Theorem 5.7, on the distinct real roots of the
reduced numerators of Theorem 4.11. A gap label is the mass to the left of a point outside the
support, so the exterior components give the labels `0` and `1`. -/
theorem conjecture_5_13 :
    let μ : Measure ℝ := Measure.sum fun n : ℕ ↦
      ((6 : ℝ≥0∞) * 2 ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ •
        ∑ x ∈ (zeta (n + 1)).num.roots.toFinset, Measure.dirac x
    ∀ x : ℝ, x ∉ μ.support →
      ∃ j k : ℕ, μ (Set.Iic x) = (j : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 ^ k := by
  sorry

end Ambrose2026Spectral

title: Complementation of Subquandles
source_label: Unnumbered conjecture (end of Section 3, arXiv v1, p. 18)
problem_statement: In amsberry2025complementation.lean, prove either Amsberry2025Complementation.profinite_subquandle_complement or refute it by proving its logical negation Amsberry2025Complementation.profinite_subquandle_complement_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Complementation of Subquandles

Authors: Kieran Amsberry, August Bergquist, Thomas Horstkamp, Meghan Lee, and David Yetter.
Origin: [Kansas State University SUMaR
2022](https://www.math.ksu.edu/research/reu/results2022_files/results2022.html).
Reference: K. J. Amsberry, A. Bergquist, T. Horstkamp, M. Lee, and D. Yetter, *Complementation of
subquandles*, Involve **18** (2025), no. 3, 417-435; arXiv:2304.09747v1.
-/

universe u v

namespace Amsberry2025Complementation

/-- A subquandle: a subset closed under both quandle operations (Definition 2.12). -/
def IsSubquandle {Q : Type u} [Quandle Q] (S : Set Q) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, x ∈ S → y ∈ S → Shelf.act x y ∈ S ∧ Rack.invAct x y ∈ S

/-- The subquandle generated by a subset (Section 3). -/
def generatedSubquandle {Q : Type u} [Quandle Q] (S : Set Q) : Set Q :=
  ⋂₀ {T : Set Q | IsSubquandle T ∧ S ⊆ T}

/-- The inverse limit: compatible tuples in the product of the inverse system (Definition 3.31). -/
def QuandleLimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] (Q : I → Type v) [∀ i, Quandle (Q i)]
    (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → ShelfHom (Q j) (Q i)) : Type (max u v) :=
  {x : ∀ i, Q i // ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), f i j h (x j) = x i}

/-- The quandle structure on the inverse limit, with coordinatewise operations
(Proposition 3.32). -/
instance limitQuandle {I : Type u} [Preorder I] (Q : I → Type v)
    [∀ i, Quandle (Q i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → ShelfHom (Q j) (Q i)) :
    Quandle (QuandleLimit Q f) where
  act x y := ⟨fun i ↦ Shelf.act (x.val i) (y.val i), by
    intro i j h
    change f i j h (Shelf.act (x.val j) (y.val j)) = Shelf.act (x.val i) (y.val i)
    rw [ShelfHom.map_act, x.property i j h, y.property i j h]⟩
  invAct x y := ⟨fun i ↦ Rack.invAct (x.val i) (y.val i), by
    intro i j h
    apply (Rack.act' (x.val i)).injective
    change Shelf.act (x.val i) (f i j h (Rack.invAct (x.val j) (y.val j))) =
      Shelf.act (x.val i) (Rack.invAct (x.val i) (y.val i))
    rw [← x.property i j h, ← ShelfHom.map_act, Rack.act_invAct_eq,
      Rack.act_invAct_eq, y.property i j h]⟩
  self_distrib := by
    intro x y z
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    exact Shelf.self_distrib
  left_inv := by
    intro x y
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    exact Rack.invAct_act_eq (x.val i) (y.val i)
  right_inv := by
    intro x y
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    exact Rack.act_invAct_eq (x.val i) (y.val i)
  fix := by
    intro x
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    exact Quandle.fix

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (end of Section 3, arXiv v1, p. 18). Every subquandle of a
profinite quandle has a disjoint subquandle that generates the whole quandle together with it.

All algebraic subquandles are included, not just closed ones; Mathlib's left action reverses the
source operation's arguments. -/
theorem profinite_subquandle_complement
    {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [IsDirectedOrder I]
    {Q : I → Type v} [∀ i, Quandle (Q i)] [∀ i, Finite (Q i)]
    {f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → ShelfHom (Q j) (Q i)}
    [InverseSystem (fun {i j} h ↦ (f i j h : Q j → Q i))]
    (S : Set (QuandleLimit Q f)) (hS : IsSubquandle S) :
    ∃ T : Set (QuandleLimit Q f), IsSubquandle T ∧
      Disjoint S T ∧ generatedSubquandle (S ∪ T) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Amsberry2025Complementation

theorem Amsberry2025Complementation.profinite_subquandle_complement_neg.{u0, u1} : ¬ type_of% @Amsberry2025Complementation.profinite_subquandle_complement.{u0, u1} := by
  sorry

title: Jacobi-Trudi determinants over finite fields
problem_statement: In anzis2018jacobi.lean, prove either Anzis2018Jacobi.conjecture_5_10 or refute it by proving its logical negation Anzis2018Jacobi.conjecture_5_10_neg.

/-!
# Jacobi-Trudi determinants over finite fields

Authors: Ben Anzis, Shuli Chen, Yibo Gao, Jesse Kim, Zhaoqi Li, and Rebecca Patrias.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2016](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: B. Anzis, S. Chen, Y. Gao, J. Kim, Z. Li, and R. Patrias, *Jacobi-Trudi determinants
over finite fields*, Ann. Comb. **22** (2018), 447-489; arXiv:1611.00216v1.
-/

namespace Anzis2018Jacobi

/-- The Jacobi-Trudi matrix, with `h` listing the values of `h_1, h_2, ...` (Definition 2.3).
Entries beyond the supplied finite list are zero. -/
def jacobiTrudi {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (lam : YoungDiagram) (h : List R) :
    Matrix (Fin (lam.colLen 0)) (Fin (lam.colLen 0)) R :=
  fun i j ↦
    let m : ℤ := (lam.rowLen i : ℤ) - (i.val : ℤ) + (j.val : ℤ)
    if m < 0 then 0 else if m = 0 then 1 else h.getD (m.toNat - 1) 0

/-- **Conjecture 5.10** (p. 15). The vanishing probability of a Schur function under uniform
finite-field specialization is at most the singularity probability of a uniformly random square
matrix with as many rows as the partition. -/
theorem conjecture_5_10 (K : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype K]
    (lam : YoungDiagram) (hlam : lam.cells.Nonempty) :
    (Nat.card {x : Fin (lam.rowLen 0 + lam.colLen 0 - 1) → K //
        (jacobiTrudi lam (List.ofFn x)).det = 0} : ℚ) /
        (Fintype.card K : ℚ) ^ (lam.rowLen 0 + lam.colLen 0 - 1) ≤
      1 - (Nat.card (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin (lam.colLen 0)) K) : ℚ) /
        (Fintype.card K : ℚ) ^ (lam.colLen 0 ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end Anzis2018Jacobi

  sorry

title: Origamis associated to minimally-intersecting filling pairs
problem_statement: In aougab2022origamis.lean, prove either Aougab2022Origamis.conjecture_1_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Aougab2022Origamis.conjecture_1_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Origamis associated to minimally-intersecting filling pairs

Authors: Tarik Aougab, William W. Menasco, and Mark Nieland.
Origin: [Summer@ICERM 2018](https://icerm.brown.edu/program/summer@icerm/si-18).
Reference: T. Aougab, W. W. Menasco, and M. Nieland, *Origamis associated to
minimally-intersecting filling pairs*, preprint (2022), 15 pp.; arXiv:2108.10268v2.
-/

namespace Aougab2022Origamis

/-- Square-gluing permutations of degree `2g - 1` in the minimal stratum `H(2g - 2)`. Products act
right to left, and connectedness follows from the full commutator cycle. -/
def Origami (g : ℕ) :=
  { p : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * g - 1)) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * g - 1)) //
    2 ≤ g ∧ (p.1 * p.2 * p.1⁻¹ * p.2⁻¹).IsCycleOn Set.univ }

instance (g : ℕ) : Finite (Origami g) := by
  unfold Origami
  infer_instance

/-- Relabel every square simultaneously in the horizontal and vertical gluings. -/
def relabel {g : ℕ} (s : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * g - 1)))
    (o : Origami g) : Origami g :=
  ⟨(s * o.val.1 * s⁻¹, s * o.val.2 * s⁻¹), o.property.1, by
    have h := o.property.2.conj (g := s)
    have he : (s * o.val.1 * s⁻¹) * (s * o.val.2 * s⁻¹) *
        (s * o.val.1 * s⁻¹)⁻¹ * (s * o.val.2 * s⁻¹)⁻¹ =
        s * (o.val.1 * o.val.2 * o.val.1⁻¹ * o.val.2⁻¹) * s⁻¹ := by
      group
    rw [he]
    simpa only [Set.image_univ, Equiv.range_eq_univ] using h⟩

/-- The standard determinant-one horizontal shear and its inverse on ambient origamis. -/
def shearT (g : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (Origami g) where
  toFun o := ⟨(o.val.1, o.val.2 * o.val.1⁻¹), o.property.1, by
    convert o.property.2 using 1; group⟩
  invFun o := ⟨(o.val.1, o.val.2 * o.val.1), o.property.1, by
    convert o.property.2 using 1; group⟩
  left_inv o := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    group
  right_inv o := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    group

/-- The standard determinant-one vertical shear and its inverse on ambient origamis. -/
def shearU (g : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (Origami g) where
  toFun o := ⟨(o.val.1 * o.val.2⁻¹, o.val.2), o.property.1, by
    convert o.property.2 using 1; group⟩
  invFun o := ⟨(o.val.1 * o.val.2, o.val.2), o.property.1, by
    convert o.property.2 using 1; group⟩
  left_inv o := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    group
  right_inv o := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    group

/-- Generating moves for the `SL(2, ℤ)` orbit, including square relabeling. Paths in the
equivalence closure may pass through non-minimal origamis. -/
def OrbitStep {g : ℕ} (o p : Origami g) : Prop :=
  (∃ s : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * g - 1)), relabel s o = p) ∨
    shearT g o = p ∨ shearU g o = p

/-- Minimal [1,1] origamis: both gluing permutations are cycles on every square. -/
def MinimalOrigami (g : ℕ) :=
  { o : Origami g // o.val.1.IsCycleOn Set.univ ∧ o.val.2.IsCycleOn Set.univ }

instance (g : ℕ) : Finite (MinimalOrigami g) := by
  unfold MinimalOrigami
  infer_instance

/-- The count `N_g` of orbits containing a minimal `[1,1]` origami (Conjecture 1.2). Orbits are
formed among all origamis before restricting to minimal ones. -/
noncomputable def orbitCount (g : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let Q := Quotient (Setoid.comap (fun o : MinimalOrigami g ↦ o.val)
    (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (@OrbitStep g)))
  letI : Fintype Q := Fintype.ofFinite Q
  Fintype.card Q

/-- **Conjecture 1.2** (arXiv v2). The orbit counts `N_g` eventually exceed every exponential
in `g`.

The moves are the standard determinant-one shears, not the source's erroneous matrix display. -/
theorem conjecture_1_2 (b : ℝ) (hb : 1 < b) :
    ∃ G ≥ 3,
      ∀ g ≥ G, b ^ g < (orbitCount g : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Aougab2022Origamis

theorem Aougab2022Origamis.conjecture_1_2_neg : ¬ type_of% @Aougab2022Origamis.conjecture_1_2 := by
  sorry

title: Agnostic Product Mixed State Tomography via Robust Statistics
problem_statement: In arulandu2025agnostic.lean, prove either Arulandu2025Agnostic.adaptive_measurements_necessary or refute it by proving its logical negation Arulandu2025Agnostic.adaptive_measurements_necessary_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Agnostic Product Mixed State Tomography via Robust Statistics

Authors: Alvan Arulandu, Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel Kane, and Jerry Li.
Origin: [Quantum@UW REU 2025](https://quantumreu.cs.washington.edu/past-reus/2025).
Reference: A. Arulandu, I. Diakonikolas, D. Kane, and J. Li, *Agnostic product mixed state
tomography via robust statistics*, preprint; arXiv:2510.08472v2 (2026; first version 2025).
-/

noncomputable section
namespace Arulandu2025Agnostic

open scoped ComplexOrder

/-- Self-delimited unary natural-number fields over the alphabet `Option Bool`. Unary headers
keep resource fields from encoding exponential workspace for free. -/
def fieldEncoding : Computability.Encoding (List ℕ) (Option Bool) :=
  let encode : List ℕ → List (Option Bool) :=
    List.flatMap (fun n ↦ List.replicate n (some true) ++ [none])
  let step : Option Bool → Option (List ℕ) → Option (List ℕ)
    | none, rest => (List.cons 0) <$> rest
    | some true, rest => rest.bind (fun ns ↦ match ns with
        | n :: tail => some ((n+1) :: tail)
        | _ => none)
    | some false, _ => none
  let decode : List (Option Bool) → Option (List ℕ) :=
    fun word ↦ word.foldr step (some [])
  have readPrefix (n : ℕ) (w : List (Option Bool)) :
      decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: w) =
        (List.cons n) <$> decode w := by
    induction n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ n ih =>
      simp only [List.replicate_succ, List.cons_append]
      change step (some true)
        (decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: w)) = _
      rw [ih]
      cases decode w <;> rfl
  ⟨encode, decode, by
    intro ns
    induction ns with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons n ns ih =>
      change decode ((List.replicate n (some true) ++ [none]) ++ encode ns) = _
      rw [List.append_assoc]
      change decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: encode ns) = _
      rw [readPrefix, ih]
      rfl⟩

/-- A computational-basis label for an n-qubit register. -/
abbrev BasisLabel (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Bool

/-- The fixed one-qubit gates used by this concrete interpreter. -/
inductive OneQubitGate
  | hadamard
  | phaseT

/-- The exact `H` and `T` matrices. -/
def OneQubitGate.matrix : OneQubitGate → Matrix.unitaryGroup Bool ℂ
  | .hadamard => by
      let s : ℂ := (√2 : ℝ)
      refine ⟨Matrix.of (fun x y ↦ (if x && y then -1 else 1) / s), ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
      ext x y
      cases x <;> cases y <;>
        simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.false_eq_true, Bool.true_eq_false,
          Complex.conj_ofReal, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton,
          Finset.mem_singleton, Finset.sum_const, Finset.sum_insert, Finset.sum_singleton,
          Fintype.univ_bool, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.of_apply,
          Matrix.one_apply_eq, Matrix.one_apply_ne, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Nat.cast_ofNat,
          Nat.reduceAdd, RCLike.star_def, and_false, and_true, map_neg, map_one, ne_eq,
          not_false_eq_true, nsmul_eq_mul, one_div, s, star_div₀, star_inv₀, ↓reduceIte]
      all_goals
        apply Complex.ext <;>
          norm_num [Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im, Complex.normSq_apply]
        all_goals field_simp
        all_goals norm_num
  | .phaseT => by
      let z : ℂ := (1 + Complex.I) / (√2 : ℝ)
      have hz : (starRingEnd ℂ) z * z = 1 := by
        apply Complex.ext
        · simp [z, Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im, Complex.normSq_apply]
          field_simp
          nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 by norm_num)]
        · simp [z, Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im, Complex.normSq_apply]
          ring
      refine ⟨Matrix.diagonal (fun b ↦ if b then z else 1), ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
      ext x y
      cases x <;> cases y <;>
        simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose,
          hz]

/-- One primitive operation, with wire indices already checked against register width. -/
inductive Gate (n : ℕ)
  | single (kind : OneQubitGate) (wire : Fin n)
  | controlledNot (control target : Fin n) (different : control ≠ target)

/-- The unitary of a primitive gate acting on its named wires. -/
def Gate.matrix {n : ℕ} : Gate n → Matrix.unitaryGroup (BasisLabel n) ℂ
  | .single kind wire => by
      let e := Equiv.funSplitAt wire Bool
      let u := Matrix.kronecker kind.matrix.val
        (1 : Matrix ({j : Fin n // j ≠ wire} → Bool)
          ({j : Fin n // j ≠ wire} → Bool) ℂ)
      have hu : u ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup _ ℂ :=
        Matrix.kronecker_mem_unitary kind.matrix.property (one_mem _)
      refine ⟨u.submatrix e e, ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff'] at hu ⊢
      change u.conjTranspose * u = 1 at hu
      change (u.submatrix e e).conjTranspose * u.submatrix e e = 1
      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_submatrix, Matrix.submatrix_mul_equiv _ _ e e e, hu,
        Matrix.submatrix_one_equiv]
  | .controlledNot c t h => by
      let f : BasisLabel n → BasisLabel n := fun x ↦ Function.update x t (xor (x c) (x t))
      have hf : Function.Involutive f := by
        intro x
        funext i
        by_cases hi : i = t
        · subst i
          simp [f, h]
        · simp [f, hi]
      let e := hf.toPerm
      refine ⟨e.permMatrix ℂ, ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
      change (e.permMatrix ℂ).conjTranspose * e.permMatrix ℂ = 1
      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_permMatrix, ← Matrix.permMatrix_mul]
      simp

/-- A finite circuit with a fixed register width and checked H/T/CNOT instructions. -/
structure Circuit where
  /-- The number of qubits in the register. -/
  width : ℕ
  /-- The list of gate instructions, applied in order. -/
  operations : List (Gate width)

/-- The circuit unitary in physical execution order. -/
def Circuit.matrix (c : Circuit) : Matrix.unitaryGroup (BasisLabel c.width) ℂ :=
  c.operations.foldl (fun u g ↦ g.matrix * u) 1

/-- Parse finite circuit instructions with validated gate tags and wire indices. -/
private def Circuit.decodeGates (width : ℕ) : List ℕ → Option (List (Gate width))
    | 0 :: wire :: tail => do
        if h : wire < width then
          return .single .hadamard ⟨wire,h⟩ :: (← Circuit.decodeGates width tail)
        else none
    | 1 :: wire :: tail => do
        if h : wire < width then
          return .single .phaseT ⟨wire,h⟩ :: (← Circuit.decodeGates width tail)
        else none
    | 2 :: control :: target :: tail => do
        if hc : control < width then
          if ht : target < width then
            if hct : control ≠ target then
              return .controlledNot ⟨control,hc⟩ ⟨target,ht⟩
                (fun h ↦ hct (congrArg Fin.val h)) :: (← Circuit.decodeGates width tail)
            else none
          else none
        else none
    | [] => some []
    | _ => none

/-- Finite circuit description with unary width and validated gate and wire fields. -/
def Circuit.encoding : Computability.Encoding Circuit (Option Bool) :=
  let fields {n : ℕ} (g : Gate n) : List ℕ := match g with
    | .single .hadamard wire => [0, wire.val]
    | .single .phaseT wire => [1, wire.val]
    | .controlledNot control target _ => [2, control.val, target.val]
  let encode (c : Circuit) := fieldEncoding.encode
    (c.width :: c.operations.flatMap fields)
  let decode (word : List (Option Bool)) : Option Circuit := do
    let width :: rest ← fieldEncoding.decode word | none
    return ⟨width, ← Circuit.decodeGates width rest⟩
  ⟨encode, decode, by
    rintro ⟨width, ops⟩
    have h : ∀ ops : List (Gate width),
        Circuit.decodeGates width (ops.flatMap fields) = some ops := by
      intro ops
      induction ops with
      | nil => rfl
      | cons g ops ih =>
        cases g with
        | single kind wire =>
          cases kind <;> simp [List.flatMap_cons, fields, Circuit.decodeGates, wire.isLt, ih]
        | controlledNot c t different =>
          have hct : c.val ≠ t.val := fun h ↦ different (Fin.ext h)
          simp [List.flatMap_cons, fields, Circuit.decodeGates, c.isLt, t.isLt, hct, ih]
    simp [encode, decode, h]⟩

/-- A mixed quantum state on a finite computational basis. -/
abbrev Density (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] :=
  {ρ : Matrix ι ι ℂ // ρ.PosSemidef ∧ ρ.trace = 1}

/-- Trace distance is half the sum of singular values for the Euclidean operator. -/
def traceDistance {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ρ σ : Density ι) : ℝ :=
  ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (ρ.val - σ.val)).singularValues.sum (fun _ x ↦ x)) / 2

/-- Tensor product of the arbitrary one-qubit mixed factors, in qubit order. -/
def productState : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Density Bool) → Density (BasisLabel n)
  | 0, _ => ⟨1, Matrix.PosSemidef.one, by simp [Matrix.trace_one, BasisLabel]⟩
  | n + 1, π => by
    let prev := productState n (fun i ↦ π i.castSucc)
    let last := π (Fin.last n)
    let M := Matrix.kronecker prev.val last.val
    let e := Fin.succFunEquiv Bool n
    refine ⟨M.submatrix e e, (prev.property.1.kronecker last.property.1).submatrix e, ?_⟩
    change (∑ x : BasisLabel (n + 1), M (e x) (e x)) = 1
    rw [e.sum_comp (fun x ↦ M x x)]
    change M.trace = 1
    dsimp [M]
    rw [Matrix.trace_kronecker, prev.property.2, last.property.2, mul_one]

/-- The product-mixed ansatz (Definition 1.1). -/
def productMixedStates (n : ℕ) : Set (Density (BasisLabel n)) :=
  Set.range (productState n)

/-- The best product-mixed approximation error `opt(ρ)`. -/
def opt {n : ℕ} (ρ : Density (BasisLabel n)) : ℝ :=
  sInf {e : ℝ | ∃ π ∈ productMixedStates n, e = traceDistance ρ π}

/-- Append fresh zero ancillas while retaining the original computational-basis order. -/
def zeroEmbedding (n a : ℕ) : Matrix (BasisLabel (n + a)) (BasisLabel n) ℂ :=
  fun y x ↦ if y = Fin.append x (fun _ : Fin a ↦ false) then 1 else 0

/-- The ancilla embedding is an isometry. -/
theorem zeroEmbedding_isometry (n a : ℕ) :
    (zeroEmbedding n a).conjTranspose * zeroEmbedding n a = 1 := by
  classical
  ext x z
  have h : Fin.append z (fun _ : Fin a ↦ false) =
      Fin.append x (fun _ : Fin a ↦ false) ↔ z = x := by
    constructor
    · intro heq
      funext i
      have hi := congrFun heq (Fin.castAdd a i)
      simpa using hi
    · rintro rfl
      rfl
  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.one_apply,
    zeroEmbedding, apply_ite, h, eq_comm]

/-- Apply a unitary to a mixed state after appending fresh zero ancillas. -/
def evolve {n a : ℕ} (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup (BasisLabel (n + a)) ℂ)
    (ρ : Density (BasisLabel n)) : Density (BasisLabel (n + a)) :=
  let J := zeroEmbedding n a
  let E := U.val * J
  have hU : U.val.conjTranspose * U.val = 1 := U.property.1
  have hE : E.conjTranspose * E = 1 := by
    dsimp [E]
    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.mul_assoc,
      ← Matrix.mul_assoc U.val.conjTranspose, hU, Matrix.one_mul,
      zeroEmbedding_isometry]
  ⟨E * ρ.val * E.conjTranspose, ρ.property.1.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same E, by
    calc
      (E * ρ.val * E.conjTranspose).trace =
          (E.conjTranspose * E * ρ.val).trace := Matrix.trace_mul_cycle E ρ.val E.conjTranspose
      _ = 1 := by rw [hE, Matrix.one_mul, ρ.property.2]⟩

/-- Proper one-qubit state encoded by a complex Gram matrix, with a fixed zero fallback. -/
def gramState (B : Matrix Bool Bool ℂ) : Density Bool :=
  let H := B * B.conjTranspose
  have hH : H.PosSemidef := Matrix.posSemidef_self_mul_conjTranspose B
  let t := H.trace.re
  have him : H.trace.im = 0 := (RCLike.nonneg_iff.mp hH.trace_nonneg).2
  have hreal : (t : ℂ) = H.trace := by
    apply Complex.ext <;> simp [t, him]
  if ht : t = 0 then
    ⟨(1 / 2 : ℝ) • (1 : Matrix Bool Bool ℂ),
      Matrix.PosSemidef.one.smul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2), by
        simp [Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_one]⟩
  else
    have hnonneg : 0 ≤ t := (RCLike.nonneg_iff.mp hH.trace_nonneg).1
    ⟨t⁻¹ • H, hH.smul (inv_nonneg.mpr hnonneg), by
      rw [Matrix.trace_smul, ← hreal]
      simp [ht]⟩

/-- A fixed finite dyadic Gram description: sign and magnitude bits for eight real entries. -/
structure DyadicGram (p : ℕ) where
  /-- The sign bit of each entry's real or imaginary part, indexed by row, column and part. -/
  sign : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool
  /-- The binary digits of each entry's real or imaginary part magnitude. -/
  magnitude : Bool → Bool → Bool → Fin (p + 1) → Bool

/-- Decode signed dyadic entries exactly as rational numbers before embedding into C. -/
def DyadicGram.matrix {p : ℕ} (c : DyadicGram p) : Matrix Bool Bool ℂ :=
  fun i j ↦
    let component := fun part ↦
      ((if c.sign i j part then -1 else 1 : ℚ) *
        (∑ k : Fin (p + 1), if c.magnitude i j part k then (2 : ℚ) ^ k.val else 0)) /
        (2 : ℚ) ^ p
    (component false : ℂ) + (component true : ℂ) * Complex.I

/-- Decode a finite dyadic output block to a product of one-qubit mixed states. -/
def decodeProduct (n p : ℕ) (bits : Fin ((n * 8) * (p + 2)) → Bool) :
    Density (BasisLabel n) :=
  let read := fun (q : Fin n) (i j part : Bool) (offset : Fin (p + 2)) ↦
    let component : Fin 8 := ⟨(if i then 4 else 0) + (if j then 2 else 0) +
      (if part then 1 else 0), by cases i <;> cases j <;> cases part <;> decide⟩
    bits (finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (q, component), offset))
  productState n (fun q ↦
    let c : DyadicGram p :=
      { sign := fun i j part ↦ read q i j part 0
        magnitude := fun i j part k ↦ read q i j part k.succ }
    gramState c.matrix)

/-- Public widths and finite precision for the seed, copies, and final private workspace. -/
structure Layout where
  /-- The number of measured qubits in the seed register. -/
  seed : ℕ
  /-- The number of seed-circuit qubits retained privately for postprocessing. -/
  retained : ℕ
  /-- The number of copies of the input state that are measured. -/
  copies : ℕ
  /-- The number of ancilla qubits used in each copy measurement. -/
  copyAncillas : ℕ
  /-- The number of ancilla qubits used in the postprocessing circuit. -/
  postAncillas : ℕ
  /-- The dyadic precision of the output description. -/
  precision : ℕ

/-- Every resource field has an explicit unary description; malformed layouts are rejected. -/
def Layout.encoding : Computability.Encoding Layout (Option Bool) :=
  let encode (L : Layout) := fieldEncoding.encode
    [L.seed, L.retained, L.copies, L.copyAncillas, L.postAncillas, L.precision]
  let decode (word : List (Option Bool)) : Option Layout := do
    let [s, k, N, c, q, p] ← fieldEncoding.decode word | none
    return ⟨s, k, N, c, q, p⟩
  ⟨encode, decode, by
    rintro ⟨s, k, N, c, q, p⟩
    simp [encode, decode]⟩

/-- The finite controller interface separates outcome-independent copy design from final
processing. -/
inductive Request
  | layout (n accuracy confidence : ℕ)
  | seed (n accuracy confidence : ℕ)
  | measurement (n accuracy confidence index : ℕ) (seed : List Bool)
  | postprocess (n accuracy confidence : ℕ) (seed transcript : List Bool)

/-- Tagged requests use unary numeric fields and literal seed/transcript bits in finite
alphabets. -/
def Request.encoding :
    Computability.Encoding Request ((Option Bool ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Bool) :=
  let blocks := Computability.encodingProd
    (Computability.encodingProd fieldEncoding (Computability.encodingList Bool))
    (Computability.encodingList Bool)
  let encode : Request → List ((Option Bool ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Bool)
    | .layout n a b => blocks.encode (([0, n, a, b], []), [])
    | .seed n a b => blocks.encode (([1, n, a, b], []), [])
    | .measurement n a b i r => blocks.encode (([2, n, a, b, i], r), [])
    | .postprocess n a b r y => blocks.encode (([3, n, a, b], r), y)
  let decode (word : List ((Option Bool ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Bool)) : Option Request := do
    let ((fields, r), y) ← blocks.decode word
    match fields, r, y with
    | [0, n, a, b], [], [] => return .layout n a b
    | [1, n, a, b], [], [] => return .seed n a b
    | [2, n, a, b, i], r, [] => return .measurement n a b i r
    | [3, n, a, b], r, y => return .postprocess n a b r y
    | _, _, _ => none
  ⟨encode, decode, by
    intro request
    cases request <;> simp [encode, decode]⟩

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 1.1.1). No uniformly efficient nonadaptive single-copy
learner achieves a dimension-independent vanishing semi-agnostic rate for the product-mixed
ansatz.

Learners are finite-gate circuits with a private quantum seed workspace retained only for final
processing. Problem 1's ket notation is read by the mixed-state Definition 1.1, and register
widths include zero. -/
theorem adaptive_measurements_necessary :
    ¬∃ generate : Request → List (Option Bool),
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime Request.encoding.encode
        (Computability.encodingList (Option Bool)).encode generate,
        (∀ stack : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ stack)) ∧
        ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
          (∀ t ≥ (0 : ℝ), 0 ≤ f t) ∧
          MonotoneOn f (Set.Ici 0) ∧ f 0 = 0 ∧
          (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ),
            ∀ t ≥ (0 : ℝ), t < δ → f t < ε) ∧
          ∀ n a b : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b →
            ∃ L : Layout,
              Layout.encoding.decode (generate (.layout n a b)) = some L ∧
              ∃ seedGates : List (Gate (L.seed + L.retained)),
              ∃ copyGates : BasisLabel L.seed → Fin L.copies →
                  List (Gate (n + L.copyAncillas)),
              let copyWidth := n + L.copyAncillas
              let postWidth := (L.retained + (L.seed + L.copies * copyWidth)) + L.postAncillas
              ∃ postGates : BasisLabel L.seed → (Fin L.copies → BasisLabel copyWidth) →
                  List (Gate postWidth),
                Circuit.encoding.decode (generate (.seed n a b)) =
                    some ⟨L.seed + L.retained, seedGates⟩ ∧
                (∀ r : BasisLabel L.seed, ∀ i : Fin L.copies,
                  Circuit.encoding.decode
                    (generate (.measurement n a b i.val (List.ofFn r))) =
                    some ⟨copyWidth, copyGates r i⟩) ∧
                (let flatten := fun y : Fin L.copies → BasisLabel copyWidth ↦
                    fun j : Fin (L.copies * copyWidth) ↦
                      y (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).1 (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).2
                 let charged := fun request : Request ↦
                    (Request.encoding.encode request).length + (generate request).length +
                    machine.time.eval (Request.encoding.encode request).length
                 ∃ houtput : ((n * 8) * (L.precision + 2)) ≤ postWidth,
                   (∀ r : BasisLabel L.seed, ∀ y : Fin L.copies → BasisLabel copyWidth,
                     Circuit.encoding.decode (generate (.postprocess n a b
                       (List.ofFn r) (List.ofFn (flatten y)))) =
                         some ⟨postWidth, postGates r y⟩ ∧
                     n + a + b + L.seed + L.retained + L.copies +
                       L.copies * copyWidth + postWidth + L.precision +
                       ((n * 8) * (L.precision + 2)) + seedGates.length +
                       (∑ i : Fin L.copies, (copyGates r i).length) +
                       (postGates r y).length + charged (.layout n a b) +
                       charged (.seed n a b) +
                       (∑ i : Fin L.copies,
                         charged (.measurement n a b i.val (List.ofFn r))) +
                       charged (.postprocess n a b (List.ofFn r)
                         (List.ofFn (flatten y))) ≤ bound.eval (n + a + b + 1)) ∧
                   ∀ ρ : Density (BasisLabel n),
                     1 - 1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ b ≤ (∑ r : BasisLabel L.seed,
                       ∑ y : Fin L.copies → BasisLabel copyWidth,
                       ∑ z : BasisLabel postWidth,
                         if traceDistance ρ
                             (decodeProduct n L.precision (fun j ↦ z (Fin.castLE houtput j))) ≤
                               f (opt ρ) + 1 / (a : ℝ) then
                           (∏ i : Fin L.copies,
                             (evolve (n := n) (a := L.copyAncillas)
                               (Circuit.mk copyWidth (copyGates r i)).matrix ρ).val
                               (y i) (y i) |>.re) *
                           Complex.normSq
                             (∑ u : BasisLabel L.retained,
                               (Circuit.mk postWidth (postGates r y)).matrix.val z
                                 (Fin.append (Fin.append u (Fin.append r (flatten y)))
                                   (fun _ : Fin L.postAncillas ↦ false)) *

/-- Upper density along degree cutoffs, an equivalent form of the upper density of
Definition 4.1. Each polynomial of degree at most `n` is counted once. -/
def upperDensity (K : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype K] (A : Set (Polynomial K)) : ℝ :=
  Filter.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦
    let B := Finset.univ.image (Polynomial.ofFn (R := K) (n + 1))
    ((#{f ∈ B | f ∈ A} : ℝ) / (#B : ℝ))) Filter.atTop

/-- **Conjecture 6.3** (arXiv v2, p. 11). Over every finite field, the supremum of upper
densities of sets avoiding three-term progressions with nonunit polynomial ratio equals `m_q`
from Theorem 4.3.

nonunit polynomial ratios are forbidden; Definition 4.1's `A ⊆ F_q` is read as `A ⊆ F_q[x]`. -/

    sSup {d : ℝ | ∃ A : Set (Polynomial K),

        f ∈ A → f * r ∈ A → f * r ^ 2 ∉ A) ∧ upperDensity K A = d} =
      (1 - ((Fintype.card K : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ 2) *
        ∏' i : ℕ, (1 + ((Fintype.card K : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ (3 ^ (i + 1))) := by
  sorry

# Distinct Angles and Angle Chains in Three Dimensions

Authors: Ruben Ascoli, Livia Betti, Jacob Lehmann Duke, Xuyan Liu, Wyatt Milgrim,

  (∀ Q ∈ P.powersetCard 3,

title: A monotonicity conjecture for the local maximal singularity of the Hilbert scheme of points
problem_statement: In ascott2025monotonicity.lean, prove either Ascott2025Monotonicity.conjecture_c or refute it by proving its logical negation Ascott2025Monotonicity.conjecture_c_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A monotonicity conjecture for the local maximal singularity of the Hilbert scheme of points

Authors: Alexia Ascott, Fatemeh Rezaee, and Zhichen Zhou.
Origin: [Cambridge SRIM 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17704v2).
Reference: A. Ascott, F. Rezaee, and Z. Zhou, *A monotonicity conjecture for the local maximal
singularity of the Hilbert scheme of points*, preprint, 8 pp.; arXiv:2506.17704v2 (2026; first
version 2025).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Ascott2025Monotonicity

/-- The complex polynomial ring in `N` ordered variables. -/
abbrev PolynomialRing (N : ℕ) := MvPolynomial (Fin N) ℂ

/-- Borel-fixed monomial ideals, i.e. strongly stable monomial ideals in characteristic zero. -/
def IsBorelFixed {N : ℕ} (I : Ideal (PolynomialRing N)) : Prop :=
  (∃ S : Set (Fin N →₀ ℕ),
    I = Ideal.span ((fun d ↦ MvPolynomial.monomial d (1 : ℂ)) '' S)) ∧
  ∀ d : Fin N →₀ ℕ, MvPolynomial.monomial d (1 : ℂ) ∈ I →
    ∀ i j : Fin N, i < j → 0 < d j →
      MvPolynomial.monomial
        (d - Finsupp.single j 1 + Finsupp.single i 1) (1 : ℂ) ∈ I

/-- The least exponent `m_i` with `x_i ^ m_i ∈ I`. -/
def pureExponent {N : ℕ} (I : Ideal (PolynomialRing N)) (i : Fin N) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | MvPolynomial.X i ^ m ∈ I}

/-- The tangent dimension `T(I)`: the complex dimension of `Hom_R(I, R / I)`. -/
def tangentDimension {N : ℕ} (I : Ideal (PolynomialRing N)) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank ℂ (I →ₗ[PolynomialRing N] (PolynomialRing N ⧸ I))

/-- **Conjecture C** (p. 2). For fixed colength, the maximal tangent dimension of Borel-fixed
ideals strictly increases with the smallest pure exponent.

"Increasing" is read as strict, following the stated consequence and Figure 1. The
for-all-`I`/exists-`J` form is equivalent since fiber maxima are attained, and the binomial bound
makes the higher-exponent fiber nonempty. -/
theorem conjecture_c {N : ℕ} (l m n : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (hl : 0 < l)
    (hm : 0 < m) (hmn : m < n) (hn : Nat.choose (N + n - 1) N ≤ l)
    (I : Ideal (PolynomialRing N)) (hI : IsBorelFixed I)
    (hlength : Module.finrank ℂ (PolynomialRing N ⧸ I) = l)
    (hexponent : pureExponent I ⟨0, by omega⟩ = m) :
    ∃ J : Ideal (PolynomialRing N), IsBorelFixed J ∧
      Module.finrank ℂ (PolynomialRing N ⧸ J) = l ∧
      pureExponent J ⟨0, by omega⟩ = n ∧ tangentDimension I < tangentDimension J := by
  sorry

end Ascott2025Monotonicity

theorem Ascott2025Monotonicity.conjecture_c_neg : ¬ type_of% @Ascott2025Monotonicity.conjecture_c := by
  sorry

title: Fine-Grained Buy-Many Mechanisms Are Not Much Better Than Bundling
problem_statement: In assadi2023fine.lean, prove either Assadi2023Fine.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Assadi2023Fine.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Fine-Grained Buy-Many Mechanisms Are Not Much Better Than Bundling

Authors: Sepehr Assadi, Vikram Kher, George Li, and Ariel Schvartzman.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2022](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.14312v2#page=1).
Reference: S. Assadi, V. Kher, G. Li, and A. Schvartzman, *Fine-grained buy-many mechanisms are
not much better than bundling*, in Proc. EC (2023); doi:10.1145/3580507.3597662;
arXiv:2205.14312v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Assadi2023Fine

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal ENNReal

/-- Finite-valued monotone valuations of two items, normalized at no purchase (Section 2). -/
abbrev Valuation :=
  {v : Finset (Fin 2) → ℝ≥0 // v ∅ = 0 ∧ Monotone v}

/-- An allocation: an independent probability for each item (Section 2). -/
abbrev Allocation := Fin 2 → Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The expected value of a product-Bernoulli allocation (Section 2). -/
def allocationValue (v : Valuation) (q : Allocation) : ℝ :=
  ∑ S : Finset (Fin 2), (v.val S : ℝ) *
    (∏ j ∈ S, (q j : ℝ)) * (∏ j ∈ Finset.univ \ S, (1 - (q j : ℝ)))

/-- The allocation `Lot` of a union of independently drawn, nonadaptively chosen tickets
(Section 2). -/
def lottery {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → Allocation) : Allocation :=
  fun j ↦ ⟨1 - ∏ a, (1 - (q a j : ℝ)), by
    constructor
    · exact sub_nonneg.mpr (Finset.prod_le_one₀
        (fun a _ ↦ sub_nonneg.mpr (q a j).property.2)
        (fun a _ ↦ sub_le_self 1 (q a j).property.1))
    · exact sub_le_self 1 (Finset.prod_nonneg
        (fun a _ ↦ sub_nonneg.mpr (q a j).property.2))⟩

/-- A direct mechanism: a price and allocation for each valuation in the support (Section 2). -/
structure Mechanism (D : ProbabilityMeasure Valuation) where
  /-- The price charged for each valuation in the support. -/
  price : (D : Measure Valuation).support → ℝ≥0
  /-- The allocation offered for each valuation in the support. -/
  allocation : (D : Measure Valuation).support → Allocation
  measurable_price : Measurable price
  measurable_allocation : Measurable allocation

/-- Pointwise buy-`k` incentive compatibility, including empty purchases (Section 2). -/
def Mechanism.BuyKIC {D : ProbabilityMeasure Valuation} (M : Mechanism D) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : (D : Measure Valuation).support, ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ k →
    ∀ reports : Fin m → (D : Measure Valuation).support,
      allocationValue v.val (lottery (fun a ↦ M.allocation (reports a))) -
        ∑ a, (M.price (reports a) : ℝ) ≤
      allocationValue v.val (M.allocation v) - (M.price v : ℝ)

/-- **Conjecture 1**. Some two-item distribution strictly separates every pair of consecutive
optimal buy-`k` revenues.

Optimal revenues are greatest achievable values. Normalization, Borel measurable support-wise
mechanisms and designated weak-IC tie selection make the source's informal conventions explicit;
valuations need not be additive or finitely supported. -/
theorem conjecture_1 :
    ∃ D : ProbabilityMeasure Valuation, ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞, ∀ k ≥ 1,
      IsGreatest
        {z : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ M : Mechanism D, M.BuyKIC k ∧
          z = ∫⁻ v, (M.price v : ℝ≥0∞)
            ∂((D : Measure Valuation).comap
              (Subtype.val : (D : Measure Valuation).support → Valuation))}
        (r k) ∧ r (k + 1) < r k := by
  sorry

end Assadi2023Fine

theorem Assadi2023Fine.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Assadi2023Fine.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

title: Quantitative Transversal Theorems in the Plane
problem_statement: In axelrodfreed2026quantitative.lean, prove either Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative.conjecture_6_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative.conjecture_6_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Quantitative Transversal Theorems in the Plane

Authors: Ilani Axelrod-Freed, Joao Pedro Carvalho, and Yuki Takahashi.
Origin: [NYC Discrete Math REU 2021](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.11024v3#page=21).
Reference: I. Axelrod-Freed, J. P. Carvalho, and Y. Takahashi, *Quantitative transversal theorems
in the plane*, Discrete Comput. Geom. (2026); doi:10.1007/s00454-026-00859-1; arXiv:2308.11024v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative

open Finset

/-- The space `C(ℝ^d)` of compact convex sets, including the empty set, with the Hausdorff
topology. -/
abbrev CompactConvex (d : ℕ) :=
  {K : TopologicalSpace.Compacts (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) //
    Convex ℝ (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))}

/-- The part `H^+(C)` in the closed positive half-space of `H`, with normal `v` and offset `t`. -/
def positivePart {d : ℕ} (K : CompactConvex d)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ) : CompactConvex d :=
  ⟨⟨(K.val : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) ∩ {x | t ≤ inner ℝ v x},
      K.val.isCompact.inter_right (isClosed_le continuous_const (innerSL ℝ v).continuous)⟩,
    K.property.inter (convex_halfSpace_ge (innerSL ℝ v).toLinearMap.isLinear t)⟩

/-- The part `H^-(C)` in the opposite closed half-space. -/
def negativePart {d : ℕ} (K : CompactConvex d)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ) : CompactConvex d :=
  ⟨⟨(K.val : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) ∩ {x | inner ℝ v x ≤ t},
      K.val.isCompact.inter_right (isClosed_le (innerSL ℝ v).continuous continuous_const)⟩,
    K.property.inter (convex_halfSpace_le (innerSL ℝ v).toLinearMap.isLinear t)⟩

/-- A hyperplane stabs `K` when both closed half-space parts reach the threshold
(Definition 13). -/
def HyperplaneStabs {d : ℕ} (K : CompactConvex d) (f : CompactConvex d → ℝ)
    (α : ℝ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  α ≤ f (positivePart K v t) ∧ α ≤ f (negativePart K v t)

/-- An `(f, α)`-consistent labeling in `ℝ^k`: small quantitatively separated subfamilies have
disjoint label hulls (Definition 14). The labeling need not be injective or spanning. -/
def HasConsistentOrdering {d : ℕ} (F : Finset (CompactConvex d))
    (f : F → CompactConvex d → ℝ) (α : F → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : F → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k),
    ∀ A B : Finset F, #A + #B ≤ k + 2 →
      ∀ v ≠ (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), ∀ t : ℝ,
        (∀ i ∈ A, f i (negativePart i.val v t) < α i) →
        (∀ i ∈ B, f i (positivePart i.val v t) < α i) →
        Disjoint (convexHull ℝ (φ '' (A : Set F)))
          (convexHull ℝ (φ '' (B : Set F)))

/-- **Conjecture 6.2**. An `(f, α)`-consistent labeling in any dimension below `d` forces a
quantitative hyperplane transversal, under the standing monotonicity, Hausdorff continuity,
empty-set normalization and individual-direction assumptions. -/
theorem conjecture_6_2
    {d : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (hkd : k < d) (F : Finset (CompactConvex d))
    (f : F → CompactConvex d → ℝ) (α : F → ℝ)
    (hmono : ∀ i, Monotone (f i))
    (hcont : ∀ i, Continuous (f i))
    (hempty : ∀ i, f i ⟨⊥, convex_empty⟩ = 0)
    (hdirections : ∀ (i : F) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), v ≠ 0 →
      ∃ t : ℝ, HyperplaneStabs i.val (f i) (α i) v t)
    (hordering : HasConsistentOrdering F f α k) :
    ∃ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ i : F, HyperplaneStabs i.val (f i) (α i) v t := by
  sorry

end Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative

theorem Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative.conjecture_6_2_neg : ¬ type_of% @Axelrodfreed2026Quantitative.conjecture_6_2 := by
  sorry

/-!
# Sets in R^d determining k taxicab distances

Authors: Vajresh Balaji, Olivia Edwards, Anne Marie Loftin, Solomon Mcharo, Lo Phillips,
Alex Rice, and Bineyam Tsegaye.
Origin: [Millsaps College Kinnaird Institute Research Experience
2019](https://millsaps.edu/inaugural-kinnaird-institute-research-experience/).
Reference: V. Balaji, O. Edwards, A. M. Loftin, S. Mcharo, L. Phillips, A. Rice, and B. Tsegaye,
*Sets in R^d determining k taxicab distances*, Involve **13** (2020), 487-509.
-/

namespace Balaji2020Sets

/-- Integer points of taxicab norm at most `k` whose coordinate sum has the parity of `k`,
embedded in real taxicab space (Definition 2.1). -/
def latticePoints (d k : ℕ) : Set (PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d ↦ ℝ)) :=
  {x | ∃ z : Fin d → ℤ,
    (∀ i, x i = (z i : ℝ)) ∧
    (∑ i, (z i).natAbs) ≤ k ∧
    (∑ i, z i) % 2 = (k : ℤ) % 2}

/-- `ℓ¹`-similarity by translations, coordinate reflections, uniform nonzero scaling and
coordinate permutations (Definition 2.4). -/
def L1Similar {d : ℕ} (P Q : Set (PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d ↦ ℝ))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d ↦ ℝ)) (r : ℝ), 0 < r ∧
    ∃ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (signs : Fin d → Bool),
      Q = (fun x : PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d ↦ ℝ) ↦
        WithLp.toLp 1 (fun i ↦ a i + r * (if signs i then 1 else -1) * x (σ i))) '' P

/-- **Conjecture 2.7** (arXiv v3, p. 4; published p. 491). The parity-restricted integer
taxicab ball is, up to `ℓ¹`-similarity, the unique largest configuration with at most `k` nonzero
distances. -/
theorem conjecture_2_7 {d : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hk : 0 < k)
    (P : Set (PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d ↦ ℝ)))
    (hP : {r : ℝ | ∃ x ∈ P, ∃ y ∈ P, x ≠ y ∧ dist x y = r}.encard ≤ k) :
    P.encard ≤ (latticePoints d k).encard ∧
      (P.encard = (latticePoints d k).encard ↔ L1Similar P (latticePoints d k)) := by
  sorry

end Balaji2020Sets

title: L^p Regularity of Toeplitz Operators on Generalized Hartogs Triangles
problem_statement: In balay2022l.lean, prove either Balay2022L.open_berezin_boundary_vanishing_not_compact_counterexample or refute it by proving its logical negation Balay2022L.open_berezin_boundary_vanishing_not_compact_counterexample_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# L^p Regularity of Toeplitz Operators on Generalized Hartogs Triangles

Authors: Meijke Balay, Trent Neutgens, Nick Rosen, Nathan Wagner, and Yunus E. Zeytuncu.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.07260).
Reference: M. Balay, T. Neutgens, N. Rosen, N. Wagner, and Y. E. Zeytuncu, *L^p Regularity of
Toeplitz Operators on Generalized Hartogs Triangles*, arXiv:2009.07260.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Balay2022L

open MeasureTheory

/-- The rational generalized Hartogs triangle `H_{m/n}` (Section 1.1). -/
def rationalHartogsTriangle (m n : ℕ) : Set (ℂ × ℂ) :=
  {z | (‖z.1‖ : ℝ) ^ ((m : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) < ‖z.2‖ ∧ ‖z.2‖ < 1}

/-- The Bergman kernel, summed over the square-integrable Laurent monomials (Section 1.1,
equation (1)). The denominator is their squared `L²` norm for Lebesgue volume. -/
def bergmanKernel (m n : ℕ) (z w : ℂ × ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' α : ℕ × ℤ,
    if -((m : ℤ) + (n : ℤ)) + 1 ≤ (n : ℤ) * (α.1 : ℤ) + (m : ℤ) * α.2 then
      (z.1 ^ α.1 * z.2 ^ α.2) * star (w.1 ^ α.1 * w.2 ^ α.2) /
        ((∫ u : ℂ × ℂ, ‖u.1 ^ α.1 * u.2 ^ α.2‖ ^ 2
          ∂(volume.restrict (rationalHartogsTriangle m n))) : ℂ)
    else 0

open Filter
open scoped Topology ENNReal

/-- **Section 3(3), Further Questions**. There is a bounded symbol on a rational Hartogs triangle
whose Berezin transform tends to zero at every boundary point, but whose Toeplitz operator on
`L²` is not compact, as the authors predict. -/
theorem open_berezin_boundary_vanishing_not_compact_counterexample :
    ∃ m n : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ 0 < n ∧ Nat.Coprime m n ∧
      let Ω := rationalHartogsTriangle m n
      let μ : Measure (ℂ × ℂ) := volume.restrict Ω
      ∃ φ : (ℂ × ℂ) → ℂ, MemLp φ ⊤ μ ∧
        ∃ T : Lp ℂ 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ,
          (∀ f : Lp ℂ 2 μ,
            (T f : (ℂ × ℂ) → ℂ) =ᵐ[μ]
              fun z ↦ ∫ w, bergmanKernel m n z w * φ w * f w ∂μ) ∧
          (∀ z ∈ frontier Ω, Tendsto (fun interior_z ↦
            (∫ w : ℂ × ℂ, φ w * (‖bergmanKernel m n interior_z w‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)
              ∂(volume.restrict (rationalHartogsTriangle m n))) /
                bergmanKernel m n interior_z interior_z) (𝓝[Ω] z) (𝓝 0)) ∧
          ¬IsCompactOperator T := by
  sorry

end Balay2022L

theorem Balay2022L.open_berezin_boundary_vanishing_not_compact_counterexample_neg : ¬ type_of% @Balay2022L.open_berezin_boundary_vanishing_not_compact_counterexample := by
  sorry

/-!
# Partial Word DFAs

Authors: Eric Balkanski, F. Blanchet-Sadri, Matthew Kilgore, and B. J. Wyatt.
Origin: [UNCG REU 2012](https://home.uncg.edu/cmp/reu/summer2012/).
Reference: E. Balkanski, F. Blanchet-Sadri, M. Kilgore, and B. J. Wyatt, *Partial word DFAs*,
in CIAA 2013, Lecture Notes in Comput. Sci. **7982**, 36-47.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Balkanski2013Partial

/-- Hole substitution: each hole independently becomes a letter from one fixed subset, while
ordinary letters stay unchanged (Section 1). -/
def holeSubstitution {α : Type} (S : Set α) (L : Language (Option α)) : Language α :=
  {w | ∃ u ∈ L, List.Forall₂ (fun o a ↦ match o with
    | none => a ∈ S
    | some b => a = b) u w}

/-- The minimum partial-word DFA state count, over all hole substitutions and complete DFAs
representing the language (Section 1). -/
def partialStateComplexity {α : Type} (L : Language α) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ S : Set α, ∃ M : DFA (Option α) (Fin k),
    holeSubstitution S M.accepts = L}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 4, p. 47). Every count from `n` to `2 ^ n - 1` occurs as
the minimum complete-DFA size of a regular language whose minimum partial-word DFA size is `n`.

The alphabet may vary, and rejecting sink states are counted. -/
theorem state_complexity_spectrum (n m : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hnm : n ≤ m)
    (hm : m ≤ 2 ^ n - 1) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ L : Language (Fin k),
      L.IsRegular ∧ partialStateComplexity L = n ∧
        Nat.card (Set.range L.leftQuotient) = m := by
  sorry

end Balkanski2013Partial

title: Friezes over Z[sqrt(2)]
problem_statement: In banaian2023friezes.lean, prove either Banaian2023Friezes.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Banaian2023Friezes.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Friezes over Z[sqrt(2)]

Authors: Esther Banaian, Libby Farrell, Amy Tao, Kayla Wright, and Joy Zhichun Zhang.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2021](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: E. Banaian, L. Farrell, A. Tao, K. Wright, and J. Z. Zhang, *Friezes over
Z[sqrt(2)]*, arXiv:2307.00440v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Banaian2023Friezes

open Finset

/-- A polygon dissection, represented by its noncrossing arcs together with every boundary edge
(Section 2.2). -/
def IsDissection {n : ℕ} (D : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, D.Adj i (finRotate n i)) ∧
    ∀ a b c d, sbtw a b c → sbtw c d a →
      D.Adj a c → ¬D.Adj b d

open scoped Classical in
/-- The subpolygons of a dissection: its chordless cycles, represented by
their vertex sets in the inherited cyclic order. -/
def cells {n : ℕ} (D : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Finset (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  {S | 3 ≤ #S ∧ (D.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).Connected ∧
    ∀ v, (D.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).degree v = 2}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The frieze of a triangle/quadrilateral dissection (Section 2.2). Entries are continuant
determinants of the incident-polygon quiddity. -/
def friezeEntry {n : ℕ} (D : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (i j : Fin n) : Zsqrtd 2 :=
  let lo := min i.val j.val
  let hi := max i.val j.val
  if i = j then 0 else
    Matrix.det fun a b : Fin (hi - lo - 1) ↦
      if a = b then
        let v : Fin n := ⟨lo + a.val + 1, by dsimp [lo, hi] at *; omega⟩
        (#{S ∈ cells D | v ∈ S ∧ #S = 3} : Zsqrtd 2) +
          (#{S ∈ cells D | v ∈ S ∧ #S = 4} : Zsqrtd 2) *
            Zsqrtd.sqrtd
      else if a.val + 1 = b.val ∨ b.val + 1 = a.val then 1 else 0

/-- **Conjecture 1**. A triangle/quadrilateral dissection produces a unitary
frieze exactly when it is a gluing of towers. -/
theorem conjecture_1 {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (D : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hD : IsDissection D)
    (hpieces : ∀ S ∈ cells D, #S = 3 ∨ #S = 4) :
    (∃ T : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsDissection T ∧ (∀ S ∈ cells T, #S = 3) ∧
        ∀ i j, T.Adj i j → IsUnit (friezeEntry D i j)) ↔
    (∃ C : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsDissection C ∧ C ≤ D ∧ ∀ S ∈ cells C,
        #{F ∈ {F ∈ cells D | F ⊆ S} | #F = 3} = 1 ∧
          ∀ v ∈ S, #{F ∈ {F ∈ cells D | F ⊆ S} | v ∈ F} ≤ 2) := by
  sorry

end Banaian2023Friezes

theorem Banaian2023Friezes.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Banaian2023Friezes.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

/-!
# Bounds in simple hexagonal lattice and classification of 11-stick knots

Authors: Yueheng Bao, Ari Benveniste, Marion Campisi, Nicholas Cazet, Ansel Goh, Jiantong Liu,
and Ethan Sherman.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2022](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu/results2022).
Reference: Y. Bao, A. Benveniste, M. Campisi, N. Cazet, A. Goh, J. Liu, and E. Sherman, *Bounds
in simple hexagonal lattice and classification of 11-stick knots*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications
**32** (2023), no. 14, 2350097; arXiv:2211.00687v2.
-/

namespace Bao2023Bounds

/-- A non-self-intersecting polygon: distinct vertices and straight edges meeting only at common
endpoints (Section 2). -/
structure PolygonalKnot (n : ℕ) extends Polygon (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) n where
  three_le : 3 ≤ n
  vertices_injective : Function.Injective toPolygon.vertices
  nondegenerate_edges : toPolygon.HasNondegenerateEdges
  simple : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    toPolygon.edgeSet ℝ i ∩ toPolygon.edgeSet ℝ j ⊆
      ({toPolygon i, toPolygon (finRotate n i)} ∩
        {toPolygon j, toPolygon (finRotate n j)})

/-- **Conjecture 2** (p. 20). Every knot admitting a simple-hexagonal lattice representative with
at most fourteen sticks has crossing number at most five.

The crossing number uses regular projections of arbitrary ambient-isotopic polygons, not only of
the given lattice representative. -/
theorem conjecture_2 {n : ℕ} (P : PolygonalKnot n) (hn : n ≤ 14)
    (hvertices : ∀ i, ∃ a b c : ℤ,
      P.toPolygon i = WithLp.toLp 2
        ![(a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) / 2, (b : ℝ) * √3 / 2, (c : ℝ)])
    (hsticks : ∀ i, ∃ k ≠ (0 : ℤ),
      (P.toPolygon (finRotate n i) - P.toPolygon i =
          (k : ℝ) • WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0, 0] ∨
        P.toPolygon (finRotate n i) - P.toPolygon i =
          (k : ℝ) • WithLp.toLp 2 ![1 / 2, √3 / 2, 0] ∨
        P.toPolygon (finRotate n i) - P.toPolygon i =
          (k : ℝ) • WithLp.toLp 2 ![-1 / 2, √3 / 2, 0] ∨
        P.toPolygon (finRotate n i) - P.toPolygon i =
          (k : ℝ) • WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0, 1])) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∃ Q : PolygonalKnot m,
      ∃ H : unitInterval → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ∧
      H 1 '' P.toPolygon.boundary ℝ = Q.toPolygon.boundary ℝ ∧
      let π : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
        fun p ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 ![p 0, p 1]
      (∀ i, π (Q.toPolygon i) ≠ π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m i))) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → i ≠ finRotate m j →
        π (Q.toPolygon i) ∉
          segment ℝ (π (Q.toPolygon j)) (π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m j)))) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j →
        openSegment ℝ (π (Q.toPolygon i)) (π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m i))) ∩
          openSegment ℝ (π (Q.toPolygon j)) (π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m j))) ≠ ∅ →
        LinearIndependent ℝ
          ![π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m i)) - π (Q.toPolygon i),
            π (Q.toPolygon (finRotate m j)) - π (Q.toPolygon j)]) ∧
      (∀ q, {p | p ∈ Q.toPolygon.boundary ℝ ∧ π p = q}.encard ≤ 2) ∧
      {q | ∃ p ∈ Q.toPolygon.boundary ℝ, ∃ r ∈ Q.toPolygon.boundary ℝ,
        p ≠ r ∧ π p = q ∧ π r = q}.encard ≤ 5 := by
  sorry

end Bao2023Bounds

title: Lower central series of free algebras in symmetric tensor categories
problem_statement: In bapat2013lower.lean, prove either Bapat2013Lower.conjecture_8_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Bapat2013Lower.conjecture_8_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Lower central series of free algebras in symmetric tensor categories

Authors: Asilata Bapat and David Jordan.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2009](https://asilatabapat.org/assets/papers/2009-bapat-lcq.pdf).
Reference: A. Bapat and D. Jordan, *Lower central series of free algebras in symmetric tensor
categories*, J. Algebra **373** (2013), 299-311; arXiv:1001.1375v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Bapat2013Lower

/-- The free superalgebra, with the first `m` generators even and the last `n` odd (Section 5). -/
abbrev A (m n : ℕ) := MonoidAlgebra ℂ (FreeMonoid (Fin (m + n)))

/-- The supercommutator, extended bilinearly from homogeneous words (Section 5). -/
def superBracket {m n : ℕ} (a b : A m n) : A m n :=
  a.coeff.sum fun w c ↦ b.coeff.sum fun v d ↦
    MonoidAlgebra.single (w * v) (c * d) -
      MonoidAlgebra.single (v * w)
        ((-1 : ℂ) ^
          (w.toList.countP (fun i ↦ m ≤ i.val) *
            v.toList.countP (fun i ↦ m ≤ i.val)) * c * d)

/-- The lower central series (Sections 1 and 3). Index `r` denotes `L_(r+1)`. -/
def lowerCentral (m n : ℕ) : ℕ → Submodule ℂ (A m n)
  | 0 => ⊤
  | r + 1 => Submodule.span ℂ
      {z | ∃ a b, b ∈ lowerCentral m n r ∧ z = superBracket a b}

/-- The multidegree-`e` component, spanned by all words with the prescribed multiplicities. -/
def homogeneousPiece {m n : ℕ} (e : Fin (m + n) →₀ ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ (A m n) :=
  Submodule.span ℂ
    {z | ∃ w : FreeMonoid (Fin (m + n)),
      (∀ i, w.toList.count i = e i) ∧ z = MonoidAlgebra.single w 1}

/-- The multigraded Hilbert series of `L_k / L_(k+1)` (Section 5). -/
def hilbertSeries (m n k : ℕ) : MvPowerSeries (Fin (m + n)) ℤ := fun e ↦
  let U := lowerCentral m n (k - 1) ⊓ homogeneousPiece e
  (Module.finrank ℂ (U ⧸ (lowerCentral m n k).comap U.subtype) : ℤ)

/-- **Conjecture 8.1** (Section 8). Every lower central quotient in the stated range has a
multigraded Hilbert series with the prescribed simple denominator.

The polynomial numerator may cancel factors; the denominator need not be reduced. -/
theorem conjecture_8_1 (m n k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + n)) ℤ,
      hilbertSeries m n k *
        (∏ i : Fin (m + n), (1 - MvPowerSeries.X i)) =
          (P : MvPowerSeries (Fin (m + n)) ℤ) := by
  sorry

end Bapat2013Lower

theorem Bapat2013Lower.conjecture_8_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Bapat2013Lower.conjecture_8_1 := by
  sorry

title: Bender-Knuth Billiards in Coxeter Groups
problem_statement: In barkley2025bender.lean, prove either Barkley2025Bender.question_12_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Barkley2025Bender.question_12_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Bender-Knuth Billiards in Coxeter Groups

Authors: Grant Barkley, Colin Defant, Eliot Hodges, Noah Kravitz, and Mitchell Lee.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2023](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: G. Barkley, C. Defant, E. Hodges, N. Kravitz, and M. Lee, *Bender-Knuth Billiards in
Coxeter Groups*, Forum Math. Sigma **13** (2025), e7, 1-55; arXiv:2401.17360v3.
-/

namespace Barkley2025Bender

/-- A convex subset: it contains every element lying on a shortest path in the left Cayley
graph between two of its elements (p. 4, Remark 1.1).

Lying on a shortest path is encoded as additivity of length in the simple generators. -/
def CoxeterConvex {n : ℕ} {M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)} (L : Set M.Group) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ L, ∀ z : M.Group,
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (y * x⁻¹) =
      M.toCoxeterSystem.length (z * x⁻¹) + M.toCoxeterSystem.length (y * z⁻¹) → z ∈ L

open scoped Classical in
/-- The noninvertible Bender-Knuth toggle `τ_i` with respect to `L` (Definition 1.2).

It is encoded through the right-inversion identity (10): `u` stays fixed exactly when all of `L`
lies on the same side of the separating wall as `u`. -/
noncomputable def toggle {n : ℕ} {M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)} (L : Set M.Group) (i : Fin n)
    (u : M.Group) : M.Group :=
  if ∀ v ∈ L, ¬M.toCoxeterSystem.IsRightDescent (v * u⁻¹) i then u else M.simple i * u

/-- The billiards map `Pro_c`: one round applying each toggle once, in the given order
(Definition 1.6). -/
noncomputable def promotion {n : ℕ} {M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)} (L : Set M.Group)
    (order : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (u : M.Group) : M.Group :=
  (List.finRange n).foldl (fun w j ↦ toggle L (order j) w) u

/-- A futuristic Coxeter element: every nonempty convex set is heavy, that is, contains every
periodic point of `Pro_c` (Definitions 1.6 and 1.9).

The Coxeter element is encoded by the order in which the simple generators are toggled. -/
def Futuristic {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) (order : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : Set M.Group, L.Nonempty → CoxeterConvex L →
    Function.periodicPts (promotion L order) ⊆ L

/-- **Question 12.1** (Section 12.1, arXiv v3 p. 48). There is a contemporary Coxeter group:
one with a futuristic and a non-futuristic Coxeter element.

All finite ranks and all Coxeter labels, including `∞` (matrix entry zero), are allowed. -/
theorem question_12_1 :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) (future other : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)),
      Futuristic M future ∧ ¬Futuristic M other := by
  sorry

end Barkley2025Bender

theorem Barkley2025Bender.question_12_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Barkley2025Bender.question_12_1 := by
  sorry

title: Nathanson heights in finite vector spaces
problem_statement: In batson2008nathanson.lean, prove either Batson2008Nathanson.conjecture_section_7 or refute it by proving its logical negation Batson2008Nathanson.conjecture_section_7_neg.
