/-!
# Nathanson heights in finite vector spaces

Author: Joshua Batson.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2007](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: J. Batson, *Nathanson heights in finite vector spaces*, J. Number Theory **128** (2008),
no. 9, 2616-2633.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Batson2008Nathanson

open scoped Topology

/-- The Nathanson height: the least sum of nonnegative coordinate representatives of a nonzero
vector in the subspace (Section 1). -/
def nathansonHeight {p n : ℕ} (V : Submodule (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p)) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ v ∈ V, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∑ i, (v i).val = k}

/-- The limiting height of an integer vector (Section 5). It takes the punctured liminf of the
sum of fractional parts, then the infimum over one period. -/
def limitingHeight {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℤ) : ℝ :=
  sInf ((fun x : ℝ ↦
    Filter.liminf (fun t : ℝ ↦ ∑ i, Int.fract ((a i : ℝ) * t)) (𝓝[≠] x)) ''
      Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 7, p. 16). For every fixed codimension, the normalized
Nathanson-height range approaches the limiting-height range at rate `O(p ^ (-1 / n))`. -/
theorem conjecture_section_7 (n m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m < n) :
    (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦
      Metric.hausdorffDist
        {x : ℝ | ∃ a ≠ (0 : Fin (m + 1) → ℤ), limitingHeight a = x}
        {x : ℝ | ∃ V : Submodule (ZMod (p : ℕ)) (Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)),
          Module.finrank (ZMod (p : ℕ)) V = n - m ∧
            (nathansonHeight V : ℝ) / (p : ℕ) = x})
      =O[Filter.comap (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ (p : ℕ)) Filter.atTop]
        (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / n)) := by
  sorry

end Batson2008Nathanson

theorem Batson2008Nathanson.conjecture_section_7_neg : ¬ type_of% @Batson2008Nathanson.conjecture_section_7 := by
  sorry

title: Constructions of Macaulay Posets and Macaulay Rings
source_label: Conjecture 7.4 (journal and arXiv v2; Conjecture 6.4 in v1)
problem_statement: In beall2026constructions.lean, prove either Beall2026Constructions.conjecture_7_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Beall2026Constructions.conjecture_7_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Constructions of Macaulay Posets and Macaulay Rings

Authors: Penelope Beall, Erenay Boyali, Nancy Chen, Ellen Chlachidze, Trong Toan Dao,
Frederic Garvey, Mitchell Johnson, Yu Olivier Li, Nikola Kuzmanovski, Kelvin Ma, Treanungkur Mal,
Rukshan Marasinghe Mudiyanselage, Quinlan Mayo, Nava Minsky-Primus, Alexandra Seceleanu, and
Sriram Veerapaneni.
Origin: [Polymath Jr.](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu).
Reference: P. Beall et al., *Constructions of Macaulay Posets and Macaulay Rings*,
arXiv:2502.15166.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Beall2026Constructions

open Finset

section Posets

variable {α : Type*}

/-- A finite ranked poset: a least element of rank zero and covers that increase rank by one
(Section 2). -/
@[nolint unusedArguments]
def IsFiniteRankedPoset [PartialOrder α] [Fintype α] (rank : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ least : α, rank least = 0 ∧ (∀ x : α, least ≤ x) ∧
    ∀ ⦃a b : α⦄, a ⋖ b → rank b = rank a + 1

/-- The rank-`d` level of a finite poset. -/
def level [Fintype α] (rank : α → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : Finset α :=
  {x | rank x = d}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The upper shadow (Section 2). It is defined using covers rather than all larger elements. -/
def upperShadow [PartialOrder α] [Fintype α] (A : Finset α) : Finset α :=
  {b | ∃ a ∈ A, a ⋖ b}

/-- A total order on each rank level. -/
structure LevelOrders (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (rank : α → ℕ) where
  /-- The total order on each rank level. -/
  order : ∀ d : ℕ, LinearOrder {x : α // x ∈ level rank d}

/-- A size-`q` initial segment: the `q` largest elements of a level. -/
def IsInitialSegmentOfSize [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {rank : α → ℕ}
    (O : LevelOrders α rank) (d q : ℕ) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  S ⊆ level rank d ∧ #S = q ∧
    ∀ ⦃x y : α⦄, x ∈ S → ∀ (hx : x ∈ level rank d) (hy : y ∈ level rank d),
      (letI := O.order d;
        (⟨x, hx⟩ : {z : α // z ∈ level rank d}) ≤ ⟨y, hy⟩) → y ∈ S

/-- The Macaulay property: initial segments minimize upper shadows, and their upper shadows are
again initial segments (Section 2). -/
def IsMacaulayPoset [PartialOrder α] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {rank : α → ℕ}
    (O : LevelOrders α rank) : Prop :=
  IsFiniteRankedPoset rank ∧
    ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Finset α), A ⊆ level rank d →
      ∀ S : Finset α, IsInitialSegmentOfSize O d #A S →
        #(upperShadow S) ≤ #(upperShadow A) ∧
          IsInitialSegmentOfSize O (d + 1) #(upperShadow S) (upperShadow S)

end Posets

section Setup

attribute [local instance] MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra

/-- Nonzero monomials in the quotient, not exponent-vector representatives. Relations such as
`y ^ 2 = z ^ 2` thus identify monomials, as in the source examples. -/
abbrev QuotientMonomial {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K)) :=
  {x : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K ⧸ I // x ≠ 0 ∧
    ∃ a : Fin m →₀ ℕ, Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.monomial a (1 : K)) = x}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The finite Macaulay monomial poset of a homogeneous quotient. The order is certified as
multiplication by a monomial in the quotient, and the rank by every exponent representative. -/
def IsMacaulayQuotient {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K)) : Prop :=
  I.IsHomogeneous (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin m) K) ∧
    ∃ (fin : Fintype (QuotientMonomial I)) (order : PartialOrder (QuotientMonomial I)),
      letI := fin;
      letI := order;
      (∀ a b : QuotientMonomial I, a ≤ b ↔
        ∃ c : Fin m →₀ ℕ,
          b.1 = a.1 * Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.monomial c (1 : K))) ∧
        ∃ rank : QuotientMonomial I → ℕ,
          (∀ (a : QuotientMonomial I) (e : Fin m →₀ ℕ),
            Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.monomial e (1 : K)) = a.1 →
              rank a = e.degree) ∧
          ∃ O : LevelOrders (QuotientMonomial I) rank, IsMacaulayPoset O

end Setup

/-- **Conjecture 7.4** (journal and arXiv v2; Conjecture 6.4 in v1). Tensoring a Macaulay ring
with `K[x] / (x ^ n)` preserves the Macaulay property when `n` exceeds its largest degree.

Macaulay means the monomial-poset property defined after Definition 2.12, not an unrestricted
Hilbert-function correspondence. -/
theorem conjecture_7_4
    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K))
    (hS : IsMacaulayQuotient I) (D n : ℕ)
    (hD : IsGreatest {d : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin m →₀ ℕ,
      MvPolynomial.monomial a (1 : K) ∉ I ∧ a.degree = d} D)
    (hn : D < n) :
    IsMacaulayQuotient
      (Ideal.map (MvPolynomial.rename (Fin.castSucc : Fin m → Fin (m + 1))) I ⊔
        Ideal.span ({MvPolynomial.X (Fin.last m) ^ n} : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 1)) K))) := by
  sorry

end Beall2026Constructions

theorem Beall2026Constructions.conjecture_7_4_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Beall2026Constructions.conjecture_7_4.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: The frog model on trees with drift
problem_statement: In beckman2019frog.lean, prove either Beckman2019Frog.critical_drift_monotonicity or refute it by proving its logical negation Beckman2019Frog.critical_drift_monotonicity_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The frog model on trees with drift

Authors: Erin Beckman, Natalie Frank, Yufeng Jiang, Matthew Junge, and Si Tang.
Origin: [Duke DOmath 2018](https://math.duke.edu/domath/2018).
Reference: E. Beckman, N. Frank, Y. Jiang, M. Junge, and S. Tang, *The frog model on trees with
drift*, Electron. Commun. Probab. **24** (2019); doi:10.1214/19-ECP235; arXiv:1808.03283v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Beckman2019Frog

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped Topology

/-- Vertices of the rooted `d`-ary tree as words with zero-based child labels (Section 5). -/
abbrev Vertex (d : ℕ) := List (Fin d)

/-- The one-per-site frog model: active frog labels and positions after each simultaneous step
(Section 1). Instructions are indexed by time and frog label, with `true` selecting the parent
except at the root; woken frogs start moving at the next step. -/
def frogProcess {d : ℕ} (instructions : ℕ × Vertex d → Bool × Fin d) :
    ℕ → Finset (Vertex d) × (Vertex d → Vertex d)
  | 0 => ({[]}, id)
  | t + 1 =>
      let state := frogProcess instructions t
      let position := fun v ↦
        if v ∈ state.1 then
          let x := state.2 v
          if x ≠ [] ∧ (instructions (t, v)).1 = true then x.dropLast
          else x ++ [(instructions (t, v)).2]
        else state.2 v
      (state.1 ∪ state.1.image position, position)

/-- The critical drift: the infimum of recurrent drifts for the one-per-site frog model
(Section 1, p. 2). The recurrence set need not be an interval or contain its infimum. -/
def criticalDrift (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ p : unitInterval, r = (p : ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᵐ instructions ∂Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ × Vertex d ↦
      (bernoulliMeasure true false p).prod (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin d)).toMeasure),
      Set.Infinite {t : ℕ | ∃ v ∈ (frogProcess instructions t).1,
        (frogProcess instructions t).2 v = []}}

/-- **Open problem** (Section 1, p. 2). The critical drift weakly decreases as the
degree increases, and hence has a real limit.

No specific limit or strict decrease is asserted. The root always moves to a child, even at
drift one. -/
theorem critical_drift_monotonicity :
    (∀ d : ℕ, ∀ hd : 2 ≤ d,
      letI : NeZero d := ⟨by omega⟩
      criticalDrift (d + 1) ≤ criticalDrift d) ∧
    ∃ L : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ criticalDrift (n + 2))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  sorry

end Beckman2019Frog

theorem Beckman2019Frog.critical_drift_monotonicity_neg : ¬ type_of% @Beckman2019Frog.critical_drift_monotonicity := by
  sorry

title: Harmonic functions and the spectrum of the Laplacian on the Sierpinski carpet
source_label: Unnumbered conjecture (end of Section 4; restated in Section 8)
problem_statement: In begue2012harmonic.lean, prove either Begue2012Harmonic.counting_difference_bounded or refute it by proving its logical negation Begue2012Harmonic.counting_difference_bounded_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Harmonic functions and the spectrum of the Laplacian on the Sierpinski carpet

Authors: Matthew Begue, Tristan Kalloniatis, and Robert S. Strichartz.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.5136#page=1).
Reference: M. Begue, T. Kalloniatis, and R. S. Strichartz, *Harmonic functions and the spectrum
of the Laplacian on the Sierpinski carpet*, preprint (2012); arXiv:1201.5136v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Begue2012Harmonic

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The eight retained subsquares in the standard carpet's ternary construction. -/
abbrev CellDigit := {d : Fin 3 × Fin 3 // d ≠ (1, 1)}

instance : Nonempty CellDigit := ⟨⟨(0, 0), by decide⟩⟩

/-- An infinite address in the source's eight-map iterated function system. -/
abbrev Address := ℕ → CellDigit

/-- The geometric point of a carpet address. -/
def addressPoint (a : Address) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (∑' n : ℕ, (a n).val.1.val * (1 / 3 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1),
   ∑' n : ℕ, (a n).val.2.val * (1 / 3 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1))

/-- The square's eight symmetries, acting on the retained ternary digits. -/
def squareAction (swap flipX flipY : Bool) (d : CellDigit) : CellDigit :=
  let x := if swap then d.val.2 else d.val.1
  let y := if swap then d.val.1 else d.val.2
  ⟨(if flipX then ⟨2 - x.val, by omega⟩ else x,
    if flipY then ⟨2 - y.val, by omega⟩ else y), by
    dsimp [x, y]
    rcases d with ⟨⟨dx, dy⟩, hd⟩
    fin_cases dx <;> fin_cases dy <;> cases swap <;> cases flipX <;>
      cases flipY <;>
      simp_all only [Bool.false_eq_true, Fin.coe_ofNat_eq_mod, Fin.isValue, Fin.mk_one,
        Fin.reduceEq, Fin.reduceFinMk, Fin.zero_eta, Nat.add_one_sub_one, Nat.mod_succ, Nat.one_mod,
        Nat.zero_mod, Prod.mk.injEq, and_false, and_self, and_true, not_false_eq_true,
        not_true_eq_false, tsub_self, tsub_zero, zero_ne_one, ↓reduceIte]
    all_goals exact hd rfl⟩

/-- The address of a point in the level-`m` cell `w`, with tail `a`. -/
def cellAddress {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → CellDigit) (a : Address) : Address :=
  fun n ↦ if h : n < m then w ⟨n, h⟩ else a (n - m)

/-- Integer lower-left coordinate of a level-`m` cell, in units of `3 ^ (-m)`. -/
def cellCoordinate {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → CellDigit) : ℕ × ℕ :=
  (∑ i : Fin m, (w i).val.1.val * 3 ^ (m - 1 - i.val),
   ∑ i : Fin m, (w i).val.2.val * 3 ^ (m - 1 - i.val))

/-- BBKT's fold onto `w`, expressed on ternary addresses by reflection parity. -/
def foldAddress {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → CellDigit) (a : Address) : Address :=
  let sourceCell := cellCoordinate (m := m) (fun i ↦ a i.val)
  let targetCell := cellCoordinate w
  cellAddress w (fun n ↦ squareAction false
    (decide (sourceCell.1 % 2 ≠ targetCell.1 % 2))
    (decide (sourceCell.2 % 2 ≠ targetCell.2 % 2)) (a (n + m)))

/-- The symmetric self-similar probability measure on addresses. -/
def addressMeasure : Measure Address :=
  Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (PMF.uniformOfFintype CellDigit).toMeasure)

instance : IsProbabilityMeasure addressMeasure := by
  unfold addressMeasure
  infer_instance

/-- The canonical carpet energy of Kusuoka--Zhou and BBKT (BBKT, Definition 2.15). Closedness is
with respect to energy plus the `L²` norm, not the uniform norm. -/
structure CarpetEnergy where
  /-- The domain of the energy form, as functions on addresses. -/
  domain : Submodule ℝ (Address → ℝ)
  /-- The symmetric bilinear energy form on its domain. -/
  energy : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ domain
  continuous_mem : ∀ u : domain, Continuous (u : Address → ℝ)
  factors_mem : ∀ u : domain, Function.FactorsThrough (u : Address → ℝ) addressPoint
  symmetric : energy.IsSymm
  nonnegative : ∀ u : domain, 0 ≤ energy u u
  nonzero : ∃ u : domain, 0 < energy u u
  constant_mem : ∀ c : ℝ, (fun _ : Address ↦ c) ∈ domain
  constant_energy : ∀ c : ℝ,
    energy ⟨(fun _ ↦ c), constant_mem c⟩ ⟨(fun _ ↦ c), constant_mem c⟩ = 0
  markov_mem : ∀ u : domain, (fun a ↦ max 0 (min 1 ((u : Address → ℝ) a))) ∈ domain
  markov_energy : ∀ u : domain,
    energy ⟨(fun a ↦ max 0 (min 1 ((u : Address → ℝ) a))), markov_mem u⟩
      ⟨(fun a ↦ max 0 (min 1 ((u : Address → ℝ) a))), markov_mem u⟩ ≤ energy u u
  closed : ∀ u : ℕ → domain,
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m n : ℕ, N ≤ m → N ≤ n →
      energy (u m - u n) (u m - u n) +
        ∫ a, (((u m : domain) : Address → ℝ) a - ((u n : domain) : Address → ℝ) a) ^ 2
          ∂addressMeasure < ε) →
    ∃ v : domain, Tendsto (fun n ↦ energy (u n - v) (u n - v) +
      ∫ a, (((u n : domain) : Address → ℝ) a - (v : Address → ℝ) a) ^ 2 ∂addressMeasure)
        atTop (𝓝 0)
  regular : ∀ f : Address → ℝ, Continuous f → Function.FactorsThrough f addressPoint →
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ u : domain, ∀ a : Address, |(u : Address → ℝ) a - f a| < ε
  strongly_local : ∀ u v : domain,
    (∃ (O : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (c : ℝ), IsOpen O ∧
      closure (addressPoint '' Function.support (u : Address → ℝ)) ⊆ O ∧
      ∀ a : Address, addressPoint a ∈ O → (v : Address → ℝ) a = c) → energy u v = 0
  fold_mem : ∀ (m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → CellDigit) (u : domain),
    (fun a ↦ (u : Address → ℝ) (foldAddress w a)) ∈ domain
  cell_isometry_mem : ∀ (m : ℕ) (w₁ w₂ : Fin m → CellDigit)
    (swap flipX flipY : Bool) (g : Address → ℝ),
    (fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ foldAddress w₂ a (n + m))) ∈ domain →
    (fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ squareAction swap flipX flipY
      (foldAddress w₁ a (n + m)))) ∈ domain
  cell_isometry_energy : ∀ (m : ℕ) (w₁ w₂ : Fin m → CellDigit)
    (swap flipX flipY : Bool) (g : Address → ℝ)
    (hg : (fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ foldAddress w₂ a (n + m))) ∈ domain),
    energy ⟨(fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ squareAction swap flipX flipY
        (foldAddress w₁ a (n + m)))),
      cell_isometry_mem m w₁ w₂ swap flipX flipY g hg⟩
      ⟨(fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ squareAction swap flipX flipY
        (foldAddress w₁ a (n + m)))),
      cell_isometry_mem m w₁ w₂ swap flipX flipY g hg⟩ =
    energy ⟨(fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ foldAddress w₂ a (n + m))), hg⟩
      ⟨(fun a ↦ g (fun n ↦ foldAddress w₂ a (n + m))), hg⟩
  cell_additivity : ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : domain), energy u u =
    (8 : ℝ) ^ (-(m : ℤ)) * ∑ w : Fin m → CellDigit,
      energy ⟨(fun a ↦ (u : Address → ℝ) (foldAddress w a)), fold_mem m w u⟩
        ⟨(fun a ↦ (u : Address → ℝ) (foldAddress w a)), fold_mem m w u⟩

/-- The three compact boundary-identification fractafolds in Section 4. -/
inductive Fractafold
  | torus | kleinBottle | projectivePlane
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Generating outer-side identifications, including corner endpoints. The projective case has
two opposite-corner classes, not one four-corner class. -/
def BoundaryMatch (X : Fractafold) (a b : Address) : Prop :=
  let p := addressPoint a
  let q := addressPoint b
  (p.1 = 0 ∧ q.1 = 1 ∧ q.2 = if X = .torus then p.2 else 1 - p.2) ∨
  (p.2 = 0 ∧ q.2 = 1 ∧ q.1 = if X = .projectivePlane then 1 - p.1 else p.1)

/-- The energy domain with matched side traces. Transmission across seams is natural, so it is
not imposed separately. -/
def quotientDomain (E : CarpetEnergy) (X : Fractafold) : Submodule ℝ E.domain where
  carrier := {u | ∀ a b : Address, BoundaryMatch X a b →
    (u : Address → ℝ) a = (u : Address → ℝ) b}
  zero_mem' := by intro a b h; rfl
  add_mem' := by
    intro u v hu hv a b h
    change (u : Address → ℝ) a + (v : Address → ℝ) a =
      (u : Address → ℝ) b + (v : Address → ℝ) b
    rw [hu a b h, hv a b h]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu a b h
    change c * (u : Address → ℝ) a = c * (u : Address → ℝ) b
    rw [hu a b h]

/-- The real eigenspace of the nonnegative quotient Laplacian. Test functions range over the
whole matched form domain, including seam and corner values. -/
def weakEigenspace (E : CarpetEnergy) (X : Fractafold) (μ : ℝ) :
    Submodule ℝ E.domain where
  carrier := {u | u ∈ quotientDomain E X ∧ ∀ v : E.domain,
    v ∈ quotientDomain E X → E.energy u v =
      μ * ∫ a, (u : Address → ℝ) a * (v : Address → ℝ) a ∂addressMeasure}
  zero_mem' := by
    refine ⟨(quotientDomain E X).zero_mem, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u w hu hw
    refine ⟨(quotientDomain E X).add_mem hu.1 hw.1, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    have hiu : Integrable (fun a ↦ (u : Address → ℝ) a *
        (v : Address → ℝ) a) addressMeasure :=
      ((E.continuous_mem u).mul (E.continuous_mem v)).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
        (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
    have hiw : Integrable (fun a ↦ (w : Address → ℝ) a *
        (v : Address → ℝ) a) addressMeasure :=
      ((E.continuous_mem w).mul (E.continuous_mem v)).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
        (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
    simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hu.2 v hv, hw.2 v hv,
      Submodule.coe_add, Pi.add_apply, add_mul, integral_add hiu hiw, mul_add]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    refine ⟨(quotientDomain E X).smul_mem c hu.1, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    simp only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, hu.2 v hv, Submodule.coe_smul,
      Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, integral_const_mul]
    ring

/-- The inclusive eigenvalue count with multiplicities (4.3). Ranks are finite for this energy,
so the `finrank` junk value `0` does not arise. -/
def eigenvalueCount (E : CarpetEnergy) (X : Fractafold) (t : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank ℝ ((⨆ μ : {r : ℝ // r ≤ t}, weakEigenspace E X μ.val) :
    Submodule ℝ E.domain)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (end of Section 4; restated in Section 8). The counting-function
differences for all three compact carpet fractafolds are uniformly bounded.

The continuum energy model is used, including the projective corner singularities; the energy is
unique up to one common positive scale. -/
theorem counting_difference_bounded (E : CarpetEnergy) :
    ∃ C ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ t ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ X Y : Fractafold,
      |(eigenvalueCount E X t : ℝ) - (eigenvalueCount E Y t : ℝ)| ≤ C := by
  sorry

end Begue2012Harmonic

theorem Begue2012Harmonic.counting_difference_bounded_neg : ¬ type_of% @Begue2012Harmonic.counting_difference_bounded := by
  sorry

program: Emory University REU in Number Theory
title: l-adic properties of partition functions
problem_statement: In belmont2015l.lean, prove either Belmont2015L.conjecture_after_5_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Belmont2015L.conjecture_after_5_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# l-adic properties of partition functions

Authors: Eva Belmont, Holden Lee, Alexandra Musat, and Sarah Trebat-Leder.
Origin: [Emory University REU in Number Theory
2011](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2011).
Reference: E. Belmont, H. Lee, A. Musat, and S. Trebat-Leder, *l-adic properties of partition
functions*, Monatsh. Math. **173** (2014), no. 1, 1-34; arXiv:1510.01202v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Belmont2015L

/-- Coefficientwise reduction of a rational `q`-series modulo `ell`. It is used only for
`ell`-integral series; other denominators give junk values. -/
def reduction (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (a : PowerSeries ℚ) : PowerSeries (ZMod ell) :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun n ↦ ((a.coeff n).num : ZMod ell) / ((a.coeff n).den : ZMod ell)

/-- The reductions modulo `ell` of the `ell`-integral level-one forms in `M_k`. -/
def modularFormsMod (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (k : ℤ) : Set (PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :=
  {g | ∃ (f : ModularForm (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL (n := Fin 2) (R := ℤ) ℝ).range k)
      (a : PowerSeries ℚ),
    (∀ n, ¬ell ∣ (a.coeff n).den) ∧
    a.map (Rat.castHom ℂ) = UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 f ∧
    reduction ell a = g}

/-- The reductions modulo `ell` of the `ell`-integral level-one cusp forms in `S_k`. -/
def cuspFormsMod (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (k : ℤ) : Set (PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :=
  {g | ∃ (f : CuspForm (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL (n := Fin 2) (R := ℤ) ℝ).range k)
      (a : PowerSeries ℚ),
    (∀ n, ¬ell ∣ (a.coeff n).den) ∧
    a.map (Rat.castHom ℂ) = UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 f ∧
    reduction ell a = g}

/-- The formal `q`-series of `η(ell ^ 2 z) / η(z)` reduced modulo `ell` (equation (2.2)). The
Euler products are pentagonal series, and only primes `ell ≥ 5` are intended. -/
def phi (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] : PowerSeries (ZMod ell) :=
  let E := PowerSeries.pentagonalSeries (ZMod ell)
  let hE : PowerSeries.constantCoeff E = (1 : (ZMod ell)) := by
    simpa [PowerSeries.coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff_apply, pentagonal, E] using
      (PowerSeries.coeff_pentagonalSeries_pentagonal (ZMod ell) (0 : ℤ))
  let e : Units (PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :=
    { val := E
      inv := PowerSeries.invOfUnit E 1
      val_inv := PowerSeries.mul_invOfUnit E 1 hE
      inv_val := PowerSeries.invOfUnit_mul E 1 hE }
  PowerSeries.X ^ ((ell ^ 2 - 1) / 24) *
    PowerSeries.expand (ell ^ 2) (pow_ne_zero _ (Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out)) E *
    ((e ^ (-1 : ℤ) : Units (PowerSeries (ZMod ell))) : PowerSeries (ZMod ell))

/-- Atkin's `U` operator, extracting coefficients at multiples of `ell` (equation (2.1)). -/
def U (ell : ℕ) (g : PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) : PowerSeries (ZMod ell) :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun n ↦ g.coeff (ell * n)

/-- The operator `D_r`: multiply by `Φ_ell ^ r`, then apply `U(ell)` (equation (2.3)). -/
def D (ell r : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (g : PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :
    PowerSeries (ZMod ell) :=
  U ell (g * phi ell ^ r)

/-- The operator `X_r`: `U` followed by `D_r`, in the source's right-action notation
(equation (2.4)). -/
def X (ell r : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (g : PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :
    PowerSeries (ZMod ell) :=
  D ell r (U ell g)

/-- The odd invertible part: all subspaces of the reduced odd cusp space on which `X_r` is
bijective (Section 4, (5.2)). It uses odd-`X`/even-`Y`, correcting the reversed names printed
before (5.2). -/
def oddStableSpace (ell r : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] :
    Submodule (ZMod ell) (PowerSeries (ZMod ell)) :=
  sSup {W | (W : Set (PowerSeries (ZMod ell))) ⊆
      cuspFormsMod ell (((r / 2 + 1) * (ell - 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
    Set.BijOn (X ell r) (W : Set (PowerSeries (ZMod ell))) W}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after (5.3)). The operator `D_r` sends every reduced
`ell`-integral form in `M_(ell-1)` into the odd `X_r`-invertible part.

This is the equivalent `t = 0` form; the printed odd/even operator names are read as
odd-`X`/even-`Y`. -/
theorem conjecture_after_5_3 (r : ℕ) {ell : ℕ} [Fact ell.Prime]
    (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hell : r + 5 ≤ ell) (g : PowerSeries (ZMod ell))
    (hg : g ∈ modularFormsMod ell ((ell - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) :
    D ell r g ∈ (oddStableSpace ell r : Set (PowerSeries (ZMod ell))) := by
  sorry

end Belmont2015L

theorem Belmont2015L.conjecture_after_5_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Belmont2015L.conjecture_after_5_3 := by
  sorry

title: Calculus on the Sierpinski gasket II: point singularities, eigenfunctions, and normal derivatives of the heat kernel
problem_statement: In bengal2006calculus.lean, prove either BenGal2006Calculus.conjecture_9_6_a or refute it by proving its logical negation BenGal2006Calculus.conjecture_9_6_a_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Calculus on the Sierpinski gasket II: point singularities, eigenfunctions, and normal derivatives of the heat kernel

Authors: Nitsan Ben-Gal, Abby Shaw-Krauss, Robert S. Strichartz, and Clint Young.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU](https://math.cornell.edu/history-reu-and-spur-programs-department-mathematics).
Reference: N. Ben-Gal, A. Shaw-Krauss, R. S. Strichartz, and C. Young, *Calculus on the
Sierpinski gasket II: point singularities, eigenfunctions, and normal derivatives of the heat
kernel*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **358** (2006), no. 9, 3883-3936;
doi:10.1090/S0002-9947-06-04056-6.
-/

noncomputable section
open scoped Topology
open MeasureTheory Filter

namespace BenGal2006Calculus

/-- The three ordered boundary vertices of the equilateral triangle. -/
def boundary (i : Fin 3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if i = 0 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0]
  else if i = 1 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0]
  else WithLp.toLp 2 ![(1 : ℝ) / 2, √3 / 2]

/-- The contraction `F_i`. -/
def contraction (i : Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (x + boundary i)

/-- The cell map `F_w`, with the first letter outermost. -/
def cellMap (w : List (Fin 3)) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  w.foldr contraction x

/-- The finite vertex sets `V_m`. -/
def vertices : ℕ → Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  | 0 => Finset.univ.image boundary
  | m + 1 => Finset.univ.biUnion fun i ↦ (vertices m).image (contraction i)

/-- The compact planar gasket, the closure of its finite-level vertices. -/
def gasket : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  closure (⋃ m : ℕ, (vertices m : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))

/-- The continuous coding map of the three-map iterated function system. -/
def addressMap : C(ℕ → Fin 3, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) where
  toFun a := ∑' n : ℕ, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) • boundary (a n)
  continuous_toFun := by
    let C : ℝ := ∑ i : Fin 3, ‖boundary i‖
    have hsum : Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) * C) :=
      (summable_geometric_of_norm_lt_one (by norm_num : ‖(1 / 2 : ℝ)‖ < 1)).mul_right
        ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * C) |>.congr (fun n ↦ by ring)
    apply continuous_tsum (u := fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) * C)
    · intro n
      exact (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℕ → Fin 3 ↦
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1))).smul ((continuous_of_discreteTopology :
        Continuous boundary).comp (continuous_apply n :
          Continuous (fun a : ℕ → Fin 3 ↦ a n)))
    · exact hsum
    · intro n a
      rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (by positivity)
      exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun i _ ↦ norm_nonneg (boundary i)) (Finset.mem_univ _)

/-- The equal-cell-weight self-similar probability measure from (1.3). -/
def gasketMeasure : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  (Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin 3)).toMeasure)).map
    addressMap

/-- The graph whose edges join distinct corners of each `m`-cell. -/
def levelGraph (m : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ ∃ w : List (Fin 3), w.length = m ∧
    ∃ i k : Fin 3, x = cellMap w (boundary i) ∧ y = cellMap w (boundary k)
  symm := ⟨by
    rintro x y ⟨hne, w, hw, i, k, hx, hy⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, w, hw, k, i, hy, hx⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro x hx; exact hx.1 rfl⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- The unrenormalized graph Laplacian on `V_m`. -/
def graphLaplacian (m : ℕ) (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ y ∈ vertices m with (levelGraph m).Adj x y, (u y - u x)

/-- The continuous Kigami Laplacian, as a uniform limit of renormalized graph Laplacians. -/
def HasLaplacian (u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u gasket ∧ ContinuousOn v gasket ∧
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ M,
      ∀ x ∈ vertices m, x ∉ vertices 0 →
        |(3 / 2 : ℝ) * (5 : ℝ) ^ m * graphLaplacian m u x - v x| < ε

/-- The outward normal derivative at `q₀` (1.9). -/
def normalDerivative (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Filter.limUnder Filter.atTop (fun m : ℕ ↦ (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m *
    (2 * u (boundary 0) - u ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 1)) -
      u ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 2))))

/-- **Conjecture 9.6(a)** ((9.31), p. 3934). The double outward normal derivative of the
Dirichlet heat kernel has a positive continuous log-5-periodic leading profile.

The kernel is given by a complete real `L²` eigenbasis with full multiplicities, and the
convergent normal series models the mixed kernel normals in (9.27). No least period,
nonconstancy or rate is asserted. -/
theorem conjecture_9_6_a
    (u : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (hu : ∀ j, MemLp (u j) 2 gasketMeasure)
    (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ (Lp ℝ 2 gasketMeasure))
    (hb : ∀ j, b j = (hu j).toLp (u j))
    (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (hμ : ∀ j, 0 < μ j)
    (heigen : ∀ j, HasLaplacian (u j) (fun x ↦ -(μ j) * u j x))
    (hboundary : ∀ j i, u j (boundary i) = 0) :
    ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g ∧ (∀ s, 0 < g s) ∧
      Function.Periodic g (Real.log 5) ∧
      Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦
        t ^ (Real.log (25 / 3 : ℝ) / Real.log 5) *
          (∑' j : ℕ, Real.exp (-(μ j) * t) * normalDerivative (u j) ^ 2) -
          g (Real.log (1 / t))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

end BenGal2006Calculus

theorem BenGal2006Calculus.conjecture_9_6_a_neg : ¬ type_of% @BenGal2006Calculus.conjecture_9_6_a := by
  sorry

title: Query Complexity of Mastermind Variants
problem_statement: In berger2018query.lean, prove either Berger2018Query.problem_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Berger2018Query.problem_3_neg.
challenge:

/-!
# Query Complexity of Mastermind Variants

Authors: Aaron Berger, Christopher Chute, and Matthew Stone.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY 2015](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: A. Berger, C. Chute, and M. Stone, *Query Complexity of Mastermind Variants*,
arXiv:1607.04597v2 (2017).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Berger2018Query

open Finset

/-- The black-peg count: the number of positions where query and hidden word agree (p. 3). -/
def blackPegs {n k : ℕ} (query hidden : Fin n → Fin k) : ℕ :=
  #{i | query i = hidden i}

/-- The white-peg count: the largest black-peg count over all permutations of the query
positions, minus the black-peg count (p. 3). -/
def whitePegs {n k : ℕ} (query hidden : Fin n → Fin k) : ℕ :=
  (univ.sup fun σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) ↦ blackPegs (fun i ↦ query (σ i)) hidden) -
    blackPegs query hidden

/-- **Problem 3** (Section 5, p. 15). Non-adaptive black-and-white Mastermind without repeated
colors needs `Ω(n log k)` queries, uniformly for all `k ≥ n`.

Identification uses the full ordered response vector with no final charged guess; colors do not
repeat within a query, but whole queries may repeat. -/
theorem problem_3 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ N ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ k ≥ n, ∀ (m : ℕ) (queries : Fin m → Fin n ↪ Fin k),
      Function.Injective (fun hidden : Fin n ↪ Fin k ↦
        fun t ↦ (blackPegs (queries t) hidden, whitePegs (queries t) hidden)) →
      c * n * Real.logb 2 k ≤ m := by
  sorry

end Berger2018Query

  sorry

title: Approximate fair loaded dice
problem_statement: In berlanga2017approximate.lean, prove either Berlanga2017Approximate.minimum_square_mass or refute it by proving its logical negation Berlanga2017Approximate.minimum_square_mass_neg.
challenge:

/-!
# Approximate fair loaded dice

Authors: Berlanga, William Gasarch, and Peter Tian.
Origin: [University of Maryland REU-CAAR
2016](https://www.cs.umd.edu/projects/reucaar/highlights-2016.html).
Reference: Berlanga, W. Gasarch, and P. Tian, *Approximate fair loaded dice*, REU-CAAR research
report (2017), 12 pp.
-/

namespace Berlanga2017Approximate

/-- **Conjecture 1.1** (p. 2). The displayed loading attains the global minimum of the sum of
squared total-roll probabilities.

Faces are indexed from zero, shifting every total by the number of dice; one die and two faces
are included, and no uniqueness is asserted. A later theorem settles only the two-dice case. -/
theorem minimum_square_mass (m n : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    let D : ℝ := 2 * (m : ℝ) + ((n : ℝ) - 2) * (2 * (m : ℝ) - 1)
    let pStar : Fin m → Fin n → ℝ := fun i j ↦
      if i.val = 0 then
        if j.val = 0 ∨ j.val + 1 = n then (m : ℝ) / D
        else (2 * (m : ℝ) - 1) / D
      else if j.val = 0 ∨ j.val + 1 = n then 1 / 2 else 0
    let S : (Fin m → Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ := fun p ↦
      ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (m * (n - 1) + 1),
        (∑ a : Fin m → Fin n,
          if (∑ i : Fin m, (a i).val) = s then ∏ i : Fin m, p i (a i)
          else 0) ^ 2
    let C : ℝ := (Nat.factorial (2 * m - 1) : ℝ) /
      ((2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * m - 2) * (Nat.factorial (m - 1) : ℝ) ^ 2 * D)
    (∀ i j, 0 ≤ pStar i j) ∧ (∀ i, ∑ j, pStar i j = 1) ∧
      S pStar = C ∧
      ∀ p : Fin m → Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ (Fin n),
        C ≤ S (fun i j ↦ (p i).weights j) := by
  sorry

end Berlanga2017Approximate

title: Restricted Stacks as Functions
problem_statement: In berlow2021restricted.lean, prove either Berlow2021Restricted.conjecture_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Berlow2021Restricted.conjecture_5_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Restricted Stacks as Functions

Author: Katalin Berlow.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2020](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: K. Berlow, *Restricted stacks as functions*, Discrete Math. **344** (2021), 112571;
arXiv:2008.01164.
-/

namespace Berlow2021Restricted

/-- Classical containment of a length-three pattern as a subsequence with all pairwise order
relations preserved (Definition 1.2). -/
def Contains (p : Fin 3 → ℕ) (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : Fin 3 → Fin w.length, StrictMono i ∧
    ∀ a b, w[i a] < w[i b] ↔ p a < p b

open scoped Classical in
/-- The `T`-restricted stack sort: push greedily while the stack stays `T`-avoiding, otherwise
pop to the output (Definition 1.3). -/
noncomputable def stackSort (T : Finset (Fin 3 → ℕ)) (input : List ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  let step := fun (state : List ℕ × List ℕ × List ℕ) ↦
    let (remaining, stack, output) := state
    match remaining, stack with
    | [], [] => state
    | [], y :: ys => ([], ys, y :: output)
    | x :: xs, [] => (xs, [x], output)
    | x :: xs, y :: ys =>
      if ∃ p ∈ T, Contains p (x :: y :: ys) then
        (x :: xs, ys, y :: output)
      else
        (xs, x :: y :: ys, output)
  let result := step^[2 * input.length] (input, [], [])
  result.2.2.reverse

/-- **Conjecture 5.1** (arXiv v2, p. 14). For either specified pair of forbidden patterns, the
periodic permutations are exactly the identity and its reverse.

O. Zhang (2025), Conjecture 4.2, prints "inverse" for these pairs; the original "reverse" is
kept. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 {n : ℕ} (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (T : Finset (Fin 3 → ℕ))
    (hT : T = {![1, 3, 2], ![2, 1, 3]} ∨ T = {![2, 3, 1], ![2, 1, 3]}) :
    List.ofFn (fun i ↦ (π i).val + 1) ∈ Function.periodicPts (stackSort T) ↔
      π = Equiv.refl (Fin n) ∨ π = Fin.revPerm := by
  sorry

end Berlow2021Restricted

  sorry

title: Geometric-progression-free sets over quadratic number fields
problem_statement: In best2017geometric.lean, prove either Best2017Geometric.question_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Best2017Geometric.question_5_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Geometric-progression-free sets over quadratic number fields

Authors: Andrew Best, Karen Huan, Nathan McNew, Steven J. Miller, Jasmine Powell,
Kimsy Tor, and Madeleine Weinstein.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2014](https://www.nathanmcnew.com/math.html).
Reference: A. Best, K. Huan, N. McNew, S. J. Miller, J. Powell, K. Tor, and M. Weinstein,
*Geometric-progression-free sets over quadratic number fields*, Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A
**147** (2017), 245-262; doi:10.1017/S030821051600010X.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Best2017Geometric

open scoped NumberField
open scoped Topology
open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- The greedy ideal set (Section 3), via the prime-exponent characterization in the proof of
Theorem 3.6 and the ternary description of `A*_3` in Section 2. -/
def greedyIdeals (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Set (Ideal (𝓞 K)) :=
  {I | I ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ P : Ideal (𝓞 K), P.IsPrime → P ≠ 0 →
    2 ∉ Nat.digits 3 (factorization I P)}

/-- Asymptotic density among nonzero integral ideals ordered by absolute norm
(Definition 3.2). -/
def HasIdealDensity (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (A : Set (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (d : ℝ) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
    let B := (Ideal.finite_setOfPred_absNorm_le (S := 𝓞 K) n).toFinset.erase 0
    ((#{I ∈ B | I ∈ A} : ℝ) / (#B : ℝ)))
    Filter.atTop (𝓝 d)

/-- **Question 5.1** (pp. 259-260). In every quadratic number field, some set of integral ideals
free of three-term geometric progressions has asymptotic density strictly exceeding that of the
greedy set.

Ratios are nonzero nonunit integral ideals, not fractional ideals, and density is a limit, not a
limsup. -/
theorem question_5_1 (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (hK : Module.finrank ℚ K = 2) :
    ∃ (A : Set (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (d g : ℝ),
      0 ∉ A ∧
      (∀ I R : Ideal (𝓞 K), I ≠ 0 → R ≠ 0 → R ≠ 1 →
        I ∈ A → I * R ∈ A → I * R ^ 2 ∉ A) ∧

title: The Tri-Pants Graph of the Twice-Punctured Torus
problem_statement: In betts2021tri.lean, prove either Betts2021Tri.fibers_are_farey_dual or refute it by proving its logical negation Betts2021Tri.fibers_are_farey_dual_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Tri-Pants Graph of the Twice-Punctured Torus

Authors: Katherine Betts, Troy Larsen, Jeffrey Utley, and Avalon Vanis.
Origin: [University of Virginia REU 2021](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2021).
Reference: K. Betts, T. Larsen, J. Utley, and A. Vanis, *The tri-pants graph of the
twice-punctured torus*, preprint (2021); arXiv:2111.07136v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Betts2021Tri

open Finset

/-- The marked coordinate torus. -/
abbrev Torus := UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

/-- The torus with two distinct punctures, in fixed coordinates. -/
abbrev Surface := {x : Torus // x ≠ (0, 0) ∧ x ≠ (((1 / 2 : ℝ) : UnitAddCircle), 0)}

/-- Simple nonseparating parametrized circles in the twice-punctured surface. -/
abbrev SimpleCurve := {c : C(UnitAddCircle, Surface) //
  Function.Injective c ∧ IsConnected (Set.range c)ᶜ}

/-- Unoriented free-homotopy classes of simple curves. -/
abbrev Curve := Quotient (Relation.EqvGen.setoid fun r s : SimpleCurve ↦
  ContinuousMap.Homotopic r.val s.val ∨
    ContinuousMap.Homotopic r.val
      (s.val.comp ⟨fun t : UnitAddCircle ↦ -t, continuous_neg⟩))

/-- The minimal geometric intersection over all simple representatives (Definition 1.8).
Infinite intersections have value `⊤`. -/
def intersectionNumber (a b : Curve) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ r s : SimpleCurve,
    Quotient.mk _ r = a ∧ Quotient.mk _ s = b ∧
      (Set.range r.val ∩ Set.range s.val).encard = n}

/-- The interior of a pair of pants, a plane with two points deleted. -/
abbrev OpenPants := {x : ℝ × ℝ // x ≠ (0, 0) ∧ x ≠ (1, 0)}

open scoped Classical in
/-- An unordered nonseparating pants decomposition (Definitions 2.3 and 2.5). -/
def IsPantsPair (p : Finset Curve) : Prop :=
  ∃ r s : SimpleCurve,
    (Quotient.mk _ r : Curve) ≠ (Quotient.mk _ s : Curve) ∧
    p = {Quotient.mk _ r, Quotient.mk _ s} ∧
    Disjoint (Set.range r.val) (Set.range s.val) ∧
    Nonempty ({x : Surface // x ∉ Set.range r.val ∧ x ∉ Set.range s.val} ≃ₜ
      (OpenPants ⊕ OpenPants))

open scoped Classical in
/-- A tri-pant: six curve classes partitioned into three pants pairs (Definition 2.10). The
partition is only required to exist; it is not part of the vertex data. -/
abbrev TriPant := {t : Finset Curve // #t = 6 ∧
  ∃ P : Finset (Finset Curve), #P = 3 ∧
    (∀ p ∈ P, IsPantsPair p) ∧ P.biUnion id = t ∧
    (∀ p ∈ P, ∀ q ∈ P, p ≠ q → Disjoint p q) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ P, ∀ q ∈ P, p ≠ q →
      ∀ a ∈ p, ∀ b ∈ q, intersectionNumber a b = 1}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The tri-pants graph, where adjacency means sharing two whole pants pairs
(Definitions 2.11 and 3.9). -/
def triPantsGraph : SimpleGraph TriPant where
  Adj t u := t ≠ u ∧
    #({p ∈ t.val.powerset | IsPantsPair p} ∩
      {p ∈ u.val.powerset | IsPantsPair p}) = 2
  symm.symm := by
    intro t u h
    refine ⟨h.1.symm, ?_⟩
    rw [Finset.inter_comm]
    exact h.2
  loopless.irrefl := by
    intro t h
    exact h.1 rfl

/-- Rational slopes and infinity as primitive integer pairs modulo common sign. -/
structure FareySlope where
  /-- The numerator of the slope. -/
  num : ℤ
  /-- The denominator of the slope, zero for the slope infinity. -/
  den : ℤ
  primitive : num.natAbs.Coprime den.natAbs
  canonical : 0 < den ∨ (den = 0 ∧ num = 1)

/-- A triangle of the full Farey graph of Definition 3.1. -/
abbrev FareyTriangle := {t : Finset FareySlope // #t = 3 ∧
  ∀ v ∈ t, ∀ w ∈ t, v ≠ w → (v.num * w.den - w.num * v.den).natAbs = 1}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The dual Farey graph, with shared-edge adjacency (Definition 3.3). -/
def fareyDual : SimpleGraph FareyTriangle where
  Adj t u := t ≠ u ∧ #(t.val ∩ u.val) = 2
  symm.symm := by
    intro t u h
    refine ⟨h.1.symm, ?_⟩
    rw [Finset.inter_comm]
    exact h.2
  loopless.irrefl := by
    intro t h
    exact h.1 rfl

/-- The slopes of the projection: the set of filled slopes of the six curve classes, so classes
with equal slope contribute one element. Representatives may have either orientation. -/
def slopeImage (t : TriPant) : Set FareySlope :=
  {v | ∃ a ∈ t.val, ∃ r : SimpleCurve, Quotient.mk _ r = a ∧
    ContinuousMap.Homotopic
      ((⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩ : C(Surface, Torus)).comp r.val)
      (⟨fun t : UnitAddCircle ↦ (v.num • t, v.den • t), by fun_prop⟩ :
        C(UnitAddCircle, Torus))}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Conclusion, p. 32). Every vertex fiber of the puncture-filling
projection is graph-isomorphic to the dual Farey graph.

Curves are unparametrized and unoriented, although Definition 1.2 omits reversal. A fiber is the
set of tri-pants with a given slope image, with all inherited edges, including the big-flip edges
collapsed by the projection; the isomorphism need not be canonical. -/
theorem fibers_are_farey_dual (v : FareyTriangle) :
    Nonempty ((triPantsGraph.induce {t | slopeImage t = (v.val : Set FareySlope)}) ≃g
      fareyDual) := by
  sorry

end Betts2021Tri

theorem Betts2021Tri.fibers_are_farey_dual_neg : ¬ type_of% @Betts2021Tri.fibers_are_farey_dual := by
  sorry

/-!
# Generic classification and asymptotic enumeration of dope matrices

Author: Ankit Bisain.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2022](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: A. Bisain, *Generic classification and asymptotic enumeration of dope matrices*,
arXiv:2209.13811v1.

open Filter
open scoped Asymptotics

namespace Bisain2024Generic

/-- The dope matrices: zero patterns of a degree-`n` complex polynomial and its derivatives at
`m` ordered distinct complex numbers (Section 1). -/
def dopeMatrices (m n : ℕ) : Set (Matrix (Fin m) (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin 2)) :=
  {M | ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.degree = (n : WithBot ℕ) ∧
    ∃ z : Fin m → ℂ, Function.Injective z ∧
      ∀ i j, M i j = 1 ↔ ((Polynomial.derivative^[j.val]) p).eval (z i) = 0}

/-- **Conjecture 5.1**. The logarithm of the number of dope matrices has the proposed sharp
asymptotic throughout `1 < m ≤ (n ^ 2 + n) / 2` as `n` tends to infinity. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 (m n : ℕ → ℕ) (hm : ∀ t, 1 < m t)
    (hmn : ∀ t, 2 * m t ≤ n t ^ 2 + n t) (hn : Tendsto n atTop atTop) :
    (fun t ↦ Real.log ((dopeMatrices (m t) (n t)).ncard : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun t ↦ Real.log
        (((n t ^ m t * (m t * n t).choose (n t) : ℕ) : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

title: Covering half-grids with lines and planes
problem_statement: In bishnoi2025covering.lean, prove either Bishnoi2025Covering.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Bishnoi2025Covering.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Covering half-grids with lines and planes

Authors: Anurag Bishnoi and Shantanu Nene.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2023](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu/results2023).
Reference: A. Bishnoi and S. Nene, *Covering half-grids with lines and planes*,
arXiv:2501.11156v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Bishnoi2025Covering

open Finset

/-- A conical grid of order `n`: `n - i` points on the `i`th of `n` strictly increasing
horizontal levels, and no other points (Definition 1). -/
def IsConicalGrid (n : ℕ) (G : Finset (ℝ × ℝ)) : Prop :=
  0 < n ∧ ∃ a : Fin n → ℝ, StrictMono a ∧
    (∀ p ∈ G, ∃ i, p.2 = a i) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, #{p ∈ G | p.2 = a i} = n - i.val

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 1** (p. 7). A single absolute positive constant `C` gives the lower bound
`2 * n * k / 3 - C * k` for every multiplicity cover of every conical grid. -/
theorem conjecture_1 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      ∀ (n k : ℕ) (G : Finset (ℝ × ℝ)), IsConicalGrid n G → 0 < k →
        ∀ L : Multiset (AffineSubspace ℝ (ℝ × ℝ)),
          (∀ l ∈ L, Module.finrank ℝ l.direction = 1) →
          (∀ p ∈ G, k ≤ (L.filter fun l ↦ p ∈ l).card) →
          (2 : ℝ) * n * k / 3 - C * k ≤ (L.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Bishnoi2025Covering

title: Extreme Genera and Other Techniques of Graph Embeddings
problem_statement: In blanchard2016extreme.lean, prove either Blanchard2016Extreme.conjecture_1_13 or refute it by proving its logical negation Blanchard2016Extreme.conjecture_1_13_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Extreme Genera and Other Techniques of Graph Embeddings

Authors: Eion Blanchard and Esther Hunt.
Origin: [University of Washington REU 2016](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~reu/papers/2016/).
Reference: E. Blanchard and E. Hunt, *Extreme genera and other techniques of graph embeddings*,
University of Washington REU report (2016), 25 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Blanchard2016Extreme

/-- The appended 3-to-1 graph: the labeled graph of p. 4 with vertex `14` joined to the fourteen
boundary vertices (Section 1.1, Definition 1.5). -/
def appendedThreeToOne : SimpleGraph (Fin 23) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v ↦
    (u = 14 ∧ v < 14) ∨
    (u = 15 ∧ v ∈ ({0, 1, 12, 13} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 16 ∧ v ∈ ({5, 6, 12, 13} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 17 ∧ v ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 18 ∧ v ∈ ({2, 3, 4, 5} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 19 ∧ v ∈ ({4, 5, 6, 7} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 20 ∧ v ∈ ({4, 6, 8, 9} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 21 ∧ v ∈ ({0, 8, 9, 10} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 22 ∧ v ∈ ({0, 1, 10, 11} : Finset (Fin 23))) ∨
    (u = 1 ∧ v = 10)

/-- A rotation system: a cyclic ordering of the neighbors of each vertex (Definition 2.15). Without
edge signatures it describes only orientable embeddings (Remark 2.17). -/
structure RotationSystem {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The cyclic permutation of the neighbors of each vertex. -/
  rotation : (v : V) → Equiv.Perm (G.neighborSet v)
  cyclic : ∀ v, (rotation v).IsCycleOn Set.univ

/-- The dart successor tracing the oriented face boundaries in Section 2.3. -/
def RotationSystem.facePermutation {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (r : RotationSystem G) : Equiv.Perm G.Dart where
  toFun d :=
    let w := r.rotation d.snd (Subtype.mk d.fst d.adj.symm)
    { toProd := (d.snd, w.val), adj := w.property }
  invFun d :=
    let w := (r.rotation d.fst).symm (Subtype.mk d.snd d.adj)
    { toProd := (w.val, d.fst), adj := w.property.symm }
  left_inv d := by
    apply SimpleGraph.Dart.ext
    apply Prod.ext
    · exact congrArg Subtype.val
        ((r.rotation d.snd).symm_apply_apply (Subtype.mk d.fst d.adj.symm))
    · rfl
  right_inv d := by
    apply SimpleGraph.Dart.ext
    apply Prod.ext
    · rfl
    · exact congrArg Subtype.val
        ((r.rotation d.fst).apply_symm_apply (Subtype.mk d.snd d.adj))

/-- **Conjecture 1.13**. The 3-to-1 graph is 3-circular, equivalently its appended graph has
minimum orientable genus three.

Face cycles and the Euler equation are those of Section 2.3; the boundary order is not
prescribed. -/
theorem conjecture_1_13 :
    let eulerCharacteristic := fun r : RotationSystem appendedThreeToOne ↦
      (Nat.card (Fin 23) : ℤ) - Nat.card appendedThreeToOne.edgeSet +
        Nat.card (Quotient (Equiv.Perm.SameCycle.setoid r.facePermutation))
    (∃ r : RotationSystem appendedThreeToOne,
      eulerCharacteristic r = 2 - 2 * 3) ∧
      (∀ r : RotationSystem appendedThreeToOne,
        eulerCharacteristic r ≤ 2 - 2 * 3) := by
  sorry

end Blanchard2016Extreme

theorem Blanchard2016Extreme.conjecture_1_13_neg : ¬ type_of% @Blanchard2016Extreme.conjecture_1_13 := by
  sorry

title: Consequences of the packing problem
problem_statement: In bodas2021consequences.lean, prove either Bodas2021Consequences.FiniteHypergraph.conjecture_coloring or refute it by proving its logical negation Bodas2021Consequences.FiniteHypergraph.conjecture_coloring_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Consequences of the packing problem

Authors: Hrishikesh Bodas, Benjamin Drabkin, Caleb Fong, Su Jin, Justin Kim,
Wenxuan Li, Alexandra Seceleanu, Tingting Tang, and Brendan Williams.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2020](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu).
Reference: H. Bodas, B. Drabkin, C. Fong, S. Jin, J. Kim, W. Li, A. Seceleanu, T. Tang, and
B. Williams, *Consequences of the packing problem*, J. Algebraic Combin. **54** (2021),
1095-1117; doi:10.1007/s10801-021-01039-5; arXiv:2101.04010.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Bodas2021Consequences

open Finset

/-- A finite clutter: a hypergraph on the whole finite vertex type whose edge set is an
antichain under inclusion. -/
@[nolint unusedArguments]
def FiniteHypergraph (V : Type*) [Fintype V] :=
  {H : Hypergraph V // H.vertexSet = Set.univ ∧
    IsAntichain (fun s t : Set V ↦ s ⊆ t) H.edgeSet}

namespace FiniteHypergraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- A vertex cover of `H`: a set of vertices meeting every edge. -/
def IsVertexCover (H : FiniteHypergraph V) (C : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ H.val.edgeSet, ∃ v ∈ e, v ∈ C

/-- The transversal number `τ(H)`: the minimum cardinality of a vertex cover. -/
def transversalNumber (H : FiniteHypergraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | ∃ C : Finset V, H.IsVertexCover C ∧ #C = m}

/-- An edge packing or matching: a set of pairwise-disjoint edges of `H`. -/
def IsEdgePacking (H : FiniteHypergraph V) (M : Finset (Set V)) : Prop :=
  (∀ e ∈ M, e ∈ H.val.edgeSet) ∧
    ∀ ⦃e₁ : Set V⦄, e₁ ∈ M → ∀ ⦃e₂ : Set V⦄, e₂ ∈ M → e₁ ≠ e₂ →
      ∀ v ∈ e₁, v ∈ e₂ → False

/-- The packing number `π(H)`: the maximum cardinality of an edge packing. -/
def packingNumber (H : FiniteHypergraph V) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m : ℕ | ∃ M : Finset (Set V), H.IsEdgePacking M ∧ #M = m}

/-- A König hypergraph: one satisfying `τ(H) = π(H)`. -/
def IsKonig (H : FiniteHypergraph V) : Prop :=
  H.transversalNumber = H.packingNumber

/-- The deletion-contraction minor, keeping only the inclusion-minimal edge images on the
surviving vertex type. -/
def minor (H : FiniteHypergraph V) (D C : Finset V) :
    FiniteHypergraph {v : V // v ∉ D ∧ v ∉ C} :=
  let images : Set (Set {v : V // v ∉ D ∧ v ∉ C}) :=
    (fun e : Set V ↦ Subtype.val ⁻¹' e) '' {e ∈ H.val.edgeSet | Disjoint e (D : Set V)}
  ⟨{ vertexSet := Set.univ
     edgeSet := {s ∈ images | ∀ t ∈ images, t ⊆ s → s ⊆ t}
     subset_vertexSet_of_mem_edgeSet' := fun _ _ ↦ Set.subset_univ _ },
   rfl, by
     intro s hs t ht hne hst
     exact hne (Set.Subset.antisymm hst (ht.2 s hs.1 hst))⟩

/-- The packing property: every deletion-contraction minor is König (Definition 2.14).
Minors with an empty edge (the unit ideal) are excluded, a convention not printed there. -/
def HasPackingProperty (H : FiniteHypergraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ D C : Finset V, Disjoint D C →
    (∅ : Set {v : V // v ∉ D ∧ v ∉ C}) ∉ (H.minor D C).val.edgeSet →
      (H.minor D C).IsKonig

/-- The initial degree `alpha(I(H))` of the edge ideal. It is encoded as the least cardinality
of an edge. -/
def initialDegree (H : FiniteHypergraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | ∃ e ∈ H.val.edgeSet, e.ncard = m}

/-- An `(a : b)`-rainbow coloring of `H`: each vertex receives a `b`-subset of `Fin a`, and
every edge sees every color. -/
def HasRainbowColoring (H : FiniteHypergraph V) (a b : ℕ) (color : V → Finset (Fin a)) : Prop :=
  (∀ v : V, #(color v) = b) ∧
    ∀ e ∈ H.val.edgeSet, ∀ i : Fin a, ∃ v ∈ e, i ∈ color v

/-- `(a : b)`-partite, also called `(a : b)`-rainbow colorable. -/
def IsPartite (H : FiniteHypergraph V) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ color : V → Finset (Fin a), H.HasRainbowColoring a b color

/-- **Conjecture 5.8**. A clutter with the packing property is `(α(I) ht(I) : ht(I))`-partite.

The height is encoded as the transversal number; the target uses the nonempty, non-unit domain
and the minor convention above. -/
theorem conjecture_coloring (H : FiniteHypergraph V)
    (hedges : H.val.edgeSet.Nonempty) (hproper : (∅ : Set V) ∉ H.val.edgeSet)
    (hpack : H.HasPackingProperty) :
    H.IsPartite (H.initialDegree * H.transversalNumber) H.transversalNumber := by
  sorry

end FiniteHypergraph

end Bodas2021Consequences

theorem Bodas2021Consequences.FiniteHypergraph.conjecture_coloring_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Bodas2021Consequences.FiniteHypergraph.conjecture_coloring.{u0} := by
  sorry
