title: Frog model wakeup time on the complete graph
problem_statement: In cartern2015frog.lean, prove either Cartern2015Frog.further_questions_ii or refute it by proving its logical negation Cartern2015Frog.further_questions_ii_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Frog model wakeup time on the complete graph

Authors: Nikki Cartern, Brittany Dygert, Matthew Junge, Stephen Lacina,
Collin Litterell, Austin Stromme, and Andrew You.
Origin: [University of Washington REU 2015](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~reu/papers/2015/).
Reference: N. Cartern, B. Dygert, M. Junge, S. Lacina, C. Litterell, A. Stromme, and A. You,
*Frog model wakeup time on the complete graph*, arXiv:1510.05995.
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped Topology ENNReal

namespace Cartern2015Frog

/-- The awake sets and frog positions over time, from the initial state (Section 2.1). Only awake
frogs move in a step, and frogs at their destinations wake afterwards. -/
noncomputable def frogStates {n : ℕ} (root : Fin n)
    (moves : List (Fin n → Fin n)) : List (Finset (Fin n) × (Fin n → Fin n)) :=
  moves.scanl (fun s move ↦
    let position := fun v ↦ if v ∈ s.1 then move v else s.2 v
    (s.1 ∪ s.1.image position, position)) ({root}, id)

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Further Question (ii)** (Section 1.2). For each fixed positive edge density, the frog model
on an Erdos-Renyi graph wakes every frog in logarithmic time with high probability. -/
theorem further_questions_ii (p : unitInterval) (hp : 0 < (p : ℝ)) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
        ∫⁻ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (n + 1)),
          ∑' moves : Fin ⌊C * Real.log (n + 1)⌋₊ → Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1),
            if ((frogStates 0 (List.ofFn moves)).getLastD ({0}, id)).1 = Finset.univ then
              ∏ t : Fin ⌊C * Real.log (n + 1)⌋₊, ∏ v : Fin (n + 1),
                let s := (frogStates 0 (List.ofFn moves)).getD t.val ({0}, id)
                let jump := if v ∈ s.1 then
                  if h : (G.neighborFinset (s.2 v)).Nonempty then
                    PMF.uniformOfFinset (G.neighborFinset (s.2 v)) h
                  else PMF.pure (s.2 v)
                else PMF.pure (s.2 v)
                jump (moves t v)
            else 0
          ∂(SimpleGraph.binomialRandom (Fin (n + 1)) p))
        atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Cartern2015Frog

theorem Cartern2015Frog.further_questions_ii_neg : ¬ type_of% @Cartern2015Frog.further_questions_ii := by
  sorry

title: Singular Curves and Metric Lines in 2-Jet Space
problem_statement: In catala2025singular.lean, prove either Catala2025Singular.conjecture_13_open_and_simply_connected or refute it by proving its logical negation Catala2025Singular.conjecture_13_open_and_simply_connected_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Singular Curves and Metric Lines in 2-Jet Space

Authors: Dani Catala and Miriam Vollmayr-Lee.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2025](https://lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/reu-su22/2025/Catala%2C%20Dani-Singular%20Curves%20and%20Metric%20Lines%20in%202-Jet%20Space.pdf).
Reference: D. Catala and M. Vollmayr-Lee, *Singular curves and metric lines in 2-jet space*,
University of Michigan REU report (2025).
-/

open scoped Real Topology
open Set MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

namespace Catala2025Singular

/-- The domain `X̃`: positive parameters with a nondegenerate positive hill interval
(Section 3.3). -/
def periodDomain (b : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ 0 < 2 * p.1 - b ^ 2 * p.2 ^ 2}

/-- The two-coordinate period map (Definition 11). The positive endpoint of the hill interval is
written as the positive root of `C - B * x - A * x ^ 2`. -/
def tildeTheta (a b : ℝ) (p : periodDomain b) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  let q : ℝ × ℝ := p.1
  let P := fun x : ℝ ↦ (1 - x ^ 2, b * x + a * x ^ 2)
  let G := fun x : ℝ ↦ (1 - q.1 * x ^ 2, q.2 * (b * x + a * x ^ 2))
  let A := q.1 ^ 2 + q.2 ^ 2 * a ^ 2
  let B := 2 * a * b * q.2 ^ 2
  let C := 2 * q.1 - b ^ 2 * q.2 ^ 2
  let x₁ := (-B + √(B ^ 2 + 4 * A * C)) / (2 * A)
  (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..x₁,
      (1 - (P x).1) * (G x).1 /
        √(1 - ((G x).1 ^ 2 + (G x).2 ^ 2)),
   ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..x₁,
      (P x).2 * (G x).2 /
        √(1 - ((G x).1 ^ 2 + (G x).2 ^ 2)))

/-- **Conjecture 13**. The image of the period map is open and simply connected. -/
theorem conjecture_13_open_and_simply_connected
    (a b : ℝ) (hparams : a ≠ 0 ∨ b ≠ 0) (hb : 0 < 2 - b ^ 2) :
    IsOpen (Set.range (tildeTheta a b)) ∧
      SimplyConnectedSpace (Set.range (tildeTheta a b)) := by
  sorry

end Catala2025Singular

theorem Catala2025Singular.conjecture_13_open_and_simply_connected_neg : ¬ type_of% @Catala2025Singular.conjecture_13_open_and_simply_connected := by
  sorry

title: The cycle structure of a Markoff automorphism over finite fields
problem_statement: In cerbu2020cycle.lean, prove either Cerbu2020Cycle.longest_orbit_growth or refute it by proving its logical negation Cerbu2020Cycle.longest_orbit_growth_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The cycle structure of a Markoff automorphism over finite fields

Authors: Alois Cerbu, Elijah Gunther, Michael Magee, and Luke Peilen.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: A. Cerbu, E. Gunther, M. Magee, and L. Peilen, *The cycle structure of a Markoff
automorphism over finite fields*, preprint (2018); arXiv:1610.07077v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Cerbu2020Cycle

open scoped Topology

/-- Affine three-space over `ZMod p`. -/
abbrev MarkoffPoint (p : ℕ) := Fin 3 → ZMod p

/-- The Markoff surface `X_{-2}`, in the normalization of equation (1.1). -/
def markoffSet (p : ℕ) : Set (MarkoffPoint p) :=
  {P | P 0 ^ 2 + P 1 ^ 2 + P 2 ^ 2 = P 0 * P 1 * P 2}

/-- The punctured surface `X^*_{-2}`, with the origin removed. -/
def puncturedMarkoffSet (p : ℕ) : Set (MarkoffPoint p) :=
  markoffSet p \ {0}

open scoped Classical in
instance (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : Fintype (puncturedMarkoffSet p) :=
  Fintype.ofFinite _

/-- The even sign change `n_i` keeps coordinate `i` and negates the other two. -/
def signChange (p : ℕ) (i : Fin 3) : Equiv.Perm (puncturedMarkoffSet p) :=
  let e : Equiv.Perm (MarkoffPoint p) :=
    { toFun := fun P j ↦ if j = i then P j else -P j
      invFun := fun P j ↦ if j = i then P j else -P j
      left_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        by_cases h : j = i <;> simp [h]
      right_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        by_cases h : j = i <;> simp [h] }
  e.subtypeEquiv (p := fun P ↦ P ∈ puncturedMarkoffSet p) fun P ↦ by
    change (P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ P ≠ 0) ↔ (e P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ e P ≠ 0)
    have hs : P ∈ markoffSet p ↔ e P ∈ markoffSet p := by
      fin_cases i <;> simp [e, markoffSet]
    have hz : e 0 = 0 := by
      funext j
      simp [e]
    exact and_congr hs (not_congr (by rw [← e.injective.eq_iff, hz]))

/-- The group `N` generated by the three even sign changes. -/
def N (p : ℕ) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (puncturedMarkoffSet p)) :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range (signChange p))

/-- The orbit space `Y_{-2}(F_p) = X^*_{-2}(F_p) / N`. -/
abbrev MarkoffOrbit (p : ℕ) :=
  Quotient (MulAction.orbitRel (N p) (puncturedMarkoffSet p))

open scoped Classical in
instance (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : Fintype (MarkoffOrbit p) :=
  Quotient.fintype _

/-- The map `U(x,y,z) = (z,y,zy-x)` from Lemma 3.3 on the punctured surface. -/
def UOnPunctured (p : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (puncturedMarkoffSet p) :=
  let e : Equiv.Perm (MarkoffPoint p) :=
    { toFun := fun P ↦ ![P 2, P 1, P 2 * P 1 - P 0]
      invFun := fun P ↦ ![P 0 * P 1 - P 2, P 1, P 0]
      left_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        fin_cases j <;> simp
      right_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        fin_cases j <;> simp }
  e.subtypeEquiv (p := fun P ↦ P ∈ puncturedMarkoffSet p) fun P ↦ by
    change (P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ P ≠ 0) ↔ (e P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ e P ≠ 0)
    have hs : P ∈ markoffSet p ↔ e P ∈ markoffSet p := by
      constructor <;> intro h <;> simp [markoffSet, e] at h ⊢ <;>
        linear_combination h
    have hz : e 0 = 0 := by
      funext j
      fin_cases j <;> simp [e]
    exact and_congr hs (not_congr (by rw [← e.injective.eq_iff, hz]))

/-- The map `V(x,y,z) = (x,z,xz-y)` from Lemma 3.3 on the punctured surface. -/
def VOnPunctured (p : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (puncturedMarkoffSet p) :=
  let e : Equiv.Perm (MarkoffPoint p) :=
    { toFun := fun P ↦ ![P 0, P 2, P 0 * P 2 - P 1]
      invFun := fun P ↦ ![P 0, P 0 * P 1 - P 2, P 1]
      left_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        fin_cases j <;> simp
      right_inv := by
        intro P
        funext j
        fin_cases j <;> simp }
  e.subtypeEquiv (p := fun P ↦ P ∈ puncturedMarkoffSet p) fun P ↦ by
    change (P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ P ≠ 0) ↔ (e P ∈ markoffSet p ∧ e P ≠ 0)
    have hs : P ∈ markoffSet p ↔ e P ∈ markoffSet p := by
      constructor <;> intro h <;> simp [markoffSet, e] at h ⊢ <;>
        linear_combination h
    have hz : e 0 = 0 := by
      funext j
      fin_cases j <;> simp [e]
    exact and_congr hs (not_congr (by rw [← e.injective.eq_iff, hz]))

/-- The map `U`, descended to the even-sign quotient. -/
def U (p : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (MarkoffOrbit p) :=
  have hn : UOnPunctured p ∈ Subgroup.normalizer (N p : Set _) := by
    apply Subgroup.normalizer_le_normalizer_closure
    apply Subgroup.mem_normalizer_fintype
    rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨Equiv.swap 0 2 i, ?_⟩
    apply Equiv.ext
    intro P
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [UOnPunctured, signChange, Equiv.swap_apply_def] <;> ring
  Quotient.congr (UOnPunctured p) fun P Q ↦ by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      refine ⟨⟨UOnPunctured p * s.val * (UOnPunctured p)⁻¹,
        (Subgroup.mem_normalizer_iff.mp hn s.val).mp s.property⟩, ?_⟩
      change (UOnPunctured p * s.val * (UOnPunctured p)⁻¹) (UOnPunctured p Q) =
        UOnPunctured p P
      change s.val Q = P at hs
      simpa using congrArg (UOnPunctured p) hs
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      refine ⟨⟨(UOnPunctured p)⁻¹ * s.val * UOnPunctured p,
        (Subgroup.mem_normalizer_iff''.mp hn s.val).mp s.property⟩, ?_⟩
      change (UOnPunctured p).symm (s.val (UOnPunctured p Q)) = P
      change s.val (UOnPunctured p Q) = UOnPunctured p P at hs
      rw [hs, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]

/-- The map `V`, descended to the even-sign quotient. -/
def V (p : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (MarkoffOrbit p) :=
  have hn : VOnPunctured p ∈ Subgroup.normalizer (N p : Set _) := by
    apply Subgroup.normalizer_le_normalizer_closure
    apply Subgroup.mem_normalizer_fintype
    rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨Equiv.swap 1 2 i, ?_⟩
    apply Equiv.ext
    intro P
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [VOnPunctured, signChange, Equiv.swap_apply_def] <;> ring
  Quotient.congr (VOnPunctured p) fun P Q ↦ by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      refine ⟨⟨VOnPunctured p * s.val * (VOnPunctured p)⁻¹,
        (Subgroup.mem_normalizer_iff.mp hn s.val).mp s.property⟩, ?_⟩
      change (VOnPunctured p * s.val * (VOnPunctured p)⁻¹) (VOnPunctured p Q) =
        VOnPunctured p P
      change s.val Q = P at hs
      simpa using congrArg (VOnPunctured p) hs
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      refine ⟨⟨(VOnPunctured p)⁻¹ * s.val * VOnPunctured p,
        (Subgroup.mem_normalizer_iff''.mp hn s.val).mp s.property⟩, ?_⟩
      change (VOnPunctured p).symm (s.val (VOnPunctured p Q)) = P
      change s.val (VOnPunctured p Q) = VOnPunctured p P at hs
      rw [hs, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]

/-- The action of a positive reduced `UV`-word on the sign-orbit quotient. -/
def wordAction (p : ℕ) (w : List (PNat × PNat)) :
    Equiv.Perm (MarkoffOrbit p) :=
  w.foldl (fun acc nm ↦ (acc.trans (U p ^ (nm.1 : ℕ))).trans
    (V p ^ (nm.2 : ℕ))) (Equiv.refl _)

/-- The longest orbit length `L(g; p)`, with value zero for an empty quotient. -/
noncomputable def longestOrbit (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] (w : List (PNat × PNat)) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun x : MarkoffOrbit p ↦ Function.minimalPeriod (wordAction p w) x

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Conjecture 1.10, p. 6). For every fixed hyperbolic class,
the logarithmic longest-orbit exponent along the primes tends to one if the class is ambiguous
and to two otherwise.

Classes are positive reduced `UV`-words (Lemma 1.6), and ambiguity is cyclic reversal of the
expanded word (Definition 1.7, Proposition 1.9). The normalization follows (1.1), despite the
missing `-2` on p. 12, and written `U` acts before `V`. -/
theorem longest_orbit_growth (w : List (PNat × PNat)) (hw : w ≠ []) :
    let letters := w.flatMap fun nm ↦
      List.replicate (nm.1 : ℕ) false ++ List.replicate (nm.2 : ℕ) true
    Filter.Tendsto (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦
      letI : NeZero (p : ℕ) := ⟨p.property.ne_zero⟩
      Real.log (longestOrbit (p : ℕ) w : ℝ) / Real.log (p : ℕ))
      (Filter.comap (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ (p : ℕ)) Filter.atTop)
      (𝓝 (if List.IsRotated letters.reverse letters then (1 : ℝ) else 2)) := by
  sorry

end Cerbu2020Cycle

  sorry

title: On structural decompositions of finite frames
problem_statement: In chan2016structural.lean, prove either Chan2016Structural.conjecture_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Chan2016Structural.conjecture_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On structural decompositions of finite frames

Authors: Alice Z.-Y. Chan, Martin S. Copenhaver, Sivaram K. Narayan, Logan Stokols,
and Allison Theobold.
Origin: [Central Michigan University REU 2013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6138).
Reference: A. Z.-Y. Chan, M. S. Copenhaver, S. K. Narayan, L. Stokols, and A. Theobold, *On
structural decompositions of finite frames*, Adv. Comput. Math. **42** (2016), 721-756;
doi:10.1007/s10444-015-9440-1.
-/

namespace Chan2016Structural

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

open scoped Classical in
/-- The factor poset: the indexed tight subframes, together with the empty set (Definition 7). -/
noncomputable def factorPoset {n k : ℕ} (F : Fin k → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    Finset (Finset (Fin k)) :=
  {s | s = ∅ ∨
    ∃ A > (0 : ℝ), ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
      ∑ i ∈ s, ⟪x, F i⟫ ^ 2 = A * ‖x‖ ^ 2}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The scalability poset: the subframes admitting a nonnegative Parseval scaling, with the empty
set included by convention (Definitions 13 and 16). -/
noncomputable def scalabilityPoset {n k : ℕ} (F : Fin k → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    Finset (Finset (Fin k)) :=
  {s | s = ∅ ∨
    ∃ w : Fin k → ℝ, (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w i) ∧
      ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ∑ i ∈ s, w i * ⟪x, F i⟫ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2}

/-- **Conjecture 3**. Unit-norm frames with the same scalability poset admit a
strict scaling reproducing the factor poset of either frame that is tight. -/
theorem conjecture_3 {n k : ℕ} (F G : Fin k → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (hF : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range F) = ⊤)
    (hFunit : ∀ i, ‖F i‖ = 1) (hGunit : ∀ i, ‖G i‖ = 1)
    (hG : ∃ A > (0 : ℝ), ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
      ∑ i, ⟪x, G i⟫ ^ 2 = A * ‖x‖ ^ 2)
    (hsame : scalabilityPoset F = scalabilityPoset G) :
    ∃ w : Fin k → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < w i) ∧
      (∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ∑ i, w i * ⟪x, F i⟫ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2) ∧
      factorPoset (fun i ↦ √(w i) • F i) = factorPoset G := by
  sorry

end Chan2016Structural

theorem Chan2016Structural.conjecture_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Chan2016Structural.conjecture_3 := by
  sorry

title: Towards the Gaussianity of Random Zeckendorf Games
problem_statement: In cheigh2025towards.lean, prove either Cheigh2025Towards.conjecture_6_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Cheigh2025Towards.conjecture_6_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Towards the Gaussianity of Random Zeckendorf Games

Authors: Justin Cheigh, Guilherme Zeus Dantas e Moura, Ryan Jeong, Jacob Lehmann
Duke, Wyatt Milgrim, Steven J. Miller, and Prakod Ngamlamai.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2022](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.11038v1#page=28).
Reference: J. Cheigh, G. Z. Dantas e Moura, R. Jeong, J. Lehmann Duke, W. Milgrim, S. J. Miller,
and P. Ngamlamai, *Towards the Gaussianity of random Zeckendorf games*, preprint (2022);
arXiv:2210.11038v1.
-/

namespace Cheigh2025Towards

open scoped Topology
open Finset

/-- A state of the Bergman game: a finitely supported integer-indexed chip tape (Baily et al.,
Definition 1.1). -/
abbrev State := ℤ →₀ ℕ

/-- All legal next states: combine chips at `i, i + 1` into `i + 2`, or split two
chips at `i` into `i - 2, i + 1` (Baily et al., Definition 1.1). -/
noncomputable def successors (s : State) : Finset State :=
  s.support.biUnion fun i ↦
    (if 0 < s (i + 1) then
      {s - Finsupp.single i 1 - Finsupp.single (i + 1) 1 +
        Finsupp.single (i + 2) 1}
    else {} : Finset State) ∪
    (if 2 ≤ s i then
      {s - Finsupp.single i 2 + Finsupp.single (i - 2) 1 +
        Finsupp.single (i + 1) 1}
    else {})

/-- A complete Bergman game from `N` chips at index zero, as its ordered states from the initial
to the terminal state (Baily et al., Definition 1.1; Section 1.2). -/
structure Game (N : ℕ) where
  /-- The ordered list of chip configurations visited by the game. -/
  states : List State
  starts : states.head? = some (Finsupp.single 0 N)
  legal : states.IsChain (fun s t ↦ t ∈ successors s)
  terminal : ∀ s, states.getLast? = some s → successors s = {}

/-- **Conjecture 6.1**. Each player's winning probability tends to one half for random Bergman
games, both when complete games are uniform and when available moves are uniform.

An odd number of moves means Player 1 wins, and an even number means Player 2 wins. -/
theorem conjecture_6_1 :
    let mass : Bool → (N : ℕ) → Game N → ℝ := fun byMove N g ↦
      if byMove then
        (g.states.dropLast.map (fun s ↦ 1 / (#(successors s) : ℝ))).prod
      else 1 / (Nat.card (Game N) : ℝ)
    ∀ (byMove : Bool) (parity : Fin 2),
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ ↦ ∑' g : Game N,
          if (g.states.length - 1) % 2 = parity.val then mass byMove N g else 0)
        Filter.atTop (𝓝 (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Cheigh2025Towards

theorem Cheigh2025Towards.conjecture_6_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Cheigh2025Towards.conjecture_6_1 := by
  sorry

title: Permutation Invariant Parking Assortments
problem_statement: In chen2023permutation.lean, prove either Chen2023Permutation.conjecture_6_1_four_car_boolean_characterization or refute it by proving its logical negation Chen2023Permutation.conjecture_6_1_four_car_boolean_characterization_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Permutation Invariant Parking Assortments

Authors: Douglas M. Chen, Pamela E. Harris, J. Carlos Martinez Mori, Eric J. Pabon-Cancel,
and Gabriel Sargent.
Origin: [Summer@ICERM 2022](https://icerm.brown.edu/summerug/2022/).
Reference: D. M. Chen, P. E. Harris, J. C. Martinez Mori, E. J. Pabon-Cancel, and G. Sargent,
*Permutation invariant parking assortments*, Enumer. Combin. Appl. **4**:1 (2024), Article #S2R4;
doi:10.54550/ECA2024V4S1R4.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Chen2023Permutation

open scoped Classical in
/-- The result of parking a single arriving car of length `len` with preference `pref`. -/
def parkCar (M len pref : ℕ) (occupied : Finset ℕ) : Option (Finset ℕ) :=
  if h : ∃ start ≥ 1, pref ≤ start ∧ start + len - 1 ≤ M ∧
      ∀ t, t < len → start + t ∉ occupied then
    some (occupied ∪ Finset.Ico (Nat.find h) (Nat.find h + len))
  else
    none

/-- The final occupied set, if the cars park successfully in their given order. -/
def parkingOutcome {n : ℕ} (y x : Fin n → ℕ) : Option (Finset ℕ) :=
  (List.finRange n).foldl
    (fun state i ↦ state.bind fun occupied ↦ parkCar (∑ j, y j) (y i) (x i) occupied)
    (some ∅)

/-- `x ∈ PA_n(y)`: all cars park under the preference list `x` for car lengths `y`. -/
def ParkingAssortment {n : ℕ} (y x : Fin n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, 1 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ ∑ j, y j) ∧
    ∃ occupied, parkingOutcome y x = some occupied

/-- `x ∈ PA_n^inv(y)`: every rearrangement of the preference list is a parking
assortment for the same ordered list of car lengths. -/
def InvariantParkingAssortment {n : ℕ} (y x : Fin n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ParkingAssortment y (x ∘ σ)

/-- Minimal invariance: the all-ones preference list is the only invariant parking assortment
for `y`. -/
def MinimallyInvariant {n : ℕ} (y : Fin n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℕ, InvariantParkingAssortment y x ↔ x = fun _ ↦ 1

/-- **Conjecture 6.1**. For four cars, minimal invariance is equivalent to the displayed Boolean
formula. -/
theorem conjecture_6_1_four_car_boolean_characterization
    (y : Fin 4 → ℕ) (hy : ∀ i, 0 < y i) :
    MinimallyInvariant y ↔
      (y 0 < y 1) ∧ (y 0 < y 2) ∧ (y 0 < y 3) ∧
      (y 1 ≠ y 0 + y 2) ∧ (y 1 ≠ y 0 + y 2 + y 3) ∧
      ((y 1 < y 0 + y 2) ∨ (y 2 ≠ y 0 + y 3)) ∧
      ((y 0 + y 2 < y 1) ∨
        ((y 1 ≠ y 0 + y 3) ∧ ((y 1 < y 2) ∨ (y 2 ≠ y 0 + y 3)))) := by
  sorry

end Chen2023Permutation

theorem Chen2023Permutation.conjecture_6_1_four_car_boolean_characterization_neg : ¬ type_of% @Chen2023Permutation.conjecture_6_1_four_car_boolean_characterization := by
  sorry

title: Ribbonlength upper bounds for small crossing knots and links
problem_statement: In chen2025ribbonlength.lean, prove either Chen2025Ribbonlength.conjecture_12 or refute it by proving its logical negation Chen2025Ribbonlength.conjecture_12_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Ribbonlength upper bounds for small crossing knots and links

Authors: Zhicheng (Henry) Chen, Elizabeth Denne, Kyle Patterson, and Timi Patterson.
Origin: [Washington and Lee University Summer Research Scholars
2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16190).
Reference: Z. Chen, E. Denne, K. Patterson, and T. Patterson, *Ribbonlength upper bounds for
small crossing knots and links*, preprint (2025); arXiv:2510.16190v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Chen2025Ribbonlength

/-- A fundamental region of length `l` and width `w` in the unfolded strip, cut along oblique
transversals of slope `a`. -/
abbrev PaperDomain (l w a : ℝ) (mobius : Bool) :=
  {z : ℂ // a * z.im ≤ z.re ∧
    z.re ≤ l + (if mobius then -a else a) * z.im ∧
    z.im ∈ Set.Icc (-w / 2) (w / 2)}

/-- A folded paper strip: ordered affine cuts and Euclidean isometries on the intervening panels
encoding its flat folded map. The seam may be any fold, and cuts may subdivide a panel without
creating a new fold. -/
structure PaperStrip where
  /-- The length of the fundamental region of the strip. -/
  length : ℝ
  /-- The width of the strip. -/
  width : ℝ
  length_pos : 0 < length
  width_pos : 0 < width
  /-- Whether the end identification produces a Mobius ribbon. -/
  mobius : Bool
  /-- The slope of the seam cut at which the strip ends are identified. -/
  seamSlope : ℝ
  /-- The number of panels; consecutive cuts bound one panel. -/
  panels : ℕ
  panels_pos : 0 < panels
  /-- The ordered affine cuts, each the line `x = a + b * y` given by `(a, b)`. -/
  cuts : Fin (panels + 1) → ℝ × ℝ
  first_cut : cuts 0 = (0, seamSlope)
  last_cut : cuts (Fin.last panels) = (length, if mobius then -seamSlope else seamSlope)
  ordered_cuts : ∀ i : Fin panels, ∀ y : ℝ,
    y ∈ Set.Icc (-width / 2) (width / 2) →
    (cuts i.castSucc).1 + (cuts i.castSucc).2 * y <
      (cuts i.succ).1 + (cuts i.succ).2 * y
  /-- The Euclidean isometry by which each panel is placed in the plane. -/
  panel : Fin panels → (ℂ ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] ℂ)
  /-- The flat folded map of the fundamental region into the plane. -/
  flatMap : C(PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius, ℂ)
  on_panel : ∀ i : Fin panels, ∀ z : PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius,
    (cuts i.castSucc).1 + (cuts i.castSucc).2 * z.val.im ≤ z.val.re →
    z.val.re ≤ (cuts i.succ).1 + (cuts i.succ).2 * z.val.im →
    flatMap z = panel i z.val
  end_match : ∀ x y : PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius,
    x.val.re = seamSlope * x.val.im →
    y.val.re = length + (if mobius then -seamSlope else seamSlope) * y.val.im →
    x.val.im = (if mobius then -y.val.im else y.val.im) → flatMap x = flatMap y

/-- The end gluing of the intrinsic annulus or Mobius strip. -/
def PaperStrip.Seam (R : PaperStrip)
    (x y : PaperDomain R.length R.width R.seamSlope R.mobius) : Prop :=
  x.val.re = R.seamSlope * x.val.im ∧
    y.val.re = R.length + (if R.mobius then -R.seamSlope else R.seamSlope) * y.val.im ∧
    x.val.im = (if R.mobius then -y.val.im else y.val.im)

/-- The topological ribbon surface. -/
abbrev PaperStrip.Surface (R : PaperStrip) := Quot R.Seam

/-- The continuous folded map on the glued paper surface. -/
def PaperStrip.surfaceMap (R : PaperStrip) : C(R.Surface, ℂ) where
  toFun := Quot.lift R.flatMap
    (fun x y h ↦ R.end_match x y h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2)
  continuous_toFun := continuous_quot_lift _ R.flatMap.continuous

/-- Intrinsic centerline points, parametrized proportionally to paper length. -/
def PaperStrip.corePoint (R : PaperStrip) (t : unitInterval) : R.Surface :=
  Quot.mk R.Seam ⟨⟨R.length * (t : ℝ), 0⟩, by
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [mul_zero] using mul_nonneg (le_of_lt R.length_pos) t.property.1
    · simp only [mul_zero, add_zero]
      nlinarith [t.property.2, R.length_pos]
    · linarith [R.width_pos]
    · linarith [R.width_pos]⟩

/-- Continuous, antisymmetric, transitive over-under information on distinct coincident points
(Denne--Kamp--Terry--Zhu, Definition 2.2). `true` means the first sheet is above the second. -/
structure CrossingInformation {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] (f : X → ℂ) where
  /-- Whether the first of two distinct coincident points lies above the second. -/
  isOver : {p : X × X // p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ f p.1 = f p.2} → Bool
  continuous_isOver : Continuous isOver
  reversed : ∀ p,
    isOver ⟨(p.val.2, p.val.1), Ne.symm p.property.1, p.property.2.symm⟩ = !(isOver p)
  transitive : ∀ x y z (hxy : x ≠ y) (hyz : y ≠ z) (hxz : x ≠ z)
    (fxy : f x = f y) (fyz : f y = f z),
    isOver ⟨(x, y), hxy, fxy⟩ = true → isOver ⟨(y, z), hyz, fyz⟩ = true →
    isOver ⟨(x, z), hxz, fxy.trans fyz⟩ = true

/-- An allowed folded ribbon with continuous sheet order on its surface and a compatible closed
spatial lift of its core. Regular crossings, framing, stick number and orientability are not
fixed. -/
structure FoldedRibbon where
  /-- The underlying folded paper strip. -/
  strip : PaperStrip
  /-- The over-under information of the folded strip. -/
  crossing : CrossingInformation strip.surfaceMap
  /-- The height function along the core giving its closed spatial lift. -/
  height : C(unitInterval, ℝ)
  height_closed : height 0 = height 1
  height_order : ∀ s t : unitInterval,
    ∀ (hne : strip.corePoint s ≠ strip.corePoint t)
      (heq : strip.surfaceMap (strip.corePoint s) =
        strip.surfaceMap (strip.corePoint t)),
    crossing.isOver ⟨(strip.corePoint s, strip.corePoint t), hne, heq⟩ = true ↔
      height t < height s

/-- The spatial knot of a ribbon: the lift of its folded core by the height function, which is
compatible with the crossing information. -/
def FoldedRibbon.realization (R : FoldedRibbon) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :=
  Set.range (fun t : unitInterval ↦ WithLp.toLp 2
    ![(R.strip.surfaceMap (R.strip.corePoint t)).re,
      (R.strip.surfaceMap (R.strip.corePoint t)).im, R.height t])

/-- The figure-eight knot `T_2`, in its standard trigonometric realization. -/
def figureEightKnot : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :=
  Set.range (fun t : ℝ ↦ WithLp.toLp 2
    ![(2 + Real.cos (2 * t)) * Real.cos (3 * t),
      (2 + Real.cos (2 * t)) * Real.sin (3 * t), Real.sin (4 * t)])

/-- **Conjecture 12**. The infimal folded ribbonlength of the figure-eight knot, over all allowed
folded ribbons of this knot type, is eight.

The infimum is stated as a greatest lower bound; no minimizing ribbon or fixed framing is
assumed. -/
theorem conjecture_12 :
    IsGLB {r : ℝ | ∃ R : FoldedRibbon,
      (∃ H : unitInterval →
          (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
        Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
        Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦
          (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
        H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ∧
        H 1 '' figureEightKnot = R.realization) ∧ r = R.strip.length / R.strip.width} 8 := by
  sorry

end Chen2025Ribbonlength

theorem Chen2025Ribbonlength.conjecture_12_neg : ¬ type_of% @Chen2025Ribbonlength.conjecture_12 := by
  sorry

title: Clones of Borel Boolean Functions
problem_statement: In chen2026clones.lean, prove either Chen2026Clones.conjecture_1_5 or refute it by proving its logical negation Chen2026Clones.conjecture_1_5_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Clones of Borel Boolean Functions

Authors: Ruiyuan Chen and Ilir Ziba.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2023](https://prod.lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/reu-su22/reu-2023/Ziba,%20Ilir_REU_2023.pdf).
Reference: R. Chen and I. Ziba, *Clones of Borel Boolean functions*, revised author manuscript
(2026), 59 pp.; arXiv:2407.06719; https://rynchn.github.io/math/borelclone.pdf.
-/

namespace Chen2026Clones

/-- Arity indices: `none` is countably infinite arity and `some k` is arity `k + 1`
(Conventions 2.3 and 2.23). Nullary operations are excluded. -/
def ArityIndex : Option ℕ → Type
  | none => ℕ
  | some k => Fin (k + 1)

/-- A Borel clone: a family of Borel Boolean operations containing all projections and closed
under arity-compatible substitution (Definitions 2.5 and 4.1). -/
structure BorelClone where
  /-- The operations of each arity belonging to the clone. -/
  operations : (a : Option ℕ) → Set ((ArityIndex a → Bool) → Bool)
  measurable_mem : ∀ a f, f ∈ operations a → Measurable f
  projection_mem : ∀ a (i : ArityIndex a), (fun x ↦ x i) ∈ operations a
  substitution_mem : ∀ (a b : Option ℕ)
    (g : (ArityIndex a → Bool) → Bool)
    (fs : ArityIndex a → (ArityIndex b → Bool) → Bool),
    g ∈ operations a → (∀ i, fs i ∈ operations b) →
      (fun x ↦ g (fun i ↦ fs i x)) ∈ operations b

/-- **Conjecture 1.5** (revised author manuscript). At least continuum many distinct Borel clones
have as finitary part exactly the finite operations preserving binary meet, zero and one. -/
theorem conjecture_1_5 :
    Cardinal.continuum ≤ Cardinal.mk {C : BorelClone //
      ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ f : (Fin (k + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
        f ∈ C.operations (some k) ↔
          ∃ h : InfTopHom (Fin (k + 1) → Bool) Bool,
            ⇑h = f ∧ h (fun _ ↦ false) = false} := by
  sorry

end Chen2026Clones

theorem Chen2026Clones.conjecture_1_5_neg : ¬ type_of% @Chen2026Clones.conjecture_1_5 := by
  sorry

title: Arborescences of covering graphs
problem_statement: In chepuri2022arborescences.lean, prove either Chepuri2022Arborescences.conjecture_1_7 or refute it by proving its logical negation Chepuri2022Arborescences.conjecture_1_7_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Arborescences of covering graphs

Authors: Sunita Chepuri, CJ Dowd, Andrew Hardt, Gregory Michel,
Sylvester W. Zhang, and Valerie Zhang.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2019](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: S. Chepuri, C. Dowd, A. Hardt, G. Michel, S. W. Zhang, and V. Zhang, *Arborescences of
covering graphs*, Algebr. Comb. **5** (2022), no. 2, 319-346; doi:10.5802/alco.212.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Chepuri2022Arborescences

open scoped Classical in
/-- The weighted sum of spanning arborescences directed toward the root (Definition 2.1),
computed as an outgoing Laplacian minor (Definition 2.3, Theorem 2.4). -/
def arborescenceSum {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [Quiver V]
    [∀ u v : V, Fintype (u ⟶ v)] {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (wt : Quiver.Labelling V R) (r : V) : R :=
  let L : Matrix V V R := fun u v ↦
    (if u = v then ∑ w : V, ∑ e : u ⟶ w, wt e else 0) -
      ∑ e : u ⟶ v, wt e
  (L.submatrix (fun u : {u : V // u ≠ r} ↦ u.val)
    (fun v : {v : V // v ≠ r} ↦ v.val)).det

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 1.7**. The arborescence quotient has nonnegative integer coefficients wherever
it is defined, i.e. when the chosen base-root arborescence polynomial is nonzero.

This is the ordinary-quotient reading supported by Corollary 1.6; an unguarded determinant
extension is a possible alternative. The guard concerns the formal polynomial, not its numerical
specializations, and covers with zero numerator remain allowed. -/
theorem conjecture_1_7 {V U : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype U]
    [Quiver V] [Quiver U] [∀ v w : V, Fintype (v ⟶ w)]
    [∀ u w : U, Fintype (u ⟶ w)] (π : U ⥤q V) (hπ : π.IsCovering)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)
    (hdegree : ∀ v : V, Fintype.card {u : U // π.obj u = v} = k) (r : U)
    (hbase : arborescenceSum
      (fun {v w} e ↦ (MvPolynomial.X ⟨v, w, e⟩ : MvPolynomial (Quiver.Total V) ℤ))
      (π.obj r) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Quiver.Total V) ℤ,
      (∀ d, 0 ≤ P.coeff d) ∧
      arborescenceSum (fun {u w} e ↦ MvPolynomial.X ⟨π.obj u, π.obj w, π.map e⟩) r =
        arborescenceSum (fun {v w} e ↦ MvPolynomial.X ⟨v, w, e⟩) (π.obj r) * P := by
  sorry

end Chepuri2022Arborescences

title: Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets
problem_statement: In chiang2024bender.lean, prove either Chiang2024Bender.conjecture_3_24 or refute it by proving its logical negation Chiang2024Bender.conjecture_3_24_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets

Authors: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall,
Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki, and Janabel Xia.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2022](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: J. H.-H. Chiang, A. T. N. Hoang, M. Kendall, R. Lynch, S. Nguyen, B. Przybocki, and
J. Xia, *Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets*, Discrete Math. **347** (2024),
no. 9, 114068; arXiv:2302.12425v2.
-/

namespace Chiang2024Bender

/-- The double-tailed diamond `d_k(1)`: two chains of `k - 2` elements separated by two
incomparable elements ([PS19], Section 2). -/
abbrev DoubleTailedDiamond (k : ℕ) : Type :=
  Lex (Lex (Fin (k - 2) ⊕ (PUnit ⊕ PUnit)) ⊕ Fin (k - 2))

/-- The `d_k`-minus shape: `d_k(1)` without its greatest element ([PS19], Section 6). -/
abbrev DiamondMinus (k : ℕ) := {x : DoubleTailedDiamond k // ¬IsMax x}

/-- A convex embedded `d_k`-minus set ([PS19], Section 6). -/
def IsDiamondMinusSet {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] (k : ℕ) (s : Set P) : Prop :=
  s.OrdConnected ∧ Nonempty (DiamondMinus k ≃o s)

/-- The three d-complete axioms ([PS19], Sections 6 and 9), in the root-at-minimum orientation
of Section 3.3. -/
def IsDComplete (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] : Prop :=
  ∀ k ≥ 3,
    (∀ s : Set Pᵒᵈ, IsDiamondMinusSet k s →
      ∃ z : Pᵒᵈ, z ∉ s ∧
        ∃ a : Pᵒᵈ, s ∪ {z} = Set.Icc a z ∧
          Nonempty (DoubleTailedDiamond k ≃o {x : Pᵒᵈ // x ∈ s ∪ {z}})) ∧
    (∀ a b : Pᵒᵈ,
      Nonempty (DoubleTailedDiamond k ≃o Set.Icc a b) →
        ∀ x : Pᵒᵈ, x ⋖ b → x ∈ Set.Icc a b) ∧
    ∀ s t : Set Pᵒᵈ,
      IsDiamondMinusSet k s → IsDiamondMinusSet k t →
        ∀ a b : Pᵒᵈ, IsLeast s a → IsLeast t b →
          s \ {a} = t \ {b} → s = t

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Bender-Knuth involution `t_i`: swap adjacent labels exactly when their elements are
incomparable (Definition 2.5). Labels are zero-based while `i` is one-based, and outside the
source range the map is the identity. -/
noncomputable def bk {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] {n : ℕ}
    (i : ℕ) (L : P ≃ Fin n) : P ≃ Fin n :=
  if h : 0 < i ∧ i < n then
    let a : Fin n := { val := i - 1, isLt := lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le i 1) h.2 }
    let b : Fin n := { val := i, isLt := h.2 }
    if ¬L.symm a ≤ L.symm b ∧ ¬L.symm b ≤ L.symm a then
      L.trans (Equiv.swap a b)
    else L
  else L

/-- Partial promotion `∂_i = t_i ⋯ t_1`, acting right first (Section 2.2). -/
noncomputable def promotion {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] {n : ℕ}
    (i : ℕ) (L : P ≃ Fin n) : P ≃ Fin n :=
  (List.range i).foldl (fun M j ↦ bk (j + 1) M) L

/-- Partial evacuation `q_i = ∂_0 ∂_1 ⋯ ∂_i` (Section 2.2). -/
noncomputable def evacuation {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] {n : ℕ}
    (i : ℕ) (L : P ≃ Fin n) : P ≃ Fin n :=
  (List.range (i + 1)).foldr (fun j M ↦ promotion j M) L

/-- **Conjecture 3.24**. All cactus relations hold on the linear extensions of every finite
d-complete poset, in the root-at-minimum convention. -/
theorem conjecture_3_24 {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] [Fintype P]
    (hP : IsDComplete P) (i j k : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i)
    (hij : i + 1 < j) (hjk : j < k) (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card P)
    (L : P ≃ Fin (Fintype.card P)) (hL : StrictMono L) :
    let q := fun M : P ≃ Fin (Fintype.card P) ↦
      evacuation (k - 1) (evacuation (k - j) (evacuation (k - 1) M))
    bk i (q (bk i (q L))) = L := by
  sorry

end Chiang2024Bender

theorem Chiang2024Bender.conjecture_3_24_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Chiang2024Bender.conjecture_3_24.{u0} := by
  sorry

/-!
# Isoperimetric Pentagonal Tilings

Authors: Ping Ngai Chung, Miguel A. Fernandez, Yifei Li, Michael Mara, Frank Morgan,
Isamar Rosa Plata, Niralee Shah, Luis Sordo Vieira, and Elena Wikner.
Origin: Williams College SMALL REU.

namespace Chung2012Isoperimetric

open Set Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal Real

/-- A polygonal region: a compact region bounded by a simple polygonal loop (Definition 2.1).
Regular closedness excludes lower-dimensional pieces. -/
structure PolygonalRegion where
  /-- The number of sides of the boundary polygon. -/
  sides : ℕ
  three_le : 3 ≤ sides
  /-- The simple polygonal loop bounding the region. -/
  polygon : Polygon ℂ sides
  /-- The compact region as a subset of the plane. -/
  carrier : Set ℂ
  compact : IsCompact carrier
  regularClosed : closure (interior carrier) = carrier
  frontier_eq : frontier carrier = polygon.boundary ℝ
  simpleBoundary : Nonempty (AddCircle (1 : ℝ) ≃ₜ ↥(polygon.boundary ℝ))

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction; remarks after Theorem 3.5). Cairo and Prismatic
pentagons minimize the perimeter ratio even when nonconvex tiles are allowed.

Interfaces are counted once, and no periodicity or edge-to-edge condition is imposed. -/
theorem nonconvex_perimeter_bound {ι : Type*} (T : ι → PolygonalRegion)
    (hsides : ∀ i, (T i).sides ≤ 5)
    (harea : ∀ i, volume (T i).carrier = 1)
    (hdisjoint : Pairwise fun i j ↦ Disjoint (interior (T i).carrier)
      (interior (T j).carrier))
    (hcover : (⋃ i, (T i).carrier) = univ) :

      limsup (fun R : ℝ ↦
        (Measure.hausdorffMeasure 1)
          ((⋃ i, frontier (T i).carrier) ∩ Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) R) /
            ENNReal.ofReal (π * R ^ 2)) atTop := by
  sorry

end Chung2012Isoperimetric

/-!
# On the Speed of an Excited Asymmetric Random Walk

Authors: Mike Cinkoske, Joe Jackson, and Claire Plunkett.
Origin: [Purdue PRiME 2017](https://www.math.purdue.edu/research/past-research-projects.html).
Reference: M. Cinkoske, J. Jackson, and C. Plunkett, *On the Speed of an Excited Asymmetric
Random Walk*, Rose-Hulman Undergrad. Math. J. **19** (2018), no. 1, Article 6; arXiv:1708.08576v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Cinkoske2017Speed

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The excited walk's visited sites in reverse chronological order, starting at zero, using
one independent uniform coordinate for each departure (Section 1). -/
def walkHistory (M : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (u : ℕ → unitInterval) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => [0]
  | n + 1 =>
      let h := walkHistory M p u n
      let x := h.headD 0
      let threshold : ℝ := if h.count x ≤ M then p else 1 / 2
      (x + if (u n : ℝ) < threshold then 1 else -1) :: h

/-- **Open question** (Section 4.3, p. 16). Spreading the same total drift over more equal
cookies makes the deterministic limiting speed nonincreasing.

The affirmative direction follows the decreasing-speed prediction on p. 16 and the question's
non-strict inequality; the added-cookie index includes zero. -/
theorem speed_nonincreasing (M : ℕ) (hM : 3 ≤ M) (p : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp_one : p < 1) (hdrift : 2 < (M : ℝ) * (2 * p - 1)) :
    ∃ v : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ i : ℕ,
        ∀ᵐ u ∂(Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (volume : Measure unitInterval))),
          Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (((walkHistory (M + i)
              (1 / 2 + (M : ℝ) * (2 * p - 1) / (2 * ((M + i : ℕ) : ℝ)))
              u n).headD 0 : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (v i))) ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, v (i + 1) ≤ v i := by
  sorry

end Cinkoske2017Speed

  sorry

title: Parameter identifiability of linear-compartmental mammillary models
problem_statement: In clemens2026parameter.lean, prove either Clemens2026Parameter.conjecture_3_18 or refute it by proving its logical negation Clemens2026Parameter.conjecture_3_18_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Parameter identifiability of linear-compartmental mammillary models

Authors: Katherine Clemens, Jonathan Martinez, Anne Shiu, Michaela Thompson,
and Benjamin Warren.
Origin: [Texas A&M University REU
2023](https://artsci.tamu.edu/mathematics/academics/undergraduate/research/reu/results/results-2023.html).
Reference: K. Clemens, J. Martinez, A. Shiu, M. Thompson, and B. Warren, *Parameter
identifiability of linear-compartmental mammillary models*, Bull. Math. Biol. **88** (2026),
article 12; arXiv:2506.21889v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Clemens2026Parameter

open MeasureTheory

/-- Indices `(i, j)` for the rate from `j` to `i` in the leak-free star (Definitions 2.1-2.2
and (5)). Lean vertex `i` is source compartment `i.val + 1`. -/
abbrev ParameterIndex (n : ℕ) :=
  {ij : Fin n × Fin n //
    (ij.1.val = 0 ∧ ij.2.val ≠ 0) ∨ (ij.1.val ≠ 0 ∧ ij.2.val = 0)}

/-- The compartmental matrix of a leak-free mammillary model (Definition 2.3). -/
def compartmentalMatrix {n : ℕ} (k : ParameterIndex n → ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
  fun i j ↦
    if i = j then -∑ e : ParameterIndex n, if e.val.2 = j then k e else 0
    else if h : (i.val = 0 ∧ j.val ≠ 0) ∨ (i.val ≠ 0 ∧ j.val = 0) then
      k ⟨(i, j), h⟩
    else 0

/-- The coefficients of the input-output equation (3), using the adjugate entry
`(output, input)` for its signed minor (Section 2.2). Constant zero coordinates are retained;
they do not change any fiber. -/
def coefficientMap {n : ℕ} (input output : Fin n) (k : ParameterIndex n → ℝ) :
    (Fin n → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  let B := (compartmentalMatrix k).charmatrix
  (fun d ↦ B.det.coeff d.val, fun d ↦ (B.adjugate output input).coeff d.val)

/-- Almost every real parameter vector has a coefficient-map fiber whose projection onto the
specified parameter is finite (Definition 2.18(3)). -/
def GenericallyLocallyIdentifiable {n : ℕ} (input output : Fin n)
    (e : ParameterIndex n) : Prop :=
  ∀ᵐ k : ParameterIndex n → ℝ ∂volume,
    Set.Finite {v : ℝ | ∃ l : ParameterIndex n → ℝ,
      coefficientMap input output l = coefficientMap input output k ∧ l e = v}

/-- **Conjecture 3.18**. For every `n ≥ 5`, the parameters `k12`, `k13`, and every `ki1` of
`M_n(2,3)` are unidentifiable.

Definition 2.18 is used over all real rates, without positivity restrictions; unidentifiable is
the negation of generic local identifiability, not almost-everywhere infinite fibers. -/
theorem conjecture_3_18 {n : ℕ} (hn : 5 ≤ n) (e : ParameterIndex n)
    (he : e.val.2.val ≤ 2) :
    ¬GenericallyLocallyIdentifiable ⟨1, by omega⟩ ⟨2, by omega⟩ e := by
  sorry

end Clemens2026Parameter

theorem Clemens2026Parameter.conjecture_3_18_neg : ¬ type_of% @Clemens2026Parameter.conjecture_3_18 := by
  sorry

/-!
# The Lorentz Lattice Gas Model

Author: Benjamin Coate.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2008](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/proceedings/2008.html).
Reference: B. Coate, *The Lorentz Lattice Gas Model*, Oregon State University Research
Experiences for Undergraduates Proceedings (2008), 37--48.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Coate2008Lorentz

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The position and outgoing velocity of the northward light ray (Sections 1--2). One uniform
coordinate per vertex fixes its mirror for all visits (below `p / 2` NW, then NE up to `p`,
else vacant), and the origin's mirror acts only on later arrivals. -/
def ray (p : ℝ) (u : ℤ × ℤ → unitInterval) :
    ℕ → (ℤ × ℤ) × (ℤ × ℤ)
  | 0 => ((0, 0), (0, 1))
  | t + 1 =>
      let s := ray p u t
      let x : ℤ × ℤ := (s.1.1 + s.2.1, s.1.2 + s.2.2)
      let v : ℤ × ℤ :=
        if (u x : ℝ) < p / 2 then (-s.2.2, -s.2.1)
        else if (u x : ℝ) < p then (s.2.2, s.2.1)
        else s.2
      (x, v)

/-- **Conjecture 4.2** (p. 47). Above every density lower bound in `(0, 1)` there is a nonempty
open interval on which the probability of reaching the boundary of a growing centered odd
square tends to zero.

Radius `r` means side length `2 * r + 1`; the event is boundary hitting at any time, not
finite-time escape or return to the origin. The domain of `α` follows pp. 42--43. -/
theorem recurrence_intervals (α : ℝ) (hpos : 0 < α) (hlt : α < 1) :
    ∃ p₁ p₂ : ℝ, α ≤ p₁ ∧ p₁ < p₂ ∧ p₂ ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ p : ℝ, p₁ < p → p < p₂ →
        Tendsto (fun r : ℕ ↦
          (Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℤ × ℤ ↦ (volume : Measure unitInterval)))
            {u | ∃ t : ℕ, max (ray p u t).1.1.natAbs (ray p u t).1.2.natAbs = r}) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

end Coate2008Lorentz

title: On the size and complexity of scrambles
problem_statement: In connor2023size.lean, prove either Connor2023Size.disjoint_scramble_np_hard or refute it by proving its logical negation Connor2023Size.disjoint_scramble_np_hard_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the size and complexity of scrambles

Authors: Seamus Connor, Steven DiSilvio, Sasha Kononova, Ralph Morrison,
and Krish Singal.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU](https://math.williams.edu/small/).
Reference: S. Connor, S. DiSilvio, S. Kononova, R. Morrison, and K. Singal, *On the size and
complexity of scrambles*, arXiv:2311.17342v3 (2026).
-/

namespace Connor2023Size

open Finset

/-- The multigraph presented by an explicit edge-instance list. Repeated endpoint pairs remain
distinct edges, indexed by their list positions. -/
def graphFromEdges {n m : ℕ} (ends : Fin m → Fin n × Fin n) :
    Graph (Fin n) (Fin m) where
  vertexSet := Set.univ
  edgeSet := Set.univ
  IsLink e u v := ends e = (u, v) ∨ ends e = (v, u)
  isLink_symm _ _ := ⟨fun _ _ h ↦ h.symm⟩
  eq_or_eq_of_isLink_of_isLink := by
    intro e x y v w hx hv
    rcases hx with hx | hx <;> rcases hv with hv | hv
    · exact Or.inl (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).1
    · exact Or.inr (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).1
    · exact Or.inr (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).2
    · exact Or.inl (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).2
  edge_mem_iff_exists_isLink e := by
    constructor
    · intro _; exact ⟨(ends e).1, (ends e).2, Or.inl (Prod.eta _)⟩
    · intro _; exact Set.mem_univ _
  left_mem_of_isLink := by intro _ _ _ _; trivial

/-- A nonempty family of pairwise vertex-disjoint, nonempty connected eggs (Section 2.2). Eggs
are encoded as vertex sets with their induced subgraphs. -/
def IsDisjointScramble {n m : ℕ} (G : Graph (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  S.Nonempty ∧
    (∀ A ∈ S, A.Nonempty ∧ (G.induce (A : Set (Fin n))).toSimpleGraph.Connected) ∧
    (S : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Pairwise fun A B ↦ Disjoint A B

/-- One side of an egg-cut: two connected complementary vertex sets, each containing an entire
egg (Section 2.2). The cut size is `edgeCut.ncard` in the target. -/
def IsEggCutSide {n m : ℕ} (G : Graph (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  A.Nonempty ∧ Aᶜ.Nonempty ∧
    (G.induce (A : Set (Fin n))).toSimpleGraph.Connected ∧
    (G.induce ((Aᶜ : Finset (Fin n)) : Set (Fin n))).toSimpleGraph.Connected ∧
    (∃ egg ∈ S, egg ⊆ A) ∧ (∃ egg ∈ S, egg ⊆ Aᶜ)

/-- A canonical finite explicit multigraph input. Endpoint pairs are increasing, the pair list
is sorted with repetitions, and connectivity includes the one-vertex graph. -/
structure Instance where
  /-- The number of vertices. -/
  vertices : ℕ
  /-- The number of edges. -/
  edges : ℕ
  /-- The target lower bound for the order of a disjoint scramble. -/
  threshold : ℕ
  vertices_pos : 0 < vertices
  /-- The ordered endpoint pair of each edge. -/
  ends : Fin edges → Fin vertices × Fin vertices
  endpoints_ordered : ∀ e, (ends e).1 < (ends e).2
  pairs_sorted : (List.ofFn ends).Pairwise fun a b ↦
    a.1 < b.1 ∨ (a.1 = b.1 ∧ a.2 ≤ b.2)
  connected : (graphFromEdges ends).toSimpleGraph.Connected

open scoped Classical in
/-- The decoder of escaped canonical binary naturals: vertex count, edge count, threshold, then
endpoint pairs. Malformed, trailing and out-of-domain inputs fail. -/
noncomputable def readInstance (input : List Bool) : Option Instance := do
  let rec
    /-- Read one escaped binary word, returning its digits and the remaining input. -/
    readBits : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
    | false :: rest => some ([], rest)
    | true :: b :: rest => do
      let (bits, tail) ← readBits rest
      some (b :: bits, tail)
    | _ => none
  let readNat := fun word ↦ do
    let (bits, rest) ← readBits word
    let value := Computability.decodeNat bits
    if Computability.encodeNat value = bits then some (value, rest) else none
  let (v, rest) ← readNat input
  let (e, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (k, rest) ← readNat rest
  if hv : 0 < v then
    let rec
      /-- Read `m` endpoint pairs of vertex indices below `v`, with the remaining input. -/
      readEdges : (m : ℕ) → List Bool →
        Option ((Fin m → Fin v × Fin v) × List Bool)
      | 0, word => some (Fin.elim0, word)
      | m + 1, word => do
        let (a, word) ← readNat word
        let (b, word) ← readNat word
        if ha : a < v then
          if hb : b < v then
            let (tail, word) ← readEdges m word
            some (Fin.cases (⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩) tail, word)
          else none
        else none
    let (ends, rest) ← readEdges e rest
    if rest = [] then
      if ho : ∀ i, (ends i).1 < (ends i).2 then
        if hs : (List.ofFn ends).Pairwise fun a b ↦
            a.1 < b.1 ∨ (a.1 = b.1 ∧ a.2 ≤ b.2) then
          if hc : (graphFromEdges ends).toSimpleGraph.Connected then
            some { vertices := v, edges := e, threshold := k,
                   vertices_pos := hv, ends, endpoints_ordered := ho,
                   pairs_sorted := hs, connected := hc }
          else none
        else none
      else none
    else none
  else none

/-- **Following Question 6.5** (Section 6.1, p. 16). Deciding the disjoint scramble threshold is
NP-hard.

Graphs are finite connected loopless multigraphs, not only simple ones; inputs are explicit
edge lists with binary thresholds under many-one reductions, with no succinct multiplicities. -/
theorem disjoint_scramble_np_hard :
    let pairCode := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList Bool) (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    ∀ language : Set (List Bool),
      (∃ verifier : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool,
        ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime pairCode
            Computability.encodeBool verifier,
          (∀ stack : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ stack)) ∧
          ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ input : List Bool,
            input ∈ language ↔ ∃ certificate : List Bool,
              certificate.length ≤ bound.eval input.length ∧
                verifier (input, certificate) = true) →
      ∃ reduction : List Bool → List Bool,
        ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id reduction,
          (∀ stack : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ stack)) ∧
          ∀ input, input ∈ language ↔
            ∃ g : Instance, readInstance (reduction input) = some g ∧
              ∃ S : Finset (Finset (Fin g.vertices)),
                IsDisjointScramble (graphFromEdges g.ends) S ∧ g.threshold ≤ #S ∧
                ∀ A : Finset (Fin g.vertices), IsEggCutSide (graphFromEdges g.ends) S A →
                  g.threshold ≤

/-!
# Numerical sets, core partitions, and integer points in polytopes

Authors: Hannah Constantin, Ben Houston-Edwards, and Nathan Kaplan.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: H. Constantin, B. Houston-Edwards, and N. Kaplan, *Numerical sets, core partitions,
and integer points in polytopes*, arXiv:1509.06077.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Constantin2017Numerical

open Finset

/-- A numerical set is a subset of `ℕ` containing `0` and with finite complement. -/
structure NumericalSet where
  /-- The underlying subset of `ℕ`. -/
  carrier : Set ℕ
  zero_mem : 0 ∈ carrier
  finite_complement : Set.Finite {n : ℕ | n ∉ carrier}

instance : Membership ℕ NumericalSet := ⟨fun T n ↦ n ∈ T.carrier⟩

/-- A numerical set is a numerical semigroup when it is closed under addition. -/
def NumericalSet.IsNumericalSemigroup (T : NumericalSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ T, ∀ y ∈ T, x + y ∈ T

open scoped Classical in
/-- The profile bijection relation `φ(T) = λ`. With the gaps of `T` in decreasing order, the row
for a gap `n` has length `#{t ∈ T : t < n}`. -/
def Phi (T : NumericalSet) (lam : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  ∃ gapList : List ℕ,
    gapList.Nodup ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, n ∈ gapList ↔ n ∉ T) ∧
      gapList.Pairwise (fun m n ↦ n < m) ∧
      lam.rowLens =
        gapList.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ #{t ∈ Finset.range n | t ∈ T})

open Filter
open scoped Topology

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 8.1**. If `P(n)` counts partitions of size at most `n` and `S'(n)` counts those
associated via `φ` to numerical semigroups, then `S'(n) / P(n) → 0`. -/
theorem conjecture_8_1_semigroup_associated_partitions_density_zero :
    Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦
        let partitions := Finset.univ.biUnion (fun k : Fin (n + 1) ↦
          Finset.univ.image (fun p : Nat.Partition k.val ↦ YoungDiagram.ofPartition p))
        ((#{lam ∈ partitions |
            ∃ T : NumericalSet, T.IsNumericalSemigroup ∧ Phi T lam} : ℝ) /
          (#partitions : ℝ)))
      atTop (𝓝 0) := by sorry

end Constantin2017Numerical

/-!
# Multilinear polynomials of small degree evaluated on matrices over a unital algebra

Authors: Katherine Cordwell and George Wang.
Origin: [Kent State University REU
2015](https://www.kent.edu/math/research-experiences-undergraduates).
Reference: K. Cordwell and G. Wang, *Multilinear polynomials of small degree evaluated on
matrices over a unital algebra*, Linear Algebra Appl. **496** (2016), 262--287;
DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2015.12.033.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Cordwell2016Multilinear

/-- **Conjecture 1** (p. 264). Every traceless matrix over a unital associative algebra is the
sum of two values of each nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most one more than the
matrix size.

The coefficient algebra need not be commutative; trace is the diagonal sum in that algebra, and
nonzero means formally nonzero. -/
theorem traceless_sum_two_values
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K]
    (R : Type*) [Ring R] [Algebra K R]
    (n : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hnm : m - 1 ≤ n)
    (c : Equiv.Perm (Fin m) → K) :
    let f : FreeAlgebra K (Fin m) :=
      ∑ s : Equiv.Perm (Fin m),
        c s • (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin m ↦ FreeAlgebra.ι K (s i))).prod
    f ≠ 0 →
      ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R, Matrix.trace A = 0 →
        ∃ X Y : Fin m → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R,
          (FreeAlgebra.lift K X) f + (FreeAlgebra.lift K Y) f = A := by
  sorry

end Cordwell2016Multilinear

/-!
# Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture

Authors: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan, and Thomas Wang.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: C. Cowen-Breen, E. Karangozishvili, N. Varadarajan, and T. Wang, *Pattern problems
related to the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture*, preprint (2020), arXiv:2011.07056v1, 30 pp.
-/

namespace CowenBreen2020Pattern

open Topology
open Finset

/-- The least cardinality `G'_U(N)` of an integer set containing an affine copy of `U` with each
of `N` distinct integer basepoints and nonzero scaling (Section 2.1). -/
noncomputable def patternCardinality (U : Finset ℚ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | ∃ B : Finset ℤ, ∃ S : Finset ℤ,
    #B = m ∧ #S = N ∧
      ∀ x ∈ S, ∃ r ≠ (0 : ℚ),
        ∀ u ∈ U, ∃ b : ℤ,
          b ∈ B ∧ (b : ℚ) = (x : ℚ) + r * u}

/-- **Conjecture 2.1**. For every increasing chain of positive rational patterns of cardinality
`k`, the limiting logarithmic growth exponents of `G'` tend to one. -/
theorem conjecture_2_1 (U : ℕ → Finset ℚ) (hU : Monotone U)
    (hcard : ∀ k : ℕ, #(U k) = k)
    (hpos : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ u ∈ U k, 0 < u) :
    ∃ L : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ k > 0,
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun N : ℕ ↦ Real.log (patternCardinality (U k) N : ℝ) / Real.log (N : ℝ))
          Filter.atTop (𝓝 (L k))) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto L Filter.atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end CowenBreen2020Pattern

import Mathlib

/-!
# Finite cobordism

Author: Samuel Coyle.
Origin: [University of Chicago REU 2025](https://math.uchicago.edu/~may/REU2025/).
Reference: S. Coyle, *Finite cobordism*, University of Chicago REU research report (2025), 28 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Coyle2025Finite

open Finset

universe u

/-- The source finite-space topology has precisely the lower sets as its open sets. -/
instance finiteSpaceTopology (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : TopologicalSpace P :=
  Topology.lowerSet P

/-- The strict upper set of an up-beat point has a least element (Definition 2.7). -/
def IsUpBeat {P : FinPartOrd.{u}} (x : P) : Prop :=
  ∃ y : P, IsLeast (Set.Ioi x) y

/-- All points below an up-beat point (Definition 3.1). -/
def upBoundary (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : Set P :=
  {x | ∃ y : P, IsUpBeat y ∧ x ≤ y}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The subdivision by nonempty chains ordered by inclusion (Theorem 2.10). -/
def Sd (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : FinPartOrd.{u} :=
  FinPartOrd.of {s : Finset P // s.Nonempty ∧ IsChain (· ≤ ·) (s : Set P)}

/-- Barystability as an equality of induced subspaces in `Sd(P)` (Definition 3.8). -/
def Barystable (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : Prop :=
  upBoundary (Sd P) = {s | (s.val : Set P) ⊆ upBoundary P}

/-- The largest chain has `n + 1` points and every maximal chain has that size (Definition 3.15
and Section 3.3). Maximal means inclusion-maximal, not saturated. -/
def HomogeneousHeight (n : ℕ) (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : Prop :=
  (Set.univ : Set P).chainHeight (· ≤ ·) = (n + 1 : ENat) ∧
    ∀ s : Finset P, IsMaxChain (· ≤ ·) (s : Set P) → #s = n + 1

/-- The class `BStab_n`, which includes the empty finite space (Section 4). -/
def BStab (n : ℕ) (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : Prop :=
  IsEmpty P ∨ (Barystable P ∧ HomogeneousHeight n P)

/-- Closedness in the source sense: empty up-boundary, not topological closedness. -/
def Closed (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) : Prop :=
  upBoundary P = ∅

/-- A weak point: its strict lower or strict upper finite subspace is contractible (p. 5). -/
def IsWeakPoint {P : FinPartOrd.{u}} (x : P) : Prop :=
  ContractibleSpace {y : P // y < x} ∨ ContractibleSpace {y : P // x < y}

set_option genInjectivity false in
set_option genCtorIdx false in
set_option genSizeOf false in
/-- An arbitrary finite ambient poset with the same pointwise incoming marking. -/
structure MarkedFiniteSpace (X : FinPartOrd.{u}) where
  /-- The ambient finite poset. -/
  space : FinPartOrd.{u}
  /-- The order embedding marking `X` inside the ambient poset. -/
  mark : X ↪o space

open scoped Classical in
/-- Delete one unmarked point, retaining the original marking pointwise. -/
def MarkedFiniteSpace.delete {X : FinPartOrd.{u}} (M : MarkedFiniteSpace X)
    (p : M.space) (away : ∀ x : X, M.mark x ≠ p) : MarkedFiniteSpace X where
  space := FinPartOrd.of {y : M.space // y ≠ p}
  mark :=
    { toFun := fun x ↦ ⟨M.mark x, away x⟩
      inj' := fun _ _ h ↦ M.mark.injective (congrArg Subtype.val h)
      map_rel_iff' := M.mark.map_rel_iff }

/-- The generators of the fixed-incoming relative weak-point relation (pp. 23--24). -/
inductive RelativeMove (X : FinPartOrd.{u}) :
    MarkedFiniteSpace X → MarkedFiniteSpace X → Prop
  | delete (M : MarkedFiniteSpace X) (p : M.space)
      (away : ∀ x : X, M.mark x ≠ p) (hp : IsWeakPoint p) :
      RelativeMove X M (M.delete p away)
  | rename (M N : MarkedFiniteSpace X) (e : M.space ≃o N.space)
      (fixed : ∀ x : X, e (M.mark x) = N.mark x) :
      RelativeMove X M N

set_option genInjectivity false in
set_option genCtorIdx false in
set_option genSizeOf false in
/-- A finite cobordism with its boundary identification (Definition 4.1). The w-cobordism
condition is the separate structure `WCobordism`. -/
structure FiniteCobordism (n : ℕ) (X : FinPartOrd.{u}) where
  /-- The outgoing boundary poset. -/
  outgoing : FinPartOrd.{u}
  /-- The finite poset forming the cobordism. -/
  space : FinPartOrd.{u}
  incoming_bstab : BStab n X
  incoming_closed : Closed X
  outgoing_bstab : BStab n outgoing
  outgoing_closed : Closed outgoing
  space_bstab : BStab (n + 1) space
  /-- The identification of the incoming and outgoing posets with the up-boundary. -/
  boundary : (X ⊕ outgoing) ≃o {x : space // x ∈ upBoundary space}

/-- The incoming inclusion obtained from this cobordism's boundary isomorphism. -/
def FiniteCobordism.incoming {n : ℕ} {X : FinPartOrd.{u}}
    (C : FiniteCobordism n X) : X ↪o C.space where
  toFun x := (C.boundary (Sum.inl x)).val
  inj' := by
    intro x y h
    exact Sum.inl_injective (C.boundary.injective (Subtype.ext h))
  map_rel_iff' := by
    intro x y
    change C.boundary (Sum.inl x) ≤ C.boundary (Sum.inl y) ↔ x ≤ y
    exact C.boundary.map_rel_iff.trans Sum.inl_le_inl_iff

/-- The outgoing inclusion obtained from the same boundary isomorphism. -/
def FiniteCobordism.outgoingInclusion {n : ℕ} {X : FinPartOrd.{u}}
    (C : FiniteCobordism n X) : C.outgoing ↪o C.space where
  toFun y := (C.boundary (Sum.inr y)).val
  inj' := by
    intro x y h
    exact Sum.inr_injective (C.boundary.injective (Subtype.ext h))
  map_rel_iff' := by
    intro x y
    change C.boundary (Sum.inr x) ≤ C.boundary (Sum.inr y) ↔ x ≤ y
    exact C.boundary.map_rel_iff.trans Sum.inr_le_inr_iff

/-- The incoming marked pair of a cobordism. -/
def FiniteCobordism.marked {n : ℕ} {X : FinPartOrd.{u}}
    (C : FiniteCobordism n X) : MarkedFiniteSpace X where
  space := C.space
  mark := C.incoming

open Set Convexity

/-- The source order complex: nonempty chains of a finite ordered space. -/
def orderComplex (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] : AbstractSimplicialComplex P where
  faces := {s | s.Nonempty ∧ IsChain (· ≤ ·) (s : Set P)}
  isRelLowerSet_faces := by
    intro s hs
    refine ⟨hs.1, ?_⟩
    intro t hts ht
    exact ⟨ht, hs.2.mono (by simpa using hts)⟩
  singleton_mem p := by
    simp

/-- The geometric realization by standard-simplex weights supported on a face. -/
def realization {P : Type*} (K : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex P) :
    Set (StdSimplex ℝ P) :=
  {w | w.weights.support ∈ K}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The affine realization of a vertex map that takes faces to faces. -/
def realizationMap {P Q : Type*} (K : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex P)
    (L : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex Q) (f : P → Q)
    (hf : ∀ s ∈ K, s.image f ∈ L) : C(realization K, realization L) where
  toFun w := ⟨StdSimplex.map f w.val, by
    apply (L.isRelLowerSet_faces (hf _ w.property)).2
    · exact Finsupp.mapDomain_support
    · exact StdSimplex.support_weights_nonempty _⟩
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply Continuous.subtype_mk
    exact (StdSimplex.continuous_map ℝ f).comp continuous_subtype_val

open scoped Classical in
/-- The realization of a monotone map on the source finite-space order complexes. -/
def orderRealizationMap {P Q : Type*} [PartialOrder P] [PartialOrder Q]
    (f : P →o Q) :
    C(realization (orderComplex P).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex,
      realization (orderComplex Q).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex) :=
  realizationMap _ _ f (by
    intro s hs
    refine ⟨hs.1.image _, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Finset.coe_image] using f.monotone.isChain_image hs.2)

/-- A finite Hausdorff CW complex with its underlying space and Mathlib characteristic maps. -/
structure FiniteCW where
  /-- The underlying space of the CW complex. -/
  Carrier : Type u
  [topology : TopologicalSpace Carrier]
  [hausdorff : T2Space Carrier]
  [cw : CWComplex (Set.univ : Set Carrier)]
  [finite : CWComplex.Finite (Set.univ : Set Carrier)]

attribute [instance] FiniteCW.topology FiniteCW.hausdorff FiniteCW.cw FiniteCW.finite

set_option genCtorIdx false in
set_option genSizeOf false in
/-- A CW identification with a subcomplex: a homeomorphism onto it preserving open cells
dimension by dimension. -/
structure CWSubcomplexEmbedding (X Y : FiniteCW.{u}) where
  /-- The subcomplex of `Y` onto which `X` is identified. -/
  image : CWComplex.Subcomplex (Set.univ : Set Y.Carrier)
  /-- The homeomorphism from `X` onto the subcomplex. -/
  homeomorph : X.Carrier ≃ₜ image
  /-- The bijection between the `n`-cells of `X` and those of the subcomplex. -/
  cells (n : ℕ) : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set X.Carrier) n ≃ image.I n
  open_cells (n : ℕ) (i : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set X.Carrier) n) :
    (fun x ↦ (homeomorph x).val) '' CWComplex.openCell n i =
      CWComplex.openCell n (cells n i).val

/-- The actual map into the ambient space, not an independently chosen map. -/
def CWSubcomplexEmbedding.inclusion {X Y : FiniteCW.{u}}
    (j : CWSubcomplexEmbedding X Y) : C(X.Carrier, Y.Carrier) where
  toFun x := (j.homeomorph x).val
  continuous_toFun := continuous_subtype_val.comp j.homeomorph.continuous

/-- A characteristic map for a specified CW cell, not necessarily the one stored in the CW
structure. The ball is Mathlib's maximum-norm ball, a cube. -/
structure CWCharacteristicMap (X : FiniteCW.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (i : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set X.Carrier) n) where

  map : PartialEquiv (Fin n → ℝ) X.Carrier
  source_eq : map.source = Metric.ball 0 1
  target_eq : map.target = CWComplex.openCell n i
  continuousOn : ContinuousOn map (Metric.closedBall 0 1)
  continuousOn_symm : ContinuousOn map.symm map.target

/-- A CW pair over a fixed, pointwise marked incoming CW complex. -/
structure MarkedCWPair (A : FiniteCW.{u}) where
  /-- The ambient finite CW complex. -/
  space : FiniteCW.{u}
  /-- The identification of the incoming complex `A` with a subcomplex. -/

set_option genCtorIdx false in
set_option genSizeOf false in
/-- A CW isomorphism relative to the incoming marking (Cohen 5.2). It preserves cells but not
necessarily the chosen parametrizations. -/
structure RelativeCWIsomorphism {A : FiniteCW.{u}} (P Q : MarkedCWPair A) where
  /-- The underlying homeomorphism of ambient spaces. -/
  homeomorph : P.space.Carrier ≃ₜ Q.space.Carrier
  /-- The induced bijection between `n`-cells. -/
  cells (n : ℕ) :
    RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set P.space.Carrier) n ≃
      RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set Q.space.Carrier) n
  open_cells (n : ℕ) (i : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set P.space.Carrier) n) :
    homeomorph '' CWComplex.openCell n i = CWComplex.openCell n (cells n i)
  relative (a : A.Carrier) :
    homeomorph (P.incoming.inclusion a) = Q.incoming.inclusion a

set_option genInjectivity false in
set_option genCtorIdx false in
set_option genSizeOf false in
/-- An elementary expansion relative to `A` (Cohen Section 4). Cohen's ball pair is modelled by a
cube whose free face is the first-coordinate `+1` face, via `Fin.cons 1`. -/
structure RelativeCWExpansion {A : FiniteCW.{u}} (P Q : MarkedCWPair A) where
  /-- The identification of the smaller complex with a subcomplex of the larger. -/
  old : CWSubcomplexEmbedding P.space Q.space
  relative (a : A.Carrier) :
    old.inclusion (P.incoming.inclusion a) = Q.incoming.inclusion a
  /-- The dimension `n` of the adjoined free face. -/
  dimension : ℕ
  /-- The adjoined `n`-cell. -/
  face : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set Q.space.Carrier) dimension
  /-- The adjoined `(n + 1)`-cell. -/
  coface : RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set Q.space.Carrier) (dimension + 1)
  face_new : ¬old.image.I dimension face
  coface_new : ¬old.image.I (dimension + 1) coface
  adjoining : (Set.univ : Set Q.space.Carrier) =
    (old.image : Set Q.space.Carrier) ∪
      (CWComplex.openCell dimension face ∪ CWComplex.openCell (dimension + 1) coface)
  /-- The characteristic map of the adjoined `(n + 1)`-cell. -/
  characteristic : CWCharacteristicMap Q.space (dimension + 1) coface
  /-- The characteristic map of the adjoined `n`-cell. -/
  faceCharacteristic : CWCharacteristicMap Q.space dimension face
  on_face (x : Fin dimension → ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Metric.closedBall 0 1) :
    characteristic.map (Fin.cons 1 x) = faceCharacteristic.map x
  on_complement : Set.MapsTo characteristic.map
    (closure (Metric.sphere (0 : Fin (dimension + 1) → ℝ) 1 \ {x | x 0 = 1}))
    (old.inclusion ''
      CWComplex.skeletonLT (Set.univ : Set P.space.Carrier) (dimension + 1))

/-- A finite formal CW deformation relative to the marked base. Collapses are reverse expansions
in the equivalence closure, which also includes relative CW renaming. -/
def FormalCWDeformation {A : FiniteCW.{u}} (P Q : MarkedCWPair A) : Prop :=
  Relation.EqvGen (fun B C : MarkedCWPair A ↦
    Nonempty (RelativeCWExpansion B C) ∨ Nonempty (RelativeCWIsomorphism B C)) P Q

/-- A homotopically trivial CW pair (Cohen Section 6). -/
structure HomotopicallyTrivialCWPair (A : FiniteCW.{u}) extends MarkedCWPair A where
  inclusion_equivalence : ∃ e : ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv A.Carrier space.Carrier,
    e.toFun = incoming.inclusion

/-- A w-cobordism: both boundary inclusions realize to weak homotopy equivalences
(Definition 4.1). -/
structure WCobordism (n : ℕ) (X : FinPartOrd.{u}) where
  /-- The underlying finite cobordism. -/
  data : FiniteCobordism n X
  incoming_equivalence : ∃ e : ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv
    (realization (orderComplex X).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex)
    (realization (orderComplex data.space).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex),
    e.toFun = orderRealizationMap data.incoming.toOrderHom
  outgoing_equivalence : ∃ e : ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv
    (realization (orderComplex data.outgoing).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex)
    (realization (orderComplex data.space).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex),
    e.toFun = orderRealizationMap data.outgoingInclusion.toOrderHom

/-- The canonical chain-cell structure on the order-complex realization, as a finite CW
complex. -/
structure CanonicalCWRealization (P : FinPartOrd.{u}) where
  /-- The finite CW complex realizing the order complex. -/
  complex : FiniteCW.{u}
  /-- The homeomorphism from the order-complex realization to the CW complex. -/
  identify :
    realization (orderComplex P).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex ≃ₜ complex.Carrier
  /-- The bijection between chains with `n + 1` elements and `n`-cells. -/
  cells (n : ℕ) :
    {s : Finset P // s ∈ orderComplex P ∧ #s = n + 1} ≃
      RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set complex.Carrier) n
  open_cells (n : ℕ) (s : {s : Finset P // s ∈ orderComplex P ∧ #s = n + 1}) :

structure CanonicalCWPairRealization {n : ℕ} {X : FinPartOrd.{u}}

  /-- The homeomorphism from the cobordism's order-complex realization to the pair. -/
  identify :
    realization (orderComplex C.data.space).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex ≃ₜ
      pair.space.Carrier
  /-- The bijection between chains with `k + 1` elements and `k`-cells. -/
  cells (k : ℕ) :
    {s : Finset C.data.space // s ∈ orderComplex C.data.space ∧ #s = k + 1} ≃
      RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set pair.space.Carrier) k
  open_cells (k : ℕ)
      (s : {s : Finset C.data.space // s ∈ orderComplex C.data.space ∧ #s = k + 1}) :
    identify '' {w | w.val.weights.support = s.val} =
      CWComplex.openCell k (cells k s)
  incoming (x : realization (orderComplex X).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex) :
    identify (orderRealizationMap C.data.incoming.toOrderHom x) =
      pair.incoming.inclusion (A.identify x)

/-- **Conjecture 5.4** (p. 24). The incoming-torsion correspondence classifies all finite
w-cobordisms relative to the incoming boundary, uniformly in sufficiently large dimensions.

Cohen's CW-pair carrier represents componentwise Whitehead values (Theorem 21.1), and pair
torsion is map torsion transported to the incoming space; the correspondence is stated as a graph
(totality, uniqueness, descent, surjectivity and injectivity for the weak-point relation), with
intermediates not required to be cobordisms and empty or disconnected endpoints retained. -/
theorem conjecture_5_4 :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ X : FinPartOrd.{u},
      BStab n X → Closed X →
      Nonempty (CanonicalCWRealization X) ∧
      ∀ A : CanonicalCWRealization X,
        let G := fun (d : WCobordism n X) (c : HomotopicallyTrivialCWPair A.complex) ↦
          ∃ b : CanonicalCWPairRealization A d,
            FormalCWDeformation b.pair.toMarkedCWPair c.toMarkedCWPair
        (∀ d : WCobordism n X, ∃ c, G d c) ∧
        (∀ (d : WCobordism n X) c c', G d c → G d c' →
          FormalCWDeformation c.toMarkedCWPair c'.toMarkedCWPair) ∧
        (∀ d e : WCobordism n X,
          Relation.EqvGen (RelativeMove X) d.data.marked e.data.marked →
            ∀ c, G d c ↔ G e c) ∧
        (∀ c : HomotopicallyTrivialCWPair A.complex, ∃ d, G d c) ∧
        (∀ (d e : WCobordism n X) c c', G d c → G e c' →
          FormalCWDeformation c.toMarkedCWPair c'.toMarkedCWPair →
            Relation.EqvGen (RelativeMove X) d.data.marked e.data.marked) := by
  sorry

end Coyle2025Finite

title: Accepted Elasticity in Local Arithmetic Congruence Monoids

/-!
# Accepted Elasticity in Local Arithmetic Congruence Monoids

Authors: Lorin Crawford, Vadim Ponomarenko, Jason Steinberg, and Marla Williams.
Origin: [San Diego State University REU 2012](https://cdoneill.sdsu.edu/reu/research.html).
Reference: L. Crawford, V. Ponomarenko, J. Steinberg, and M. Williams, *Accepted elasticity in
local arithmetic congruence monoids*, Results Math. **66** (2014), 227--245.
-/

namespace Crawford2014Accepted

/-- A sequence over a finite abelian group, a partition, and a subpartition satisfying the
prescribed product, avoidance, and ratio conditions (Definition 1). -/
structure Configuration {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [Finite G]
    (g : G) (δ γ : ℕ) where
  order_le : orderOf g ≤ δ
  gamma_lt : γ < orderOf g
  /-- The number of blocks in the subpartition. -/
  c : ℕ
  /-- The number of blocks in the partition. -/
  d : ℕ
  c_pos : 0 < c
  d_pos : 0 < d
  /-- The underlying sequence over `G`, as a multiset. -/
  sequence : Multiset G
  /-- The blocks of the partition of the sequence. -/
  partition : Fin d → Multiset G
  /-- The blocks of the subpartition of the sequence. -/
  subpartition : Fin c → Multiset G
  partition_sum : ∑ i, partition i = sequence
  subpartition_le : ∑ i, subpartition i ≤ sequence
  partition_prod : ∀ i, (partition i).prod = g ^ (γ + 1)
  partition_avoids : ∀ i, ∀ T : Multiset G,
    T ≤ partition i → T ≠ 0 →
      ∀ k ≥ 1, k ≤ γ → T.prod ≠ g ^ k
  subpartition_prod : ∀ i, (subpartition i).prod = g ^ γ
  ratio : 1 + ((δ : ℚ) - 1) / ((δ : ℚ) - γ) ≤ (c : ℚ) / d

/-- **Conjecture 1** (author manuscript, Section 6). Configuration existence is downward closed in
positive `γ`. -/
theorem conjecture_1 {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [Finite G]
    (g : G) (δ γ : ℕ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (h : Nonempty (Configuration g δ γ)) :
    Nonempty (Configuration g δ (γ - 1)) := by
  sorry

end Crawford2014Accepted

title: Two-type annihilating systems on the complete and star graph
problem_statement: In cristali2021two.lean, prove either Cristali2021Two.section_1_3_star_asymptotic or refute it by proving its logical negation Cristali2021Two.section_1_3_star_asymptotic_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Two-type annihilating systems on the complete and star graph

Authors: Irina Cristali, Yufeng Jiang, Matthew Junge, Remy Kassem,
David Sivakoff, and Grayson York.
Origin: [Duke DOmath 2018](https://agraysonyork.com/research.html).
Reference: I. Cristali, Y. Jiang, M. Junge, R. Kassem, D. Sivakoff, and G. York, *Two-type
annihilating systems on the complete and star graph*, Stochastic Process. Appl. **139** (2021),
321--342.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Cristali2021Two

open Filter
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 1.3). For every sufficiently large fixed blue-selection
probability `p < 1`, the expected extinction time on the star with `2 * n` initially occupied
leaves is asymptotic to `4 * log (1 / (1 - p)) * n`.

The limit is in `n` with `p` fixed, not an iterated limit or the always-blue-core heuristic;
selection is uniform among particles with multiplicity, the expectation is the extended
nonnegative survival-tail sum, and the initial leaves carry a canonical balanced coloring. -/
theorem section_1_3_star_asymptotic :
    ∃ p₀ ≥ (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0), p₀ < 1 ∧
      ∀ p : ℝ≥0, p₀ < p → (hp : p < 1) →
        Tendsto
          (fun n : ℕ ↦
            let V := Option (Fin (2 * n))
            let State := Multiset V × Multiset V
            let initial : State :=
              ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).val.map
                  (fun i ↦ some ⟨i.val, by omega⟩),
                (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).val.map
                  (fun i ↦ some ⟨n + i.val, by omega⟩))
            let step : State → PMF State := fun s ↦
              if s.1 = 0 ∧ s.2 = 0 then PMF.pure s else
                (PMF.ofFintype (fun blue : Bool ↦
                    cond blue (p : ℝ≥0∞) (1 - (p : ℝ≥0∞)))
                  (by simp [show (p : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ 1 by exact_mod_cast hp.le])).bind
                  (fun blue ↦
                    if h : (if blue then s.1 else s.2) = 0 then PMF.pure s else
                      (PMF.ofMultiset (if blue then s.1 else s.2) h).bind (fun x ↦
                        if hN : ((SimpleGraph.starGraph (none : V)).neighborFinset x).Nonempty then
                          (PMF.uniformOfFinset
                              ((SimpleGraph.starGraph (none : V)).neighborFinset x) hN).map
                            (fun y ↦
                              if blue then
                                if y ∈ s.2 then (s.1.erase x, s.2.erase y)
                                else (y ::ₘ s.1.erase x, s.2)
                              else
                                if y ∈ s.1 then (s.1.erase y, s.2.erase x)
                                else (s.1, y ::ₘ s.2.erase x))
                        else PMF.pure s))
            (∑' t : ℕ,
                (((fun ν : PMF State ↦ ν.bind step)^[t]) (PMF.pure initial)).toOuterMeasure
                  {s | s.1 ≠ 0 ∨ s.2 ≠ 0}) / (n : ℝ≥0∞))
          atTop (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal (4 * Real.log (1 / (1 - (p : ℝ)))))) := by
  sorry

end Cristali2021Two
