  sorry

title: On rationally ergodic and rationally weakly mixing rank-one transformations
problem_statement: In dai2015rationally.lean, prove either Dai2015Rationally.almost_steep_doubly_ergodic or refute it by proving its logical negation Dai2015Rationally.almost_steep_doubly_ergodic_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On rationally ergodic and rationally weakly mixing rank-one transformations

Authors: Irving Dai, Xavier Garcia, Tudor Padurariu, and Cesar E. Silva.
Origin: Williams College SMALL REU 2012.
Reference: I. Dai, X. Garcia, T. Padurariu, and C. E. Silva, *On rationally ergodic and rationally
weakly mixing rank-one transformations*, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems **35** (2015), no. 4,
1141--1164; arXiv:1208.3161v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Dai2015Rationally

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped ENNReal

/-- The common width of the levels at stage `n`, starting with unit width and cutting into
`cuts k` equal pieces at each preceding stage (Section 1.3). -/
def columnWidth (cuts : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, (cuts k : ℝ))⁻¹

/-- The ordered left endpoints of the interval levels of a column. Old levels are cut left to
right, spacers follow the old occupied interval, and list order is tower order. -/
def columnStarts (cuts : ℕ → ℕ) (spacers : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → List ℝ
  | 0 => [0]
  | n + 1 =>
    let old := columnStarts cuts spacers n
    let w := columnWidth cuts (n + 1)
    let endOfOld := (old.length : ℝ) * columnWidth cuts n
    (List.range (cuts n)).flatMap fun (k : ℕ) ↦
      old.map (fun a ↦ a + (k : ℝ) * w) ++
        (List.range (spacers n k)).map (fun (j : ℕ) ↦
          endOfOld + (((∑ u ∈ Finset.range k, spacers n u) + j : ℕ) : ℝ) * w)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction, p. 3). The almost-steep construction of Section 4
and Theorem 4.4 is doubly ergodic for all positive-measure measurable sets, not just levels.

The cutting and spacer data are arbitrary summable data, and the transformation is specified
modulo null endpoints by its upward column translations. -/
theorem almost_steep_doubly_ergodic
    (cuts : ℕ → ℕ) (spacers : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ)
    (hcuts : ∀ n, 3 ≤ cuts n)
    (hfirst : ∀ n, spacers n 0 = 0)
    (hsecond : ∀ n, spacers n 1 = 1)
    (hsteep : ∀ n i, 2 ≤ i → i < cuts n →
      4 * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range i, ((columnStarts cuts spacers n).length + spacers n k)) ≤
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (i + 1), ((columnStarts cuts spacers n).length + spacers n k))
    (hsummable : Summable (fun n ↦ (cuts n : ℝ)⁻¹))
    (T : ℝ ≃ᵐ ℝ)
    (hergodic : Ergodic T (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))))
    (hconservative : Conservative T (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))))
    (hcolumns : ∀ n j, j + 1 < (columnStarts cuts spacers n).length →
      ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))),
        x ∈ Ioo ((columnStarts cuts spacers n).getD j 0)
          ((columnStarts cuts spacers n).getD j 0 + columnWidth cuts n) →
        T x = x - (columnStarts cuts spacers n).getD j 0 +
          (columnStarts cuts spacers n).getD (j + 1) 0)
    (A B : Set ℝ) (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    (hA₀ : 0 < (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))) A)
    (hB₀ : 0 < (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))) B) :
    ∃ m > 0,
      0 < (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))) (A ∩ (T^[m]) ⁻¹' A) ∧
      0 < (volume.restrict (Ici (0 : ℝ))) (A ∩ (T^[m]) ⁻¹' B) := by
  sorry

end Dai2015Rationally

theorem Dai2015Rationally.almost_steep_doubly_ergodic_neg : ¬ type_of% @Dai2015Rationally.almost_steep_doubly_ergodic := by
  sorry

title: A relation on (omega, <) of intermediate degree spectrum on a cone
problem_statement: In damaj2025relation.lean, prove either Damaj2025Relation.conjecture_4_16 or refute it by proving its logical negation Damaj2025Relation.conjecture_4_16_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A relation on (omega, <) of intermediate degree spectrum on a cone

Authors: Jad Damaj and Matthew Harrison-Trainor.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2023](https://lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/reu-su22/reu-2023/Damaj%2CJad_REU_Report_2023.pdf).
Reference: J. Damaj and M. Harrison-Trainor, *A relation on (omega, <) of intermediate degree
spectrum on a cone*, J. Symbolic Logic (2025), 1--39; doi:10.1017/jsl.2025.10164.
-/

namespace Damaj2025Relation

/-- Every point lies in a finite interval closed under the function and under all inverse images
(Definition 2.6). The function need not be injective. -/
def IsBlockFunction (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, ∃ a b : ℕ,
    n ∈ Set.Icc a b ∧ ∀ x, (f x ∈ Set.Icc a b ↔ x ∈ Set.Icc a b)

/-- The degree spectrum on `(ω, <)`: the degrees of transported functions joined with `X`
(Definition 2.3). -/
def relativeDegreeSpectrum (f : ℕ → ℕ) (X : ℕ → Bool) : Set TuringDegree :=
  fun d ↦ ∃ e : Equiv.Perm ℕ,
    ComputableIn {fun n ↦ Part.some (X n).toNat}
        (fun p : ℕ × ℕ ↦ decide (e.symm p.1 < e.symm p.2)) ∧
      d = toAntisymmetrization TuringReducible
        (fun n ↦ Part.some
          (if n % 2 = 0 then e (f (e.symm (n / 2))) else (X (n / 2)).toNat))

/-- **Conjecture 4.16**. Two block functions have incomparable degree spectra on a cone.

Containment on a cone is interpreted as eventual inclusion, as in Definition 2.4. -/
theorem conjecture_4_16 :
    ∃ f g : ℕ → ℕ,
      IsBlockFunction f ∧ IsBlockFunction g ∧
        (¬∃ X : ℕ → Bool,
          ∀ Y : ℕ → Bool,
            TuringReducible (fun n ↦ Part.some (X n).toNat)
              (fun n ↦ Part.some (Y n).toNat) →
            relativeDegreeSpectrum f Y ⊆ relativeDegreeSpectrum g Y) ∧
        ¬∃ X : ℕ → Bool,
          ∀ Y : ℕ → Bool,
            TuringReducible (fun n ↦ Part.some (X n).toNat)
              (fun n ↦ Part.some (Y n).toNat) →
            relativeDegreeSpectrum g Y ⊆ relativeDegreeSpectrum f Y := by
  sorry

end Damaj2025Relation

theorem Damaj2025Relation.conjecture_4_16_neg : ¬ type_of% @Damaj2025Relation.conjecture_4_16 := by
  sorry

title: The Discrete Harmonic Cohomology Module on Networks
problem_statement: In dana2015discrete.lean, prove either Dana2015Discrete.conjecture_4_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Dana2015Discrete.conjecture_4_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Discrete Harmonic Cohomology Module on Networks

Authors: Will Dana, David Jekel, Collin Litterell, and Austin Stromme.
Origin: [University of Washington REU 2015](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~reu/papers/2015/).
Reference: W. Dana, D. Jekel, C. Litterell, and A. Stromme, *The discrete harmonic cohomology
module on networks*, University of Washington REU report (November 29, 2015), 35 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Dana2015Discrete

open scoped Real

/-- Reduction to the empty graph by boundary-edge deletion, removal of isolated boundary
vertices, boundary-spike contraction, and splitting boundary cutpoints (Section 1.1). -/
inductive QuasiLayerable : {V : Type} → [Finite V] → SimpleGraph V → Set V → Prop
  /-- The terminal graph has no vertices, not merely no edges. -/
  | empty {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (hV : IsEmpty V) : QuasiLayerable G boundary
  /-- Delete precisely one edge whose two endpoints are boundary vertices. -/
  | deleteBoundaryEdge {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (b c : V) (hb : b ∈ boundary) (hc : c ∈ boundary) (hbc : G.Adj b c)
      (next : QuasiLayerable (G.deleteEdges {s(b, c)}) boundary) :
      QuasiLayerable G boundary
  /-- Remove an isolated boundary vertex, retaining all other vertex labels. -/
  | deleteIsolatedBoundary {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (b : V) (hb : b ∈ boundary) (hisolated : ∀ v, ¬G.Adj b v)
      (next : QuasiLayerable (G.induce {v | v ≠ b}) {v | v.val ∈ boundary}) :
      QuasiLayerable G boundary
  /-- Remove a degree-one boundary vertex and promote its interior neighbor. -/
  | contractBoundarySpike {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (b i : V) (hb : b ∈ boundary) (hi : i ∉ boundary) (hbi : G.Adj b i)
      (hunique : ∀ v, G.Adj b v → v = i)
      (next : QuasiLayerable (G.induce {v | v ≠ b})
        {v | v.val ∈ boundary ∨ v.val = i}) : QuasiLayerable G boundary
  /-- Reduce each component of a disconnected graph independently. -/
  | components {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (hdisconnected : ¬G.Preconnected)
      (next : ∀ c : G.ConnectedComponent,
        QuasiLayerable (G.induce c.supp) {v | v.val ∈ boundary}) :
      QuasiLayerable G boundary
  /-- Split a boundary cutpoint into one copy per component of its deletion. -/
  | splitBoundaryCutpoint {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
      (b : V) (hb : b ∈ boundary) (hconnected : G.Connected)
      (hcut : ¬(G.induce {v | v ≠ b}).Preconnected)
      (next : ∀ c : (G.induce {v | v ≠ b}).ConnectedComponent,
        QuasiLayerable (G.induce (insert b (Subtype.val '' c.supp)))
          {v | v.val ∈ boundary}) : QuasiLayerable G boundary

/-- The Eisenstein integer ring, generated by a primitive cube root of unity in `ℂ`. -/
abbrev eisenstein :=
  (Subring.closure {Complex.exp (((2 * π / 3 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)} :
    Subring ℂ)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The module of harmonic potentials on a unit-conductance network (Section 1.2). -/
def harmonic {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (boundary : Set V)
    (w : G.edgeSet → eisensteinˣ) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module eisenstein M] :
    Submodule eisenstein (V → M) where
  carrier := {u | ∀ v, v ∉ boundary →
    (∑ n : G.neighborSet v, (w ⟨s(v, n.val), G.mem_edgeSet.mpr n.property⟩ : eisenstein) •
      (u v - u n.val)) = 0}
  zero_mem' := by simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u t hu ht v hv
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, add_sub_add_comm, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    rw [hu v hv, ht v hv, add_zero]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu v hv
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply]
    calc
      _ = ∑ n : G.neighborSet v, c •
          ((w ⟨s(v, n.val), G.mem_edgeSet.mpr n.property⟩ : eisenstein) •
            (u v - u n.val)) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro n hn
        rw [← smul_sub, smul_comm]
      _ = c • (∑ n : G.neighborSet v,
          (w ⟨s(v, n.val), G.mem_edgeSet.mpr n.property⟩ : eisenstein) •
            (u v - u n.val)) := Finset.smul_sum.symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hu v hv, smul_zero]

/-- **Conjecture 4.1** (p. 18). Over the Eisenstein ring, every non-quasi-layerable boundary
graph admits unit conductances with nonzero first harmonic cohomology.

Via Proposition 2.1, nonzero cohomology is a harmonic fraction-field quotient potential with no
harmonic lift; no nonsingularity is assumed, and the ring is fixed, unlike Conjecture 3.10. -/
theorem conjecture_4_1 {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (boundary : Set (Fin n)) (hconnected : G.Connected)
    (hboundary : boundary.Nonempty) (hnot : ¬QuasiLayerable G boundary) :
    let integralLattice :=
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap eisenstein (FractionRing eisenstein))
    ∃ w : G.edgeSet → eisensteinˣ,
      ∃ u : harmonic G boundary w (FractionRing eisenstein ⧸ integralLattice),
        ¬∃ h : harmonic G boundary w (FractionRing eisenstein),
          ∀ v, integralLattice.mkQ (h.val v) = u.val v := by
  sorry

end Dana2015Discrete

theorem Dana2015Discrete.conjecture_4_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Dana2015Discrete.conjecture_4_1 := by
  sorry

title: Recurrence Relations for S-Legal Index Difference Sequences
problem_statement: In dantas2023recurrence.lean, prove either Dantas2023Recurrence.conjecture_2_8 or refute it by proving its logical negation Dantas2023Recurrence.conjecture_2_8_neg.

/-!
# Recurrence Relations for S-Legal Index Difference Sequences

Authors: Guilherme Zeus Dantas e Moura, Andrew Keisling, Astrid Lilly, Annika Mauro,
Steven J. Miller, Matthew Phang, and Santiago Velazquez Iannuzzelli.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU
2022](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/sjmiller/public_html/math/talks/SLIDs_FibConf2022.pdf).
Reference: G. Z. Dantas e Moura, A. Keisling, A. Lilly, A. Mauro, S. J. Miller, M. Phang, and
S. Velazquez Iannuzzelli, *Recurrence relations for S-legal index difference sequences*,
Fibonacci Quart. **61** (2023), no. 3, 257--274.
-/

namespace Dantas2023Recurrence

/-- The sequence whose terms are the least positive integers not represented by an `S`-legal sum
of earlier terms (Definition 1.9). The unused zeroth term is zero, and summands are restricted
to source indices `1, ..., n - 1`. -/
noncomputable def sLIDSequence (S : Finset ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  Nat.strongRec fun n previous ↦
    if n = 0 then 0 else
      sInf {m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧
        ∀ L : Finset (Fin n),
          (∀ i ∈ L, 0 < i.val) →
          (∀ i ∈ L, ∀ j ∈ L, Nat.dist i.val j.val ∉ S) →
          (∑ i ∈ L, previous i.val i.isLt) ≠ m}

/-- **Conjecture 2.8**. Deleting the difference `k - 1` from `{1, ..., k}` gives the recurrence
`a_(n+1) = a_n + a_(n-k)` for every `k ≥ 2` and `n > k + 1`. -/
theorem conjecture_2_8 (k n : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn : k + 1 < n) :
    sLIDSequence ((Finset.Icc 1 k).erase (k - 1)) (n + 1) =
      sLIDSequence ((Finset.Icc 1 k).erase (k - 1)) n +
        sLIDSequence ((Finset.Icc 1 k).erase (k - 1)) (n - k) := by
  sorry

end Dantas2023Recurrence

/-!
# Multiplicity-free gonality on graphs

Authors: Frances Dean, Max Everett, and Ralph Morrison.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2018 and 2020](https://math.williams.edu/small/).
Reference: F. Dean, M. Everett, and R. Morrison, *Multiplicity-free gonality on graphs*,
Electron. J. Graph Theory Appl. **11** (2023), no. 2, 357-380; doi:10.5614/ejgta.2023.11.2.2;
arXiv:2107.12955v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Dean2023Multiplicity

open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- Linear equivalence of divisors: their difference lies in the integer column image of the
Laplacian (Section 2).

The Laplacian counts edge occurrences, so parallel edges are retained. -/
def DivisorEquivalent {V E : Type*} {G : Graph V E} [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet]
    (D D' : G.vertexSet → ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ z : G.vertexSet → ℤ,
    D - D' = (Matrix.of fun x y : G.vertexSet ↦
      if x = y then (#{e : G.edgeSet | G.Inc e.val x.val} : ℤ)
      else -(#{e : G.edgeSet | G.IsLink e.val x.val y.val} : ℤ)).mulVec z

/-- The divisorial gonality: the minimum degree of a divisor of positive rank (Section 2).

Positive rank is encoded as every vertex carrying a chip in some effective equivalent divisor. -/
def gonality {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet] : ℤ :=
  sInf {degree : ℤ | ∃ D : G.vertexSet → ℤ,
    (∀ v, ∃ D' : G.vertexSet → ℤ, (∀ w, 0 ≤ D' w) ∧ 1 ≤ D' v ∧ DivisorEquivalent D D') ∧
      ∑ v, D v = degree}

/-- The multiplicity-free gonality: the minimum degree of a positive-rank divisor with every
coefficient `0` or `1` (Section 2). -/
def multiplicityFreeGonality {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet]
    [Fintype G.edgeSet] : ℤ :=
  sInf {degree : ℤ | ∃ D : G.vertexSet → ℤ,
    (∀ v, 0 ≤ D v ∧ D v ≤ 1) ∧
      (∀ v, ∃ D' : G.vertexSet → ℤ, (∀ w, 0 ≤ D' w) ∧ 1 ≤ D' v ∧ DivisorEquivalent D D') ∧
      ∑ v, D v = degree}

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Question 5.9** (Section 5.4, arXiv v1 p. 15). Some 3-regular graph has gonality strictly
less than its multiplicity-free gonality.

Graphs are finite connected loopless multigraphs, and 3-regularity counts incident edges rather
than neighbours. -/
theorem question_5_9 :
    ∃ n m : ℕ, ∃ G : Graph (Fin n) (Fin m),
      G.Loopless ∧ G.toSimpleGraph.Connected ∧
        (∀ v : G.vertexSet, #{e : G.edgeSet | G.Inc e.val v.val} = 3) ∧
        gonality G < multiplicityFreeGonality G := by
  sorry

end Dean2023Multiplicity

theorem Dean2023Multiplicity.question_5_9_neg : ¬ type_of% @Dean2023Multiplicity.question_5_9 := by
  sorry

title: Some Results in the Theory of Elastic Networks
problem_statement: In dejean2016results.lean, prove either Dejean2016Results.trees_are_extremal or refute it by proving its logical negation Dejean2016Results.trees_are_extremal_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Some Results in the Theory of Elastic Networks

Authors: Bat Dejean and Christian Gorski.
Origin: [Indiana University Bloomington REU
2016](https://math.indiana.edu/undergraduate/reu-summer-research-program/past-reu/2016-projects.html).
Reference: B. Dejean and C. Gorski, *Some Results in the Theory of Elastic Networks*, Indiana REU
Research Reports (2016), 74--108.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Dejean2016Results

/-- A finite marked elastic network, with positive resistance on each edge. -/
structure ElasticNetwork (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The number of vertices. -/
  vertexCount : ℕ
  /-- The number of edges. -/
  edgeCount : ℕ
  /-- The underlying finite graph on all vertices and edges. -/
  graph : Graph (Fin vertexCount) (Fin edgeCount)
  vertices : graph.vertexSet = Set.univ
  edges : graph.edgeSet = Set.univ
  /-- The `n` distinct marked vertices. -/
  marked : Fin n ↪ Fin vertexCount
  /-- The positive elasticity (resistance) of each edge. -/
  elasticity : Fin edgeCount → ℝ
  positive : ∀ e, 0 < elasticity e

/-- The Dirichlet energy of the geodesic extension of a vertex map. -/
def ElasticNetwork.dirichletEnergy {n : ℕ} (G : ElasticNetwork n)
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (f : Fin G.vertexCount → X) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e : Fin G.edgeCount,
    let h := (G.graph.edge_mem_iff_exists_isLink e).mp
      (by rw [G.edges]; exact Set.mem_univ e)
    let a := Classical.choose h
    let b := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec h)
    dist (f a) (f b) ^ 2 / G.elasticity e

/-- The Dirichlet energy of a marked homotopy class in a tree or real line. -/
def ElasticNetwork.harmonicEnergy {n : ℕ} (G : ElasticNetwork n)
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (boundary : Fin n → X) : ℝ :=
  sInf {E : ℝ | ∃ f : Fin G.vertexCount → X,
    (∀ i, f (G.marked i) = boundary i) ∧ E = G.dirichletEnergy f}

/-- Electrical equivalence, expressed through the boundary-voltage energy form. -/
def ElectricallyEquivalent {n : ℕ} (G H : ElasticNetwork n) : Prop :=
  ∀ boundary : Fin n → ℝ, G.harmonicEnergy boundary = H.harmonicEnergy boundary

/-- **Conjecture 6.1**. An elastic tree has no greater harmonic Dirichlet energy than any
electrically equivalent elastic graph, for every pipe-tree target.

Pipe trees are given by geodesic four-point metrics on finite vertex spans, zero-length edges
are collapsed, and harmonic energy is the Definition 1.3 infimum, not an attained minimum. -/
theorem trees_are_extremal
    {n : ℕ} (T G : ElasticNetwork n) [T.graph.Simple]
    (hT : T.graph.toSimpleGraph.IsTree) (h : ElectricallyEquivalent T G)
    {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [Nonempty X]
    (geodesic : ∀ x y : X, ∃ γ : ℝ → X,
      γ 0 = x ∧ γ (dist x y) = y ∧
      ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (dist x y),
        ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (dist x y),
          dist (γ s) (γ t) = |s - t|)
    (fourPoint : ∀ w x y z : X,
      dist w x + dist y z ≤
        max (dist w y + dist x z) (dist w z + dist x y))
    (boundary : Fin n → X) :
    T.harmonicEnergy boundary ≤ G.harmonicEnergy boundary := by
  sorry

end Dejean2016Results

theorem Dejean2016Results.trees_are_extremal_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Dejean2016Results.trees_are_extremal.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Optimal Bounds for the Number of Pieces of Real Near-Circuit Hypersurfaces
problem_statement: In deng2025optimal.lean, prove either Deng2025Optimal.three_components_in_every_dimension or refute it by proving its logical negation Deng2025Optimal.three_components_in_every_dimension_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Optimal Bounds for the Number of Pieces of Real Near-Circuit Hypersurfaces

Authors: Weixun Deng, J. Maurice Rojas, and Cordelia Russell.
Origin: [Texas A&M University REU
2024](https://artsci.tamu.edu/mathematics/academics/undergraduate/research/reu/results/results-2024.html).
Reference: W. Deng, J. M. Rojas, and C. Russell, *Optimal bounds for the number of pieces of real
near-circuit hypersurfaces*, ISSAC 2025 (2025), 9 pp.; doi:10.1145/3747199.3747576.
-/

namespace Deng2025Optimal

open Finset

/-- No `n + 1` distinct support points lie in an affine hyperplane (p. 1). -/
def GenericSupport {n : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset (Fin n → ℝ), S ⊆ A → #S = n + 1 →
    AffineIndependent ℝ (fun a : S ↦ a.val)

/-- The positive zero set (p. 1). Exponents are arbitrary reals, as the p. 1 footnote permits. -/
def positiveZeroSet {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) →₀ ℝ) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {x | (∀ i, 0 < x i) ∧
    f.sum (fun a c ↦ c * ∏ i : Fin n, x i ^ a i) = 0}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Example 1.6, p. 2). In every dimension `n ≥ 4` a generic,
honest real-exponent near-circuit has exactly three positive connected components.

Unlike the separate upper-bound theorem, no smoothness or coefficient sign pattern is imposed. -/
theorem three_components_in_every_dimension (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) :
    ∃ f : (Fin n → ℝ) →₀ ℝ,
      #f.support = n + 3 ∧
      affineSpan ℝ (f.support : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) = ⊤ ∧
      GenericSupport f.support ∧
      Nonempty (ConnectedComponents (positiveZeroSet f) ≃ Fin 3) := by
  sorry

end Deng2025Optimal

theorem Deng2025Optimal.three_components_in_every_dimension_neg : ¬ type_of% @Deng2025Optimal.three_components_in_every_dimension := by
  sorry

program: Washington and Lee University Summer Research Scholars
title: Bounded ribbonlength for knot families and multi-twist Mobius bands
problem_statement: In denne2025bounded.lean, prove either Denne2025Bounded.conjecture_23 or refute it by proving its logical negation Denne2025Bounded.conjecture_23_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Bounded ribbonlength for knot families and multi-twist Mobius bands

Authors: Elizabeth Denne and Timi Patterson.
Origin: [Washington and Lee University Summer Research Scholars
2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18370v2).
Reference: E. Denne and T. Patterson, *Bounded ribbonlength for knot families and multi-twist
Mobius bands*, arXiv:2509.18370v2 (2025).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Denne2025Bounded

open scoped Real

/-- A fundamental region in the unfolded strip, cut along an oblique transversal of slope `a`. -/
abbrev PaperDomain (l w a : ℝ) (mobius : Bool) :=
  {z : ℂ // a * z.im ≤ z.re ∧
    z.re ≤ l + (if mobius then -a else a) * z.im ∧
    z.im ∈ Set.Icc (-w / 2) (w / 2)}

/-- A folded paper strip, whose flat folded map is encoded by ordered affine cuts and Euclidean
isometries on the intervening panels. The seam may be any fold, and cuts may subdivide an
unfolded panel without a new fold. -/
structure PaperStrip (width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}) where
  /-- The length of the fundamental region of the strip. -/
  length : ℝ
  length_pos : 0 < length
  /-- Whether the end identification produces a Mobius ribbon. -/
  mobius : Bool
  /-- The slope of the seam cut at which the strip ends are identified. -/
  seamSlope : ℝ
  /-- The total number of panels; one panel lies between each pair of consecutive cuts. -/
  panels : ℕ
  panels_pos : 0 < panels
  /-- The ordered affine cuts, each the line `x = a + b * y` given by `(a, b)`. -/
  cuts : Fin (panels + 1) → ℝ × ℝ
  first_cut : cuts 0 = (0, seamSlope)
  last_cut : cuts (Fin.last panels) = (length, if mobius then -seamSlope else seamSlope)
  ordered_cuts : ∀ i : Fin panels, ∀ y : ℝ,
    y ∈ Set.Icc (-(width : ℝ) / 2) ((width : ℝ) / 2) →
    (cuts i.castSucc).1 + (cuts i.castSucc).2 * y <
      (cuts i.succ).1 + (cuts i.succ).2 * y
  /-- The Euclidean isometry by which each panel is placed in the plane. -/
  panel : Fin panels → (ℂ ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] ℂ)
  /-- The flat folded map of the fundamental region into the plane. -/
  flatMap : C(PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius, ℂ)
  on_panel : ∀ i : Fin panels, ∀ z : PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius,
    (cuts i.castSucc).1 + (cuts i.castSucc).2 * z.val.im ≤ z.val.re →
    z.val.re ≤ (cuts i.succ).1 + (cuts i.succ).2 * z.val.im →
    flatMap z = panel i z.val
  end_match : ∀ x y : PaperDomain length width seamSlope mobius,
    x.val.re = seamSlope * x.val.im →
    y.val.re = length + (if mobius then -seamSlope else seamSlope) * y.val.im →
    x.val.im = (if mobius then -y.val.im else y.val.im) → flatMap x = flatMap y

/-- The end gluing of the intrinsic annulus or Mobius strip. -/
def PaperStrip.Seam {width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}} (R : PaperStrip width)
    (x y : PaperDomain R.length (width : ℝ) R.seamSlope R.mobius) : Prop :=
  x.val.re = R.seamSlope * x.val.im ∧
    y.val.re = R.length + (if R.mobius then -R.seamSlope else R.seamSlope) * y.val.im ∧
    x.val.im = (if R.mobius then -y.val.im else y.val.im)

/-- The topological ribbon surface. -/
abbrev PaperStrip.Surface {width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}} (R : PaperStrip width) := Quot R.Seam

/-- The continuous folded map on the glued paper surface. -/
def PaperStrip.surfaceMap {width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}} (R : PaperStrip width) :
    C(R.Surface, ℂ) where
  toFun := Quot.lift R.flatMap
    (fun x y h ↦ R.end_match x y h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2)
  continuous_toFun := continuous_quot_lift _ R.flatMap.continuous

/-- The intrinsic centerline points, parametrized proportionally to paper length. -/
def PaperStrip.corePoint {width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}} (R : PaperStrip width)
    (t : unitInterval) : R.Surface :=
  Quot.mk R.Seam ⟨⟨R.length * (t : ℝ), 0⟩, by
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [mul_zero] using mul_nonneg (le_of_lt R.length_pos) t.property.1
    · simp only [mul_zero, add_zero]
      nlinarith [t.property.2, R.length_pos]
    · linarith [width.property]
    · linarith [width.property]⟩

/-- Continuous, antisymmetric, transitive over-under information on distinct coincident points
(Denne--Kamp--Terry--Zhu, Definition 2.2). `true` means the first sheet is above the second. -/
structure CrossingInformation {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] (f : X → ℂ) where
  /-- Whether the first of two distinct coincident points lies above the second. -/
  isOver : {p : X × X // p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ f p.1 = f p.2} → Bool
  continuous_isOver : Continuous isOver
  reversed : ∀ p,
    isOver ⟨(p.val.2, p.val.1), Ne.symm p.property.1, p.property.2.symm⟩ = !(isOver p)
  transitive : ∀ x y z (hxy : x ≠ y) (hyz : y ≠ z) (hxz : x ≠ z)
    (fxy : f x = f y) (fyz : f y = f z),
    isOver ⟨(x, y), hxy, fxy⟩ = true → isOver ⟨(y, z), hyz, fyz⟩ = true →
    isOver ⟨(x, z), hxz, fxy.trans fyz⟩ = true

/-- The finitely many intrinsic ribbon components of a link, all with a single positive width
(Section 2.1). -/
structure RibbonPaper where
  /-- The common positive width of all ribbon components. -/
  width : {w : ℝ // 0 < w}
  /-- The number of ribbon components. -/
  components : ℕ
  components_pos : 0 < components
  /-- The paper strip of each component. -/
  strip : Fin components → PaperStrip width

/-- The disjoint union of the glued paper surfaces. -/
abbrev RibbonPaper.Surface (R : RibbonPaper) :=
  (i : Fin R.components) × (R.strip i).Surface

/-- The folded map of the whole ribbon link, with the disjoint-union topology. -/
def RibbonPaper.surfaceMap (R : RibbonPaper) : C(R.Surface, ℂ) where
  toFun p := (R.strip p.1).surfaceMap p.2
  continuous_toFun := continuous_sigma (fun i ↦ (R.strip i).surfaceMap.continuous)

/-- The intrinsic link centerline inside the whole paper surface. The seam quotients close each
component's centerline before heights are assigned. -/
abbrev RibbonPaper.Core (R : RibbonPaper) :=
  {x : R.Surface // ∃ t : Fin R.components × unitInterval,
    x = ⟨t.1, (R.strip t.1).corePoint t.2⟩}

/-- An allowed folded ribbon link, with one continuous sheet order on all coincident surface
points. The core height must realize every induced crossing; no framing or regular projection
is fixed. -/
structure FoldedRibbonLink where
  /-- The underlying ribbon components. -/
  paper : RibbonPaper
  /-- The over-under information on all coincident surface points. -/
  crossing : CrossingInformation paper.surfaceMap
  /-- The height function on the intrinsic core giving its spatial lift. -/
  height : C(paper.Core, ℝ)
  height_order : ∀ x y : paper.Core,
    ∀ (hne : x.val ≠ y.val)
      (heq : paper.surfaceMap x.val = paper.surfaceMap y.val),
    crossing.isOver ⟨(x.val, y.val), hne, heq⟩ = true ↔ height y < height x

/-- The spatial core of all components, using the height compatible with the whole-surface
order. -/
def FoldedRibbonLink.spatialCore (R : FoldedRibbonLink) :
    C(R.paper.Core, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) where
  toFun x := WithLp.toLp 2 ![(R.paper.surfaceMap x.val).re,
    (R.paper.surfaceMap x.val).im, R.height x]
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : Fin 3 ↦ ℝ)).comp
    exact ((Complex.continuous_re.comp
      (R.paper.surfaceMap.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val)).finCons
      ((Complex.continuous_im.comp
        (R.paper.surfaceMap.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val)).finCons
        (R.height.continuous.finCons continuous_const)))

/-- The closed two-strand braid with `q` half-twists on the standard unknotted torus. Both
antipodal strands are present, giving one component for odd `q` and two for even `q`. -/
def torusLink (q : ℤ) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :=
  Set.range (fun p : Fin 2 × unitInterval ↦
    let longitude := 2 * π * (p.2 : ℝ)
    let meridian := (q : ℝ) * π * (p.2 : ℝ) + (p.1.val : ℝ) * π
    WithLp.toLp 2
      ![(2 + Real.cos meridian) * Real.cos longitude,
        (2 + Real.cos meridian) * Real.sin longitude, Real.sin meridian])

/-- **Conjecture 23** (p. 19). For every integer `q ≥ 11`, the infimal folded ribbonlength of the
full `(2,q)`-torus link is `8 * √3`.

The ratio uses total core length and a common width, and only the ambient link type is fixed;
even `q` is included, as in the source. -/
theorem conjecture_23 (q : ℤ) (hq : 11 ≤ q) :
    IsGLB {r : ℝ | ∃ R : FoldedRibbonLink,
      (∃ H : unitInterval →
          (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
        Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
        Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦
          (H p.1).symm p.2) ∧
        H 0 = Homeomorph.refl (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ∧
        H 1 '' torusLink q = Set.range R.spatialCore) ∧
      r = (∑ i : Fin R.paper.components, (R.paper.strip i).length) /
        (R.paper.width : ℝ)} (8 * √3) := by
  sorry

end Denne2025Bounded

theorem Denne2025Bounded.conjecture_23_neg : ¬ type_of% @Denne2025Bounded.conjecture_23 := by
  sorry

title: Balls Isoperimetric in R^n with Volume and Perimeter Densities r^m and r^k
problem_statement: In di2016balls.lean, prove either Di2016Balls.centered_balls_unique or refute it by proving its logical negation Di2016Balls.centered_balls_unique_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Balls Isoperimetric in R^n with Volume and Perimeter Densities r^m and r^k

Authors: Leonardo Di Giosia, Jahangir Habib, Lea Kenigsberg, Dylanger Pittman, and Weitao Zhu.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2016](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05830v2).
Reference: L. Di Giosia, J. Habib, L. Kenigsberg, D. Pittman, and W. Zhu, *Balls Isoperimetric
in R^n with Volume and Perimeter Densities r^m and r^k*, arXiv:1610.05830 (2016), revised 2019.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Di2016Balls

open scoped ENNReal

/-- The volume with radial density `r ^ m` (Notation 2.1). -/
def radialVolumeMeasure (n : ℕ) (m : ℝ) :
    MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
  MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensity MeasureTheory.volume
    (fun x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (‖x‖ ^ m))

/-- The perimeter with radial density `r ^ k`, as weighted distributional variation. For `n ≥ 2`
and `k > 0` it agrees with the source's weighted perimeter up to null modifications. -/
def radialPerimeter (n : ℕ) (k : ℝ)
    (E : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (F : TestFunction
    (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1),
  ⨆ (_ : ∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ ^ k),
    ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x in E,
      LinearMap.trace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (fderiv ℝ F x).toLinearMap)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (corrected abstract, p. 1). Centered balls uniquely minimize
weighted perimeter at every positive finite weighted volume throughout the inclusive stability
range.

The domain `n ≥ 2` follows the cited predecessor and the source's `n > 1` lemmas; no convexity
of the generating curve is assumed, and uniqueness is up to null sets. McGillivray (J. Geom.
Anal. 33 (2023), art. 344, Theorem 1.1) proves planar uniqueness in a restricted range. -/
theorem centered_balls_unique
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (m k : ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : 0 < k)
    (hstable : m ≤ k - k / ((n : ℝ) + k - 1))
    (v : ℝ≥0∞) (hv : 0 < v) (hvfinite : v < ⊤) :
    ∃ r > (0 : ℝ),
      radialVolumeMeasure n m (Metric.ball 0 r) = v ∧
      ∀ E : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),
        MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet E MeasureTheory.volume →
        radialVolumeMeasure n m E = v →
        radialPerimeter n k (Metric.ball 0 r) ≤ radialPerimeter n k E ∧
          (radialPerimeter n k E = radialPerimeter n k (Metric.ball 0 r) →
            radialVolumeMeasure n m (symmDiff E (Metric.ball 0 r)) = 0) := by
  sorry

end Di2016Balls

theorem Di2016Balls.centered_balls_unique_neg : ¬ type_of% @Di2016Balls.centered_balls_unique := by
  sorry

title: Isoperimetric problems in sectors with density
problem_statement: In diaz2012isoperimetric.lean, prove either Diaz2012Isoperimetric.conjecture_4_18 or refute it by proving its logical negation Diaz2012Isoperimetric.conjecture_4_18_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Isoperimetric problems in sectors with density

Authors: Alexander Diaz, Nate Harman, Sean Howe, and David Thompson.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2009](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/fmorgan/G09.pdf).
Reference: A. Diaz, N. Harman, S. Howe, and D. Thompson, *Isoperimetric problems in sectors with
density*, Adv. Geom. **12** (2012), 589--619.
-/

open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped Real ENNReal

noncomputable section

namespace Diaz2012Isoperimetric

/-- The weighted area for density `r ^ p`, in unwrapped polar coordinates (Section 2). -/
def sectorArea (p : ℝ) (E : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∫⁻ x in E, ENNReal.ofReal (x.1 ^ (p + 1))

/-- The relative weighted perimeter in the sector, given by the distributional flux in polar
coordinates (Section 2). Boundary rays are not counted. -/
def sectorPerimeter (p θ : ℝ) (E : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (F : (ℝ × ℝ) → (ℝ × ℝ)) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 F)
    (_ : HasCompactSupport F)
    (_ : tsupport F ⊆ {x | 0 < x.1 ∧ 0 < x.2 ∧ x.2 < θ})
    (_ : ∀ x, (F x).1 ^ 2 + (F x).2 ^ 2 ≤ 1),
    ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x in E,
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.1 ^ (p + 1) * (F y).1) x) (1, 0) +
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.1 ^ p * (F y).2) x) (0, 1))

/-- **Conjecture 4.18**. For every positive density exponent, the two transition angles in
Theorem 4.17 are `π / √(p + 1)` and `π * (p + 2) / (2 * p + 2)`.

The centered-circle part has a later resolution; both angles are retained. -/
theorem conjecture_4_18 (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    let U := fun θ : ℝ ↦
      {x : ℝ × ℝ | 0 < x.1 ∧ 0 < x.2 ∧ x.2 < θ}
    let D := fun R : ℝ ↦
      {x : ℝ × ℝ | 0 < x.1 ∧ 0 < x.2 ∧ x.2 < π / 2 ∧
        x.1 < 2 * R * Real.cos x.2}
    sSup {θ : ℝ | 0 < θ ∧
      ∀ R > (0 : ℝ), ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
        MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ U θ →
          sectorArea p E = sectorArea p {x : ℝ × ℝ | x ∈ U θ ∧ x.1 < R} →
          sectorPerimeter p θ {x : ℝ × ℝ | x ∈ U θ ∧ x.1 < R} ≤ sectorPerimeter p θ E} =
        π / √(p + 1) ∧
    sInf {θ : ℝ | π / 2 ≤ θ ∧
      ∀ R > (0 : ℝ), ∀ E : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
        MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ U θ → sectorArea p E = sectorArea p (D R) →
          sectorPerimeter p θ (D R) ≤ sectorPerimeter p θ E} =
        π * (p + 2) / (2 * p + 2) := by
  sorry

end Diaz2012Isoperimetric

# Matroids with cycle systems are regular

Authors: Anton Dochtermann, Evan Huang, Kai Mawhinney, Suho Oh, and Yuchen Xu.
Origin: [Texas State University REU 2025](https://summerreu.wp.txstate.edu/home/123-2/).

/-- The elements lying in exactly one member of the collection (Definition 2.13). -/
def uniqueUnion {α : Type*} (C : Finset (Set α)) : Set α :=

elements contained in at least three system circuits are independent. -/

    (hUnion : M.IsCircuit (uniqueUnion C)) :
    M.Indep {e ∈ M.E | 3 ≤ #{A ∈ C | e ∈ A}} := by
  sorry

title: Generalizations of Alder's conjecture via Kang--Park
problem_statement: In duncan2020generalizations.lean, prove either Duncan2020Generalizations.conjecture_1_5_generalized_kang_park or refute it by proving its logical negation Duncan2020Generalizations.conjecture_1_5_generalized_kang_park_neg.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Generalizations of Alder's conjecture via Kang--Park

Authors: Adriana L. Duncan, Simran Khunger, Holly Swisher, and Ryan Tamura.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2020](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/reucv.html).
Reference: A. L. Duncan, S. Khunger, H. Swisher, and R. Tamura, *Generalizations of Alder's
Conjecture via a Conjecture of Kang and Park*, arXiv:2010.08646.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Duncan2020Generalizations

open Finset

/-- The count `q_d^{(a)}(n)` of partitions into parts at least `a` with successive parts differing
by at least `d` (Section 1). -/
def q (d a n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{lam : Nat.Partition n | (∀ x ∈ lam.parts, a ≤ x) ∧
      (lam.parts.sort (· ≤ ·)).IsChain (fun x y : ℕ ↦ x + d ≤ y)}

/-- The count `Q_d^{(b,-,-)}(n)` of partitions into parts congruent to `±b` modulo `d + 3`,
excluding both `b` and `d + 3 - b` (before Conjecture 1.5). -/
def QminusMinus (d b n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{lam : Nat.Partition n | ∀ x ∈ lam.parts,
      (x % (d + 3) = b % (d + 3) ∨ x % (d + 3) = (d + 3 - b) % (d + 3)) ∧
        x ≠ b ∧ x ≠ d + 3 - b}

/-- The signed difference `Delta_d^{(a,b,-,-)}(n)`. -/
def DeltaMinusMinus (d a b n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (q d a n : ℤ) - (QminusMinus d b n : ℤ)

/-- **Conjecture 1.5**. For positive `a, d` with `a ≤ d + 2`, all positive `n` satisfy
`Delta_d^{(a,a,-,-)}(n) ≥ 0`. -/
theorem conjecture_1_5_generalized_kang_park (a d n : ℕ)
    (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (had : a ≤ d + 2) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    0 ≤ DeltaMinusMinus d a a n := by sorry

end Duncan2020Generalizations

title: Geodesics with Two Self-Intersections on the Punctured Torus
problem_statement: In dziadosz1994geodesics.lean, prove either Dziadosz1994Geodesics.conjecture_4_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Dziadosz1994Geodesics.conjecture_4_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Geodesics with Two Self-Intersections on the Punctured Torus

Authors: Susan Dziadosz, Thomas Insel, and Peter Wiles.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
1994](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/reucv.html).
Reference: S. Dziadosz, T. Insel, and P. Wiles, *Geodesics with Two Self-Intersections on the
Punctured Torus*, Oregon State University REU report (1994), 29--50.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Dziadosz1994Geodesics

/-- The first generator of the modular commutator group (p. 29). -/
def A : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℤ :=
  ⟨!![1, 1; 1, 2], by norm_num [Matrix.det_fin_two]⟩

/-- The second generator of the modular commutator group (p. 29). -/
def B : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℤ :=
  ⟨!![1, -1; -1, 2], by norm_num [Matrix.det_fin_two]⟩

/-- The fixed matrix realization, inverse to the marking `theta` after projection to the modular
group (p. 31). -/
def rho : FreeGroup (Fin 2) →* Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℤ :=
  FreeGroup.lift ![A, B]

/-- The real binary quadratic form `a * X ^ 2 + b * X * Y + c * Y ^ 2` of p. 48. -/
def binaryForm (a b c : ℝ) : QuadraticForm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ) :=
  a • QuadraticMap.proj 0 0 + b • QuadraticMap.proj 0 1 +
    c • QuadraticMap.proj 1 1

/-- The absolute infimum `m(f)` over all nonzero integer pairs (p. 48). -/
def markoffMinimum (f : QuadraticForm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ)) : ℝ :=
  sInf {v : ℝ | ∃ p q : ℤ,
    (p ≠ 0 ∨ q ≠ 0) ∧ v = |f ![(p : ℝ), (q : ℝ)]|}

/-- The normalized value `M(f)` with literal discriminant `b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c` (p. 48). It is
meaningful only for positive discriminant and infimum, as required in its use below. -/
def markoffValue (a b c : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  √(b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c) / markoffMinimum (binaryForm a b c)

/-- The finite real Markoff spectrum of all real indefinite forms (p. 48). Forms with zero
infimum are excluded by the positivity guard. -/
def markoffSpectrum : Set ℝ :=
  {v | ∃ a b c : ℝ, 0 < b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ∧
    0 < markoffMinimum (binaryForm a b c) ∧ v = markoffValue a b c}

/-- **Conjecture 4.2** (p. 49). Every automorphic image of `a a b a b⁻¹` has its associated value
isolated in the Markoff spectrum.

The associated value is that of the form `t * X ^ 2 + (u - r) * X * Y - s * Y ^ 2` of the matrix
`[[r, s], [t, u]]` representing the image under the fixed marking, with no automorphism filtered;
the 1998 successor paper's limit-at-3 result is not isolation. -/
theorem conjecture_4_2 (g : MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin 2))) :
    let a := FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2)
    let b := FreeGroup.of (1 : Fin 2)
    let U := rho (g (a * a * b * a * b⁻¹))
    let v := markoffValue (U 1 0 : ℝ) ((U 1 1 : ℝ) - (U 0 0 : ℝ)) (-(U 0 1 : ℝ))
    v ∈ markoffSpectrum ∧
      ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ w ∈ markoffSpectrum, |w - v| < ε → w = v := by
  sorry

end Dziadosz1994Geodesics

theorem Dziadosz1994Geodesics.conjecture_4_2_neg : ¬ type_of% @Dziadosz1994Geodesics.conjecture_4_2 := by
  sorry

title: On the scramble number of graphs
problem_statement: In echavarria2022scramble.lean, prove either Echavarria2022Scramble.question_3_6 or refute it by proving its logical negation Echavarria2022Scramble.question_3_6_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the scramble number of graphs

Authors: Marino Echavarria, Max Everett, Robin Huang, Liza Jacoby, Ralph Morrison, and Ben Weber.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU](https://math.williams.edu/small/research-publications/).
Reference: M. Echavarria, M. Everett, R. Huang, L. Jacoby, R. Morrison, and B. Weber, *On the
scramble number of graphs*, Discrete Appl. Math. **310** (2022), 43-59; arXiv:2103.15253v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Echavarria2022Scramble

open Finset

/-- An explicitly labelled loopless multigraph, given by its vertex count and edge list.

Parallel edges are separate list entries, and isolated vertices are retained. -/
structure GraphInput where
  /-- The number of vertices. -/
  vertices : ℕ
  /-- The endpoints of each edge, in list order. -/
  ends : List (Fin vertices × Fin vertices)
  /-- Each edge lists its smaller endpoint first. -/
  ordered : ∀ e ∈ ends, e.1 < e.2

/-- The multigraph of an explicit edge list, with edges indexed by their list positions. -/
def GraphInput.toGraph (g : GraphInput) : Graph (Fin g.vertices) (Fin g.ends.length) where
  vertexSet := Set.univ
  edgeSet := Set.univ
  IsLink e u v := g.ends[e] = (u, v) ∨ g.ends[e] = (v, u)
  isLink_symm _ _ := ⟨fun _ _ h ↦ h.symm⟩
  eq_or_eq_of_isLink_of_isLink := by
    intro e x y v w hx hv
    rcases hx with hx | hx <;> rcases hv with hv | hv
    · exact Or.inl (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).1
    · exact Or.inr (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).1
    · exact Or.inr (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).2
    · exact Or.inl (Prod.mk.inj (hx.symm.trans hv)).2
  edge_mem_iff_exists_isLink e := by
    constructor
    · intro _
      exact ⟨g.ends[e].1, g.ends[e].2, Or.inl (Prod.eta _)⟩
    · intro _
      exact Set.mem_univ _
  left_mem_of_isLink := by
    intro _ _ _ _
    trivial

open scoped Classical in
/-- Decode a binary word as a graph: a unary vertex count followed by unary endpoint pairs, each
field terminated by `false`.

Malformed words, including out-of-range, looped or reversed pairs, decode to `none`. -/
def decodeGraph (input : List Bool) : Option GraphInput :=
  if input.getLast? ≠ some false then none else do
    let fields := (input.splitOn false).dropLast.map List.length
    match fields with
    | [] => none
    | n :: rest =>
      let rec /-- Reads the remaining fields in pairs as edges, rejecting out-of-range endpoints. -/
        readEdges : List ℕ → Option (List (Fin n × Fin n))
        | [] => some []
        | a :: b :: tail => do
          if ha : a < n then
            if hb : b < n then
              let edges ← readEdges tail
              some ((⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩) :: edges)
            else none
          else none
        | _ => none
      let edges ← readEdges rest
      if ho : ∀ e ∈ edges, e.1 < e.2 then
        some { vertices := n, ends := edges, ordered := ho }
      else none

/-- A scramble: a family of eggs, each a nonempty vertex set inducing a connected subgraph
(Section 2.2).

Eggs need not be disjoint, and the empty family is allowed. -/
def IsScramble (g : GraphInput) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin g.vertices))) : Prop :=
  ∀ egg ∈ S, egg.Nonempty ∧
    (g.toGraph.induce (egg : Set (Fin g.vertices))).toSimpleGraph.Connected

open scoped Classical in
/-- The order of a scramble: the largest `q` bounded by every hitting set and by every egg-cut
(Section 2.2).

The order is capped by the vertex count, and a family with no egg-cut imposes no cut bound. -/
def scrambleOrder (g : GraphInput) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin g.vertices))) : ℕ :=
  {q ∈ range (g.vertices + 1) |
    (∀ C : Finset (Fin g.vertices), (∀ egg ∈ S, (C ∩ egg).Nonempty) → q ≤ #C) ∧
    (∀ A : Finset (Fin g.vertices),
      (∃ egg ∈ S, egg ⊆ A) → (∃ egg ∈ S, egg ⊆ Aᶜ) →
        q ≤ (g.toGraph.edgeCut (A : Set (Fin g.vertices))).ncard)}.sup id

open scoped Classical in
/-- The scramble number: the maximum order of a scramble (Section 2.2).

The null graph has scramble number zero. -/
def scrambleNumber (g : GraphInput) : ℕ :=
  {S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin g.vertices)).powerset.powerset | IsScramble g S}.sup (scrambleOrder g)

/-- **Question 3.6** (Section 3, arXiv v3 p. 11). For each fixed `k`, whether the scramble number
of a graph is at most `k` can be decided in polynomial time.

Inputs are binary words in the unary encoding of `decodeGraph`, malformed words are rejected, and
each `k` has its own polynomial-time machine with finite stack alphabets. -/
theorem question_3_6 (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ decider : List Bool → Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id Computability.encodeBool decider,
        (∀ stack : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ stack)) ∧
        ∀ input : List Bool, decider input = true ↔
          ∃ g : GraphInput, decodeGraph input = some g ∧ scrambleNumber g ≤ k := by
  sorry

end Echavarria2022Scramble

theorem Echavarria2022Scramble.question_3_6_neg : ¬ type_of% @Echavarria2022Scramble.question_3_6 := by
  sorry

title: Zonotopes whose cellular strings are all coherent
problem_statement: In edman2021zonotopes.lean, prove either Edman2021Zonotopes.remark_3_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Edman2021Zonotopes.remark_3_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Zonotopes whose cellular strings are all coherent

Authors: Rob Edman, Pakawut Jiradilok, Gaku Liu, and Thomas McConville.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2015](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU2015notes/REU2015salvage.html).
Reference: R. Edman, P. Jiradilok, G. Liu, and T. McConville, *Zonotopes whose cellular strings
are all coherent*, arXiv:1801.09140v1 (2018).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Edman2021Zonotopes

open Finset

/-- A reduced antipodal gallery, encoded by its crossing order (Section 3.2). Every prefix is a
realizable chamber, with forms oriented positively on the fundamental chamber. -/
def Gallery {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) :=
  {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m) // ∀ k : Fin (m + 1), ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ,
    ∀ j : Fin m, if j.val < k.val then a (σ j) x < 0 else 0 < a (σ j) x}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The codimension-two intersection flats, counted as subspaces, not as choices of generating
hyperplanes (Section 3.2). -/
def rankTwoFlats {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) :
    Finset (Submodule ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)) :=
  {X ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).powerset.image
      (fun S ↦ ⨅ i ∈ S, LinearMap.ker (a i)) |
    Module.finrank ℝ ((Fin n → ℝ) ⧸ X) = 2}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The localization: the crossing order of hyperplanes containing the given intersection flat
(Section 3.2). -/
def localizedGallery {n m : ℕ} {a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ}
    (X : Submodule ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)) (γ : Gallery a) : List (Fin m) :=
  (List.ofFn γ.val).filter (fun i ↦ decide (X ≤ LinearMap.ker (a i)))

open scoped Classical in
/-- The L2-separation set of two reduced galleries (Section 3.2). -/
def separationSet {n m : ℕ} {a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ}
    (γ γ' : Gallery a) : Finset (Submodule ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)) :=
  {X ∈ rankTwoFlats a | localizedGallery X γ ≠ localizedGallery X γ'}

/-- Two galleries are adjacent exactly when their L2-separation set has cardinality one
(Remark 3.3). -/
def galleryGraph {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) :
    SimpleGraph (Gallery a) where
  Adj γ γ' := #(separationSet γ γ') = 1
  symm := by
    constructor
    intro γ γ' h
    simpa only [separationSet, ne_comm] using h
  loopless := by
    constructor
    intro γ
    simp [separationSet]

/-- A cellular string: an ordered partition into nonempty blocks, each with a realizable face
vanishing exactly on its block (Section 3.2). The empty partition is the trivial string. -/
structure CellularString {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) where
  /-- The number of blocks of the ordered partition. -/
  blocks : ℕ
  /-- The block containing each hyperplane index. -/
  block : Fin m → Fin blocks
  onto : Function.Surjective block
  realizable : ∀ k : Fin blocks, ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ,
    (∀ i, block i < k → a i x < 0) ∧
    (∀ i, block i = k → a i x = 0) ∧
    (∀ i, k < block i → 0 < a i x)

/-- **Remark 3.3**. All-pairs gallery distance equal to L2-separation cardinality implies
all-coherence.

Coherence uses the cellular-string and block-ratio description of Section 3.2 and Lemma 3.2,
the source's halfspace names are swapped, and no rank or essentiality restriction is imposed. -/
theorem remark_3_3 {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
    (hhyperplanes : ∀ i, a i ≠ 0)
    (hdistinct : Function.Injective (fun i ↦ LinearMap.ker (a i)))
    (b : Fin n → ℝ) (hchamber : ∀ i, 0 < a i b)
    (hdistance : ∀ γ γ' : Gallery a,
      (galleryGraph a).edist γ γ' = (#(separationSet γ γ') : ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ π : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < a i π) ∧
      ∀ s : CellularString a, ∃ ψ : Fin n → ℝ,
        (∀ i j, s.block i = s.block j → a i ψ / a i π = a j ψ / a j π) ∧
        (∀ i j, s.block i < s.block j → a i ψ / a i π < a j ψ / a j π) := by
  sorry

end Edman2021Zonotopes

theorem Edman2021Zonotopes.remark_3_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Edman2021Zonotopes.remark_3_3 := by
  sorry

title: Affine standard Lyndon words
source_label: Conjecture 6.27 (arXiv; Conjecture 6.26 in the June 19, 2025 author revision)
problem_statement: In elkins2025affine.lean, prove either Elkins2025Affine.conjecture_6_27 or refute it by proving its logical negation Elkins2025Affine.conjecture_6_27_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Affine standard Lyndon words

Authors: Corbet Elkins and Alexander Tsymbaliuk.
Origin: [Purdue University REU 2025](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~otsymbal/Papers/AffineSL.pdf).
Reference: C. Elkins and A. Tsymbaliuk, *Affine standard Lyndon words*, preprint (2025);
arXiv:2505.15432.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Elkins2025Affine

open Finset

/-- A nonempty word smaller than every nonempty proper suffix (Definition 2.3). -/
def IsLyndon {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (w : List A) : Prop :=
  w ≠ [] ∧ ∀ n > 0, n < w.length → w < w.drop n

open scoped Classical in
/-- The cut of the costandard factorization: the longest proper Lyndon suffix. -/
def costandardCut {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (w : List A) : ℕ :=
  let cuts := {n ∈ Finset.range w.length | 0 < n ∧ IsLyndon (w.drop n)}
  if h : cuts.Nonempty then cuts.min' h else 0

open scoped Classical in
/-- The standard prefix, namely the longest proper Lyndon prefix (Proposition 2.7). -/
def standardPrefix {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (w : List A) : List A :=
  w.take (({n ∈ Finset.range w.length | IsLyndon (w.take n)}).sup id)

/-- The remaining suffix of the standard factorization (Proposition 2.7). -/
def standardSuffix {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (w : List A) : List A :=
  w.drop (standardPrefix w).length

/-- Standard bracketing by the costandard factorization (Definition 2.11). Values lie in
Mathlib's Serre construction `Matrix.ToLieAlgebra`; only the empty word gets the junk value 0. -/
def standardBracket {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (a : Matrix A A ℤ)
    (w : List A) : Matrix.ToLieAlgebra ℂ a :=
  if h : w.length = 1 then
    LieSubmodule.Quotient.mk
      (FreeLieAlgebra.of ℂ (CartanMatrix.Generators.E (w[0]'(by omega))))
  else
    let n := costandardCut w
    if hcut : 0 < n ∧ n < w.length then
      ⁅standardBracket a (w.take n), standardBracket a (w.drop n)⁆
    else 0
termination_by w.length
decreasing_by
  · simp only [List.length_take]; omega
  · simp only [List.length_drop]; omega

/-- Standard Lyndon words: the bracket is outside the span of larger Lyndon
brackets in the reverse-length/lexicographic order (Definition 2.14). -/
def IsStandardLyndon {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (a : Matrix A A ℤ)
    (w : List A) : Prop :=
  IsLyndon w ∧ standardBracket a w ∉ Submodule.span ℂ
    {x | ∃ v : List A, IsLyndon v ∧
      (v.length < w.length ∨ (v.length = w.length ∧ w < v)) ∧
      x = standardBracket a v}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The standard Lyndon words of a degree in decreasing lexicographic order (Section 2.24).
Indices are zero-based, and indices outside the list return the empty word. -/
def standardWord {A : Type*} [Fintype A] [LinearOrder A]
    (a : Matrix A A ℤ) (d : A → ℕ) (i : ℕ) : List A :=
  let words := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (∑ j, d j) → A)).image List.ofFn
  let selected := {w ∈ words | (∀ j, w.count j = d j) ∧ IsStandardLyndon a w}
  (selected.sort (fun u v ↦ v ≤ u)).getD i []

section RootSystem

variable {R V W : Type*} [Fintype R]
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℝ W]
  {P : RootPairing R ℝ V W} [P.IsCrystallographic] (b : P.Base)

/-- The untwisted affine Cartan matrix (Section 2.22). The extra letter `none` represents
minus the highest finite root. -/
def affineCartan (θ : R) : Matrix (Option b.support) (Option b.support) ℤ
  | none, none => 2
  | none, some j => -P.pairingIn ℤ j θ
  | some i, none => -P.pairingIn ℤ θ i
  | some i, some j => P.pairingIn ℤ j i

/-- The coefficients of the minimal imaginary root `δ = α₀ + θ`. -/
def imaginaryRoot (θ : R) : Option b.support → ℕ
  | none => 1
  | some j => (b.toWeightBasisInt.repr (P.rootSpanMem ℤ θ) j).toNat

omit [Fintype R] in
/-- **Conjecture 6.27** (arXiv; Conjecture 6.26 in the June 19, 2025 author revision). Every
imaginary standard Lyndon word and its standard prefix repeat a fixed cyclic rotation of an
earlier degree-`δ` word.

All untwisted types, alphabet orders, indices and positive multiples are retained, not merely
eventual periodicity. -/
theorem conjecture_6_27 [Finite R] [Nonempty R] [P.IsRootSystem] [P.IsReduced] [P.IsIrreducible]
    (θ : R) (hθ : ∀ β : R, b.height β ≤ b.height θ)
    [LinearOrder (Option b.support)] (i : Fin #b.support) :
    let δ := imaginaryRoot b θ
    let a := affineCartan b θ
    let u := standardWord a δ i.val
    ∃ j : ℕ, j ≤ i.val ∧ ∃ w : List (Option b.support),
      List.IsRotated w (standardWord a δ j) ∧
      ∀ k > 0,
        let v := standardWord a (fun x ↦ k * δ x) i.val
        v = standardPrefix u ++
            (List.replicate (k - 1) w).flatten ++
              standardSuffix u ∧
        standardPrefix v = standardPrefix u ++
          (List.replicate (k - 1) w).flatten := by
  sorry

end RootSystem

end Elkins2025Affine

theorem Elkins2025Affine.conjecture_6_27_neg.{u0, u1, u2} : ¬ type_of% @Elkins2025Affine.conjecture_6_27.{u0, u1, u2} := by
  sorry

title: On the cardinality of minimal presentations of numerical semigroups
problem_statement: In elmacioglu2024cardinality.lean, prove either Elmacioglu2024Cardinality.conjecture_7_1_embedding_dimension_four_families_complete or refute it by proving its logical negation Elmacioglu2024Cardinality.conjecture_7_1_embedding_dimension_four_families_complete_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the cardinality of minimal presentations of numerical semigroups

Authors: Ceyhun Elmacioglu, Kieran Hilmer, Christopher O'Neill, Melin Okandan,
and Hannah Park-Kaufmann.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2021](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu).
Reference: C. Elmacioglu, K. Hilmer, C. O'Neill, M. Okandan, and H. Park-Kaufmann, *On the
cardinality of minimal presentations of numerical semigroups*, arXiv:2211.16283.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Elmacioglu2024Cardinality

/-- A numerical monoid, given by its positive minimal generators. -/
structure NumericalMonoid where
  /-- The embedding dimension, the number of minimal generators. -/
  embDim : ℕ
  /-- The minimal generators, in increasing order. -/
  gen : Fin embDim → ℕ
  positive_gen : ∀ i : Fin embDim, 0 < gen i
  strictMono_gen : StrictMono gen
  irreducible_gen : ∀ i : Fin embDim, ∀ a b : ℕ,
    a ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure (Set.range gen) →
      b ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure (Set.range gen) →
        gen i = a + b → a = 0 ∨ b = 0
  minimal_gen : ∀ i : Fin embDim,
    gen i ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure {m : ℕ | ∃ j : Fin embDim, j ≠ i ∧ gen j = m}
  cofinite : Set.Finite {n : ℕ | n ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure (Set.range gen)}

namespace NumericalMonoid

/-- The least generator `n₁` in the paper's one-indexed notation. -/
def leastGenerator (Γ : NumericalMonoid) : ℕ :=
  if h : 0 < Γ.embDim then Γ.gen ⟨0, h⟩ else 0

/-- The factorization homomorphism `φ : ℕ^e → S`, evaluated as a natural number through the
chosen generators of `S`. -/
def factorizationValue (S : NumericalMonoid)
    (a : Fin S.embDim → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin S.embDim, a i * S.gen i

/-- A trade (relation): a pair of factorizations of a numerical monoid. -/
abbrev Trade (S : NumericalMonoid) := (Fin S.embDim → ℕ) × (Fin S.embDim → ℕ)

/-- A presentation: all listed trades preserve the factorization homomorphism, and the
congruence they generate is exactly its kernel congruence. -/
def IsPresentation (S : NumericalMonoid) (ρ : Set (Trade S)) : Prop :=
  (∀ r ∈ ρ,
    factorizationValue S r.1 =
      factorizationValue S r.2) ∧
  ∀ a b : Fin S.embDim → ℕ,
    factorizationValue S a =
        factorizationValue S b ↔
      addConGen (fun x y ↦ (x, y) ∈ ρ) a b

/-- A minimal presentation: no proper subset remains a presentation. -/
def IsMinimalPresentation (S : NumericalMonoid) (ρ : Set (Trade S)) : Prop :=
  IsPresentation S ρ ∧ ∀ τ : Set (Trade S), τ ⊂ ρ → ¬IsPresentation S τ

/-- The invariant `η(S)`: every minimal presentation has cardinality `η`. -/
def MinimalPresentationCardinality (S : NumericalMonoid) (η : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∃ ρ : Set (Trade S), ρ.Finite ∧ IsMinimalPresentation S ρ ∧ ρ.ncard = η) ∧
    ∀ ρ : Set (Trade S), ρ.Finite → IsMinimalPresentation S ρ → ρ.ncard = η

end NumericalMonoid

open NumericalMonoid

/-- **Conjecture 7.1**. For embedding dimension `4`, the families from Theorems 4.2 and 6.3 and
Proposition 6.2 attain all possible values of `η` for each multiplicity `m ≥ 4`. -/
theorem conjecture_7_1_embedding_dimension_four_families_complete
    (m η : ℕ) (hm : 4 ≤ m)
    (h : ∃ S : NumericalMonoid, S.embDim = 4 ∧ S.leastGenerator = m ∧
      NumericalMonoid.MinimalPresentationCardinality S η) :
    (∃ r s : ℕ, m = r + 4 ∧ s ≤ Nat.min (4 - 2) r ∧ η = Nat.choose 4 2 - s) ∨
      (8 ≤ m ∧ η = 3) ∨
        (6 ≤ η ∧ (η - 2) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m) := by
  sorry

end Elmacioglu2024Cardinality

theorem Elmacioglu2024Cardinality.conjecture_7_1_embedding_dimension_four_families_complete_neg : ¬ type_of% @Elmacioglu2024Cardinality.conjecture_7_1_embedding_dimension_four_families_complete := by
  sorry

title: On Solving the Inverse Conductivity Problem for Annular Networks
problem_statement: In esser2000solving.lean, prove either Esser2000Solving.conjecture_4_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Esser2000Solving.conjecture_4_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On Solving the Inverse Conductivity Problem for Annular Networks

Author: Ernie Esser.
Origin: [University of Washington REU 2000](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~reu/papers/2000/).
Reference: E. Esser, *On Solving the Inverse Conductivity Problem for Annular Networks*,
August 2000 (appendix added 2005).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Esser2000Solving

open scoped Classical in
/-- The pairwise conductance, summing over all edges with the two given ends, parallel edges
included (Curtis-Morrow, p. 27). -/
def conductance {V E : Type*} [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (w : E → ℝ) :
    Matrix V V ℝ :=
  fun x y ↦ ∑ e, if G.IsLink e x y then w e else 0

open scoped Classical in
/-- The weighted Kirchhoff matrix (Esser p. 3; Curtis-Morrow pp. 33-34). Loop contributions
cancel on the diagonal. -/
def kirchhoff {V E : Type*} [Fintype V] [Fintype E]
    (G : Graph V E) (w : E → ℝ) : Matrix V V ℝ :=
  Matrix.diagonal (fun x ↦ ∑ y, conductance G w x y) - conductance G w

open scoped Classical in
/-- The response matrix on the six boundary labels, given by the Schur complement formula
(Esser p. 3; Curtis-Morrow pp. 42-43). -/
def response {I E : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype E]
    (G : Graph (Fin 6 ⊕ I) E) (w : E → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 6) (Fin 6) ℝ :=
  let K := kirchhoff G w
  K.submatrix Sum.inl Sum.inl -
    K.submatrix Sum.inl Sum.inr * (K.submatrix Sum.inr Sum.inr)⁻¹ *
      K.submatrix Sum.inr Sum.inl

/-- Esser's graph G(3,2) with the fifteen edges of pp. 32-33 (Figure 3). Source vertices
1, ..., 12 are `Sum.inl 0`, ..., `Sum.inl 5`, `Sum.inr 0`, ..., `Sum.inr 5` in order. -/
def annularGraph : Graph (Fin 6 ⊕ Fin 6) (Fin 15) :=
  let ends : Fin 15 → (Fin 6 ⊕ Fin 6) × (Fin 6 ⊕ Fin 6) :=
    ![(Sum.inl 0, Sum.inr 0), (Sum.inl 1, Sum.inr 1), (Sum.inl 2, Sum.inr 2),
      (Sum.inl 3, Sum.inr 3), (Sum.inl 4, Sum.inr 4), (Sum.inl 5, Sum.inr 5),
      (Sum.inr 0, Sum.inr 1), (Sum.inr 1, Sum.inr 2), (Sum.inr 0, Sum.inr 2),
      (Sum.inr 3, Sum.inr 4), (Sum.inr 4, Sum.inr 5), (Sum.inr 3, Sum.inr 5),
      (Sum.inr 0, Sum.inr 3), (Sum.inr 1, Sum.inr 4), (Sum.inr 2, Sum.inr 5)]
  { vertexSet := Set.univ
    edgeSet := Set.univ
    IsLink := fun e x y ↦ (x = (ends e).1 ∧ y = (ends e).2) ∨
      (x = (ends e).2 ∧ y = (ends e).1)
    isLink_symm := by
      intro e _
      exact ⟨fun x y h ↦ h.elim (fun h ↦ Or.inr ⟨h.2, h.1⟩)
        (fun h ↦ Or.inl ⟨h.2, h.1⟩)⟩
    eq_or_eq_of_isLink_of_isLink := by
      intro e x y v z h h'
      exact h.elim
        (fun h ↦ h'.elim (fun h' ↦ Or.inl (h.1.trans h'.1.symm))
          (fun h' ↦ Or.inr (h.1.trans h'.2.symm)))
        (fun h ↦ h'.elim (fun h' ↦ Or.inr (h.1.trans h'.2.symm))
          (fun h' ↦ Or.inl (h.1.trans h'.1.symm)))
    edge_mem_iff_exists_isLink := by
      intro e
      constructor
      · intro _
        exact ⟨(ends e).1, (ends e).2, Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩
      · intro _
        trivial
    left_mem_of_isLink := by intros; trivial }

/-- **Conjecture 4.1** (p. 18; inequality list p. 13). A finite positive six-boundary W2
network has a response realizable by positive conductances on G(3,2) if and only if the cubic
relation and all thirteen ordered strict minor inequalities hold.

Boundary label `k + 1` is `Sum.inl k`, and all `Sum.inr` vertices are interior. Loops and
parallel edges are allowed and every component meets the boundary; no embedding, global
connectedness or nonempty interior is required (Curtis-Morrow, pp. 11, 27, 30 and 39). -/
theorem conjecture_4_1 {I E : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype E]
    (G : Graph (Fin 6 ⊕ I) E)
    (hV : G.vertexSet = Set.univ) (hE : G.edgeSet = Set.univ)
    (w : E → ℝ) (hw : ∀ e, 0 < w e)
    (hW2 : ∀ v, ∃ b : Fin 6,
      Relation.ReflTransGen G.Adj v (Sum.inl b)) :
    let L := response G w
    (∃ γ : Fin 15 → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 < γ e) ∧ response annularGraph γ = L) ↔
      (L.submatrix ![0, 1, 3] ![2, 4, 5]).det -
        (L.submatrix ![0, 3, 4] ![1, 2, 5]).det = 0 ∧
      (L.submatrix ![0, 1, 2] ![3, 4, 5]).det < 0 ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 1, 4] ![2, 3, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![1, 0, 3] ![2, 4, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![1, 2, 4] ![0, 3, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![1, 2, 5] ![0, 4, 3]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 2, 3] ![1, 4, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 2, 5] ![1, 3, 4]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 1] ![3, 4]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![1, 2] ![4, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 2] ![3, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 3] ![1, 4]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![0, 3] ![2, 5]).det ∧
      0 < (L.submatrix ![1, 4] ![2, 5]).det := by
  sorry

end Esser2000Solving

theorem Esser2000Solving.conjecture_4_1_neg.{u0, u1} : ¬ type_of% @Esser2000Solving.conjecture_4_1.{u0, u1} := by
  sorry

title: Spectral Analysis of the Kohn Laplacian on Lens Spaces
problem_statement: In fan2023spectral.lean, prove either Fan2023Spectral.kohn_spectral_rigidity or refute it by proving its logical negation Fan2023Spectral.kohn_spectral_rigidity_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Spectral Analysis of the Kohn Laplacian on Lens Spaces

Authors: Colin Fan, Elena Kim, Zoe Plzak, Ian Shors, Samuel Sottile,
and Yunus E. Zeytuncu.
Origin: [University of Michigan-Dearborn REU](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12220-022-01164-y).
Reference: C. Fan, E. Kim, Z. Plzak, I. Shors, S. Sottile, and Y. E. Zeytuncu, *Spectral
Analysis of the Kohn Laplacian on Lens Spaces*, J. Geom. Anal. **33** (2023), Article 116.
-/

namespace Fan2023Spectral

open Finset

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction, p. 1). The Kohn spectrum determines the
CR-isometry class of every three-dimensional lens space.

The spectrum is encoded by the multiplicities of all positive eigenvalues `2m` (Theorem 1.4 and
Proposition 1.5), since the zero eigenspace is infinite-dimensional for all these spaces. The
conclusion is the unit-and-permutation classification of CR isometry, not Riemannian isometry. -/
theorem kohn_spectral_rigidity (k k' : ℕ) (weights weights' : Fin 2 → ℤ)
    (hk : 0 < k) (hk' : 0 < k')
    (hweights : ∀ i, Int.gcd (weights i) (k : ℤ) = 1)
    (hweights' : ∀ i, Int.gcd (weights' i) (k' : ℤ) = 1) :
    let multiplicity : ℕ → (Fin 2 → ℤ) → ℕ → ℕ := fun k weights m ↦
      #{exponents : (Fin 2 → Fin (m + 1)) × (Fin 2 → Fin (m + 1)) |
          let a := exponents.1
          let b := exponents.2
          0 < (b 0).val + (b 1).val ∧
          ((b 0).val + (b 1).val) * ((a 0).val + (a 1).val + 1) = m ∧
          ((a 0).val = 0 ∨ (b 0).val = 0) ∧
          (k : ℤ) ∣ weights 0 * ((a 0).val - (b 0).val : ℤ) +
            weights 1 * ((a 1).val - (b 1).val : ℤ)}
    ((∀ m > 0, multiplicity k weights m = multiplicity k' weights' m) ↔
        k = k' ∧ ∃ (a : ℤ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 2)),
          Int.gcd a (k : ℤ) = 1 ∧
          ∀ i, Int.ModEq (k : ℤ) (weights' i) (a * weights (σ i))) := by
  sorry

end Fan2023Spectral

theorem Fan2023Spectral.kohn_spectral_rigidity_neg : ¬ type_of% @Fan2023Spectral.kohn_spectral_rigidity := by
  sorry

title: Algebraic Properties of the Ideal of Spectral Invariants for the Discrete Laplacian
problem_statement: In faust2026algebraic.lean, prove either Faust2026Algebraic.conjecture_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Faust2026Algebraic.conjecture_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Algebraic Properties of the Ideal of Spectral Invariants for the Discrete Laplacian

Authors: Matthew Faust, Leo Friedman, Gavin O'Malley, Rolando Ramos, and Aaryan Sharma.
Origin: [Michigan State University SURIEM](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2244461.json).
Reference: M. Faust, L. Friedman, G. O'Malley, R. Ramos, and A. Sharma, *Algebraic properties
of the ideal of spectral invariants for the discrete Laplacian*, preprint (2026), 17 pp.;
arXiv:2602.08304v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Faust2026Algebraic

/-- The antisymmetric specialized potential (Section 4). For odd period the middle entry is 0. -/
def specializedPotential (q : ℕ) {R : Type*} [Zero R] [Neg R]
    (u : Fin (q / 2) → R) (i : Fin q) : R :=
  if h : i.val < q / 2 then u ⟨i.val, h⟩
  else if h : q - 1 - i.val < q / 2 then -u ⟨q - 1 - i.val, h⟩
  else 0

/-- The specialized ideal `I'` generated by the even spectral invariants (Section 4). -/
def specializedIdeal (q : ℕ) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (q / 2)) ℂ) :=
  let A := (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph q).adjMatrix (MvPolynomial (Fin (q / 2)) ℂ)
  let U := specializedPotential q MvPolynomial.X
  let ζ := (A + Matrix.diagonal U).charpoly - A.charpoly
  Ideal.span (Set.range (fun k : Fin (q / 2) ↦
    (-1) ^ (k.val + 1) * ζ.coeff (q - 2 * (k.val + 1))))

/-- The scheme-theoretic multiplicity of a point (Section 3). It uses the ideal, not its radical. -/
def pointMultiplicity (q : ℕ) (u : Fin (q / 2) → ℂ) :=
  let P := MvPolynomial (Fin (q / 2)) ℂ
  let S := Localization.AtPrime (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal ℂ {u})
  Module.length S (S ⧸ (specializedIdeal q).map (algebraMap P S))

/-- **Conjecture 3**. The local multiplicities of `I'` at zero and at its nonzero points are
classified by the parity of the period.

The Section 5 nonzero-solution convention applies to the singular orbit, whose symmetries are
negation and conjugation (Remark 4). -/
theorem conjecture_3 (q : ℕ) (hq : 3 ≤ q) :
    pointMultiplicity q 0 = (2 : ENat) ^ (q / 2) ∧
    (Odd q → ∀ u ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus ℂ (specializedIdeal q),
      u ≠ 0 → pointMultiplicity q u = 1) ∧
    (Even q → 6 < q →
      ∃ u ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus ℂ (specializedIdeal q),
        u ≠ 0 ∧ pointMultiplicity q u = (2 : ENat) ^ (q / 2 - 2) ∧
        ∀ v ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus ℂ (specializedIdeal q), v ≠ 0 →
          (pointMultiplicity q v ≠ 1 ↔
            v = u ∨ v = -u ∨ v = (fun i ↦ star (u i)) ∨
              v = (fun i ↦ -star (u i)))) := by
  sorry

end Faust2026Algebraic

theorem Faust2026Algebraic.conjecture_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Faust2026Algebraic.conjecture_3 := by
  sorry

title: Crescent configurations in normed spaces
problem_statement: In fish2019crescent.lean, prove either Fish2019Crescent.eventually_no_strong_crescents or refute it by proving its logical negation Fish2019Crescent.eventually_no_strong_crescents_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Crescent configurations in normed spaces

Authors: Sara Fish, Dylan King, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson,
and Catherine Wahlenmayer.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2019](https://math.williams.edu/small/research-publications/).
Reference: S. Fish, D. King, S. J. Miller, E. A. Palsson, and C. Wahlenmayer, *Crescent
configurations in normed spaces*, Integers **20** (2020), Paper A96, 38 pp.; arXiv:1909.08769v2.
-/

namespace Fish2019Crescent

open Finset

/-- The distance-equality pattern agrees, after relabeling, with that of equally spaced points on
a line (Definition 2.10). -/
def IsLineLike (p : Seminorm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ)) (P : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : Fin #P ≃ P, ∀ i j k l,
    p ((e i : Fin 2 → ℝ) - e j) = p ((e k : Fin 2 → ℝ) - e l) ↔
      Nat.dist i.val j.val = Nat.dist k.val l.val

/-- No three points are collinear, no four lie on one norm-circle, and no four form a line-like
configuration (Definition 2.13). -/
def InStrongGeneralPosition (p : Seminorm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ))
    (P : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ Q ∈ P.powersetCard 3, ¬Collinear ℝ (Q : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ))) ∧
    ∀ Q ∈ P.powersetCard 4,
      (¬∃ c : Fin 2 → ℝ, ∃ r > (0 : ℝ), ∀ x ∈ Q, p (x - c) = r) ∧
      ¬IsLineLike p Q

/-- Strong general position with exactly `n - 1` distances, one of each multiplicity from 1 to
`n - 1` (Definition 2.15). -/
def IsStrongCrescent (p : Seminorm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ))
    (P : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)) : Prop := by
  classical
  let pairs := {z ∈ P.sym2 | ¬z.IsDiag}
  let length : Sym2 (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ := Sym2.lift
    ⟨fun x y ↦ p (x - y), fun x y ↦ by
      simpa only [neg_sub] using (map_neg_eq_map p (x - y)).symm⟩
  exact InStrongGeneralPosition p P ∧
    #(pairs.image length) = #P - 1 ∧
    ∀ i ≥ 1, i ≤ #P - 1 →
      ∃ r ∈ pairs.image length, #{z ∈ pairs | length z = r} = i

/-- **Conjecture 6.2** (p. 36). For each norm on the plane there is a threshold beyond which no
strong crescent configurations exist.

The threshold depends on the norm; positive definiteness turns the seminorm `p` into a norm. -/
theorem eventually_no_strong_crescents (p : Seminorm ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ))
    (hp : ∀ x, p x = 0 → x = 0) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ),
      N ≤ #P → ¬IsStrongCrescent p P := by
  sorry

end Fish2019Crescent

theorem Fish2019Crescent.eventually_no_strong_crescents_neg : ¬ type_of% @Fish2019Crescent.eventually_no_strong_crescents := by
  sorry

title: Intrinsically projectively linked graphs
problem_statement: In foisy2022intrinsically.lean, prove either Foisy2022Intrinsically.apex_obstruction_is_intrinsically_projectively_linked or refute it by proving its logical negation Foisy2022Intrinsically.apex_obstruction_is_intrinsically_projectively_linked_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Intrinsically projectively linked graphs

Authors: Joel Foisy, Luis Angel Topete Galvan, Evan Knowles, Uriel Alejandro Nolasco,
Yuanyuan Shen, and Lucy Wickham.
Origin: [SUNY Potsdam-Clarkson REU 2021](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.06877v1).
Reference: J. Foisy, L. A. Topete Galvan, E. Knowles, U. A. Nolasco, Y. Shen, and L. Wickham,
*Intrinsically projectively linked graphs*, preprint (2022), 29 pp.; arXiv:2206.06877.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Foisy2022Intrinsically

open scoped Classical in
/-- The geometric realization of a finite graph in real coordinates, with the subtype topology. -/
abbrev GraphRealization {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Type _ :=
  {x : V → ℝ // x ∈ Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite ℝ ℝ V ''
    (Geometry.SimplicialComplex.ofSimpleGraph G :
      Geometry.SimplicialComplex ℝ (V →₀ ℝ)).space}

/-- A finite graph minor, represented by disjoint connected nonempty branch sets. -/
def IsMinor {V W : Type*}
    (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (branch w)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ w₁ w₂, w₁ ≠ w₂ → Disjoint (branch w₁) (branch w₂)) ∧
    (∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ →
      ∃ v₁ ∈ branch w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ branch w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂)

/-- The quotient topology on real projective space. -/
scoped instance projectivizationTopology (d : ℕ) :
    TopologicalSpace (Projectivization ℝ (Fin (d + 1) → ℝ)) := by
  unfold Projectivization
  infer_instance

/-- A PL embedding of a graph in real projective space. PL is encoded by finitely many affine
lifts to the antipodal polyhedral sphere. -/
structure PLGraphEmbedding {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The underlying map from the graph realization to real projective space. -/
  toFun : GraphRealization G → Projectivization ℝ (Fin (d + 1) → ℝ)
  isEmbedding : Topology.IsEmbedding toFun
  piecewiseLinear : by
    classical
    exact ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
      ∃ k > 0,
      ∃ t : Fin (k + 1) → ℝ,
        StrictMono t ∧ t 0 = 0 ∧ t (Fin.last k) = 1 ∧
        ∃ a : Fin k → AffineMap ℝ ℝ (Fin (d + 1) → ℝ),
          ∀ j : Fin k, ∀ r : ℝ,
            r ∈ Set.Icc (t j.castSucc) (t j.succ) →
            ∃ hn : a j r ≠ 0,
              (∑ i, |a j r i|) = 1 ∧
              ∃ x : GraphRealization G,
                x.val = (1 - r) • Pi.single u (1 : ℝ) + r • Pi.single v (1 : ℝ) ∧
                toFun x = Projectivization.mk ℝ (a j r) hn

/-- A split pair has one component in a topological 3-ball disjoint from the other. -/
def IsSplit (L₁ L₂ : Set (Projectivization ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ))) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Set (Projectivization ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ)),
    Nonempty (A ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1) ∧
      ((L₁ ⊆ A ∧ Disjoint L₂ A) ∨ (L₂ ⊆ A ∧ Disjoint L₁ A))

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 3.7, p. 29). Adjoining a universal vertex to every
minor-minimal non-projective-planar graph gives an intrinsically projectively linked graph.

Proper minors exclude isomorphic copies, and PL maps are represented in the standard antipodal
polyhedral model. -/
theorem apex_obstruction_is_intrinsically_projectively_linked
    {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hG : ¬Nonempty (PLGraphEmbedding G 2))
    (hmin : ∀ (m : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)),
      IsMinor H G → ¬Nonempty (H ≃g G) → Nonempty (PLGraphEmbedding H 2)) :
    let J := G.sum (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) ⊔ completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) Unit
    ∀ f : PLGraphEmbedding J 3,
      ∃ u v, ∃ p : J.Walk u u, ∃ q : J.Walk v v,
          p.IsCycle ∧ q.IsCycle ∧
          Disjoint {x | x ∈ p.support} {x | x ∈ q.support} ∧
          let L₁ : Set (Projectivization ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ)) :=
            f.toFun '' {x : GraphRealization J |
              ∃ e ∈ p.darts, ∃ r : ℝ,
                r ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧
                x.val = (1 - r) • (Pi.single e.fst (1 : ℝ) : Fin n ⊕ Unit → ℝ) +
                  r • (Pi.single e.snd (1 : ℝ) : Fin n ⊕ Unit → ℝ)}
          let L₂ : Set (Projectivization ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ)) :=
            f.toFun '' {x : GraphRealization J |
              ∃ e ∈ q.darts, ∃ r : ℝ,
                r ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧
                x.val = (1 - r) • (Pi.single e.fst (1 : ℝ) : Fin n ⊕ Unit → ℝ) +
                  r • (Pi.single e.snd (1 : ℝ) : Fin n ⊕ Unit → ℝ)}
          ¬IsSplit L₁ L₂ := by
  sorry

end Foisy2022Intrinsically

theorem Foisy2022Intrinsically.apex_obstruction_is_intrinsically_projectively_linked_neg : ¬ type_of% @Foisy2022Intrinsically.apex_obstruction_is_intrinsically_projectively_linked := by
  sorry

/-!
# Growth functions of finitely generated algebras

Authors: Eric Fredette, Dan Kubala, Eric Nelson, Kelsey Wells, and Harold W. Ellingsen, Jr.
Origin: [SUNY Potsdam-Clarkson REU 2012](https://people.clarkson.edu/~ctamon/reu/reu-papers.html).
Reference: E. Fredette, D. Kubala, E. Nelson, K. Wells, and H. W. Ellingsen, Jr., *Growth
functions of finitely generated algebras*, Involve **8** (2015), 71-74;
doi:10.2140/involve.2015.8.71.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Fredette2015Growth

open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number of normal words of length at most `n` (p. 71). Letters `false` and `true` are
the two free generators, and by the p. 71 basis convention this is the growth function of the
monomial quotient. -/
def growthFunction (relations : Finset (List Bool)) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{w ∈ (List.finite_length_le Bool n).toFinset | ∀ r ∈ relations, ¬r <:+: w}

/-- **Final conjecture** (p. 74). The upper bound for polynomial growth degree is attained for
every maximal defining-word length `d + 1` with `d ≥ 2`.

Polynomial growth degree means asymptotic order, not equality to one polynomial at every
argument. -/
theorem sharp_growth_bound (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    ∃ relations : Finset (List Bool),
      (∀ r ∈ relations, r.length ≤ d + 1) ∧
      (∃ r ∈ relations, r.length = d + 1) ∧
      Asymptotics.IsTheta Filter.atTop
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (growthFunction relations n : ℝ))
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^
          ((∑ k ∈ d.divisors, Nat.totient k * 2 ^ (d / k)) / d)) := by
  sorry

end Fredette2015Growth
