  sorry

title: Extremal Arithmetic in Numerical Semigroups
problem_statement: In fry2014extremal.lean, prove either Fry2014Extremal.goldmember_conjecture or refute it by proving its logical negation Fry2014Extremal.goldmember_conjecture_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Extremal Arithmetic in Numerical Semigroups

Authors: Andy Fry, Sarah McConnell, Claire Spychalla, Zofia Stanley, and Brandon Van Over.
Origin: [San Diego State University REU 2014](https://cdoneill.sdsu.edu/reu/research.html).
Reference: A. Fry, S. McConnell, C. Spychalla, Z. Stanley, and B. Van Over, *Extremal
Arithmetic in Numerical Semigroups*, SDSU Mathematics REU, August 8, 2014, 79 pp.
-/

namespace Fry2014Extremal

open Finset

/-- All nonnegative coefficient factorizations over the listed generators (Section 1). -/
def factorizations (A : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Set (A → ℕ) :=
  {c | ∑ g : A, c g * g.val = m}

/-- The lengths of all factorizations of an element (Section 1). -/
def lengthSet (A : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  (fun c : A → ℕ ↦ ∑ g, c g) '' factorizations A m

/-- All successive length gaps over the entire generated monoid (Section 1). -/
def deltaSet (A : Finset ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {d | ∃ m : ℕ,
    m ∈ (AddSubmonoid.closure (A : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ) ∧
      ∃ l r : lengthSet A m, CovBy l r ∧ d = r.val - l.val}

/-- A nonempty positive set with odd maximum meeting each complementary pair about that maximum
(Definitions 4.3-4.4). -/
def IsGolden (G : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  G.Nonempty ∧ (∀ g : G, 0 < g.val) ∧ Odd (G.sup id) ∧
    ∀ j > 0, j < G.sup id →
      j ∈ (G : Set ℕ) ∨ G.sup id - j ∈ (G : Set ℕ)

/-- **Conjecture 4.22** (Goldmember; p. 46). A changed delta set requires a missing golden or
reflected golden set of index `⌊t / 2⌋`.

Golden sets are read in generator-offset coordinates, as in the source's examples and tables,
not in affine generator values; this is the full necessary condition, not Conjecture 4.23. -/
theorem goldmember_conjecture (a x t : ℕ) (I : Finset ℕ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hx : 0 < x) (ht : 0 < t) (hat : t < a)
    (hcoprime : Nat.Coprime a x)
    (hI : I ≤ Finset.range (t + 1))
    (hzero : 0 ∈ (I : Set ℕ)) (hlast : t ∈ (I : Set ℕ))
    (hcard : 2 ≤ #I) (hindex : (I.erase 0).gcd id = 1) :
    (∀ g : (Finset.range (t + 1)).image (fun i ↦ a + i * x),
      g.val ∉ (AddSubmonoid.closure
        (((Finset.range (t + 1)).image (fun i ↦ a + i * x)).erase g.val : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ)) →
    (∀ g : I.image (fun i ↦ a + i * x),
      g.val ∉ (AddSubmonoid.closure
        ((I.image (fun i ↦ a + i * x)).erase g.val : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ)) →
    deltaSet (I.image (fun i ↦ a + i * x)) ≠ ({x} : Set ℕ) →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ G : Finset ℕ,
      0 < N ∧ N = t / 2 ∧ IsGolden G ∧ G.sup id = 2 * N - 1 ∧
        (G ≤ Finset.Ioo 0 t \ I ∨ G.image (fun g ↦ t - g) ≤ Finset.Ioo 0 t \ I) := by
  sorry

end Fry2014Extremal

theorem Fry2014Extremal.goldmember_conjecture_neg : ¬ type_of% @Fry2014Extremal.goldmember_conjecture := by
  sorry

title: K-Knuth Equivalence for Increasing Tableaux
problem_statement: In gaetz2016k.lean, prove either Gaetz2016K.conjecture_4_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gaetz2016K.conjecture_4_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# K-Knuth Equivalence for Increasing Tableaux

Authors: Christian Gaetz, Michelle Mastrianni, Rebecca Patrias, Hailee Peck,
Colleen Robichaux, David Schwein, and Ka Yu Tam.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2014](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: C. Gaetz, M. Mastrianni, R. Patrias, H. Peck, C. Robichaux, D. Schwein, and K. Y. Tam,
*K-Knuth equivalence for increasing tableaux*, Electron. J. Combin. **23** (2016), no. 1,
Paper 1.40; arXiv:1409.6659v2.
-/

namespace Gaetz2016K

/-- A straight increasing tableau with positive integer labels (Section 2.1). -/
structure IncreasingTableau where
  /-- The Young diagram giving the straight shape. -/
  shape : YoungDiagram
  /-- The positive integer label in each box of the shape. -/
  entry : {b : ℕ × ℕ // b ∈ shape} → ℕ+
  increasing : ∀ a b, a.val ≤ b.val → a.val ≠ b.val → entry a < entry b

/-- The reading word: each row left to right, starting at the bottom row (Section 2.4). -/
noncomputable def rowWord (T : IncreasingTableau) : List ℕ+ :=
  ((T.shape.cells.attach.toList.mergeSort fun a b ↦
    decide (b.val.1 < a.val.1 ∨ (a.val.1 = b.val.1 ∧ a.val.2 ≤ b.val.2))).map
      (fun b ↦ T.entry ⟨b.val, b.property⟩))

/-- The four K-Knuth moves in an arbitrary word context (Section 2.3). -/
inductive KKnuthMove : List ℕ+ → List ℕ+ → Prop
  | duplicate (u v : List ℕ+) (x : ℕ+) :
      KKnuthMove (u ++ [x] ++ v) (u ++ [x, x] ++ v)
  | braid (u v : List ℕ+) (x y : ℕ+) :
      KKnuthMove (u ++ [x, y, x] ++ v) (u ++ [y, x, y] ++ v)
  | firstKnuth (u v : List ℕ+) (x y z : ℕ+) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) :
      KKnuthMove (u ++ [x, z, y] ++ v) (u ++ [z, x, y] ++ v)
  | secondKnuth (u v : List ℕ+) (x y z : ℕ+) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) :
      KKnuthMove (u ++ [y, x, z] ++ v) (u ++ [y, z, x] ++ v)

/-- **Conjecture 4.3** (arXiv; published Conjecture 57). Equivalent tableaux can be connected
through words no longer than the largest tableau in their entire K-Knuth class. -/
theorem conjecture_4_3 (T T' : IncreasingTableau)
    (h : Relation.EqvGen KKnuthMove (rowWord T) (rowWord T')) :
    ∃ k : ℕ,
      IsGreatest {m : ℕ | ∃ U : IncreasingTableau,
        Relation.EqvGen KKnuthMove (rowWord T) (rowWord U) ∧ U.shape.card = m} k ∧
      ∃ path : List (List ℕ+),
        path.head? = some (rowWord T) ∧ path.getLast? = some (rowWord T') ∧
        path.IsChain (Relation.SymmGen KKnuthMove) ∧
        ∀ w ∈ path, w.length ≤ k := by
  sorry

end Gaetz2016K

theorem Gaetz2016K.conjecture_4_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gaetz2016K.conjecture_4_3 := by
  sorry

title: Support Equalities Among Ribbon Schur Functions
problem_statement: In gaetz2019support.lean, prove either Gaetz2019Support.conjecture_4_8 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gaetz2019Support.conjecture_4_8_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Support Equalities Among Ribbon Schur Functions

Authors: Marisa Gaetz, Will Hardt, and Shruthi Sridhar.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2017](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: M. Gaetz, W. Hardt, and S. Sridhar, *Support equalities among ribbon Schur
functions*, preprint; arXiv:1709.03011v2.
-/

namespace Gaetz2019Support

open Finset

/-- The cells of a ribbon with rows read top to bottom, adjacent rows overlapping in one column
(Section 2.2). Coordinates increase downward and rightward. -/
def ribbonCells {m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  Finset.univ.biUnion fun r : Fin m ↦
    (Finset.range (a r)).image fun c ↦
      (r.val, ∑ s : Fin m with r < s, (a s - 1) + c)

/-- The Schur support, via the Littlewood-Richardson tableaux of Corollary 2.10 (Definition 2.1).
Labels are zero-based, and prefixes are read right to left, then top to bottom. -/
def schurSupport (D : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) : Set YoungDiagram :=
  {μ | ∃ T : D → ℕ,
    (∀ b c : D, b.val.1 = c.val.1 → b.val.2 < c.val.2 → T b ≤ T c) ∧
    (∀ b c : D, b.val.2 = c.val.2 → b.val.1 < c.val.1 → T b < T c) ∧
    (∀ (b : D) (i : ℕ),
      #{c : D | (c.val.1 < b.val.1 ∨ (c.val.1 = b.val.1 ∧ b.val.2 ≤ c.val.2)) ∧
          T c = i + 1} ≤
      #{c : D | (c.val.1 < b.val.1 ∨ (c.val.1 = b.val.1 ∧ b.val.2 ≤ c.val.2)) ∧
          T c = i}) ∧
    (∀ i : ℕ, #{b : D | T b = i} = μ.rowLen i)}

/-- **Conjecture 4.8** (p. 21). A decreasing ribbon has the same Schur support under every
permutation of its rows exactly when all the stated inequalities for `N_j` hold. -/
theorem conjecture_4_8 {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (a : Fin m → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 2 ≤ a i) (horder : Antitone a) :
    (∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin m),
      schurSupport (ribbonCells a) = schurSupport (ribbonCells (fun i ↦ a (p i)))) ↔
    (∀ j ≥ 1, j + 2 ≤ m →
      sSup {k : ℕ | ∑ i : Fin m with i.val < j, (k - a i) ≤ m - j - 2} <
        (∑ i : Fin m with j ≤ i.val, a i) - (m - j - 2)) := by
  sorry

end Gaetz2019Support

theorem Gaetz2019Support.conjecture_4_8_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gaetz2019Support.conjecture_4_8 := by
  sorry

problem_statement: In gallian1979cyclotomic.lean, prove either Gallian1979Cyclotomic.conjecture_largest_label_log_bound or refute it by proving its logical negation Gallian1979Cyclotomic.conjecture_largest_label_log_bound_neg.

/-!
# Cyclotomic polynomials and nonstandard dice

Authors: Joseph A. Gallian and David J. Rusin.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 1977](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: J. A. Gallian and D. J. Rusin, *Cyclotomic polynomials and nonstandard dice*,
Discrete Math. **27** (1979), 245-259.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gallian1979Cyclotomic

open Polynomial

/-- The standard die of size `m`, with labels `1, 2, …, m`. -/
def standardDiePolynomial (m : ℕ) : ℤ[X] :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, X ^ k

/-- An `n`-dice game of dice-size `m`, expressed by equality of sum-generating
polynomials with `n` standard dice. -/
def IsNDiceGame (n m : ℕ) (dice : Fin n → ℤ[X]) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Fin n,
    (∀ k : ℕ, 0 ≤ (dice i).coeff k) ∧ (dice i).coeff 0 = 0 ∧
      (dice i).Monic ∧ (dice i).eval 1 = (m : ℤ)) ∧
    ∏ i : Fin n, dice i = (standardDiePolynomial m) ^ n

/-- `P` is a solution die of dice-size `m` for some nontrivial dice game. -/
def IsSolutionDie (m : ℕ) (P : ℤ[X]) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, 1 < n ∧ ∃ dice : Fin n → ℤ[X],
    IsNDiceGame n m dice ∧ ∃ i : Fin n, dice i = P

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Theorem 6, p. 254). Every label of a solution die of size
`m` is at most `m log m / (2 log 2) + 1`, with equality attainable for powers of two. -/
theorem conjecture_largest_label_log_bound
    (m L : ℕ) (hm : 1 < m) (P : ℤ[X]) (hP : IsSolutionDie m P)
    (hL : 0 < P.coeff L) :
    (L : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * Real.log (m : ℝ) / (2 * Real.log 2) + 1 := by
  sorry

end Gallian1979Cyclotomic

title: Non-monotonicity of closed convexity in neural codes
problem_statement: In gambacini2022non.lean, prove either Gambacini2022Non.conjecture_3_13 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gambacini2022Non.conjecture_3_13_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Non-monotonicity of closed convexity in neural codes

Authors: Brianna Gambacini, R. Amzi Jeffs, Sam Macdonald, and Anne Shiu.
Origin: [Texas A&M University REU
2019](https://artsci.tamu.edu/mathematics/academics/undergraduate/research/reu/results/results-2019.html).
Reference: B. Gambacini, R. A. Jeffs, S. Macdonald, and A. Shiu, *Non-monotonicity of closed
convexity in neural codes*, Vietnam J. Math. **50** (2022), 359-373; arXiv:1912.00963v3.
-/

namespace Gambacini2022Non

open Convexity

/-- The complete membership patterns of the sets on stimulus space `X` (Definition 2.3). -/
def code {n d : ℕ} (U : Fin n → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Set (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  {σ | ∃ x ∈ X, ∀ i, x ∈ U i ↔ i ∈ σ}

/-- Realization by ambient-open convex sets in a stimulus subset of some Euclidean space
(Definition 2.4). -/
def IsOpenConvex {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (U : Fin n → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
    (∀ i, U i ⊆ X ∧ IsOpen (U i) ∧ Convex ℝ (U i)) ∧ C = code U X

/-- Realization by ambient-closed convex sets in a stimulus subset of some Euclidean space
(Definition 2.4). -/
def IsClosedConvex {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (U : Fin n → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
    (∀ i, U i ⊆ X ∧ IsClosed (U i) ∧ Convex ℝ (U i)) ∧ C = code U X

/-- The simplicial complex generated by the code (Definition 2.10). Following Mathlib, only
nonempty faces are stored. -/
def codeComplex {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Finset (Fin n))) : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin n) where
  faces := {σ | σ.Nonempty ∧ ∃ α ∈ C, σ ⊆ α}
  isRelLowerSet_faces := by
    intro σ hσ
    refine ⟨hσ.1, ?_⟩
    intro τ hτσ hτ
    obtain ⟨α, hα, hσα⟩ := hσ.2
    exact ⟨hτ, α, hα, hτσ.trans hσα⟩

/-- The link of a face (Definition 2.13). Only nonempty faces are stored. -/
def link {n : ℕ} (K : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin n)) (σ : Finset (Fin n)) :
    PreAbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin n) where
  faces := {τ | τ.Nonempty ∧ Disjoint σ τ ∧ σ ∪ τ ∈ K}
  isRelLowerSet_faces := by
    intro τ hτ
    refine ⟨hτ.1, ?_⟩
    intro υ hυτ hυ
    refine ⟨hυ, Finset.disjoint_of_subset_right hυτ hτ.2.1, ?_⟩
    exact (K.isRelLowerSet_faces hτ.2.2).2
      (Finset.union_subset_union_right hυτ) (hυ.mono Finset.subset_union_right)

/-- The geometric realization on the standard simplex, with zero coordinates outside a face
(Section 2.2). Omitting the abstract empty face leaves this space unchanged. -/
def geometricRealization {n : ℕ} (K : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin n)) :
    Set (StdSimplex ℝ (Fin n)) :=
  {x | ∃ σ ∈ K, ∀ i, i ∉ σ → x.weights i = 0}

/-- Every nonempty face with noncontractible link is a codeword (Definitions 2.14-2.15). -/
def IsLocallyGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ ∈ codeComplex C,
    ¬ContractibleSpace {x // x ∈ geometricRealization (link (codeComplex C) σ)} → σ ∈ C

/-- **Conjecture 3.13** (arXiv v3; accepted manuscript, p. 11). Every locally good code on at
most seven neurons is open convex or closed convex.

Convexity uses the arbitrary stimulus space of Definition 2.4, without an empty-codeword
assumption. -/
theorem conjecture_3_13 {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 7) (C : Set (Finset (Fin n)))
    (hC : IsLocallyGood C) : IsOpenConvex C ∨ IsClosedConvex C := by
  sorry

end Gambacini2022Non

  sorry

abbrev sandpile {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :=

/-!
# The Accelerated Zeckendorf Game

Authors: Diego Garcia-Fernandezsesma, Steven J. Miller, Thomas Rascon,
Risa Vandegrift, and Ajmain Yamin.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2022](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu/results2022).
Reference: D. Garcia-Fernandezsesma, S. J. Miller, T. Rascon, R. Vandegrift, and A. Yamin,
*The accelerated Zeckendorf game*, Fibonacci Quart. **62** (2024), no. 1, 3-14.
-/

namespace GarciaFernandezSesma2024Accelerated

/-- One turn: any positive number of copies of one combining or splitting move on the finitely
supported Fibonacci-count state (Definition 1.2). -/
def LegalMove (s t : Finsupp ℕ ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i m : ℕ, 0 < i ∧ 0 < m ∧
    ((m ≤ s i ∧ m ≤ s (i + 1) ∧
      t = s - Finsupp.single i m - Finsupp.single (i + 1) m +
        Finsupp.single (i + 2) m) ∨
     (2 * m ≤ s i ∧
      t = s - Finsupp.single i (2 * m) +
        if i = 1 then Finsupp.single 2 m
        else if i = 2 then Finsupp.single 1 m + Finsupp.single 3 m
        else Finsupp.single (i - 2) m + Finsupp.single (i + 1) m))

/-- A winning state: a move either ends the game or permits a winning continuation after every
opponent reply, the last player to move winning (Section 2.2). -/
inductive Winning : Finsupp ℕ ℕ → Prop
  | move {s t : Finsupp ℕ ℕ} (legal : LegalMove s t)
      (reply : ∀ u : Finsupp ℕ ℕ, LegalMove t u → Winning u) : Winning s

/-- **Conjecture 1.6**. Player 1 has a winning strategy in the two-player Accelerated
Zeckendorf Game starting from `n` copies of `F_1` for every `n > 9`. -/
theorem conjecture_1_6 (n : ℕ) (hn : 9 < n) :
    Winning (Finsupp.single 1 n) := by
  sorry

end GarciaFernandezSesma2024Accelerated

problem_statement: In garg2021cyclic.lean, prove either Garg2021Cyclic.betti_support or refute it by proving its logical negation Garg2021Cyclic.betti_support_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Cyclic Group Invariants and The Minimal Free Resolution of S over S^{C_n}

Authors: Swapnil Garg, Frank Lu, Kevin Ren, and Brian Sun.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2021](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: S. Garg, F. Lu, K. Ren, and B. Sun, *Cyclic Group Invariants and The Minimal Free
Resolution of S over S^{C_n}*, REU report, August 2021, 40 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Garg2021Cyclic

open CategoryTheory
open Finset

/-- The invariant subalgebra for the diagonal cyclic action. Since `y_r` has character `r`,
invariant monomials are those of cyclic weight zero. -/
def invariantRing (n : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℂ (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) where
  carrier := {p | MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous
    (fun r : Fin n ↦ (r.val : ZMod n)) p 0}
  zero_mem' := MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_zero _ _ _
  one_mem' := MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_one _ _
  add_mem' hp hq := hp.add hq
  mul_mem' hp hq := by simpa using hp.mul hq
  algebraMap_mem' c := MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_C _ c

/-- The character-`k` eigenspace, as a module over the invariant ring. -/
def characterModule (n : ℕ) (k : ZMod n) :
    Submodule (invariantRing n) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) where
  carrier := {p | MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous
    (fun r : Fin n ↦ (r.val : ZMod n)) p k}
  zero_mem' := MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_zero _ _ _
  add_mem' hp hq := hp.add hq
  smul_mem' r p hp := by
    change MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous _
      ((r : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) * p) k
    simpa using r.property.mul hp

/-- The module structure of `characterModule n k` over the invariant ring. -/
instance (n : ℕ) (k : ZMod n) : Module (invariantRing n) (characterModule n k) :=
  Submodule.module _

/-- **Conjecture 5.5** (p. 39). The shifts in every homological degree of the minimal free
resolution of a nontrivial character module lie in the stated total-degree interval.

This is the containment conjectured on p. 39, not the stronger support equality of the
introduction; nontrivial characters include nonunits and `n = 2`. Betti numbers count free
summands over integer multidegrees, and the resolution is exact including its augmentation, with
multidegree-preserving matrices having zero constant coefficient. -/
theorem betti_support
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (k : ZMod n) (hk : k ≠ 0)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (invariantRing n) (characterModule n k)))
    (rank : ℕ → ℕ)
    (basis : ∀ i, Module.Basis (Fin (rank i)) (invariantRing n) (P.complex.X i))
    (degree : ∀ i, Fin (rank i) → (Fin n → ℤ))
    (haugmentation : ∀ a : Fin (rank 0),
      MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous (fun r : Fin n ↦ Pi.single r (1 : ℤ))
        ((characterModule n k).subtype
          ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.down ℕ) 0
            (ModuleCat.of (invariantRing n) (characterModule n k))).hom.hom
              ((P.π.f 0).hom (basis 0 a)))) (degree 0 a))
    (hmaps : ∀ (i : ℕ) (a : Fin (rank i)) (b : Fin (rank (i + 1))),
      let c : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ :=
        ((basis i).repr ((P.complex.d (i + 1) i).hom (basis (i + 1) b)) a :
          invariantRing n)
      MvPolynomial.constantCoeff c = 0 ∧
        ∀ d ∈ c.support, ∀ r : Fin n,
          (d r : ℤ) + degree i a r = degree (i + 1) b r)
    (i : ℕ) (j : ℤ)
    (hbetti : #{a : Fin (rank i) | ∑ r : Fin n, degree i a r = j} ≠ 0) :
    3 * (i : ℤ) + 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ (n : ℤ) * i + n - 1 := by
  sorry

end Garg2021Cyclic

  sorry

title: Classical and Consecutive Pattern Avoidance in Rooted Forests
problem_statement: In garg2023classical.lean, prove either Garg2023Classical.conjecture_7_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Garg2023Classical.conjecture_7_3_neg.

/-!
# Classical and Consecutive Pattern Avoidance in Rooted Forests

Authors: Swapnil Garg and Alan Peng.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2019](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: S. Garg and A. Peng, *Classical and consecutive pattern avoidance in rooted
forests*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A **194** (2023), 105699; arXiv:2005.08889.
-/

namespace Garg2023Classical

/-- A classical pattern occurs in a word when a subsequence has exactly the same relative order
as the pattern (Section 2). -/
def Contains {k n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (w : List (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : Fin k → Fin w.length, StrictMono i ∧
    ∀ a b, w[i a] < w[i b] ↔ σ a < σ b

/-- The set `F_n(S)` of avoiding forests on `[n]` (Section 2). Forests are encoded by joining
their roots to an extra vertex `none`, which is omitted from label paths. -/
def avoidingForests (S : Finset ((k : ℕ) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + 1)))) (n : ℕ) :
    Set (SimpleGraph (Option (Fin n))) :=
  {G | G.IsTree ∧ ∀ v : Fin n, ∀ p : G.Path none (some v),
    ∀ σ ∈ S, ¬Contains σ.2 (p.val.support.filterMap id)}

/-- **Conjecture 7.3** (arXiv v2, p. 38). Forest-Wilf equivalence of two sets of patterns implies
their Wilf equivalence for permutations. -/
theorem conjecture_7_3
    (S T : Finset ((k : ℕ) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + 1))))
    (h : ∀ n, (avoidingForests S n).ncard = (avoidingForests T n).ncard)
    (n : ℕ) :
    {pi : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | ∀ σ ∈ S,
      ¬Contains σ.2 (List.ofFn pi)}.ncard =
    {pi : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | ∀ σ ∈ T,
      ¬Contains σ.2 (List.ofFn pi)}.ncard := by
  sorry

end Garg2023Classical

  sorry

/-!
# Ramsey Game Numbers

Authors: William Gasarch, Clyde Kruskal, Dao Lu, Eric Weaver, and Natalie Wilkinson.
Origin: [University of Maryland REU-CAAR
2014](https://www.cs.umd.edu/projects/reucaar/highlights-2014.html).
Reference: W. Gasarch, C. Kruskal, D. Lu, E. Weaver, and N. Wilkinson, *Ramsey Game Numbers*,
undated research report (PDF version November 23, 2015).

noncomputable section

namespace Gasarch2015Ramsey

open scoped Classical in
/-- Blue can force the first star on `n` vertices in the achievement game on `m` vertices
(Definitions 1.1-1.3). Here `true` means Blue moves next, and exhausted tied boards are not wins. -/
inductive BlueWins (n m : ℕ) :
    SimpleGraph (Fin m) → SimpleGraph (Fin m) → Bool → Prop
  | won {B R : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} {turn : Bool}
      (blue : ∃ v, n - 1 ≤ B.degree v) (red : ∀ v, R.degree v < n - 1) :
      BlueWins n m B R turn
  | blueMove {B R : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} {u v : Fin m}
      (blue : ∀ w, B.degree w < n - 1) (red : ∀ w, R.degree w < n - 1)
      (distinct : u ≠ v) (uncoloredBlue : ¬B.Adj u v) (uncoloredRed : ¬R.Adj u v)
      (next : BlueWins n m (B ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge u v) R false) :
      BlueWins n m B R true
  | redMove {B R : SimpleGraph (Fin m)}
      (blue : ∀ w, B.degree w < n - 1) (red : ∀ w, R.degree w < n - 1)
      (available : ∃ u v, u ≠ v ∧ ¬B.Adj u v ∧ ¬R.Adj u v)
      (next : ∀ u v, u ≠ v → ¬B.Adj u v → ¬R.Adj u v →
        BlueWins n m B (R ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge u v) true) :
      BlueWins n m B R false

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 4(2)). For every star on at least six vertices, its Ramsey
game number is `2 * n - 4`.

Both first-player victory on that board and failure on every smaller complete board are
retained, with no Maker-Breaker or induced-star substitution. -/
theorem star_ramsey_game_number (n : ℕ) (hn : 6 ≤ n) :
    BlueWins n (2 * n - 4) ⊥ ⊥ true ∧
      ∀ m : ℕ, m < 2 * n - 4 → ¬BlueWins n m ⊥ ⊥ true := by
  sorry

end Gasarch2015Ramsey

title: Realization of Groups with Pairing as Jacobians of Finite Graphs
problem_statement: In gaudet2018realization.lean, prove either Gaudet2018Realization.conjecture_27_no_graph_realizes_exceptional_e_power or refute it by proving its logical negation Gaudet2018Realization.conjecture_27_no_graph_realizes_exceptional_e_power_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Realization of Groups with Pairing as Jacobians of Finite Graphs

Authors: Louis Gaudet, David Jensen, Dhruv Ranganathan, Nicholas Wawrykow,
and Theodore Weisman.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY 2014](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: L. Gaudet, D. Jensen, D. Ranganathan, N. Wawrykow, and T. Weisman, *Realization of
groups with pairing as Jacobians of finite graphs*, arXiv:1410.5144.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gaudet2018Realization

variable {V E : Type}

/-- Divisors whose coefficients sum to zero (Section 2.1). -/
def degreeZeroDivisor (V : Type) [Fintype V] : AddSubgroup (V →₀ ℤ) :=
  (∑ v : V, Finsupp.applyAddHom v : (V →₀ ℤ) →+ ℤ).ker

open scoped Classical in
/-- The chip-firing divisor, with sign opposite to the source's positive Laplacian `div(f)`.
Parallel edges are counted individually. -/
def principalDivisor (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet]
    (f : G.vertexSet → ℤ) : G.vertexSet →₀ ℤ :=
  Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun v ↦ ∑ e : G.edgeSet,
    if h : G.Inc e.val v.val then
      f ⟨h.other, h.isLink_other.right_mem⟩ - f v else 0

/-- The principal subgroup, pulled back to degree-zero divisors (Section 2.1). Changing the
Laplacian sign does not change this subgroup. -/
def principalSubgroup (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet] :
    AddSubgroup (degreeZeroDivisor G.vertexSet) :=
  (AddSubgroup.closure (Set.range (principalDivisor G))).comap
    (degreeZeroDivisor G.vertexSet).subtype

/-- The Jacobian: degree-zero divisors modulo principal divisors (Section 2.1). -/
abbrev Jacobian (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet] :=
  degreeZeroDivisor G.vertexSet ⧸ principalSubgroup G

/-- The value of the monodromy pairing on divisor representatives. The source's positive
Laplacian is `-principalDivisor G f`. -/
def MonodromyPairingValue (G : Graph V E) [Fintype G.vertexSet] [Fintype G.edgeSet]
    (x y : Jacobian G) (q : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (D₁ D₂ : degreeZeroDivisor G.vertexSet) (m : ℕ) (f : G.vertexSet → ℤ),
    0 < m ∧ QuotientAddGroup.mk D₁ = x ∧ QuotientAddGroup.mk D₂ = y ∧
      (-principalDivisor G f = fun v ↦ (m : ℤ) * (D₁ : G.vertexSet →₀ ℤ) v) ∧
        (∃ z : ℤ, q - (((m : ℚ)⁻¹) *
          (∑ v : G.vertexSet,
            ((D₂ : G.vertexSet →₀ ℤ) v : ℚ) * (f v : ℚ))) = z)

/-- **Conjecture 27** (after Proposition 26). For every `r, k ≥ 1`, no graph realizes
`(E_{2^r}) ^ k` as its Jacobian with monodromy pairing. -/
theorem conjecture_27_no_graph_realizes_exceptional_e_power
    (r k : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ¬∃ (V E : Type) (G : Graph V E) (_ : Fintype G.vertexSet) (_ : Fintype G.edgeSet),
      G.Loopless ∧ G.toSimpleGraph.Connected ∧
        ∃ e : (Fin k → ZMod (2 ^ r) × ZMod (2 ^ r)) ≃+ Jacobian G,
          ∀ x y : Fin k → ZMod (2 ^ r) × ZMod (2 ^ r),
            MonodromyPairingValue G (e x) (e y)
              (∑ i : Fin k,
                ((x i).1.val * (y i).2.val + (x i).2.val * (y i).1.val : ℚ) /
                  (2 ^ r : ℚ)) := by
  sorry

end Gaudet2018Realization

  sorry

Authors: Lauren Gernes and Laurel Newman.
Origin: [Texas A&M University REU
2019](https://artsci.tamu.edu/mathematics/academics/undergraduate/research/reu/results/results-2019.html).
Reference: L. Gernes and L. Newman, *The Probability of Easily Approximating the Positive Real

namespace Gernes2019Probability

/-- The failure set with normalized null vector `(a / b - 1, 1, -a / b)` (Definition 3.5). Its
three-term threshold follows the same authors' slide clarification, not the printed text. -/
def failureSet (a b : ℕ) : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ) :=
  let r := (a : ℝ) / (b : ℝ)
  {c | c 0 * c 1 < 0 ∧ c 2 * c 1 < 0 ∧
    0 < Real.log |c 1| - (1 - r) * Real.log |c 0| - r * Real.log |c 2| ∧
    Real.log |c 1| - (1 - r) * Real.log |c 0| - r * Real.log |c 2| ≤
      -(1 - r) * Real.log (1 - r) - r * Real.log r}

/-- **Conjecture 1**. The unconditional Gaussian failure probability satisfies the full uniform
three-regime envelope in exponent spread and middle scale.

Sigma denotes standard deviation, as in the experiment, with independent sampling. -/
theorem conjecture_1 :
    ∃ Csmall Cmiddle Clarge : ℝ,
      0 < Csmall ∧ 0 < Cmiddle ∧ 0 < Clarge ∧
      ∀ (a b : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
        (σ : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ),
        ((MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun i : Fin 3 ↦
          ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0
            (if i = 1 then Real.toNNReal (σ ^ 2) else 1))
          (failureSet a b)).toReal ≤
          min (Csmall * √(min (a : ℝ) ((b : ℝ) - (a : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ)) * σ)
            (min (Cmiddle * √(min (a : ℝ) ((b : ℝ) - (a : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ)))
              (Clarge * √(min (a : ℝ) ((b : ℝ) - (a : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ)) * σ ^ (-(37 : ℝ) / 50))) := by
  sorry

end Gernes2019Probability

  sorry

title: Uniform Generation of w-free Strings and H-free Subgraphs with Partial Rejection Sampling
problem_statement: In gil2018uniform.lean, prove either Gil2018Uniform.conjecture_6_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gil2018Uniform.conjecture_6_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Uniform Generation of w-free Strings and H-free Subgraphs with Partial Rejection Sampling

Authors: Juan Gil and Joshua Amaniampong.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2018](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: J. Gil and J. Amaniampong, *Uniform Generation of w-free Strings and H-free
Subgraphs with Partial Rejection Sampling*, MIT SPUR final paper, 2018.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gil2018Uniform

open Filter
open scoped ENNReal
open Finset

/-- The bad events: all starting positions of an occurrence of `w` (Section 2.1). Positions are
zero-based, and every complete window, including the last, is tested. -/
def badEvents (w x : List Bool) : Finset ℕ :=
  {i ∈ Finset.range (x.length + 1 - w.length) | (x.drop i).take w.length = w}

/-- The set `var(R)` of positions belonging to the selected word events (Sections 2-3). -/
def eventVariables (k : ℕ) (R : Finset ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  R.biUnion fun i ↦ Finset.Ico i (i + k)

/-- The resampling set (Algorithm 2). It uses the simultaneous boundary update of the authors'
SPUR implementation, iterated once per window since each nonterminal pass marks a new event. -/
def resamplingSet (w x : List Bool) : Finset ℕ :=
  let positions := Finset.range (x.length + 1 - w.length)
  let pass := fun RN : Finset ℕ × Finset ℕ ↦
    let boundary := {i ∈ positions |
      i ∉ RN.1 ∧ i ∉ RN.2 ∧
        ∃ j ∈ RN.1, ¬Disjoint (Finset.Ico i (i + w.length))
          (Finset.Ico j (j + w.length))}
    let unblocked := {i ∈ boundary |
      ∀ j ∈ Finset.Ico i (i + w.length) ∩ eventVariables w.length RN.1,
        x[j]? = w[j - i]?}
    (RN.1 ∪ unblocked, RN.2 ∪ (boundary \ unblocked))
  ((pass^[#positions]) (badEvents w x, ∅)).1

/-- The successive assignments, starting from the initial independent sample (Algorithm 3). Each
draw replaces exactly the selected variables, so a terminal assignment remains fixed. -/
def assignments (w : List Bool) {n : ℕ} (initial : Fin n → Bool)
    (draws : List (Fin n → Bool)) : List (Fin n → Bool) :=
  draws.scanl (fun x draw ↦
    let R := eventVariables w.length (resamplingSet w (List.ofFn x))
    fun i ↦ if i.val ∈ R then draw i else x i) initial

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 6.1). For binary words, PRS takes quadratic expected
rounds for `01` and `10`, and logarithmic expected rounds for `00`, `11` and all words of length
at least three.

The tail sum uses independent fair-bit tables, including the initial sample, and the
simultaneous expansion convention of the authors' linked program. -/
theorem conjecture_6_1 (w : List Bool) :
    let E : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞ := fun n ↦ ∑' t : ℕ,
      (#{tape : Fin (t + 1) → Fin n → Bool |
        (badEvents w (List.ofFn
          ((assignments w (tape 0) (List.ofFn tape).tail).getLastD (tape 0)))).Nonempty} :
            ℝ≥0∞) /
          2 ^ (n * (t + 1))
    ((w = [false, true] ∨ w = [true, false]) →
      ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ENNReal.ofReal (c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ E n ∧
          E n ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) ∧
    ((3 ≤ w.length ∨ w = [false, false] ∨ w = [true, true]) →
      ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        E n ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * Real.log (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Gil2018Uniform

theorem Gil2018Uniform.conjecture_6_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gil2018Uniform.conjecture_6_1 := by
  sorry

title: Monotone Catenary Degree in Numerical Monoids
problem_statement: In gonzalez2019monotone.lean, prove either Gonzalez2019Monotone.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gonzalez2019Monotone.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Monotone Catenary Degree in Numerical Monoids

Authors: Daniel Gonzalez Cedre, Cameron Wright, and Jenna Zomback.
Origin: [PURE Math 2015](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1045147).
Reference: D. Gonzalez Cedre, C. Wright, and J. Zomback, *Monotone Catenary Degree in Numerical
Monoids*, preprint; arXiv:1912.08114v3.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gonzalez2019Monotone

open scoped ENNReal

/-- The factorizations of `m` into the indexed generators (Section 3). -/
def Factorizations {k : ℕ} (generators : Fin k → ℕ) (m : ℕ) :=
  {z : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, z i * generators i = m}

/-- The distance: the larger length minus the length of the componentwise gcd (Definition 2). -/
def factorizationDistance {k : ℕ} (z w : Fin k → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  max (∑ i, z i) (∑ i, w i) - ∑ i, min (z i) (w i)

/-- The least uniform chain bound over all factorizations of all monoid elements (Definitions 3-4,
Section 3). The value is in `ℕ∞`, allowing infinity for a general tuple. -/
def catenaryDegree {k : ℕ} (generators : Fin k → ℕ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {N : ℕ∞ | ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ z w : Factorizations generators m,
    Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun x y : Factorizations generators m ↦
        (factorizationDistance x.val y.val : ℕ∞) ≤ N) z w}

/-- The uniform bound using nondecreasing-length chains (Definition 8, Section 3). Only one
length order is encoded, since reversing a chain covers the other. -/
def monotoneCatenaryDegree {k : ℕ} (generators : Fin k → ℕ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {N : ℕ∞ | ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ z w : Factorizations generators m,
    (∑ i, z.val i) ≤ ∑ i, w.val i →
      Relation.ReflTransGen
        (fun x y : Factorizations generators m ↦
          (factorizationDistance x.val y.val : ℕ∞) ≤ N ∧
            (∑ i, x.val i) ≤ ∑ i, y.val i) z w}

/-- **Conjecture 1** (Section 5). The generalized arithmetic numerical monoid has equal ordinary
and monotone catenary degrees when `gcd(h - 1, d) > 1`.

The parameters express the source's minimal three-generator family. -/
theorem conjecture_1 (a h d : ℕ) (ha : 3 ≤ a) (hh : 2 ≤ h)
    (hd : 0 < d) (had : Nat.Coprime a d) (hgcd : 1 < Nat.gcd (h - 1) d) :
    monotoneCatenaryDegree (![a, a * h + d, a * h + 2 * d] : Fin 3 → ℕ) =
      catenaryDegree (![a, a * h + d, a * h + 2 * d] : Fin 3 → ℕ) := by
  sorry

end Gonzalez2019Monotone

theorem Gonzalez2019Monotone.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gonzalez2019Monotone.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

title: Optimally Solving Colored Generalized Sliding-Tile Puzzles: Complexity and Bounds
problem_statement: In gozon2026optimally.lean, prove either Gozon2026Optimally.single_escort_np_hard or refute it by proving its logical negation Gozon2026Optimally.single_escort_np_hard_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Optimally Solving Colored Generalized Sliding-Tile Puzzles: Complexity and Bounds

Authors: Marcus Gozon and Jingjin Yu.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2023](https://archive.reu.dimacs.rutgers.edu/2023/mg2010/public_html/).
Reference: M. Gozon and J. Yu, *Optimally solving colored generalized sliding-tile puzzles:
complexity and bounds*, preprint (2024); arXiv:2410.14947v1.
-/

namespace Gozon2026Optimally

/-- A complete injective placement of the labeled tiles on the full rectangle. Labels and
row/column coordinates are zero-based. -/
abbrev Configuration (rows columns tiles : ℕ) :=
  Fin tiles ↪ Fin rows × Fin columns

/-- The single-escort GSTP instance with both complete placements as input (Section 2.1). The
missing cell is the escort, not an additional labeled tile. -/
structure Puzzle where
  /-- The number of rows of the board. -/
  rows : ℕ
  /-- The number of columns of the board. -/
  columns : ℕ
  /-- The number of labeled tiles. -/
  tiles : ℕ
  rows_pos : 0 < rows
  columns_pos : 0 < columns
  one_escort : rows * columns = tiles + 1
  /-- The initial placement of the tiles. -/
  initial : Configuration rows columns tiles
  /-- The goal placement of the tiles. -/
  goal : Configuration rows columns tiles

/-- One synchronous unit step or wait for every tile, with no head-on exchange and
nonperpendicular corner-following. Injectivity enforces the no-meet constraint. -/
def Move {rows columns tiles : ℕ}
    (a b : Configuration rows columns tiles) : Prop :=
  let d := fun i : Fin tiles ↦
    (((b i).1.val : ℤ) - ((a i).1.val : ℤ),
      ((b i).2.val : ℤ) - ((a i).2.val : ℤ))
  (∀ i, d i = (0, 0) ∨ d i = (1, 0) ∨ d i = (-1, 0) ∨
    d i = (0, 1) ∨ d i = (0, -1)) ∧
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    ¬(a i = b j ∧ b i = a j) ∧
    (b i = a j → (d i).1 * (d j).1 + (d i).2 * (d j).2 ≠ 0)

/-- The binary input: rows, columns, tile count, blank count (exactly one), positive `K`, then
every initial and goal row-major cell index in label order. Each natural field writes each
`encodeNat` bit `b` as `[true, b]` and ends in `false`, and malformed inputs reject. -/
def readPuzzle (word : List Bool) : Option (Puzzle × ℕ) := do
  let rec /-- Reads one natural-number field: the payload bits before the terminating `false`. -/
    readBits : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
    | false :: rest => some ([], rest)
    | true :: b :: rest => do
        let (bits, rest) ← readBits rest
        some (b :: bits, rest)
    | _ => none
  let readNat := fun word : List Bool ↦ do
    let (bits, rest) ← readBits word
    let n := Computability.decodeNat bits
    if Computability.encodeNat n = bits then some (n, rest) else none
  let (rows, rest) ← readNat word
  let (columns, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (tiles, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (escorts, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (K, rest) ← readNat rest
  if hr : 0 < rows then
    if hc : 0 < columns then
      if he : rows * columns = tiles + 1 then
        if escorts = 1 ∧ 0 < K then
          let rec /-- Reads `count` cell indices, rejecting any outside the board. -/
            readPositions : (count : ℕ) → List Bool →
              Option ((Fin count → Fin rows × Fin columns) × List Bool)
            | 0, w => some ((fun i ↦ Fin.elim0 i), w)
            | count + 1, w => do
              let (index, w) ← readNat w
              if h : index < rows * columns then
                let q : Fin rows × Fin columns :=
                  (⟨index / columns, (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hc).mpr h⟩,
                    ⟨index % columns, Nat.mod_lt _ hc⟩)
                let (tail, w) ← readPositions count w
                some (Fin.cases q tail, w)
              else none
          let (initial, rest) ← readPositions tiles rest
          let (goal, rest) ← readPositions tiles rest
          if rest = [] then
            if hi : Function.Injective initial then
              if hg : Function.Injective goal then
                some ({ rows, columns, tiles, rows_pos := hr, columns_pos := hc,
                        one_escort := he, initial := ⟨initial, hi⟩, goal := ⟨goal, hg⟩ }, K)
              else none
            else none
          else none
        else none
      else none
    else none
  else none

/-- The one-escort makespan deadline language: all tiles reach the supplied goal at a common
`T ≤ K`. Malformed inputs reject, and `T = 0` is allowed although `K` is positive. -/
def MOGSTP : Set (List Bool) :=
  {word | ∃ (g : Puzzle) (K : ℕ),
    readPuzzle word = some (g, K) ∧
    ∃ T ≤ K, ∃ path : Fin (T + 1) → Configuration g.rows g.columns g.tiles,
      path 0 = g.initial ∧ path (Fin.last T) = g.goal ∧
      ∀ t : Fin T, Move (path t.castSucc) (path t.succ)}

/-- **Open question** (Section 5, p. 16). The full rectangular single-escort MOGSTP deadline
language is NP-hard.

MOGSTP is as in M. Gozon and J. Yu, arXiv:2312.10887v1, Section 3.1. Rectangles include
one-row and one-column boards and the zero-tile 1x1 board; no NP membership, other escort count
or feasibility promise is asserted. Goals are arbitrary complete input placements; the
successor's ordered-goal wording is read in its algorithmic scope, not as a deadline-preserving
normalization. -/
theorem single_escort_np_hard :
    let pairCode := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList Bool)
      (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    let np : Set (List Bool) → Prop := fun language ↦
      ∃ verifier : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime pairCode
          Computability.encodeBool verifier,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ input : List Bool,
          input ∈ language ↔ ∃ certificate : List Bool,
            certificate.length ≤ bound.eval input.length ∧
            verifier (input, certificate) = true
    ∀ language : Set (List Bool), np language →
      ∃ reduction : List Bool → List Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id reduction,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∀ word, word ∈ language ↔ reduction word ∈ MOGSTP := by
  sorry

end Gozon2026Optimally

theorem Gozon2026Optimally.single_escort_np_hard_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gozon2026Optimally.single_escort_np_hard := by
  sorry

title: Ramsey theory on Steiner triples
problem_statement: In granath2018ramsey.lean, prove either Granath2018Ramsey.concluding_conjecture or refute it by proving its logical negation Granath2018Ramsey.concluding_conjecture_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Ramsey theory on Steiner triples

Authors: Elliot Granath, Andras Gyarfas, Jerry Hardee, Trent Watson, and Xiaoze Wu.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics 2016](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: E. Granath, A. Gyarfas, J. Hardee, T. Watson, and X. Wu, *Ramsey theory on Steiner
triples*, J. Combin. Des. **26** (2018), no. 1, 5-11; doi:10.1002/jcd.21585.
-/

namespace Granath2018Ramsey

/-- A configuration: a partial Steiner triple system with no isolated points (Section 1). -/
def IsConfiguration {v : ℕ} (C : Hypergraph (Fin v)) : Prop :=
  C.vertexSet = Set.univ ∧
  (∀ b ∈ C.edgeSet, b.ncard = 3) ∧
  C.IsLinear ∧
  (∀ x : Fin v, ¬C.IsIsolated x)

/-- A Steiner triple system: triples covering every pair of distinct points exactly once
(Section 1). -/
def IsSteinerTripleSystem {n : ℕ} (S : Hypergraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  S.vertexSet = Set.univ ∧
  (∀ b ∈ S.edgeSet, b.ncard = 3) ∧
  ∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → ∃! b, b ∈ S.edgeSet ∧ x ∈ b ∧ y ∈ b

/-- Every sufficiently large Steiner triple system contains an injective, not necessarily induced,
copy of the configuration (Section 1). -/
def Unavoidable {v : ℕ} (C : Hypergraph (Fin v)) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, (n % 6 = 1 ∨ n % 6 = 3) →
    ∀ S : Hypergraph (Fin n), IsSteinerTripleSystem S →
      ∃ f : Fin v ↪ Fin n, ∀ b ∈ C.edgeSet, f '' b ∈ S.edgeSet

/-- Every `t`-coloring of the blocks of every sufficiently large STS contains a monochromatic copy
of the configuration (Section 1). -/
def IsRamsey {v : ℕ} (C : Hypergraph (Fin v)) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, (n % 6 = 1 ∨ n % 6 = 3) →
    ∀ S : Hypergraph (Fin n), IsSteinerTripleSystem S →
      ∀ color : S.edgeSet → Fin t,
        ∃ f : Fin v ↪ Fin n, ∃ i : Fin t, ∀ b ∈ C.edgeSet,
          ∃ hb : f '' b ∈ S.edgeSet, color ⟨f '' b, hb⟩ = i

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 5, concluding conjecture). Every unavoidable configuration is
`t`-Ramsey for every positive `t`, with all sufficiently large STS as hosts. -/
theorem concluding_conjecture {v : ℕ} (C : Hypergraph (Fin v))
    (hC : IsConfiguration C) (hU : Unavoidable C) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    IsRamsey C t := by
  sorry

end Granath2018Ramsey

theorem Granath2018Ramsey.concluding_conjecture_neg : ¬ type_of% @Granath2018Ramsey.concluding_conjecture := by
  sorry

title: Equivalence between Restricted Non-interactive Statistical Zero-knowledge Classes
problem_statement: In gray2022equivalence.lean, prove either Gray2022Equivalence.disjunctive_logspace_closure or refute it by proving its logical negation Gray2022Equivalence.disjunctive_logspace_closure_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Equivalence between Restricted Non-interactive Statistical Zero-knowledge Classes

Authors: Jacob Gray, Saachi Mutreja, and Pengxiang Wang, with Eric Allender and
Harsha Tirumala.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2022](https://archive.reu.dimacs.rutgers.edu/2022/jg1884/public_html/).
Reference: J. Gray, S. Mutreja, and P. Wang, *Equivalence between restricted non-interactive
statistical zero-knowledge classes*, DIMACS final research report (July 29, 2022).
-/

namespace Gray2022Equivalence

open Finset

/-- One output depending on at most four input coordinates, with a 16-bit table. An absent
coordinate is supplied as `false`. -/
structure FourLocalGate (m : ℕ) where
  /-- The input coordinates read by the gate, with `none` for an absent coordinate. -/
  input : Fin 4 → Option (Fin m)
  /-- The truth table of the gate on its four input bits. -/
  table : Fin 16 → Bool

/-- A finite distribution circuit, retaining the declared number of random inputs. -/
structure FourLocalCircuit where
  /-- The number of random input bits. -/
  inputs : ℕ
  /-- The number of output bits. -/
  outputs : ℕ
  /-- The gate computing each output bit. -/
  gate : Fin outputs → FourLocalGate inputs

/-- Evaluate a table in little-endian order of its four argument bits. -/
def FourLocalGate.eval {m : ℕ} (g : FourLocalGate m) (x : Fin m → Bool) : Bool :=
  let b := fun j ↦ (g.input j).elim false x
  g.table ⟨(b 0).toNat + 2 * (b 1).toNat + 4 * (b 2).toNat + 8 * (b 3).toNat, by
    have h₀ := Bool.toNat_le (b 0)
    have h₁ := Bool.toNat_le (b 1)
    have h₂ := Bool.toNat_le (b 2)
    have h₃ := Bool.toNat_le (b 3)
    omega⟩

/-- Evaluate every output on the same input bit vector, preserving correlations. -/
def FourLocalCircuit.eval (c : FourLocalCircuit)
    (x : Fin c.inputs → Bool) : Fin c.outputs → Bool :=
  fun j ↦ (c.gate j).eval x

/-- The base-two Shannon entropy of the circuit's output on independent uniform bits (before
Definition 5 of the full paper). Zero masses contribute zero. -/
noncomputable def FourLocalCircuit.entropy (c : FourLocalCircuit) : ℝ :=
  (∑ y : Fin c.outputs → Bool,
    Real.negMulLog
      (#{x : Fin c.inputs → Bool | c.eval x = y} /
        (2 : ℝ) ^ c.inputs)) / Real.log 2

/-- The unary encoding of a circuit: input ports, output count, and each output's four
option-coded wire indices and sixteen table bits. -/
def FourLocalCircuit.encode (c : FourLocalCircuit) : List Bool :=
  ([c.inputs, c.outputs] ++
    (List.ofFn fun j ↦
      List.ofFn (fun a ↦ ((c.gate j).input a).elim 0 (fun i ↦ i.val + 1)) ++
      List.ofFn (fun a ↦ ((c.gate j).table a).toNat)).flatten).flatMap
    (fun n ↦ List.replicate n true ++ [false])

/-- The encoding of a query list: each circuit bit is preceded by `true`, and each circuit ends
in `false`. -/
def encodeCircuitList (cs : List FourLocalCircuit) : List Bool :=
  cs.flatMap fun c ↦ c.encode.flatMap (fun b ↦ [true, b]) ++ [false]

/-- Finite-control instructions of a deterministic transducer, with two-way
read-only input, one work tape, and unreadable append-only output. -/
inductive Instruction (s : ℕ)
  | move (next : Fin (s + 1)) (inputMove workMove : Option Turing.Dir)
      (write : Option (Option Bool)) (emit : Option Bool)
  | halt

/-- A finite transition table. The input alphabet has distinct end markers, and `none` is the
blank work-tape symbol. -/
structure Machine (s : ℕ) where
  /-- The instruction for each state, input-tape symbol and work-tape symbol. -/
  transition : Fin (s + 1) → Option (Option Bool) → Option Bool → Instruction s

/-- A configuration of the transducer. Neither the input position nor the accumulated output is
visible to the control. -/
structure Configuration (s : ℕ) where
  /-- The current control state. -/
  state : Fin (s + 1) := 0
  /-- The input-head position, with `0` the left end marker. -/
  inputPosition : ℕ := 0
  /-- The work-tape head position relative to its starting cell. -/
  position : ℤ := 0
  /-- The contents of the work tape around its head. -/
  work : Turing.Tape (Option Bool) := default
  /-- The output emitted so far. -/
  output : List Bool := []
  /-- Whether the machine has halted. -/
  halted : Bool := false

/-- One transition step. -/
def Machine.step {s : ℕ} (M : Machine s) (input : List Bool)
    (c : Configuration s) : Configuration s :=
  if c.halted then c else
  let symbol := if c.inputPosition = 0 then none
    else some (input[c.inputPosition - 1]?)
  match M.transition c.state symbol c.work.head with
  | .halt => { c with halted := true }
  | .move q di dw w e =>
      let inputPosition := match di with
        | none => c.inputPosition
        | some .left => c.inputPosition - 1
        | some .right => min (c.inputPosition + 1) (input.length + 1)
      let work := match w with
        | none => c.work
        | some b => c.work.write b
      let work := match dw with
        | none => work
        | some d => work.move d
      let position := match dw with
        | none => c.position
        | some .left => c.position - 1
        | some .right => c.position + 1
      { c with
        state := q
        inputPosition := inputPosition
        position := position
        work := work
        output := c.output ++ e.toList }

/-- Execution from the left input marker and blank work/output tapes. -/
def Machine.run {s : ℕ} (M : Machine s) (input : List Bool) :
    ℕ → Configuration s
  | 0 => {}
  | t + 1 => M.step input (M.run input t)

/-- **Conjecture 4.3** (p. 4). `NISZK_L` is closed under logspace disjunctive truth-table
reductions.

Closure is expressed through the complete fixed-threshold `EA_NC0` problem (full paper,
Definition 5 and Theorem 7), with arbitrary query lists and gap queries retained; adding
independent uniform outputs justifies the signed thresholds at small output counts. -/
theorem disjunctive_logspace_closure :
    ∃ s : ℕ, ∃ M : Machine s, ∃ K d : ℕ, 0 < K ∧
      (∀ input : List Bool,
        (M.run input (K * (input.length + 1) ^ d)).halted = true ∧
          ∀ u : ℕ, u ≤ K * (input.length + 1) ^ d →
            (M.run input u).position.natAbs ≤
              K * (Nat.log 2 (input.length + 2) + 1)) ∧
      (∀ cs : List FourLocalCircuit,
        ∃ result : FourLocalCircuit,
          (M.run (encodeCircuitList cs)
              (K * ((encodeCircuitList cs).length + 1) ^ d)).output = result.encode ∧
          ((∃ c ∈ cs, (c.outputs : ℝ) - 2 < c.entropy) →
            (result.outputs : ℝ) - 2 < result.entropy) ∧
          ((∀ c ∈ cs, c.entropy < (c.outputs : ℝ) - 4) →
            result.entropy < (result.outputs : ℝ) - 4)) := by
  sorry

end Gray2022Equivalence

theorem Gray2022Equivalence.disjunctive_logspace_closure_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gray2022Equivalence.disjunctive_logspace_closure := by
  sorry

title: Fixed perimeter analogues of some partition results
problem_statement: In gray2026fixed.lean, prove either Gray2026Fixed.conjecture_1_5 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gray2026Fixed.conjecture_1_5_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Fixed perimeter analogues of some partition results

Authors: Gabriel Gray, Emily Payne, Holly Swisher, and Ren Watson.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2024](https://math.oregonstate.edu/sites/math.oregonstate.edu/files/2024-08/EmilyGabeRen_0.pdf).
Reference: G. Gray, E. Payne, H. Swisher, and R. Watson, *Fixed perimeter analogues of some
partition results*, preprint (2025), 15 pp.; arXiv:2502.12394v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gray2026Fixed

open Finset

/-- The largest hook length: largest part plus number of parts minus one. -/
def perimeter {s : ℕ} (p : Nat.Partition s) : ℕ :=
  p.parts.toFinset.sup id + p.parts.card - 1

open scoped Classical in
/-- The count `h_d^(a)(n)` of perimeter-`n` partitions with parts at least `a` and pairwise
differences at least `d` (Section 1.2). All partition sizes are included. -/
def distinctCount (a d n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (n * n + 1),
    #{p : Nat.Partition s |
      0 < p.parts.card ∧ perimeter p = n ∧
      (∀ x ∈ p.parts, a ≤ x) ∧
      p.parts.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ d ≤ Nat.dist x y)}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The count `ell_m^(m₁,m₂)(n)` of perimeter-`n` partitions whose positive parts lie in either
indicated residue class (Section 1.5). Zero residues are included. -/
def residueCount (m₁ m₂ m n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (n * n + 1),
    #{p : Nat.Partition s |
      0 < p.parts.card ∧ perimeter p = n ∧
      ∀ x ∈ p.parts, x % m = m₁ % m ∨ x % m = m₂ % m}

/-- **Conjecture 1.5**. The difference of the two fixed-perimeter counts diverges to positive or
negative infinity according as `m` is above or below `2d + 2`; no assertion is made at the
critical modulus. -/
theorem conjecture_1_5 (a d m₁ m₂ m : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (had : a ≤ d)
    (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₁₂ : m₁ < m₂) (hm₂ : m₂ ≤ m) :
    (2 * d + 2 < m → Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (distinctCount a d n : ℤ) - (residueCount m₁ m₂ m n : ℤ))
      Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) ∧
    (m < 2 * d + 2 → Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (distinctCount a d n : ℤ) - (residueCount m₁ m₂ m n : ℤ))
      Filter.atTop Filter.atBot) := by sorry

end Gray2026Fixed

theorem Gray2026Fixed.conjecture_1_5_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gray2026Fixed.conjecture_1_5 := by
  sorry

title: An Infinite Family of Non-Abelian Monogenic Number Fields

/-!
# An Infinite Family of Non-Abelian Monogenic Number Fields

Authors: Ofer Grossman and Dongkwan Kim.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2015](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: O. Grossman and D. Kim, *An Infinite Family of Non-Abelian Monogenic Number Fields*,
MIT research report, November 11, 2015, 8 pp.,
https://math.mit.edu/documents/spur/2015grossman-kim.pdf.

namespace Grossman2015Infinite

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 4, first paragraph, p. 7). For every `n ≥ 3`, there are
infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic Galois number fields with Galois group `Sₙ` whose ring of
integers has a power integral basis.

The bound `n ≥ 3` expands the source's non-abelian antecedent. Each field is itself Galois, not
merely a degree-`n` field with `Sₙ` normal closure, so its power basis has length `n!`. -/
theorem symmetric_galois_monogenic_families (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    ∃ (K : ℕ → Type) (fields : ∀ i, Field (K i)),
      letI := fields
      ∃ (numberFields : ∀ i, NumberField (K i)),
        letI := numberFields
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → IsEmpty (K i ≃ₐ[ℚ] K j)) ∧
        ∀ i, IsGalois ℚ (K i) ∧
          Nonempty ((K i ≃ₐ[ℚ] K i) ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) ∧
          Nonempty (PowerBasis ℤ (NumberField.RingOfIntegers (K i))) := by
  sorry

end Grossman2015Infinite

title: Connected Sums and Decompositions of Plane Curves
problem_statement: In grostic2001connected.lean, prove either Grostic2001Connected.unique_prime_decomposition or refute it by proving its logical negation Grostic2001Connected.unique_prime_decomposition_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Connected Sums and Decompositions of Plane Curves

Author: Christian J. Grostic.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2000](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/proceedings/2000.html).
Reference: C. J. Grostic, *Connected Sums and Decompositions of Plane Curves*, Oregon State REU
Proceedings, manuscript dated January 26, 2001, pp. 53–74.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Grostic2001Connected

/-- Generic smooth immersions of the circle in the plane, including embeddings (p. 54). The plane
is encoded as `ℂ`, with regularity and transversality taken over `ℝ`. -/
structure GenericCurve where
  /-- The smooth immersion of the circle into the plane. -/
  curve : ContMDiffMap
    (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
    (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℂ) Circle ℂ ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat)
  regular : ∀ x : Circle,
    Function.Injective
      (mvfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) curve x)
  at_most_double : ∀ a b c : Circle,
    curve a = curve b → curve a = curve c → a = b ∨ a = c ∨ b = c
  transverse : ∀ a b : Circle, a ≠ b → curve a = curve b →
    ∀ v : ℂ,
      ∃ u : TangentSpace (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) a,
        ∃ w : TangentSpace (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) b,
          mvfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) curve a u +
            mvfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) curve b w = v
  finite_crossings :
    {z : ℂ | ∃ a b : Circle, a ≠ b ∧ curve a = z ∧ curve b = z}.Finite

/-- Equivalence of curves under smooth plane and circle reparametrizations, including orientation
reversals (p. 54). -/
def curveSetoid : Setoid GenericCurve where
  r a b := ∃ F : Diffeomorph
      (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℂ) (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℂ)
      ℂ ℂ ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat),
    ∃ h : Diffeomorph
      (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
      (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
      Circle Circle ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat),
      ∀ t : Circle, F (a.curve t) = b.curve (h t)
  iseqv := {
    refl := by
      intro a
      refine ⟨Diffeomorph.refl (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℂ) ℂ _,
        Diffeomorph.refl (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) Circle _, ?_⟩
      intro t
      rfl
    symm := by
      intro a b hab
      obtain ⟨F, h, heq⟩ := hab
      refine ⟨F.symm, h.symm, ?_⟩
      intro t
      have hx := congrArg F.symm (heq (h.symm t))
      simpa only [Diffeomorph.symm_apply_apply, Diffeomorph.apply_symm_apply] using hx.symm
    trans := by
      intro a b c hab hbc
      obtain ⟨F, h, heq⟩ := hab
      obtain ⟨G, k, keq⟩ := hbc
      refine ⟨F.trans G, h.trans k, ?_⟩
      intro t
      change G (F (a.curve t)) = c.curve (k (h t))
      rw [heq t, keq (h t)] }

/-- The multivalued exterior connected sum (Definition 1). A marked disk records the deleted caps
and inserted arcs, and four itineraries record the seams, without an assumed surgery law. -/
def ConnectedSum (left right result : GenericCurve) : Prop :=
  ∃ u : Fin 2 → GenericCurve, ∃ w : GenericCurve,
    curveSetoid.r left (u 0) ∧ curveSetoid.r right (u 1) ∧
    curveSetoid.r w result ∧
    (∀ t : Circle, ((u 0).curve t).re < 0 ∧ 0 < ((u 1).curve t).re) ∧
    ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∃ cap retained : Fin 2 → ℝ → Circle,
    ∃ bridge : Fin 2 → ℝ → ℂ,
    ∃ disk : (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) → ℂ,
    ∃ itinerary : Fin 4 → ℝ → Circle,
      let I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
      let J : Set ℝ := Set.Ioo (-ε) (1 + ε)
      let A : Fin 2 → ℝ → ℂ := fun i t ↦ (u i).curve (cap i t)
      let R : Fin 2 → ℝ → ℂ := fun i t ↦ (u i).curve (retained i t)
      let Z : Set ℂ := Set.range (u 0).curve ∪ Set.range (u 1).curve
      (∀ i : Fin 2,
        ContMDiffOn (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
          (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
          ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat) (cap i) J ∧
        ContMDiffOn (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
          (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
          ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat) (retained i) J ∧
        Set.InjOn (cap i) I ∧ Set.InjOn (retained i) I ∧
        (∀ t ∈ I,
          Function.Injective (mfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
            (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (cap i) t) ∧
          Function.Injective (mfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
            (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (retained i) t)) ∧
        cap i 0 = retained i 1 ∧ cap i 1 = retained i 0 ∧
        (cap i '' I) ∪ (retained i '' I) = Set.univ ∧
        (cap i '' I) ∩ (retained i '' I) = {cap i 0, cap i 1} ∧
        Set.InjOn (A i) I ∧ (u i).curve ⁻¹' (A i '' I) = cap i '' I) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 2,
        ContMDiffOn (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℂ)
          ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat) (bridge i) J ∧
        ∀ t ∈ I,
          Function.Injective (mvfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) (bridge i) t)) ∧
      Topology.IsEmbedding disk ∧
      (∀ t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        disk (⟨0, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩, t) = A 0 t ∧
        disk (⟨1, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩, t) = A 1 (1 - (t : ℝ))) ∧
      (∀ s : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        disk (s, ⟨0, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩) = bridge 0 s ∧
        disk (s, ⟨1, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩) = bridge 1 (1 - (s : ℝ))) ∧
      Set.range disk ∩ Z = (A 0 '' I) ∪ (A 1 '' I) ∧
      (∃ z ∈ Zᶜ,
        ¬Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn Zᶜ z) ∧
        ∀ q : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
          (q.1 : ℝ) ≠ 0 → (q.1 : ℝ) ≠ 1 →
          disk q ∈ connectedComponentIn Zᶜ z) ∧
      (∀ k : Fin 4,
        ContMDiffOn (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
          (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
          ((⊤ : ENat) : WithTop ENat) (itinerary k) J ∧
        Set.InjOn (itinerary k) I ∧
        (∀ t ∈ I,
          Function.Injective (mfderiv (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
            (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (itinerary k) t)) ∧
        itinerary k 1 = itinerary (k + 1) 0) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun k : Fin 4 ↦ itinerary k 0) ∧
      (⋃ k : Fin 4, itinerary k '' I) = Set.univ ∧
      (∀ k l : Fin 4, k ≠ l →
        (itinerary k '' I) ∩ (itinerary l '' I) =
          if l = k + 1 then {itinerary k 1}
          else if k = l + 1 then {itinerary k 0}
          else ∅) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ I,
        w.curve (itinerary 0 t) = R 0 t ∧
        w.curve (itinerary 1 t) = bridge 0 t ∧
        w.curve (itinerary 2 t) = R 1 t ∧
        w.curve (itinerary 3 t) = bridge 1 t)

/-- Nontrivial prime curves, where both factors of a nontrivial decomposition have double points
(Definition 3). -/
def IsPrimeCurve (g : GenericCurve) : Prop :=
  ¬Function.Injective g.curve ∧
    ¬∃ a b : GenericCurve,
      ¬Function.Injective a.curve ∧ ¬Function.Injective b.curve ∧ ConnectedSum a b g

/-- Finite prime decompositions with all bracketings and class multiplicities (Definition 2 and
Section 7). A crossing-free circle has the empty profile. -/
inductive CompletedDecomposition : GenericCurve → BinaryTree GenericCurve →
    Multiset (Quotient curveSetoid) → Prop
  | unit (g : GenericCurve) (embedded : Function.Injective g.curve) :
      CompletedDecomposition g BinaryTree.nil 0
  | prime (g : GenericCurve) (hprime : IsPrimeCurve g) :
      CompletedDecomposition g (BinaryTree.node g BinaryTree.nil BinaryTree.nil)
        {Quotient.mk curveSetoid g}
  | sum (g a b : GenericCurve) (ha : ¬Function.Injective a.curve)
      (hb : ¬Function.Injective b.curve) (joined : ConnectedSum a b g)
      (ta tb : BinaryTree GenericCurve) (pa pb : Multiset (Quotient curveSetoid))
      (da : CompletedDecomposition a ta pa) (db : CompletedDecomposition b tb pb) :
      CompletedDecomposition g (BinaryTree.node g ta tb) (pa + pb)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 7). Every generic plane curve, not only a tree-like one, has
a finite prime decomposition, and its multiset of prime classes is unique.

Proper factors are read in the nontrivial sense of Definition 6, and the crossing-free circle's
empty profile is a normalization convention not literal in Definitions 3–5. -/
theorem unique_prime_decomposition (g : GenericCurve) :
    (∃ t : BinaryTree GenericCurve, ∃ p : Multiset (Quotient curveSetoid),
      CompletedDecomposition g t p) ∧
    (∀ t₁ t₂ : BinaryTree GenericCurve,
      ∀ p₁ p₂ : Multiset (Quotient curveSetoid),
        CompletedDecomposition g t₁ p₁ → CompletedDecomposition g t₂ p₂ →
          p₁ = p₂) := by
  sorry

end Grostic2001Connected

theorem Grostic2001Connected.unique_prime_decomposition_neg : ¬ type_of% @Grostic2001Connected.unique_prime_decomposition := by
  sorry

title: Sprague-Grundy Values of the R-Wythoff Game
problem_statement: In gu2015sprague.lean, prove either Gu2015Sprague.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gu2015Sprague.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Sprague-Grundy Values of the R-Wythoff Game

Author: Albert Gu.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2013](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: A. Gu, *Sprague-Grundy Values of the R-Wythoff Game*, Electron. J. Combin. **22**
(2015), no. 2, Paper 2.13, 15 pp.; doi:10.37236/4579.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gu2015Sprague

/-- The Sprague-Grundy value of R-Wythoff (Sections 1 and 1.2). Only a largest pile may be reduced
singly, and equal positive reductions may empty either pile. -/
def grundy (a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {g : ℕ |
    (b ≤ a → ∀ c : Fin a, grundy c.val b ≠ g) ∧
    (a ≤ b → ∀ d : Fin b, grundy a d.val ≠ g) ∧
    (∀ t : Fin (min a b + 1), 0 < t.val →
      grundy (a - t.val) (b - t.val) ≠ g)}
termination_by a + b
decreasing_by
  all_goals omega

/-- The smaller coordinate of the zero-indexed `n`th `g`-position (Section 1.2). Positions are
ordered increasingly by their smaller coordinate. -/
def lowerPosition (g n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.nth (fun a ↦ ∃ b ≥ a, grundy a b = g) n

/-- The larger coordinate paired with `lowerPosition g n` (Section 1.2). These larger coordinates
are not independently sorted and may repeat. -/
def upperPosition (g n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {b : ℕ | lowerPosition g n ≤ b ∧ grundy (lowerPosition g n) b = g}

/-- The Fibonacci-type sequence `F^(a,b)` with seeds `a`, `b` (Section 3.1). -/
def fibonacciSequence (a b : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  ({ order := 2, coeffs := fun _ ↦ 1 } : LinearRecurrence ℕ).mkSol
    (fun i ↦ if i.val = 0 then a else b)

/-- **Conjecture 1** (Section 3.2). For `g > 3`, the paired `g`-positions eventually equal the
Beatty P-positions minus a common offset, except for alternating unit corrections along finitely
many disjoint Fibonacci sequences.

The printed overloaded `k` is separated into family count `r` and term index `t`, as in
Theorems 7 and 8 and the prose following the conjecture. -/
theorem conjecture_1 (g : ℕ) (hg : 3 < g) :
    let φ : ℝ := (1 + √5) / 2
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (C : ℤ) (r : ℕ) (a b : Fin r → ℕ) (x : Fin r → Fin 2),
      (∀ i j : Fin r, i ≠ j →
        Disjoint (Set.range (fibonacciSequence (a i) (b i)))
          (Set.range (fibonacciSequence (a j) (b j)))) ∧
      ∀ n ≥ N,
        (∀ (i : Fin r) (t : ℕ), n = fibonacciSequence (a i) (b i) t →
          (lowerPosition g n : ℤ) =
            Int.floor (φ * n) - (C + (-1 : ℤ) ^ (t + (x i).val)) ∧
          (upperPosition g n : ℤ) =
            Int.floor (φ ^ 2 * n) - (C + (-1 : ℤ) ^ (t + (x i).val))) ∧
        ((∀ (i : Fin r) (t : ℕ), n ≠ fibonacciSequence (a i) (b i) t) →
          (lowerPosition g n : ℤ) = Int.floor (φ * n) - C ∧
          (upperPosition g n : ℤ) = Int.floor (φ ^ 2 * n) - C) := by
  sorry

end Gu2015Sprague

theorem Gu2015Sprague.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gu2015Sprague.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

title: Hat-Guessing on Graphs
problem_statement: In gu2020hat.lean, prove either Gu2020Hat.conjecture_knn_upper_bound or refute it by proving its logical negation Gu2020Hat.conjecture_knn_upper_bound_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Hat-Guessing on Graphs

Authors: Zhuoer Gu, Yuzu Ido, and Benjamin Przybocki.
Origin: [Stanford SURIM](https://surim.stanford.edu/publications/combinatorics/hat-guessing-graphs).
Reference: Z. Gu, Y. Ido, and B. Przybocki, *Hat-Guessing on Graphs*, Stanford SURIM report, 2020.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gu2020Hat

open SimpleGraph Finset

/-- A guessing strategy for vertex `v` in the `q`-color hat-guessing game on `G`. -/
structure HatStrategy {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (q : ℕ) (v : V) where
  /-- The guess for `v`'s hat color, given a hat assignment. -/
  guess : (V → Fin q) → Fin q
  /-- The guess depends only on the colors of `v`'s neighbors. -/
  locality : ∀ h₁ h₂ : V → Fin q,
    (∀ w, G.Adj v w → h₁ w = h₂ w) → guess h₁ = guess h₂

/-- The graph `G` is hat-guessable with `q` colors: a winning strategy profile exists. The
conjunct `0 < q` records the source convention that the color set is nonempty. -/
def HatGuessable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < q ∧ ∃ s : (v : V) → HatStrategy G q v,
    ∀ h : V → Fin q, ∃ v, (s v).guess h = h v

/-- **Conjecture 3.8**. For `n ≥ 3`, the hat-guessing number satisfies `HG(K_{n,n}) ≤ n`.

The best previously known bound is `HG(K_{n,n}) ≤ n + 1` (Gadouleau–Georgiou). -/
theorem conjecture_knn_upper_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hG : HatGuessable (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin n) : SimpleGraph (Fin n ⊕ Fin n)) r) :
    r ≤ n := by
  sorry

end Gu2020Hat

theorem Gu2020Hat.conjecture_knn_upper_bound_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gu2020Hat.conjecture_knn_upper_bound := by
  sorry

program: University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
title: A formula for F-Polynomials in terms of C-Vectors and Stabilization of F-Polynomials
problem_statement: In gupta2018formula.lean, prove either Gupta2018Formula.conjecture_8_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Gupta2018Formula.conjecture_8_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A formula for F-Polynomials in terms of C-Vectors and Stabilization of F-Polynomials

Author: Meghal Gupta.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2018](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: M. Gupta, *A formula for F-Polynomials in terms of C-Vectors and Stabilization of
F-Polynomials*, arXiv:1812.01910 (2018), revised 2019.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gupta2018Formula

/-- Ordinary quiver mutation. Mutable rows are on the left and frozen rows on the right of the
index sum, and positive entries count row-to-column arrows. -/
def mutateQuiver {r : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin r ⊕ Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ)
    (k : Fin r) : Matrix (Fin r ⊕ Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ :=
  fun i j ↦ if i = Sum.inl k ∨ j = k then -Q i j else
    Q i j + max (Q i k) 0 * max (Q (Sum.inl k) j) 0 -
      max (-Q i k) 0 * max (-Q (Sum.inl k) j) 0

/-- The exchange-label part of ordinary quiver mutation. -/
def mutateLabels {r : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin r ⊕ Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ)
    (V : Fin r ⊕ Fin r → FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ)) (k : Fin r) :
    Fin r ⊕ Fin r → FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ) :=
  fun i ↦ if i = Sum.inl k then
    ((∏ j, V j ^ (Q j k).toNat) + (∏ j, V j ^ (-Q j k).toNat)) /
      V (Sum.inl k)
    else V i

/-- The signed frozen-row, mutable-column block after the given mutations (Definition 2.21). It
starts from the principal framing `i' → i`. -/
def cMatrix {r : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ) (w : List (Fin r)) :
    Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ :=
  let Q := w.foldl mutateQuiver (Matrix.fromRows B 1)
  fun i j ↦ Q (Sum.inr i) j

/-- The deformed polynomial obtained by applying `-C⁻¹` to the exponents of the just-mutated
F-polynomial (Definition 2.26). It is realized by monomial substitution in the initial frozen
labels and replay of the exchange sequence. -/
def sPolynomial {r : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℤ)
    (w : List (Fin r)) (k : Fin r) : FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ) :=
  let M := -(cMatrix B (w ++ [k]))⁻¹
  let V : Fin r ⊕ Fin r → FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ) :=
    Sum.elim (fun _ ↦ 1) (fun i ↦
      ∏ j, (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ)
        (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ)) (MvPolynomial.X j)) ^ (M j i))
  let final := (w ++ [k]).foldl
    (fun state v ↦ (mutateQuiver state.1 v, mutateLabels state.1 state.2 v))
    (Matrix.fromRows B 1, V)
  final.2 (Sum.inl k)

The ordinary-mutation and signed-C conventions resolve the duplicated path bullet and omitted
reverse-arrow sign in the printed definitions; the full non-green domain is retained. -/

title: Deficiency of chemical reaction networks: the effect of operations that preserve multistationarity and periodic orbits
problem_statement: In gutierrez2025deficiency.lean, prove either Gutierrez2025Deficiency.partial_flow_inherits_periodic_orbit or refute it by proving its logical negation Gutierrez2025Deficiency.partial_flow_inherits_periodic_orbit_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Deficiency of chemical reaction networks: the effect of operations that preserve multistationarity and periodic orbits

Authors: Awildo Gutierrez, Elijah Leake, Caelyn Rivas-Sobie, Jordy Lopez Garcia, and Anne Shiu.
Origin: [MSRI-UP 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19410v2).
Reference: A. Gutierrez, E. Leake, C. Rivas-Sobie, J. Lopez Garcia, and A. Shiu, *Deficiency of
chemical reaction networks: the effect of operations that preserve multistationarity and periodic
orbits*, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. B **30** (2025), no. 5, 1745–1761.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Gutierrez2025Deficiency

/-- A finite nonempty set of nontrivial reactions between nonnegative integer complexes
(Definition 2.1). -/
structure Network (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The reactions, as (reactant complex, product complex) pairs. -/
  reactions : Finset ((Fin n → ℕ) × (Fin n → ℕ))
  nonempty : reactions.Nonempty
  nontrivial : ∀ r ∈ reactions, r.1 ≠ r.2

/-- The real span of the reaction vectors (Definition 2.3). -/
def Network.stoichiometric {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) : Submodule ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun r : N.reactions ↦
    fun i ↦ (r.val.2 i : ℝ) - (r.val.1 i : ℝ))

/-- The mass-action species-formation vector field, with one rate constant per reaction. -/
def Network.vectorField {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) (κ : N.reactions → ℝ)
    (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  ∑ r : N.reactions, (κ r * ∏ i, x i ^ r.val.1 i) •
    (fun i ↦ (r.val.2 i : ℝ) - (r.val.1 i : ℝ))

/-- A positive nonconstant periodic orbit whose trivial Floquet multiplier is simple on its
stoichiometric subspace (Banaji, arXiv:2201.13105v3, p. 3). -/
structure Network.NondegeneratePeriodicOrbit {n : ℕ} (N : Network n)
    (κ : N.reactions → ℝ) where
  /-- The positive period of the orbit. -/
  period : ℝ
  period_pos : 0 < period
  /-- The positive periodic solution of the mass-action system. -/
  trajectory : ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ)
  positive : ∀ t i, 0 < trajectory t i
  nonconstant : ∃ t, trajectory t ≠ trajectory 0
  periodic : Function.Periodic trajectory period
  solution : IsIntegralCurve trajectory (fun _ ↦ N.vectorField κ)
  /-- The fundamental solution of the variational equation on the stoichiometric subspace. -/
  fundamental : ℝ → (N.stoichiometric →L[ℝ] N.stoichiometric)
  initial : fundamental 0 = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ N.stoichiometric
  variational : ∀ t (v : N.stoichiometric),
    HasDerivAt (fun u ↦ ((fundamental u v : N.stoichiometric) : Fin n → ℝ))
      (fderiv ℝ (N.vectorField κ) (trajectory t)
        ((fundamental t v : N.stoichiometric) : Fin n → ℝ)) t
  multiplier_one : (fundamental period).toLinearMap.charpoly.eval 1 = 0
  multiplier_simple : (fundamental period).toLinearMap.charpoly.derivative.eval 1 ≠ 0

/-- **Remark 3.2** (preprint Remark 3.3). Partial flow additions satisfying
Cappelletti–Feliu–Wiuf Theorem 8 preserve the capacity for positive nondegenerate periodic orbits.

Capacity is existential in mass-action rates on both networks, and nondegeneracy means a simple
Floquet multiplier `1`, not hyperbolicity or stability. -/
theorem partial_flow_inherits_periodic_orbit {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (N N' : Network n) (I O : Finset (Fin n))
    (hin : ∀ i ∈ I, (0, Pi.single i 1) ∉ N.reactions)
    (hout : ∀ i ∈ O, (Pi.single i 1, 0) ∉ N.reactions)
    (hext : N'.reactions = N.reactions ∪
      I.image (fun i ↦ (0, Pi.single i 1)) ∪
      O.image (fun i ↦ (Pi.single i 1, 0))) :
    let WO : Set (Module.Dual ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)) :=
      {w | w ∈ N.stoichiometric.dualAnnihilator ∧ ∀ i ∉ O, w (Pi.single i 1) = 0}
    let conserved := fun x : Fin n → ℝ ↦ fun w : {w // w ∈ WO} ↦ w.val x
    (∀ i ∈ I, i ∉ O → Pi.single i 1 ∈ N.stoichiometric) →
    (∀ w ∈ N.stoichiometric.dualAnnihilator, ∃ a ∈ WO,
      ∃ b ∈ ({v | v ∈ N.stoichiometric.dualAnnihilator ∧ ∀ i ∈ O, v (Pi.single i 1) = 0} :
      Set (Module.Dual ℝ (Fin n → ℝ))), w = a + b) →
    conserved '' {x | ∀ i, 0 < x i} =
      conserved '' {x | (∀ i ∈ I, 0 < x i) ∧ (∀ i ∉ I, x i = 0)} →
    (∃ κ : N.reactions → ℝ, (∀ r, 0 < κ r) ∧
      Nonempty (N.NondegeneratePeriodicOrbit κ)) →
    ∃ κ' : N'.reactions → ℝ, (∀ r, 0 < κ' r) ∧
      Nonempty (N'.NondegeneratePeriodicOrbit κ') := by sorry

end Gutierrez2025Deficiency

theorem Gutierrez2025Deficiency.partial_flow_inherits_periodic_orbit_neg : ¬ type_of% @Gutierrez2025Deficiency.partial_flow_inherits_periodic_orbit := by
  sorry

title: Wilf Equivalence in Weyl Groups and Signed Permutations
problem_statement: In haenni2019wilf.lean, prove either Haenni2019Wilf.conjecture_3_26 or refute it by proving its logical negation Haenni2019Wilf.conjecture_3_26_neg.
challenge:

/-!
# Wilf Equivalence in Weyl Groups and Signed Permutations

Author: Kaarel Haenni.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2019](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: K. Haenni, *Wilf equivalence in Weyl groups and signed permutations*, MIT SPUR final
paper, August 1, 2019, 31 pp.; see also Y. Gao and K. Hanni, *Counting signed vexillary
permutations*, Adv. Appl. Math. **121** (2020), 102106.
-/

namespace Haenni2019Wilf

/-- The set `B_n^j(pattern)` of signed permutations with `j` positive images of positive indices
whose increasing `2n`-letter embedding avoids the pattern (Section 3). `Fin.rev` represents sign
reversal. -/
def avoidingSignedPermutations {k : ℕ} (pattern : Fin k → ℕ) (n j : ℕ) :
    Set (Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * n))) :=
  {w | (∀ i, w i.rev = (w i).rev) ∧
    {i : Fin (2 * n) | n ≤ i.val ∧ n ≤ (w i).val}.ncard = j ∧
    ¬∃ f : Fin k → Fin (2 * n), StrictMono f ∧
      ∀ a b, w (f a) < w (f b) ↔ pattern a < pattern b}

/-- **Conjecture 3.26** (p. 30; also Gao–Hanni Conjecture 4.1). The patterns `12345` and `21354`
have equal signed-permutation avoidance counts at every positive-image count.

Containment is classical containment in the full `2n`-letter embedding, not root-system
containment. -/
theorem conjecture_3_26 (n j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ n) :
    (avoidingSignedPermutations ![0, 1, 2, 3, 4] n j).ncard =
      (avoidingSignedPermutations ![1, 0, 2, 4, 3] n j).ncard := by
  sorry

end Haenni2019Wilf
