  sorry

title: Minimum number of non-zero-entries in a stable matrix exhibiting Turing instability
problem_statement: In hambric2022minimum.lean, prove either Hambric2022Minimum.minimum_support_gap or refute it by proving its logical negation Hambric2022Minimum.minimum_support_gap_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Minimum number of non-zero-entries in a stable matrix exhibiting Turing instability

Authors: Christopher Logan Hambric, Chi-Kwong Li, Diane Christine Pelejo, and Junping Shi.
Origin: [William & Mary EXTREEMS-QED](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/1331021.json).
Reference: C. L. Hambric, C.-K. Li, D. C. Pelejo, and J. Shi, *Minimum number of non-zero-entries
in a stable matrix exhibiting Turing instability*, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. Ser. S **15**
(2022), no. 9, 2497–2511; doi:10.3934/dcdss.2021128.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Hambric2022Minimum

/-- Strict stability of a real matrix, tested on all its complex eigenvalues. -/
def Stable {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ z : ℂ, Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' (A.map Complex.ofReal)) z → z.re < 0

/-- Irreducibility: strong connectivity of the directed nonzero support on all vertices. -/
def IsIrreducible {n : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Zero K]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : Prop :=
  letI : Quiver (Fin n) := { Hom := fun i j ↦ PLift (A i j ≠ 0) }
  Quiver.IsStronglyConnected (Fin n)

/-- A sign pattern is potentially stable if it has a stable real realization. -/
def PotentiallyStable {n : ℕ} (S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) SignType) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
    (∀ i j, SignType.sign (A i j) = S i j) ∧ Stable A

/-- Turing instability: strict stability is lost after subtracting some positive multiple of a
nonnegative diagonal matrix. Zero diffusion coefficients are allowed. -/
def TuringInstability {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Prop :=
  Stable A ∧ ∃ P : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, ∃ t : ℝ,
    P.IsDiag ∧ (∀ i, 0 ≤ P i i) ∧ 0 < t ∧
      ¬Stable (A - t • P)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (following (1), p. 2499). The minimum support size of an
irreducible potentially stable sign pattern is strictly smaller than that of an irreducible matrix
exhibiting Turing instability.

The printed sentence says `n ∈ ℕ`; the model domain `n ≥ 2` is inherited from context. Both minima
are attained, and instability negates the same strict stability predicate, without requiring an
eigenvalue with strictly positive real part. -/
theorem minimum_support_gap (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ m s : ℕ,
      IsLeast {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) SignType,
        IsIrreducible S ∧ PotentiallyStable S ∧
          {p : Fin n × Fin n | S p.1 p.2 ≠ 0}.ncard = k} m ∧
      IsLeast {k : ℕ | ∃ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
        IsIrreducible A ∧ TuringInstability A ∧
          {p : Fin n × Fin n | A p.1 p.2 ≠ 0}.ncard = k} s ∧
      m < s := by
  sorry

end Hambric2022Minimum

theorem Hambric2022Minimum.minimum_support_gap_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hambric2022Minimum.minimum_support_gap := by
  sorry

title: Investigations on Automorphism Groups of Quantum Stabilizer Codes
problem_statement: In hao2021investigations.lean, prove either Hao2021Investigations.question_2_16_strong_and_weak_automorphism_groups_trivial or refute it by proving its logical negation Hao2021Investigations.question_2_16_strong_and_weak_automorphism_groups_trivial_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Investigations on Automorphism Groups of Quantum Stabilizer Codes

Author: Hanson Hao.
Origin: [Stanford SURIM
2021](https://surim.stanford.edu/publications/abstract-algebra/investigations-automorphism-groups-quantum-stabilizer-codes).
Reference: H. Hao, *Investigations on Automorphism Groups of Quantum Stabilizer Codes*,
arXiv:2109.12735.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Hao2021Investigations

/-- Single-qubit Pauli labels. -/
inductive PauliLabel : Type
  | I | X | Y | Z

namespace PauliLabel

/-- The binary `X` support of a Pauli label. -/
def xBit : PauliLabel → ZMod 2
  | I => 0
  | X => 1
  | Y => 1
  | Z => 0

/-- The binary `Z` support of a Pauli label. -/
def zBit : PauliLabel → ZMod 2
  | I => 0
  | X => 0
  | Y => 1
  | Z => 1

/-- The phase of a label in the normal form `i^phase X^x Z^z`, so that `Y = i X Z`. -/
def phase : PauliLabel → ZMod 4
  | I => 0
  | X => 0
  | Y => 1
  | Z => 0

end PauliLabel

/-- A finite Pauli word in the normal form `i^phase * ∏_j X_j^{x_j} Z_j^{z_j}`. Stabilizer
membership uses the exact phase, weak automorphism membership only the binary supports. -/
structure PauliWord (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The exponent of the phase factor `i`. -/
  phase : ZMod 4
  /-- The exponent `x_j` of `X_j` at each qubit. -/
  x : Fin n → ZMod 2
  /-- The exponent `z_j` of `Z_j` at each qubit. -/
  z : Fin n → ZMod 2

namespace PauliWord

/-- The identity Pauli word. -/
def one (n : ℕ) : PauliWord n where
  phase := 0
  x := fun _ ↦ 0
  z := fun _ ↦ 0

/-- Multiplication of Pauli words in the normal form `i^a X^u Z^v`. -/
def mul {n : ℕ} (p q : PauliWord n) : PauliWord n where
  phase := p.phase + q.phase +
    ∑ i : Fin n, if p.z i = 1 ∧ q.x i = 1 then (2 : ZMod 4) else 0
  x := fun i ↦ p.x i + q.x i
  z := fun i ↦ p.z i + q.z i

/-- The positive tensor word attached to a function of Pauli labels. -/
def ofLabels {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → PauliLabel) : PauliWord n where
  phase := ∑ i : Fin n, (f i).phase
  x := fun i ↦ (f i).xBit
  z := fun i ↦ (f i).zBit

/-- The `S_n` action on `G_n` permuting tensor factors. The phase is unchanged and supports are
pulled back by `σ⁻¹`. -/
def permute {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (p : PauliWord n) : PauliWord n where
  phase := p.phase
  x := fun i ↦ p.x (σ.symm i)
  z := fun i ↦ p.z (σ.symm i)

end PauliWord

open PauliLabel

/-- The ten positive Pauli-word generators of the `[[11,1,5]]` code (Section 2.2.7,
Question 2.16). -/
def q216Generator : Fin 10 → PauliWord 11
  | ⟨0, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![Z, Z, Z, Z, Z, Z, I, I, I, I, I]
  | ⟨1, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![X, X, X, X, X, X, I, I, I, I, I]
  | ⟨2, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![I, I, I, Z, X, Y, Y, Y, Y, X, Z]
  | ⟨3, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![I, I, I, X, Y, Z, Z, Z, Z, Y, X]
  | ⟨4, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![Z, Y, X, I, I, I, Z, Y, X, I, I]
  | ⟨5, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![X, Z, Y, I, I, I, X, Z, Y, I, I]
  | ⟨6, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![I, I, I, Z, Y, X, X, Y, Z, I, I]
  | ⟨7, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![I, I, I, X, Z, Y, Z, X, Y, I, I]
  | ⟨8, _⟩ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![Z, X, Y, I, I, I, Z, Z, Z, X, Y]
  | _ => PauliWord.ofLabels ![Y, Z, X, I, I, I, Y, Y, Y, Z, X]

/-- The ordered product of a finite family of Pauli words selected by binary coefficients. -/
def pauliProduct {m n : ℕ} (g : Fin m → PauliWord n) (coeff : Fin m → ZMod 2) :
    PauliWord n :=
  (List.finRange m).foldl
    (fun acc j ↦ if coeff j = 0 then acc else PauliWord.mul acc (g j))
    (PauliWord.one n)

/-- **Question 2.16** (with its preceding explicit suspicion). The listed `[[11,1,5]]` code has
trivial strong and weak automorphism groups.

The generator tests are Corollaries 2.3 and 2.8; for these Hermitian stabilizer elements,
equality of binary supports is equality up to sign. -/
theorem question_2_16_strong_and_weak_automorphism_groups_trivial :
    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 11),
      (∀ j : Fin 10, ∃ coeff : Fin 10 → ZMod 2,
        PauliWord.permute σ (q216Generator j) = pauliProduct q216Generator coeff) ↔ σ = 1) ∧
    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 11),
      (∀ j : Fin 10, ∃ coeff : Fin 10 → ZMod 2,
        (PauliWord.permute σ (q216Generator j)).x = (pauliProduct q216Generator coeff).x ∧
          (PauliWord.permute σ (q216Generator j)).z = (pauliProduct q216Generator coeff).z) ↔
        σ = 1) := by
  sorry

end Hao2021Investigations

theorem Hao2021Investigations.question_2_16_strong_and_weak_automorphism_groups_trivial_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hao2021Investigations.question_2_16_strong_and_weak_automorphism_groups_trivial := by
  sorry

/-!
# Sum-Product Estimates for Well-Spaced Sets

Author: Alina Harbuzova.
Origin: [MIT UROP+ 2020](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/urop-plus/papers.html).
Reference: A. Harbuzova, *Sum-Product Estimates for Well-Spaced Sets*, UROP+ Final Paper,
August 2020, 12 pp.;
https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/urop-plus/documents/2020/Harbuzova.pdf.

namespace Harbuzova2020Sum

open scoped Pointwise
open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- The largest cardinality of a subset whose distinct points have distance at least `δ`
(Definitions 2.1 and 2.2). -/
def packingNumber (S : Finset ℝ) (δ : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ({B ∈ S.powerset | (B : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y ↦ δ ≤ |x - y|)} :
    Finset (Finset ℝ)).sup Finset.card

/-- **Conjecture 2** (Full-Size Conjecture, Section 3, p. 4). One exponent gives full-size sumset
or productset packing for every fixed positive spacing constant and positive exponent loss,
uniformly in the finite input set and its size.

The asymptotic notation is expanded with one `α` chosen before `c` and `ε`, and `K` independent of
`A` and its size; nonemptiness supplies the inverse-cardinality scale. -/
theorem conjecture_2 :
    ∃ α : ℝ, 1 < α ∧
      ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
        ∃ K > (0 : ℝ),
          ∀ (A : Finset ℝ) (hA : A.Nonempty)
            (hinterval : (A : Set ℝ) ⊆ Set.Icc 1 2)
            (hspacing : (A : Set ℝ).Pairwise
              (fun a b ↦ c / (#A : ℝ) ≤ |a - b|)),
            K * ((#A : ℝ) ^ (-α)) ^ (-1 + ε) ≤
              max (packingNumber (A + A) ((#A : ℝ) ^ (-α)) : ℝ)
                (packingNumber (A * A) ((#A : ℝ) ^ (-α)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Harbuzova2020Sum

Authors: John Harding, Ekaterina Jager, and Derek Smith.

/-- **Question 2** (p. 546). The additive group generated by projections has the universal
extension property of the unigroup of the closed-subspace lattice.

The positive direction follows the expectation on p. 547. The universal property is encoded as
unique additive extension, equivalent to the source's generator-compatible additive isomorphism;
all real Hilbert spaces of dimension at least three and all abelian codomains are retained. -/

    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

title: Geometric Progression-Free Sequences with Small Gaps
problem_statement: In he2015geometric.lean, prove either He2015Geometric.conjecture_10 or refute it by proving its logical negation He2015Geometric.conjecture_10_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Geometric Progression-Free Sequences with Small Gaps

Author: Xiaoyu He.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2014](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: X. He, *Geometric progression-free sequences with small gaps*, J. Number Theory **151**
(2015), 197–210; doi:10.1016/j.jnt.2014.12.018; arXiv:1501.04121v1.
-/

namespace He2015Geometric

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

/-- The family `G_6` of increasing six-term geometric progressions of positive integers with
rational common ratio greater than one. Indexing by tuples counts each progression once. -/
def SixProgression :=
  {g : Fin 6 → ℕ // (∀ i, 0 < g i) ∧
    ∃ r : ℚ, 1 < r ∧ ∀ i : Fin 5,
      (g i.succ : ℚ) = r * (g i.castSucc : ℚ)}

/-- The remaining set `T`, with one of the two middle terms removed from each progression
(Definition 6). -/
def survivingSet (bits : SixProgression → Bool) : Set ℕ :=
  {n | 0 < n ∧ ∀ g : SixProgression,
    n ≠ (if bits g then g.val 2 else g.val 3)}

/-- **Conjecture 10**. For some fixed positive exponent, the random 6-GP-free process has
polylogarithmic gaps with positive probability.

The gap bound is expressed in eventual-interval form, without enumerating the surviving set. -/
theorem conjecture_10 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      0 < Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : SixProgression ↦
          bernoulliMeasure true false ⟨(1 : ℝ) / 2, by norm_num⟩)
        {bits : SixProgression → Bool |
        ∃ K > (0 : ℕ), ∃ N ≥ (2 : ℕ),
          ∀ x ≥ N, ∃ n : ℕ,
            n ∈ survivingSet bits ∧ x < n ∧
              (n : ℝ) ≤ x + K * (Real.log (x : ℝ)) ^ C} := by
  sorry

end He2015Geometric

theorem He2015Geometric.conjecture_10_neg : ¬ type_of% @He2015Geometric.conjecture_10 := by
  sorry

program: University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
title: Peckness of Edge Posets
problem_statement: In hemminger2017peckness.lean, prove either Hemminger2017Peckness.conjecture_1_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Hemminger2017Peckness.conjecture_1_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Peckness of Edge Posets

Authors: David Hemminger, Aaron Landesman, and Zijian Yao.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2014](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: D. Hemminger, A. Landesman, and Z. Yao, *Peckness of edge posets*, Order **34** (2017),
441–463; arXiv:1501.04540v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Hemminger2017Peckness

open scoped Pointwise
open Finset

/-- The Boolean-lattice quotient: orbits of subsets under `G`. -/
def BooleanQuotient {n : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) :=
  MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient G (Finset (Fin n))

/-- The quotient order, expressed using orbit representatives (Section 2). -/
instance {n : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) :
    PartialOrder (BooleanQuotient G) where
  le a b := ∃ g : G, g • a.out ⊆ b.out
  le_refl a := ⟨1, by simp⟩
  le_trans a b c hab hbc := by
    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hab
    obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hbc
    refine ⟨h * g, ?_⟩
    rw [mul_smul]
    exact (Finset.smul_finset_subset_smul_finset_iff.mpr hg).trans hh
  le_antisymm a b hab hba := by
    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hab
    obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hba
    have hcard : #b.out ≤ #a.out := by
      simpa only [Finset.card_smul_finset] using Finset.card_le_card hh
    have heq : g • a.out = b.out :=
      Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hg (by simpa using hcard)
    have hquot : (Quotient.mk _ b.out : BooleanQuotient G) = Quotient.mk _ a.out :=
      Quotient.sound ⟨g, heq⟩
    rw [← Quotient.out_eq a, ← Quotient.out_eq b]
    exact hquot.symm

/-- The rank of a subset orbit, independent of the chosen representative. -/
def quotientRank {n : ℕ} {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))}
    (a : BooleanQuotient G) : ℕ := #a.out

/-- The elements of the edge poset: covering pairs (Definition 1.1). -/
def Edge (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] := {p : P × P // p.1 ⋖ p.2}

/-- The edge-poset order generated by simultaneous covers (Definition 1.1). -/
instance {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] : PartialOrder (Edge P) where
  le e f := Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b : Edge P ↦
    a.val.1 ⋖ b.val.1 ∧ a.val.2 ⋖ b.val.2) e f
  le_refl _ := .refl
  le_trans _ _ _ := Relation.ReflTransGen.trans
  le_antisymm e f hef hfe := by
    have endpoints : ∀ {a b : Edge P},
        Relation.ReflTransGen (fun x y : Edge P ↦
          x.val.1 ⋖ y.val.1 ∧ x.val.2 ⋖ y.val.2) a b →
        a.val.1 ≤ b.val.1 ∧ a.val.2 ≤ b.val.2 := by
      intro a b hab
      induction hab using Relation.ReflTransGen.trans_induction_on with
      | refl _ => exact ⟨le_rfl, le_rfl⟩
      | single h => exact ⟨h.1.le, h.2.le⟩
      | trans _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact ⟨h₁.1.trans h₂.1, h₁.2.trans h₂.2⟩
    exact Subtype.ext (Prod.ext
      (le_antisymm (endpoints hef).1 (endpoints hfe).1)
      (le_antisymm (endpoints hef).2 (endpoints hfe).2))

/-- Peckness: rank symmetry, rank unimodality and the strong Sperner property (Definition 2.4). -/
def IsPeck (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] (rank : P → ℕ) (topRank : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let p := fun i ↦ Nat.card {x : P // rank x = i}
  (∀ i ≤ topRank, p i = p (topRank - i)) ∧
  (∃ k ≤ topRank,
    (∀ i j, i ≤ j → j ≤ k → p i ≤ p j) ∧
    (∀ i j, k ≤ i → i ≤ j → j ≤ topRank → p j ≤ p i)) ∧
  (∀ k ≤ topRank + 1, ∀ A : Fin k → Finset P,
    (∀ i, IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) (A i : Set P)) →
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (A i) (A j)) →
    ∃ I : Finset (Fin (topRank + 1)), #I = k ∧
      (∑ i, #(A i)) ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, p i.val)

/-- **Conjecture 1.3**. Every Boolean-lattice quotient has a Peck edge poset.

The edge order is not the coordinatewise order on pairs of orbits. -/
theorem conjecture_1_3 {n : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) :
    IsPeck (Edge (BooleanQuotient G)) (fun e ↦ quotientRank e.val.1) (n - 1) := by
  sorry

end Hemminger2017Peckness

theorem Hemminger2017Peckness.conjecture_1_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hemminger2017Peckness.conjecture_1_3 := by
  sorry

title: p-Energy and p-Harmonic Functions on Sierpinski Gasket Type Fractals
problem_statement: In herman2004p.lean, prove either Herman2004P.unique_fixed_point_global_attraction or refute it by proving its logical negation Herman2004P.unique_fixed_point_global_attraction_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# p-Energy and p-Harmonic Functions on Sierpinski Gasket Type Fractals

Authors: P. Edward Herman, Roberto Peirone, and Robert S. Strichartz.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU](https://math.cornell.edu/history-reu-and-spur-programs-department-mathematics).
Reference: P. E. Herman, R. Peirone, and R. S. Strichartz, *p-Energy and p-Harmonic Functions on
Sierpinski Gasket Type Fractals*, Potential Analysis **20** (2004), 125–148.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Herman2004P

/-- The boundary energy reconstructed by (2.10), including the constant triple and even extension.
`projIcc` only supplies the subtype for a ratio already in `[0,1]`. -/
def boundaryEnergy (p : ℝ) (g : unitInterval → ℝ)
    (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let lo := min (a 0) (min (a 1) (a 2))
  let hi := max (a 0) (max (a 1) (a 2))
  let mid := a 0 + a 1 + a 2 - lo - hi
  if lo = hi then 0 else
    ((hi - lo) / 2) ^ p *
      g (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one (|2 * mid - lo - hi| / (hi - lo)))

/-- Positive continuous normalized profiles whose reconstructed three-variable energy is convex
(Definition 3.1), without the `G_0` restriction. -/
def G (p : ℝ) : Set (unitInterval → ℝ) :=
  {g | Continuous g ∧ (∀ x, 0 < g x) ∧ g 1 = 1 ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (boundaryEnergy p g)}

/-- The trace minimum value over all three real interior vertex values (following (2.14)). It is
an infimum, attained for `p > 1` and `g ∈ G`. -/
def traceEnergy (p : ℝ) (g : unitInterval → ℝ)
    (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sInf (Set.range (fun b : Fin 3 → ℝ ↦
    boundaryEnergy p g ![a 0, b 1, b 2] +
    boundaryEnergy p g ![b 0, a 1, b 2] +
    boundaryEnergy p g ![b 0, b 1, a 2]))

/-- The three-cell trace followed by normalization at `1` (Equations (3.1)–(3.2)). Values outside
`G` are unused junk. -/
def normalizedT (p : ℝ) (g : unitInterval → ℝ) : unitInterval → ℝ :=
  fun x ↦ traceEnergy p g ![-1, (x : ℝ), 1] /
    traceEnergy p g ![-1, 1, 1]

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction, p. 129). For `p > 1`, the normalized operator has a
unique fixed point in `G`, and every start in `G` converges to it uniformly on `[0,1]`.

Global attraction is read from the cited Peirone context rather than from expanded quantifiers in
the source. -/
theorem unique_fixed_point_global_attraction (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) :
    ∃ gp ∈ G p, normalizedT p gp = gp ∧
      (∀ g ∈ G p, normalizedT p g = g → g = gp) ∧
      (∀ g ∈ G p,
        TendstoUniformly (fun n : ℕ ↦ (normalizedT p)^[n] g) gp Filter.atTop) := by
  sorry

end Herman2004P

theorem Herman2004P.unique_fixed_point_global_attraction_neg : ¬ type_of% @Herman2004P.unique_fixed_point_global_attraction := by
  sorry

title: Positive eigenvalues of generalized words in two Hermitian positive definite matrices
problem_statement: In hillar2003positive.lean, prove either Hillar2003Positive.conjecture_1_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Hillar2003Positive.conjecture_1_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Positive eigenvalues of generalized words in two Hermitian positive definite matrices

Authors: Christopher J. Hillar and Charles R. Johnson.
Origin: [William & Mary REU 1999](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0504587).
Reference: C. J. Hillar and C. R. Johnson, *Positive eigenvalues of generalized words in two
Hermitian positive definite matrices*, Fields Inst. Commun. **37** (2003), 111–122;
arXiv:math/0504587v1.
-/

noncomputable section

open scoped MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace Hillar2003Positive

/-- Generalized words in two letters with real exponents and the usual power cancellations. -/
abbrev GWord := Monoid.Coprod (Multiplicative ℝ) (Multiplicative ℝ)

/-- The reversal of a word, keeping each exponent and reversing the order of the factors. -/
def reversal (w : GWord) : GWord :=
  (Monoid.Coprod.map invMonoidHom invMonoidHom w)⁻¹

/-- Nearly symmetric words: products of two words fixed by reversal. -/
def NearlySymmetric (w : GWord) : Prop :=
  ∃ u v : GWord, w = u * v ∧ reversal u = u ∧ reversal v = v

/-- Evaluation of a generalized word by primary real powers of the two positive matrices. -/
def eval {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosDef) :
    GWord →* Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ :=
  let a : Multiplicative ℝ →* Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ :=
    { toFun := fun p ↦ CFC.rpow A p.toAdd
      map_one' := CFC.rpow_zero A hA.posSemidef.nonneg
      map_mul' := fun _ _ ↦ CFC.rpow_add hA.isUnit }
  let b : Multiplicative ℝ →* Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ :=
    { toFun := fun p ↦ CFC.rpow B p.toAdd
      map_one' := CFC.rpow_zero B hB.posSemidef.nonneg
      map_mul' := fun _ _ ↦ CFC.rpow_add hB.isUnit }
  Monoid.Coprod.lift a b

/-- A good generalized word, with strictly positive real eigenvalues in every positive dimension. -/
def Good (w : GWord) : Prop :=
  ∀ n > 0, ∀ (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosDef),
    ∀ z ∈ spectrum ℂ (eval A B hA hB w), z.im = 0 ∧ 0 < z.re

/-- **Conjecture 1.3**. A generalized real-power word is good exactly when it is nearly
symmetric. -/
theorem conjecture_1_3 (w : GWord) : Good w ↔ NearlySymmetric w := by
  sorry

end Hillar2003Positive

theorem Hillar2003Positive.conjecture_1_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hillar2003Positive.conjecture_1_3 := by
  sorry

title: The Unreasonable Rigidity of Ulam Sets
problem_statement: In hinman2017unreasonable.lean, prove either Hinman2017Unreasonable.rigidity or refute it by proving its logical negation Hinman2017Unreasonable.rigidity_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Unreasonable Rigidity of Ulam Sets

Authors: Joshua Hinman, Borys Kuca, Alexander Schlesinger, and Arseniy Sheydvasser.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY 2017](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: J. Hinman, B. Kuca, A. Schlesinger, and A. Sheydvasser, *The Unreasonable Rigidity of
Ulam Sets*, arXiv:1711.00145v1 (2017).
-/

namespace Hinman2017Unreasonable

/-- Membership in the generalized Ulam sequence seeded by `1` and `b`: after the seeds, a number
belongs when it has exactly one ordered increasing pair of smaller Ulam summands. -/
def IsUlam (b k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  if k ≤ b then k = 1 ∨ k = b else
    ∃! p : Fin k × Fin k,
      p.1.val < p.2.val ∧ p.1.val + p.2.val = k ∧
        IsUlam b p.1.val ∧ IsUlam b p.2.val
termination_by k

/-- **Conjecture 1.1**. For every `n ≥ 4`, the interval endpoints of the complete `U(1,n)` follow
one common integer-affine family.

Intervals are the ordered nonempty maximal runs of Section 3 (cf. Sheydvasser, arXiv:1910.00109v2,
Conjecture 1.3), separated by `upper_i + 1 < lower_(i+1)`, since the printed inequalities do not
express maximality. -/
theorem rigidity :
    ∃ m p k r : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ n ≥ (4 : ℕ),
      (∀ i : ℕ, m i * (n : ℤ) + p i ≤ k i * (n : ℤ) + r i ∧
        k i * (n : ℤ) + r i + 1 < m (i + 1) * (n : ℤ) + p (i + 1)) ∧
        Int.ofNat '' {t : ℕ | IsUlam n t} =
          ⋃ i : ℕ, Set.Icc (m i * (n : ℤ) + p i) (k i * (n : ℤ) + r i) := by
  sorry

end Hinman2017Unreasonable

theorem Hinman2017Unreasonable.rigidity_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hinman2017Unreasonable.rigidity := by
  sorry

title: Self-Similarity in Level Set Trees of Geometric Random Walks
problem_statement: In hirst2016self.lean, prove either Hirst2016Self.conjecture_3_11 or refute it by proving its logical negation Hirst2016Self.conjecture_3_11_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Self-Similarity in Level Set Trees of Geometric Random Walks

Authors: Anna-Sophia Hirst, Rachel Linder, and Daniel Malmuth.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
2016](https://math.oregonstate.edu/undergraduate/research/reu/proceedings-archive).
Reference: A.-S. Hirst, R. Linder, and D. Malmuth, *Self-Similarity in Level Set Trees of
Geometric Random Walks*, Oregon State University REU report, August 12, 2016, 1–11.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Hirst2016Self

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped Topology
open Finset

/-- The integer increment law of Definition 3.1, as a probability measure. Shifting by one before
the sign keeps magnitudes positive even at `r = 1`, and outside the target's hypotheses (positive
sum, nonzero `r₁`, `r₂`) the law is a junk value. -/
def kernel (p₁ p₂ : ℝ) (r₁ r₂ : unitInterval)
    (hp₁ : 0 ≤ p₁) (hp₂ : 0 ≤ p₂) (hpSumLe : p₁ + p₂ ≤ 1) :
    ProbabilityMeasure ℤ :=
  { val :=
      ENNReal.ofReal p₁ • (geometricMeasure r₁).map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℤ) + 1) +
        ENNReal.ofReal (1 - p₁ - p₂) • Measure.dirac 0 +
        ENNReal.ofReal p₂ • (geometricMeasure r₂).map (fun n : ℕ ↦ -((n : ℤ) + 1))
    property := by
      refine { measure_univ := ?_ }
      have hzero : 0 ≤ 1 - p₁ - p₂ := by
        rw [sub_sub]
        exact sub_nonneg.mpr hpSumLe
      simp only [Measure.add_apply, Measure.smul_apply,
        measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      rw [add_assoc, ← ENNReal.ofReal_add hzero hp₂, sub_add_cancel,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_add hp₁ (le_trans hzero (sub_le_self _ hp₂))]
      simp [sub_eq_add_neg] }

open scoped Classical in
/-- Supports of all attained-height superlevel components of the sampled path. -/
def levelComponents {N : ℕ} (x : Fin N → ℤ) : Finset (Finset (Fin N)) :=
  {A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)).powerset |
    ∃ h : Fin N, ∃ i : {j : Fin N // x h ≤ x j},
      A = ({j | ∃ hj : x h ≤ x j,
        ((SimpleGraph.pathGraph N).induce {k | x h ≤ x k}).Reachable i ⟨j, hj⟩} :
          Finset (Fin N))}

open scoped Classical in
/-- Horton-Strahler order on the superlevel component hierarchy. -/
def hortonRank {N : ℕ} (x : Fin N → ℤ) : Finset (Fin N) → ℕ :=
  Finset.strongInduction fun A rec ↦
    let C := {B ∈ levelComponents x |
      B ⊂ A ∧ ∀ D ∈ levelComponents x, B ⊂ D → ¬D ⊂ A}
    let order : {B // B ∈ C} → ℕ := fun B ↦
      rec B.1 (Finset.mem_filter.mp B.2).2.1
    let orders := C.attach
    let M := orders.sup order
    if C.Nonempty then
      if 2 ≤ #{B ∈ orders | order B = M} then M + 1 else M
    else 1

/-- Number of maximal connected branches with the specified Horton-Strahler order. -/
def branchCount {N : ℕ} (x : Fin N → ℤ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card
    (((SimpleGraph.hasse {A : Finset (Fin N) // A ∈ levelComponents x}).induce
      {A | hortonRank x A.1 = k}).ConnectedComponent)

/-- **Conjecture 3.11**. The geometric-walk family has ratio-asymptotic Horton exponent four exactly
when its increment mean is zero.

The finite-prefix reading follows the cited 2012 finite-chain construction; both directions,
one-sided weights, laziness and degenerate finite samples are retained. -/
theorem conjecture_3_11 (p₁ p₂ : ℝ) (r₁ r₂ : unitInterval)
    (hp₁ : 0 ≤ p₁) (hp₂ : 0 ≤ p₂) (hp : 0 < p₁ + p₂)
    (hp_le : p₁ + p₂ ≤ 1) (hr₁ : 0 < (r₁ : ℝ)) (hr₂ : 0 < (r₂ : ℝ)) :
    (∃ a : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ k ≥ 1, 0 ≤ a k) ∧
      (∀ k ≥ 1,
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure
          (MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ ↦
            (kernel p₁ p₂ r₁ r₂ hp₁ hp₂ hp_le : MeasureTheory.Measure ℤ))
          (fun N : ℕ ↦ fun w : ℕ → ℤ ↦
            (branchCount (fun i : Fin N ↦ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range i.val, w j) k : ℝ) /
              (N : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (fun _ ↦ a k)) ∧
      ((∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop, 0 < a (k + 1)) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ a k / a (k + 1)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 4))) ↔
      p₁ / (r₁ : ℝ) - p₂ / (r₂ : ℝ) = 0 := by
  sorry

end Hirst2016Self

theorem Hirst2016Self.conjecture_3_11_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hirst2016Self.conjecture_3_11 := by
  sorry

title: Preseparable Extensions of Multidimensional Preferences
problem_statement: In hodge2009preseparable.lean, prove either Hodge2009Preseparable.character_admissibility_np_hard or refute it by proving its logical negation Hodge2009Preseparable.character_admissibility_np_hard_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Preseparable Extensions of Multidimensional Preferences

Authors: Jonathan K. Hodge, Mark Krines, and Jennifer Lahr.
Origin: [Grand Valley State University REU
2007](https://www.gvsu.edu/mathreu/research-and-publications-at-previous-reu-programs-5.htm).
Reference: J. K. Hodge, M. Krines, and J. Lahr, *Preseparable extensions of multidimensional
preferences*, Order **26** (2009), 125–147; doi:10.1007/s11083-009-9112-1.
-/

namespace Hodge2009Preseparable

/-- Separability: the strict preference between outcomes on `S` is independent of the fixed
outcome outside `S` (Definition 3). -/
def Separable {n : ℕ} (order : LinearOrder (Fin n → Bool))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b u v : Fin n → Bool,
    order.lt (fun i ↦ if i ∈ S then a i else u i)
      (fun i ↦ if i ∈ S then b i else u i) →
    order.lt (fun i ↦ if i ∈ S then a i else v i)
      (fun i ↦ if i ∈ S then b i else v i)

/-- A character is admissible if some total order has exactly its listed separable sets
(p. 128). -/
def Admissible {n : ℕ} (C : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ order : LinearOrder (Fin n → Bool),
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), S ∈ C ↔ Separable order S

/-- The explicit finite-family input: a binary field for `n` followed by one `n`-bit incidence row
per listed subset, each field terminated by `none`. Malformed input is rejected, and the family
must contain the empty and full sets. -/
def readCharacter (word : List (Option Bool)) :
    Option ((n : ℕ) × Finset (Finset (Fin n))) := do
  let [] :: reversedFields ← pure (word.splitOn none).reverse | none
  let header :: rows ← pure reversedFields.reverse | none
  let headerBits := header.filterMap id
  let n := Computability.decodeNat headerBits
  if headerBits.map some = header ∧ Computability.encodeNat n = headerBits then
    let subsets ← rows.mapM fun row ↦ do
      let bits := row.filterMap id
      if bits.map some = row ∧ bits.length = n then
        some ({i | bits.getD i.val false} : Finset (Fin n))
      else none
    let C := subsets.toFinset
    if (∅ : Finset (Fin n)) ∈ C ∧ Finset.univ ∈ C then some ⟨n, C⟩ else none
  else none

/-- **Open question** (Section 7, pp. 146–147). Deciding character admissibility is
NP-hard.

The open-question paragraph gives the expected NP-hard direction. The binary domain is a reading
of the binary defaults in Sections 5–6, inputs are explicitly listed families rather than
full-power-set tables, and the conclusion is many-one NP-hardness only. -/
theorem character_admissibility_np_hard :
    let targetLanguage : Set (List (Option Bool)) := {word |
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (C : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
        readCharacter word = some ⟨n, C⟩ ∧ Admissible C}
    let pairCode := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList (Option Bool))
      (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    let np : Set (List (Option Bool)) → Prop := fun language ↦
      ∃ verifier : (List (Option Bool) × List Bool) → Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime pairCode
          Computability.encodeBool verifier,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ input : List (Option Bool),
          input ∈ language ↔ ∃ certificate : List Bool,
            certificate.length ≤ bound.eval input.length ∧
            verifier (input, certificate) = true
    ∀ language : Set (List (Option Bool)), np language →
      ∃ reduction : List (Option Bool) → List (Option Bool),
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id reduction,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∀ word, word ∈ language ↔ reduction word ∈ targetLanguage := by
  sorry

end Hodge2009Preseparable

theorem Hodge2009Preseparable.character_admissibility_np_hard_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hodge2009Preseparable.character_admissibility_np_hard := by
  sorry

title: On promotion and quasi-tangled labelings of posets
problem_statement: In hodges2024promotion.lean, prove either Hodges2024Promotion.conjecture_23 or refute it by proving its logical negation Hodges2024Promotion.conjecture_23_neg.

/-!
# On promotion and quasi-tangled labelings of posets

Author: Eliot Hodges.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2022](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: E. Hodges, *On promotion and quasi-tangled labelings of posets*, Ann. Comb. **28**
(2024), 529–554; doi:10.1007/s00026-023-00646-2.
-/

namespace Hodges2024Promotion

open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- Extended promotion, via the equivalent increasing-order Bender–Knuth toggles of
Defant–Kravitz, Proposition 2.2 (Section 2.1). Labels are zero-based. -/
noncomputable def promotion {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] {n : ℕ}
    (L : P ≃ Fin n) : P ≃ Fin n :=
  (List.finRange (n - 1)).foldl (fun M i ↦
    let a : Fin n := ⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.isLt (Nat.sub_le n 1)⟩
    let b : Fin n := ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩
    if M.symm a < M.symm b then M else M.trans (Equiv.swap a b)) L

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 23** (journal; arXiv v1 Conjecture 7.5, Section 7). At most `3(n - 1)!`
labelings remain unsorted after `n - 3` promotions.

The source assumes `n ≥ 3` from Section 3.1 onward. -/
theorem conjecture_23 {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] [Fintype P]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hcard : Fintype.card P = n) :
    #{L : P ≃ Fin n | ¬StrictMono (⇑((promotion^[n - 3]) L))} ≤
      3 * (n - 1).factorial := by
  sorry

end Hodges2024Promotion

theorem Hodges2024Promotion.conjecture_23_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Hodges2024Promotion.conjecture_23.{u0} := by
  sorry

/-!
# Order of Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions

Authors: Daniel Hu, Ikuya Kaneko, Spencer Martin, and Carl Schildkraut.
Origin: [University of Virginia REU 2021](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2021).
Reference: D. Hu, I. Kaneko, S. Martin, and C. Schildkraut, *Order of zeros of Dedekind zeta
functions*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. **150** (2022), 5111–5120; doi:10.1090/proc/16041;
arXiv:2107.03269v2.

namespace Hu2022Order

/-- **Conjecture 6.2** (p. 8). For every irreducible complex representation of a relative Galois
group, the upper field's Dedekind zeta function has infinitely many distinct nontrivial zeros of
multiplicity at least the representation's degree.

The zeta function is specified by holomorphy off `1` and its convergent ideal series, which
identifies it with the continuation; its value at `1` is irrelevant. No Artin, GRH, monomiality
or absolute-Galois hypothesis is imposed. -/
theorem conjecture_6_2
    (K L : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L]
    [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
    {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (ρ : Representation ℂ (L ≃ₐ[K] L) V) (hρ : ρ.IsIrreducible)
    (ζ : ℂ → ℂ) (hζ : DifferentiableOn ℂ ζ {s : ℂ | s ≠ 1})
    (hseries : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re → ζ s = NumberField.dedekindZeta L s) :
    Set.Infinite {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1 ∧ ζ s = 0 ∧
      (Module.finrank ℂ V : ℕ∞) ≤ analyticOrderAt ζ s} := by

end Hu2022Order

title: On a Mertens-type conjecture for number fields
problem_statement: In hu2024mertens.lean, prove either Hu2024Mertens.conjecture_6_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Hu2024Mertens.conjecture_6_1_neg.

import Mathlib

/-!
# On a Mertens-type conjecture for number fields

Authors: Daniel Hu, Ikuya Kaneko, Spencer Martin, and Carl Schildkraut.
Origin: [University of Virginia REU 2021](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2021).
Reference: D. Hu, I. Kaneko, S. Martin, and C. Schildkraut, *On a Mertens-type conjecture for
number fields*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. **177** (2024), 481–523;
doi:10.1017/S0305004124000306.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Hu2024Mertens

open scoped NumberField

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Mertens function of `K`, with half weight at norm exactly `x` (Section 1, p. 482). -/
def mertens (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ I ∈ (Ideal.finite_setOfPred_absNorm_le (S := 𝓞 K) ⌊x⌋₊).toFinset.erase ⊥,
    if (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) = x then (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.moebius I : ℝ) / 2
    else (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.moebius I : ℝ)

/-- **Conjecture 6.1** (p. 517). Infinitely many number fields, up to isomorphism, have only
finitely many Mertens sign changes.

Since the half-weighted function is constant between consecutive integers, finitely many sign
changes means eventual nonnegativity or nonpositivity, allowing zeros. No dicyclic or analytic
hypothesis is imposed. -/
theorem conjecture_6_1 :
    ∃ (K : ℕ → Type) (fields : ∀ n, Field (K n)),
      letI := fields
      ∃ (numberFields : ∀ n, NumberField (K n)),
        letI := numberFields
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → IsEmpty (K i ≃+* K j)) ∧
        ∀ n, ∃ X ≥ (1 : ℝ),
          ((∀ x ≥ X, 0 ≤ mertens (K n) x) ∨
           (∀ x ≥ X, mertens (K n) x ≤ 0)) := by
  sorry

end Hu2024Mertens

theorem Hu2024Mertens.conjecture_6_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hu2024Mertens.conjecture_6_1 := by
  sorry

title: Invariant metrics with nonnegative curvature on SO(4) and other Lie groups
problem_statement: In huizenga2007invariant.lean, prove either Huizenga2007Invariant.regular_infinitesimal_classification or refute it by proving its logical negation Huizenga2007Invariant.regular_infinitesimal_classification_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Invariant metrics with nonnegative curvature on SO(4) and other Lie groups

Authors: Jack Huizenga and Kristopher Tapp.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/published.html).
Reference: J. Huizenga and K. Tapp, *Invariant metrics with nonnegative curvature on SO(4) and
other Lie groups*, Michigan Math. J. **55** (2007), no. 3; doi:10.1307/mmj/1197056459;
arXiv:math/0702241.
-/

noncomputable section
namespace Huizenga2007Invariant

attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing

/-- A simple ideal `so(3)` of the orthogonal Lie algebra. -/
abbrev factor := LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.so (Fin 3) ℝ

/-- The Lie algebra `so(4) ≅ so(3) × so(3)` as a product of two commuting simple ideals. -/
abbrev ProductAlgebra := factor × factor

/-- The equal-factor reference metric, with the quaternion bracket normalization. -/
def referenceMetric : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ ProductAlgebra :=
  let tr := Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin 3) ℝ ℝ
  let inc := (LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.so (Fin 3) ℝ).incl.toLinearMap
  let m := ((LinearMap.mul ℝ (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ)).compl₁₂ inc inc).compr₂ tr
  let l := LinearMap.fst ℝ factor factor
  let r := LinearMap.snd ℝ factor factor
  (- (1 / 8 : ℝ)) • (m.compl₁₂ l l + m.compl₁₂ r r)

/-- Infinitesimal nonnegativity (Definition 3.2), including the vanishing obstruction of
Proposition 3.1. -/
def InfinitesimallyNonnegative (ψ : ProductAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] ProductAlgebra) : Prop :=
  ∀ X Y : ProductAlgebra, ⁅X, Y⁆ = 0 →
    let q := referenceMetric (⁅X, ψ Y⁆ + ⁅ψ X, Y⁆) ⁅ψ X, ψ Y⁆ +
      referenceMetric ⁅ψ X, X⁆ (ψ ⁅ψ Y, Y⁆) -
      referenceMetric ⁅X, ψ Y⁆ (ψ ⁅X, ψ Y⁆) -
      referenceMetric ⁅X, ψ Y⁆ (ψ ⁅ψ X, Y⁆) -
      referenceMetric ⁅ψ X, Y⁆ (ψ ⁅ψ X, Y⁆)
    0 ≤ q ∧ (q = 0 → ⁅ψ X, ψ Y⁆ - ψ (⁅ψ X, Y⁆ + ⁅X, ψ Y⁆) = 0)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 8, after Theorem 8.1). Every infinitesimally nonnegative
direction without singular eigenvectors comes from the full `S³`-action family (7.3), with a
nonnegatively curved factor metric. -/
theorem regular_infinitesimal_classification
    (ψ : ProductAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] ProductAlgebra)
    (hself : referenceMetric.IsSelfAdjoint ψ)
    (hnonneg : InfinitesimallyNonnegative ψ)
    (hregular : ∀ (r : ℝ) (V : ProductAlgebra), V ≠ 0 →
      ψ V = r • V → V.1 ≠ 0 ∧ V.2 ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (A : Module.Basis (Fin 3) ℝ factor) (e : factor ≃ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ factor)
      (α β : ℝ) (μ : Fin 3 → ℝ),
      let h := fun U V : factor ↦ referenceMetric (U, 0) (V, 0)
      let a := fun i : Fin 3 ↦ (A i, (0 : factor))
      let b := fun i : Fin 3 ↦ ((0 : factor), e (A i))
      let P := A.constr ℝ (fun i ↦ μ i • A i)
      let Pinv := A.constr ℝ (fun i ↦ (μ i)⁻¹ • A i)
      (∀ i j : Fin 3, referenceMetric (a i) (a j) = if i = j then 1 else 0) ∧
      (∀ i j : Fin 3, referenceMetric (b i) (b j) = if i = j then 1 else 0) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 3, 0 < μ i) ∧
      (∀ U V : factor,
        0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * h (⁅P U, V⁆ + ⁅U, P V⁆) ⁅U, V⁆ -
          (3 / 4 : ℝ) * h (P ⁅U, V⁆) ⁅U, V⁆ +
          (1 / 4 : ℝ) * h (⁅U, P V⁆ + ⁅V, P U⁆) (Pinv (⁅U, P V⁆ + ⁅V, P U⁆)) -
          h ⁅U, P U⁆ (Pinv ⁅V, P V⁆)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 3,
        ψ (a i) = (α - 1 / (2 * μ i)) • a i - (1 / (2 * μ i)) • b i ∧
        ψ (b i) = -(1 / (2 * μ i)) • a i + (β - 1 / (2 * μ i)) • b i) := by
  sorry

end Huizenga2007Invariant

theorem Huizenga2007Invariant.regular_infinitesimal_classification_neg : ¬ type_of% @Huizenga2007Invariant.regular_infinitesimal_classification := by
  sorry

title: Magnetic Laplacians of locally exact forms on the Sierpinski Gasket
problem_statement: In hyde2017magnetic.lean, prove either Hyde2017Magnetic.magnetic_energy_convergence or refute it by proving its logical negation Hyde2017Magnetic.magnetic_energy_convergence_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Magnetic Laplacians of locally exact forms on the Sierpinski Gasket

Authors: Jessica Hyde, Daniel Kelleher, Jesse Moeller, Luke G. Rogers, and Luis Seda.
Origin: [University of Connecticut REU
2013](https://mathreu.uconn.edu/2016/04/21/spectrum-of-the-magnetic-laplacian-on-the-sierpinski-gasket/).
Reference: J. Hyde, D. Kelleher, J. Moeller, L. G. Rogers, and L. Seda, *Magnetic Laplacians of
locally exact forms on the Sierpinski Gasket*, Commun. Pure Appl. Anal. **16** (2017), no. 6,
2299–2319; doi:10.3934/cpaa.2017113; arXiv:1604.01340v1.
-/

noncomputable section
open scoped Topology

namespace Hyde2017Magnetic

/-- The ordered vertices of the equilateral boundary triangle. -/
def boundary (i : Fin 3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if i = 0 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0]
  else if i = 1 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0]
  else WithLp.toLp 2 ![(1 : ℝ) / 2, √3 / 2]

/-- The contraction `F_i(x) = (x + p_i) / 2`. -/
def contraction (i : Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (x + boundary i)

/-- The cell map `F_w`, with the first word letter outermost. -/
def cellMap {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (List.ofFn w).foldr contraction x

/-- The finite vertex sets `V_m` of the graph approximations. -/
def vertices : ℕ → Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  | 0 => Finset.univ.image boundary
  | m + 1 => Finset.univ.biUnion fun i ↦ (vertices m).image (contraction i)

/-- The Sierpinski gasket, as the closure of its finite-level vertices. -/
def gasket : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  closure (⋃ m : ℕ, (vertices m : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))

/-- The weighted finite pairing of cell potentials, with each edge counted once. -/
def formPairing (m : ℕ) (a b : (Fin m → Fin 3) → Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m *
    ∑ w : Fin m → Fin 3, ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      if i < j then (a w j - a w i) * (b w j - b w i) else 0

/-- Harmonic refinement of mean-zero cell potentials, recentered in each child. -/
def refine (m : ℕ) (q : (Fin m → Fin 3) → Fin 3 → ℝ)
    (v : Fin (m + 1) → Fin 3) (j : Fin 3) : ℝ :=
  let w : Fin m → Fin 3 := fun k ↦ v k.castSucc
  let i := v (Fin.last m)
  if j = i then 3 * q w i / 5 else (q w j - q w i) / 5

/-- The renormalized nonmagnetic graph energy ((A2)). -/
def graphEnergy (m : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m *
    ∑ w : Fin m → Fin 3, ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      if i < j then ‖f (cellMap w (boundary j)) - f (cellMap w (boundary i))‖ ^ 2
      else 0

/-- The unrenormalized magnetic graph energy (3.1), with `a(e_xy) = a(y) - a(x)`. -/
def magneticGraphEnergy (m : ℕ) (a : (Fin m → Fin 3) → Fin 3 → ℝ)
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : Fin m → Fin 3, ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
    if i < j then
      ‖f (cellMap w (boundary i)) - f (cellMap w (boundary j)) *
        Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((a w j - a w i : ℝ) : ℂ))‖ ^ 2
    else 0

/-- **Remark 3.9**. The renormalized magnetic graph energies converge to the continuum magnetic
quadratic form for every real one-form and every complex finite-energy function.

Mean-zero compatible bounded-energy sequences represent all one-forms by Theorem 2.2, with
compatibility read as weighted adjoint compatibility (canonical cellwise projection); each cell
edge is counted once with the factor `(5 / 3) ^ m`, and the right side is the squared norm of
`∂f + i f a`; no local Coulomb gauge, convergence premise or local-exactness restriction is added.
Ambient values off the gasket are irrelevant. -/
theorem magnetic_energy_convergence
    (a : (m : ℕ) → (Fin m → Fin 3) → Fin 3 → ℝ)
    (ha_mean : ∀ (m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → Fin 3), ∑ i : Fin 3, a m w i = 0)
    (ha_bound : BddAbove (Set.range fun m : ℕ ↦ formPairing m (a m) (a m)))
    (ha_compat : ∀ (m : ℕ) (q : (Fin m → Fin 3) → Fin 3 → ℝ),
      (∀ w : Fin m → Fin 3, ∑ i : Fin 3, q w i = 0) →
      formPairing m (a m) q = formPairing (m + 1) (a (m + 1)) (refine m q))
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℂ)
    (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f gasket)
    (hf_bound : BddAbove (Set.range fun m : ℕ ↦ graphEnergy m f)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m * magneticGraphEnergy m (a m) f)
      Filter.atTop
      (𝓝 (Filter.limUnder Filter.atTop (fun m : ℕ ↦
        (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m *
          ∑ w : Fin m → Fin 3, ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
            if i < j then
              ‖(f (cellMap w (boundary j)) - f (cellMap w (boundary i))) +
                Complex.I * f (cellMap w (boundary 0)) *
                  ((a m w j - a m w i : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ^ 2
            else 0))) := by
  sorry

end Hyde2017Magnetic

theorem Hyde2017Magnetic.magnetic_energy_convergence_neg : ¬ type_of% @Hyde2017Magnetic.magnetic_energy_convergence := by
  sorry

title: Distribution of Eigenvalues of Highly Palindromic Toeplitz Matrices
problem_statement: In jackson2012distribution.lean, prove either Jackson2012Distribution.configurations_conjecture or refute it by proving its logical negation Jackson2012Distribution.configurations_conjecture_neg.

/-!
# Distribution of Eigenvalues of Highly Palindromic Toeplitz Matrices

Authors: Steven Jackson, Steven J. Miller, and Thuy Pham.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2009](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2010v2).
Reference: S. Jackson, S. J. Miller, and T. Pham, *Distribution of Eigenvalues of Highly
Palindromic Toeplitz Matrices*, J. Theoret. Probab. **25** (2012), 464–495; arXiv:1003.2010v2.
-/

noncomputable section
namespace Jackson2012Distribution

open scoped Topology

/-- The independent-entry label in a symmetric Toeplitz matrix whose first row repeats an even
palindrome of the given half-length. -/
def palindromicLink (halfLength i j : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let r := Nat.dist i j % (2 * halfLength)
  min r (2 * halfLength - 1 - r)

/-- **Conjecture 5.9**. Every pairing configuration has the same limiting normalized contribution
to an even spectral moment.

The model uses the repeated even palindrome required by Definition 1.1 and Section 4.1 rather than
the inconsistent printed link formula, and pairing counts stand for expected contributions
(Corollary 2.2, Lemma 3.2); no Gaussian-only input law is imposed. -/
theorem configurations_conjecture (n m : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m) :
    let next : Fin (2 * m) → Fin (2 * m) := fun k ↦
      ⟨(k.val + 1) % (2 * m), Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)⟩
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * m)),
      Function.Involutive p → (∀ k, p k ≠ k) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun h : ℕ ↦
        (Nat.card { t : Fin (2 * m) → Fin (2 ^ n * (2 * (h + 1))) //
          ∀ k, palindromicLink (h + 1) (t k).val (t (next k)).val =
            palindromicLink (h + 1) (t (p k)).val (t (next (p k))).val } : ℝ) /
          ((2 ^ n * (2 * (h + 1)) : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 c) := by sorry

end Jackson2012Distribution

theorem Jackson2012Distribution.configurations_conjecture_neg : ¬ type_of% @Jackson2012Distribution.configurations_conjecture := by
  sorry

title: Biases among Congruence Classes for Parts in k-regular Partitions
problem_statement: In jackson2022biases.lean, prove either Jackson2022Biases.conjecture_1_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jackson2022Biases.conjecture_1_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Biases among Congruence Classes for Parts in k-regular Partitions

Authors: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar.
Origin: [University of Virginia REU
2022](https://math.uchicago.edu/~alephnil/papers/#biases-k-regular-partitions).
Reference: F. Jackson and M. Otgonbayar, *Biases among congruence classes for parts in k-regular
partitions*, arXiv:2207.04352 (2022), 25 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Jackson2022Biases

/-- The count `D_k(r,t;n)` of all occurrences of parts congruent to `r` modulo `t` among
partitions of `n` with every multiplicity below `k` (Section 1, p. 2). -/
def residuePartCount (k r t n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ lam ∈ Nat.Partition.countRestricted n k,
    (lam.parts.filter (fun m ↦ m % t = r % t)).card

/-- **Conjecture 1.4**. For `t ≥ 6`, lower residue classes have weak bias for every `k ≥ 3` and
`n ≥ 1`, and strict bias for every `k ≥ 2` and `n > max(t + 3, 16)`.

Here `k`-regular means every multiplicity is below `k`, not indivisibility by `k`; neither clause
assumes coprimality. -/
theorem conjecture_1_4 (t r s : ℕ) (ht : 6 ≤ t) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hrs : r < s) (hs : s ≤ t) :
    (∀ (k n : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → 1 ≤ n →
      residuePartCount k s t n ≤ residuePartCount k r t n) ∧
    (∀ (k n : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → max (t + 3) 16 < n →
      residuePartCount k s t n < residuePartCount k r t n) := by
  sorry

end Jackson2022Biases

  sorry

title: Unexpected biases between congruence classes for parts in k-indivisible partitions
problem_statement: In jackson2023unexpected.lean, prove either Jackson2023Unexpected.conjecture_1_5 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jackson2023Unexpected.conjecture_1_5_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Unexpected biases between congruence classes for parts in k-indivisible partitions

Authors: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar.
Origin: [University of Virginia REU 2022](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2022).
Reference: F. Jackson and M. Otgonbayar, *Unexpected biases between congruence classes for parts
in k-indivisible partitions*, J. Number Theory **248** (2023), 310–342.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Jackson2023Unexpected

/-- The total number of occurrences of parts congruent to `r` modulo `t` among partitions of `n`
with no part divisible by `k` (Equation (1.4)). -/
def residuePartCount (k r t n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ lam ∈ Nat.Partition.restricted n (fun m ↦ m % k ≠ 0),
    (lam.parts.filter (fun m ↦ m % t = r % t)).card

/-- The `k`-indivisible strict bias ordering (Section 1). Index `i` represents the residue
representative `i + 1` in `{1, …, t}`. -/
def BiasOrder (k t : ℕ) (r s : Fin t) : Prop :=
  ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    residuePartCount k (r.val + 1) t n < residuePartCount k (s.val + 1) t n

/-- The number `O(t)` of distinct bias orderings as `k ≥ 2` ranges over integers coprime to `t`
(Section 1). -/
def orderingCount (t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card { R : Fin t → Fin t → Prop //
    ∃ k ≥ 2, Nat.Coprime k t ∧ R = BiasOrder k t }

/-- **Conjecture 1.5**. The ratio `O(t) / φ(t)` grows sublinearly and superlogarithmically as `t`
tends to infinity.

Both bounds are retained; the separate no-ties conjecture is not included. -/
theorem conjecture_1_5 :
    let q : ℕ → ℝ := fun t ↦ (orderingCount t : ℝ) / (Nat.totient t : ℝ)
    Asymptotics.IsLittleO Filter.atTop q (fun t : ℕ ↦ (t : ℝ)) ∧
      Asymptotics.IsLittleO Filter.atTop (fun t : ℕ ↦ Real.log (t : ℝ)) q := by
  sorry

end Jackson2023Unexpected

theorem Jackson2023Unexpected.conjecture_1_5_neg : ¬ type_of% @Jackson2023Unexpected.conjecture_1_5 := by
  sorry

/-!
# Extremal Primes for Elliptic Curves

Authors: Kevin James, Brandon Tran, Minh-Tam Trinh, Phil Wertheimer, and Dania Zantout.
Origin: [Clemson University REU
2012](https://www.math.clemson.edu/~kevja/PAPERS/ExtremalPrimes-FinalVersion.pdf).
Reference: K. James, B. Tran, M.-T. Trinh, P. Wertheimer, and D. Zantout, *Extremal primes for
elliptic curves*, J. Number Theory **164** (2016), 282-298.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace James2016Extremal

open scoped Topology
open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number of good-reduction primes below `X` whose Frobenius trace attains either integer
endpoint of the Hasse interval, `π_E⁺(X) + π_E⁻(X)` (Section 3). -/
def extremalPrimeCount (W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (X : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  #{p ∈ Finset.range (Nat.ceil X) |
    if hp : p.Prime then
      letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
      let Wp := (W.map (algebraMap ℚ (Padic p))).minimal (PadicInt p)
      let R := (Wp.reduction (PadicInt p)).map
        (PadicInt.residueField (p := p)).toRingHom
      Wp.HasGoodReduction (PadicInt p) ∧
        |(p : ℤ) + 1 - (Nat.card R.toAffine.Point : ℤ)| =
          Int.floor (2 * √(p : ℝ))
    else False}

/-- **Conjecture 3.3** (author manuscript p. 4). Every non-CM rational elliptic curve has
asymptotically `C_E X ^ (1 / 4) / log X` extremal primes, for some `C_E > 0`.

Non-CM is expressed through the complete list of rational CM `j`-invariants. -/
theorem conjecture_3_3 (W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [W.IsElliptic]
    (h_nonCM : W.j ∉ ({-262537412640768000, -147197952000, -884736000,
      -12288000, -884736, -32768, -3375, 0, 1728, 8000, 54000,
      287496, 16581375} : Finset ℚ)) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun X : ℝ ↦ (extremalPrimeCount W X : ℝ) /
          (C * X ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) / Real.log X))
        Filter.atTop (𝓝 1) := by sorry

end James2016Extremal

theorem James2016Extremal.conjecture_3_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @James2016Extremal.conjecture_3_3 := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture 5.1** (p. 266). Every positive real moment of a normalized continuous solution
of the two-scale recursion has a finite logarithmic integral-growth exponent.

The printed `x → 0` is read as `x → ∞`, as (1.9), (5.1) and (5.3)-(5.4) indicate; each
coefficient has its own positive period, with no common-period restriction. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1
    (ρ₁ ρ₂ : ℝ) (hρ₁ : 1 < ρ₁) (hρ₂ : 1 < ρ₂)

title: Embedding dimension gaps in sparse codes
problem_statement: In jeffs2026embedding.lean, prove either Jeffs2026Embedding.conjecture_16 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jeffs2026Embedding.conjecture_16_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Embedding dimension gaps in sparse codes

Authors: R. Amzi Jeffs, Henry Siegel, David Staudinger, and Yiqing Wang.
Origin: [Carnegie Mellon University SEMS
2023](https://www.cmu.edu/mcs/news-events/2023/1018-sems-program).
Reference: R. A. Jeffs, H. Siegel, D. Staudinger, and Y. Wang, *Embedding dimension gaps in
sparse codes*, Involve **19** (2026), 405-422; arXiv:2309.14862.
-/

namespace Jeffs2026Embedding

open Finset

/-- A Steiner triple system: triples such that each pair of distinct indices lies in exactly
one triple (Section 7). -/
structure SteinerTripleSystem (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The triples of the system. -/
  blocks : Finset (Finset (Fin n))
  triple_card : ∀ b ∈ blocks, #b = 3
  pair_unique : ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → ∃! b, b ∈ blocks ∧ i ∈ b ∧ j ∈ b

/-- The least dimension of a realization by bounded open convex sets, or `⊤` if none exists
(Section 1). -/
noncomputable def openEmbeddingDimension {n : ℕ} (C : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {m | ∃ d : ℕ, m = (d : ℕ∞) ∧
    ∃ U : Fin n → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      (∀ i, IsOpen (U i) ∧ Convex ℝ (U i) ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (U i)) ∧
      ∀ σ : Finset (Fin n), σ ∈ C ↔
        ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ∀ i, x ∈ U i ↔ i ∈ σ}

/-- **Conjecture 16** (arXiv v1, p. 14). Steiner triple codes have arbitrarily large open convex
embedding dimension. -/
theorem conjecture_16 (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    ∃ n > 0, ∃ S : SteinerTripleSystem n,
      (d : ℕ∞) ≤ openEmbeddingDimension
        (S.blocks ∪ Finset.univ.image (fun i : Fin n ↦ {i}) ∪ {∅}) := by
  sorry

end Jeffs2026Embedding

theorem Jeffs2026Embedding.conjecture_16_neg : ¬ type_of% @Jeffs2026Embedding.conjecture_16 := by
  sorry

title: Sobolev Orthogonal Polynomials on the Sierpinski Gasket
problem_statement: In jiang2021sobolev.lean, prove either Jiang2021Sobolev.normal_derivative_nonvanishing or refute it by proving its logical negation Jiang2021Sobolev.normal_derivative_nonvanishing_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Sobolev Orthogonal Polynomials on the Sierpinski Gasket

Authors: Qingxuan Jiang, Tian Lan, Kasso A. Okoudjou, Robert S. Strichartz,
Shashank Sule, Sreeram Venkat, and Xiaoduo Wang.
Origin: [Cornell SPUR
2019](https://math.cornell.edu/history-reu-and-spur-programs-department-mathematics).
Reference: Q. Jiang, T. Lan, K. A. Okoudjou, R. S. Strichartz, S. Sule, S. Venkat, and X. Wang,
*Sobolev orthogonal polynomials on the Sierpinski gasket*, J. Fourier Anal. Appl. **27** (2021),
article 38; arXiv:2010.00107v2.
-/

noncomputable section
namespace Jiang2021Sobolev

/-- The boundary values `alpha_j = P_(j,1)(q1)` (Lemma 2.1). -/
def alpha : ℕ → ℚ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => 1 / 6
  | n + 2 =>
      4 / ((5 : ℚ) ^ (n + 2) - 5) *
        ∑ l : Fin (n + 1), alpha (n + 2 - (l.val + 1)) * alpha (l.val + 1)
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by all_goals omega

/-- The boundary values `beta_j = P_(j,2)(q1)` (Lemma 2.1). -/
def beta : ℕ → ℚ
  | 0 => -1 / 2
  | n + 1 =>
      2 / (15 * ((5 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) - 1)) *
        ∑ l : Fin (n + 1),
          (3 * (5 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1 - l.val) - 5 ^ (l.val + 1) + 6) *
            alpha (n + 1 - l.val) * beta l.val
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by all_goals omega

/-- The boundary normal derivatives `eta_j = ∂_n P_(j,1)(q1)` (Lemma 2.1).
The source's summand `n_l` denotes this same sequence. -/
def eta : ℕ → ℚ
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 =>
      (((5 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) + 1) / 2) * alpha (n + 1) +
        2 * ∑ l : Fin (n + 1), eta l.val * beta (n + 1 - l.val)
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by all_goals omega

/-- The exact family-1 monomial Gram matrix of Section 3.6 (Okoudjou--Strichartz--Tuley,
Lemma 2.1 (16)). -/
def gramEntry (i j : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  2 * ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (min i j + 1),
    (alpha s * eta (i + j + 1 - s) - alpha (i + j + 1 - s) * eta s)

/-- The source `L2` pairing in finitely supported rational monomial coordinates. -/
def gramPairing (a b : ℕ →₀ ℚ) : ℚ :=
  a.sum (fun i x ↦ b.sum (fun j y ↦ x * y * gramEntry i j))

/-- The canonical monic family-1 Legendre coefficients in exact rational coordinates, by the
ordered Gram--Schmidt formula (Remark 3.1). -/
def monicCoefficients (t : ℕ) : ℕ →₀ ℚ :=
  let e := Finsupp.single t (1 : ℚ)
  e - ∑ r : Fin t,
    (gramPairing e (monicCoefficients r.val) /
        gramPairing (monicCoefficients r.val) (monicCoefficients r.val)) •
      monicCoefficients r.val
termination_by t
decreasing_by all_goals omega

/-- **Conjecture 3.1** (arXiv v2, p. 23). The Dirichlet Green image of each canonical monic
family-1 Legendre polynomial has nonzero normal derivative at `q0`.

By Lemma 3.2 and the boundary jets this is stated as the nonvanishing of an exact rational
coefficient sum, omitting the fixed nonzero factor 2. -/
theorem normal_derivative_nonvanishing (t : ℕ) :
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (t + 1), monicCoefficients t j * alpha (j + 1) ≠ 0 := by
  sorry

end Jiang2021Sobolev

theorem Jiang2021Sobolev.normal_derivative_nonvanishing_neg : ¬ type_of% @Jiang2021Sobolev.normal_derivative_nonvanishing := by
  sorry

title: On the Sprague-Grundy Values of the F-Wythoff Game
problem_statement: In jiao2013sprague.lean, prove either Jiao2013Sprague.conjecture_18 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jiao2013Sprague.conjecture_18_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the Sprague-Grundy Values of the F-Wythoff Game

Author: Yang Jiao.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2012](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: Y. Jiao, *On the Sprague-Grundy values of the F-Wythoff game*, Electron. J. Combin.
**20** (2013), no. 1, Paper 14, 12 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Jiao2013Sprague

open scoped Topology

/-- The Sprague-Grundy value: the least natural number absent from all legal followers
(Section 1). Diagonal moves preserve the integer ratio and leave both piles positive. -/
def grundy (a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {g : ℕ |
    (∀ c : Fin a, grundy c.val b ≠ g) ∧
    (∀ d : Fin b, grundy a d.val ≠ g) ∧
    (∀ t : Fin (min a b), 0 < t.val →
      (max a b - t.val) / (min a b - t.val) = max a b / min a b →
        grundy (a - t.val) (b - t.val) ≠ g)}
termination_by a + b
decreasing_by
  all_goals omega

/-- The smaller coordinate of the `n`th `g`-position, ordered increasingly (Section 3). -/
def lowerPosition (g n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.nth (fun a ↦ ∃ b ≥ a, grundy a b = g) n

/-- The larger coordinate paired with the `n`th smaller coordinate (Section 3). -/
def upperPosition (g n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {b : ℕ | lowerPosition g n ≤ b ∧ grundy (lowerPosition g n) b = g}

/-- **Conjecture 18**. For every Sprague-Grundy value, the ratio of the larger to the smaller
coordinate of its ordered positions converges to the golden ratio. -/
theorem conjecture_18 (g : ℕ) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (upperPosition g n : ℝ) / (lowerPosition g n : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 ((1 + √5) / 2)) := by
  sorry

end Jiao2013Sprague

theorem Jiao2013Sprague.conjecture_18_neg : ¬ type_of% @Jiao2013Sprague.conjecture_18 := by
  sorry

title: Iterated Differential Polynomial Rings over Locally Nilpotent Rings
problem_statement: In jin2021iterated.lean, prove either Jin2021Iterated.question_5 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jin2021Iterated.question_5_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Iterated Differential Polynomial Rings over Locally Nilpotent Rings

Authors: Steven Jin and Jooyoung Shin.
Origin: [Kent State University REU
2020](https://www.kent.edu/math/research-experiences-undergraduates).
Reference: S. Jin and J. Shin, *Iterated Differential Polynomial Rings over Locally
Nilpotent Rings*, Comm. Algebra **49** (2021), 256-262; arXiv:2007.07446v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Jin2021Iterated

universe u

/-- A derivation of a possibly nonunital associative ring: an additive map satisfying the Leibniz
rule (p. 1). -/
structure RingDerivation (A : Type u) [NonUnitalRing A] extends A →+ A where
  /-- The Leibniz rule. -/
  leibniz' (a b : A) : toAddMonoidHom (a * b) =
    toAddMonoidHom a * b + a * toAddMonoidHom b

instance {A : Type u} [NonUnitalRing A] : CoeFun (RingDerivation A) (fun _ ↦ A → A) :=
  ⟨fun d ↦ d.toAddMonoidHom⟩

variable {A : Type u} [NonUnitalRing A]

/-- The extension of a derivation to the integer unitization, vanishing on the integers. -/
def RingDerivation.unitized (d : RingDerivation A) :
    Unitization ℤ A →+ Unitization ℤ A where
  toFun x := Unitization.inr (d x.snd)
  map_zero' := by simp [map_zero]
  map_add' x y := by
    change Unitization.inr (d.toAddMonoidHom (x.snd + y.snd)) = _
    simp only [map_add, Unitization.inr_add]

/-- The extension of a derivation to the unitization satisfies the Leibniz rule. -/
lemma RingDerivation.unitized_leibniz (d : RingDerivation A)
    (x y : Unitization ℤ A) :
    d.unitized (x * y) = d.unitized x * y + x * d.unitized y := by
  apply Unitization.ext
  · change (0 : ℤ) = 0 * y.fst + x.fst * 0
    simp
  · change d.toAddMonoidHom (x.fst • y.snd + y.fst • x.snd + x.snd * y.snd) =
      ((0 : ℤ) • y.snd + y.fst • d.toAddMonoidHom x.snd +
        d.toAddMonoidHom x.snd * y.snd) +
      (x.fst • d.toAddMonoidHom y.snd + (0 : ℤ) • x.snd +
        x.snd * d.toAddMonoidHom y.snd)
    simp only [map_add, map_zsmul, d.leibniz', zero_smul, zero_add, add_zero]
    abel

/-- Left multiplication by a coefficient on finite polynomials over the unitization. -/
def coefficient : A →+ AddMonoid.End (ℕ →₀ Unitization ℤ A) where
  toFun a := Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom
    (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft (a : Unitization ℤ A))
  map_zero' := by
    apply AddMonoidHom.ext
    intro p
    apply Finsupp.ext
    intro n
    change (↑(0 : A) : Unitization ℤ A) * p n = 0
    simp
  map_add' a b := by
    apply AddMonoidHom.ext
    intro p
    apply Finsupp.ext
    intro n
    change (↑(a + b) : Unitization ℤ A) * p n =
      (a : Unitization ℤ A) * p n + (b : Unitization ℤ A) * p n
    rw [Unitization.inr_add, add_mul]

/-- The action of the formal variable: index shift plus coefficientwise derivation.

This auxiliary operator need not belong to the nonunital extension. -/
def variableOperator (d : RingDerivation A) :
    AddMonoid.End (ℕ →₀ Unitization ℤ A) :=
  Finsupp.embDomain.addMonoidHom ⟨Nat.succ, Nat.succ_injective⟩ +
    Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom d.unitized

/-- The commutation law `x * a = a * x + d a` of the formal variable with a coefficient. -/
lemma variableOperator_coefficient (d : RingDerivation A) (a : A) :
    variableOperator d * coefficient a =
      coefficient a * variableOperator d + coefficient (d a) := by
  have hc (a : A) (n : ℕ) (b : Unitization ℤ A) :
      coefficient a (Finsupp.single n b) =
        Finsupp.single n ((a : Unitization ℤ A) * b) := by
    change Finsupp.mapRange (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft (a : Unitization ℤ A))
      (map_zero _) (Finsupp.single n b) = _
    exact Finsupp.mapRange_single
  have hx (n : ℕ) (a : Unitization ℤ A) :
      variableOperator d (Finsupp.single n a) =
        Finsupp.single (n + 1) a + Finsupp.single n (d.unitized a) := by
    change Finsupp.embDomain ⟨Nat.succ, Nat.succ_injective⟩ (Finsupp.single n a) +
      Finsupp.mapRange d.unitized d.unitized.map_zero (Finsupp.single n a) = _
    simp
  apply AddMonoidHom.ext
  intro p
  change variableOperator d (coefficient a p) =
    coefficient a (variableOperator d p) + coefficient (d a) p
  induction p using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero => simp
  | @single_add n b p hn hb ih =>
    have hu : d.unitized (a : Unitization ℤ A) = (d a : Unitization ℤ A) := rfl
    have hs : variableOperator d (coefficient a (Finsupp.single n b)) =
        coefficient a (variableOperator d (Finsupp.single n b)) +
          coefficient (d a) (Finsupp.single n b) := by
      simp only [hc, hx, map_add,
        d.unitized_leibniz, hu, Finsupp.single_add]
      abel
    simp only [map_add]
    rw [ih, hs]
    abel

/-- The operator of a finite polynomial with left coefficients. -/
def normalForm (d : RingDerivation A) :
    (ℕ →₀ A) →+ AddMonoid.End (ℕ →₀ Unitization ℤ A) :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun n ↦
    (AddMonoidHom.mulRight (variableOperator d ^ n)).comp coefficient)

/-- The action of the formal variable on coefficient polynomials, without adjoining an identity. -/
def shiftDerivative (d : RingDerivation A) : AddMonoid.End (ℕ →₀ A) :=
  Finsupp.embDomain.addMonoidHom ⟨Nat.succ, Nat.succ_injective⟩ +
    Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom d.toAddMonoidHom

/-- `normalForm` turns `shiftDerivative` into left multiplication by `variableOperator`. -/
lemma normalForm_shiftDerivative (d : RingDerivation A) (p : ℕ →₀ A) :
    normalForm d (shiftDerivative d p) = variableOperator d * normalForm d p := by
  have hm (n : ℕ) (a : A) : normalForm d (Finsupp.single n a) =
      coefficient a * variableOperator d ^ n := by
    simp [normalForm]
  have hd (n : ℕ) (a : A) : shiftDerivative d (Finsupp.single n a) =
      Finsupp.single (n + 1) a + Finsupp.single n (d a) := by
    change Finsupp.embDomain ⟨Nat.succ, Nat.succ_injective⟩ (Finsupp.single n a) +
      Finsupp.mapRange d.toAddMonoidHom d.toAddMonoidHom.map_zero
        (Finsupp.single n a) = _
    simp
  induction p using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero => simp
  | @single_add n a p hn ha ih =>
    have hs : normalForm d (shiftDerivative d (Finsupp.single n a)) =
        variableOperator d * normalForm d (Finsupp.single n a) := by
      rw [hd, map_add, hm, hm, hm]
      rw [← mul_assoc, variableOperator_coefficient, Distrib.right_distrib, mul_assoc,
        ← pow_succ']
    rw [map_add, map_add, hs, ih, map_add, Distrib.left_distrib]

/-- `coefficient` is multiplicative. -/
lemma coefficient_mul (a b : A) : coefficient (a * b) = coefficient a * coefficient b := by
  apply AddMonoidHom.ext
  intro p
  apply Finsupp.ext
  intro n
  change ((a * b : A) : Unitization ℤ A) * p n =
    (a : Unitization ℤ A) * ((b : Unitization ℤ A) * p n)
  rw [Unitization.inr_mul]
  exact mul_assoc (a : Unitization ℤ A) (b : Unitization ℤ A) (p n)

/-- `normalForm` turns left coefficient multiplication into left multiplication by `coefficient`.
-/
lemma normalForm_left_coefficient (d : RingDerivation A) (a : A) (p : ℕ →₀ A) :
    normalForm d (Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft a) p) =
      coefficient a * normalForm d p := by
  have hm (n : ℕ) (b : A) : normalForm d (Finsupp.single n b) =
      coefficient b * variableOperator d ^ n := by
    simp [normalForm]
  induction p using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero => simp
  | @single_add n b p hn hb ih =>
    have hs : normalForm d
        (Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft a) (Finsupp.single n b)) =
        coefficient a * normalForm d (Finsupp.single n b) := by
      change normalForm d (Finsupp.mapRange (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft a)
        (map_zero _) (Finsupp.single n b)) = _
      rw [Finsupp.mapRange_single, hm, hm]
      exact (congrArg (fun c ↦ c * variableOperator d ^ n) (coefficient_mul a b)).trans
        (mul_assoc _ _ _)
    rw [map_add, map_add, hs, ih, map_add, Distrib.left_distrib]

/-- The product of finite coefficient polynomials, by repeated commutation. -/
def oreMul (d : RingDerivation A) (p q : ℕ →₀ A) : ℕ →₀ A :=
  p.sum fun n a ↦ Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft a)
    ((shiftDerivative d ^ n) q)

/-- `normalForm` is multiplicative for `oreMul`. -/
lemma normalForm_oreMul (d : RingDerivation A) (p q : ℕ →₀ A) :
    normalForm d (oreMul d p q) = normalForm d p * normalForm d q := by
  have hi (n : ℕ) : normalForm d ((shiftDerivative d ^ n) q) =
      variableOperator d ^ n * normalForm d q := by
    induction n with
    | zero => simp
    | succ n ih =>
      rw [pow_succ']
      change normalForm d (shiftDerivative d ((shiftDerivative d ^ n) q)) = _
      rw [normalForm_shiftDerivative, ih, ← mul_assoc, ← pow_succ']
  simp only [oreMul, Finsupp.sum, map_sum, normalForm_left_coefficient, hi]
  change (∑ n ∈ p.support, coefficient (p n) *
      (variableOperator d ^ n * normalForm d q)) = _
  rw [show normalForm d p =
    ∑ n ∈ p.support, coefficient (p n) * variableOperator d ^ n from rfl]
  calc
    _ = ∑ n ∈ p.support, (coefficient (p n) * variableOperator d ^ n) *
        normalForm d q := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro n hn
      exact (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
    _ = _ := (Finset.sum_mul p.support
      (fun n ↦ coefficient (p n) * variableOperator d ^ n) (normalForm d q)).symm

/-- The differential polynomial ring `A[X; d]`, realized as the image of `normalForm` (p. 1).

Multiplication is composition of the faithful operators. -/
def differentialExtension (d : RingDerivation A) :
    NonUnitalSubring (AddMonoid.End (ℕ →₀ Unitization ℤ A)) where
  carrier := Set.range (normalForm d)
  zero_mem' := ⟨0, map_zero _⟩
  add_mem' := by
    rintro _ _ ⟨p, rfl⟩ ⟨q, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨p + q, map_add _ _ _⟩
  neg_mem' := by
    rintro _ ⟨p, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨-p, map_neg _ _⟩
  mul_mem' := by
    rintro _ _ ⟨p, rfl⟩ ⟨q, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨oreMul d p q, normalForm_oreMul d p q⟩

/-- An iterated differential polynomial ring of length `n` over `A` (Definition 3).

Each derivation is defined on the whole preceding extension. -/
def DifferentialTower : (n : ℕ) → (A : Type u) → [NonUnitalRing A] → Type u
  | 0, _, _ => PUnit
  | n + 1, A, _ => Σ d : RingDerivation A, DifferentialTower n (differentialExtension d)

/-- The last ring of an iterated differential polynomial tower. -/
def DifferentialTower.terminal : {n : ℕ} → {A : Type u} → [NonUnitalRing A] →
    DifferentialTower n A → Type u
  | 0, A, _, _ => A
  | _ + 1, _, _, t => DifferentialTower.terminal t.2

/-- The ring structure of the last ring of a tower. -/
instance DifferentialTower.terminalRing : {n : ℕ} → {A : Type u} → [NonUnitalRing A] →
    (t : DifferentialTower n A) → NonUnitalRing t.terminal
  | 0, _, inst, _ => inst
  | _ + 1, _, _, t => DifferentialTower.terminalRing t.2

/-- **Question 5** (Section 1, arXiv v2 p. 3). Every iterated differential polynomial ring over a
locally nilpotent ring is Behrens radical.

Towers have positive length; local nilpotence means that every finitely generated subring is
nilpotent, and Behrens radicality is encoded as every quotient by a ring congruence having no
nonzero idempotent. -/
theorem question_5 (R : Type u) [NonUnitalRing R]
    (hR : ∀ F : Finset R, ∃ k > 0,
      ∀ w : FreeSemigroup (NonUnitalSubring.closure (F : Set R)),
        w.length = k → FreeSemigroup.lift (fun a ↦ (a : R)) w = 0)
    (n : ℕ) (t : DifferentialTower (n + 1) R) (c : RingCon t.terminal) (a : t.terminal)
    (ha : c (a * a) a) :
    c a 0 := by
  sorry

end Jin2021Iterated

/-!
# Reconstructing Partitions from their Multisets of k-Minors

Author: Pakawut Jiradilok.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2016](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: P. Jiradilok, *Reconstructing partitions from their multisets of k-minors*,
arXiv:1610.05354v1.

namespace Jiradilok2016Reconstructing

open Finset

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number `N(λ / μ)` of standard skew tableaux, zero when `μ ⊄ λ` (Section 2).
Entries are reindexed from `1, …, k` to `Fin k`. -/
noncomputable def skewTableauCount (lam μ : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  if μ ≤ lam then
    {T : Equiv {b // b ∈ lam.cells \ μ.cells}
        (Fin #(lam.cells \ μ.cells)) |
      (∀ b c, b.val.1 = c.val.1 → b.val.2 < c.val.2 → T b < T c) ∧
      (∀ b c, b.val.2 = c.val.2 → b.val.1 < c.val.1 → T b < T c)}.ncard
  else 0

open scoped Classical in
/-- The largest `k ≤ n` for which the multiset of `k`-minors, with skew-tableau multiplicities,
determines every partition of `n`, `G(n)` (Section 2). -/
noncomputable def G (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ({k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) |
    Function.Injective (fun lam : {lam : YoungDiagram // lam.card = n} ↦
      fun μ : {μ : YoungDiagram // μ.card = n - k} ↦
        skewTableauCount lam.val μ.val)}).sup id

/-- **Conjecture 7.1** (p. 27). The reconstruction deficit `n - G(n)` tends to infinity. -/
theorem conjecture_7_1 :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ n - G n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop := by
  sorry

end Jiradilok2016Reconstructing

title: Compressed frameworks and compressible graphs
problem_statement: In jordan2019compressed.lean, prove either Jordan2019Compressed.conjecture_21 or refute it by proving its logical negation Jordan2019Compressed.conjecture_21_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Compressed frameworks and compressible graphs

Authors: Tibor Jordan and Jialin Zhang.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: T. Jordan and J. Zhang, *Compressed frameworks and compressible graphs*, Proc. 11th
Hungarian-Japanese Symposium on Discrete Mathematics and its Applications (Tokyo, 2019),
189-198; expanded version, EGRES Technical Report 2019-10.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Jordan2019Compressed

/-- All vertex coordinates are algebraically independent over the rationals (Section 1). -/
def IsGeneric {V : Type*} (p : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : Prop :=
  AlgebraicIndependent ℚ (fun i : V × Fin 2 ↦ p i.1 i.2)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The planar rigidity matrix: the row of an edge has the coordinate differences in its two
endpoint blocks and zeros elsewhere (Section 6). -/
def rigidityMatrix {V : Type*} (p : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    Matrix (Sym2 V) (V × Fin 2) ℝ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v i ↦
    (if i.1 = u then p u i.2 - p v i.2 else 0) +
    (if i.1 = v then p v i.2 - p u i.2 else 0),
    fun u v ↦ by funext i; exact add_comm _ _⟩

/-- A circuit of the rigidity matrix is a minimally linearly dependent set of rows. -/
def IsRigidityCircuit {V : Type*} (p : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
    (C : Set (Sym2 V)) : Prop :=
  ¬LinearIndependent ℝ (fun e : C ↦ rigidityMatrix p e.val) ∧
    ∀ D ⊂ C, LinearIndependent ℝ (fun e : D ↦ rigidityMatrix p e.val)

/-- M-connectivity: at least two edges, no isolated vertices, and every pair of distinct edges
in a common generic rigidity circuit (Section 6; Jackson--Jordan (2005), Section 3). -/
def MConnected {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ∃ w, G.Adj v w) ∧
  (∃ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃ f ∈ G.edgeSet, e ≠ f) ∧
  ∃ p : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), IsGeneric p ∧
    ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ f ∈ G.edgeSet, e ≠ f →
      ∃ C ⊆ G.edgeSet, e ∈ C ∧ f ∈ C ∧ IsRigidityCircuit p C

/-- A generic planar realization in which every pairwise distance is minimal among all
realizations with the same edge lengths (Section 1). -/
def GenericallyCompressible {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), IsGeneric p ∧
    (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → p u ≠ p v) ∧
    ∀ q : V → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → dist (p u) (p v) = dist (q u) (q v)) →
      ∀ u v, dist (p u) (p v) ≤ dist (q u) (q v)

/-- The cut-pair relation (Section 3). Vertices in no cut-pair are kept as isolated vertices;
the target restricts to incident vertices. -/
def cutPairGraph {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : SimpleGraph V where
  Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ ¬(G.induce {w | w ≠ u ∧ w ≠ v}).Connected
  symm := by
    constructor
    intro u v h
    refine ⟨Ne.symm h.1, ?_⟩
    have hs : {w : V | w ≠ v ∧ w ≠ u} = {w : V | w ≠ u ∧ w ≠ v} := by
      ext w
      exact and_comm
    rw [hs]
    exact h.2
  loopless := by constructor; intro u h; exact h.1 rfl

/-- **Conjecture 21** (expanded report: Conjecture 22). An M-connected graph has a compressed
generic planar realization exactly when its cut-pair graph is a cycle or a disjoint union of
paths, including the empty union. -/
theorem conjecture_21 {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hG : MConnected G) :
    GenericallyCompressible G ↔
      let B := (cutPairGraph G).induce {v | ∃ w, (cutPairGraph G).Adj v w}
      (∃ n ≥ 3, Nonempty (B ≃g SimpleGraph.cycleGraph n)) ∨
        (∀ c : B.ConnectedComponent,
          ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (c.toSimpleGraph ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph (n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end Jordan2019Compressed

  sorry
