/-!
# Activated random walk on the comb

Authors: Matthew Junge, Josh Meisel, and Aldo Morelli.
Origin: [NYC Discrete Math REU 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14977v2).
Reference: M. Junge, J. Meisel, and A. Morelli, *Activated random walk on the comb*,
arXiv:2508.14977v2 (2025), 16 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Junge2025Activated

open Filter
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 1.3). For every positive sleep rate, the limiting
stationary densities on the teeth and spine exist and are strictly ordered below the interval
density.

Stationarity is sampled by stabilizing one active particle per nonsink site, with the terminal
law given by absorbing-event probabilities; densities are normalized by the spine length, and
`r` is the source's sleep rate `λ`. -/
theorem section_1_3_density_order (r : ℝ≥0) (hr : 0 < r) :
    let density : ℕ → Bool → Bool → ℝ := fun n withTeeth countTeeth ↦
      let V := Fin (n + 2) ⊕ Fin (if withTeeth then n else 0)
      let G : SimpleGraph V := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v w ↦
        match v, w with
        | .inl i, .inl j => (SimpleGraph.pathGraph (n + 2)).Adj i j
        | .inl i, .inr j => i.val = j.val + 1
        | _, _ => False
      let sink : V → Prop := fun v ↦
        match v with
        | .inl i => i.val = 0 ∨ i.val = n + 1
        | .inr _ => False
      let State := V → Option ℕ
      let step : State → PMF State := fun s ↦
        (PMF.uniformOfFintype V).bind fun v ↦
          if sink v then PMF.pure s else
            match s v with
            | none => PMF.pure s
            | some 0 => PMF.pure s
            | some (a + 1) =>
              let jump : PMF State :=
                if h : (G.neighborFinset v).Nonempty then
                  (PMF.uniformOfFinset (G.neighborFinset v) h).map fun w ↦
                    if sink w then Function.update s v (some a) else
                      Function.update (Function.update s v (some a)) w
                        (some (match s w with | none => 2 | some b => b + 1))
                else PMF.pure s
              if a = 0 then
                (PMF.ofFintype (fun b : Bool ↦
                    if b then (r / (1 + r) : ℝ≥0)
                    else (1 - r / (1 + r) : ℝ≥0))
                  (by
                    simp only [Fintype.sum_bool, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false, ite_true]
                    exact_mod_cast add_tsub_cancel_of_le
                      ((div_le_one (by positivity)).2 (by simp) :
                        r / (1 + r) ≤ 1))).bind fun sleep ↦
                      if sleep then PMF.pure (Function.update s v none) else jump
              else jump
      (∑ v : V,
        if ¬sink v ∧ (match v with | .inl _ => !countTeeth | .inr _ => countTeeth)
        then (⨆ t : ℕ, (((fun μ : PMF State ↦ μ.bind step)^[t])
            (PMF.pure (fun u ↦ some (if sink u then 0 else 1) : State))).toOuterMeasure
              {s | (∀ u, ¬sink u → s u = some 0 ∨ s u = none) ∧ s v = none}).toReal
        else 0) / n
    ∃ teeth spine interval : ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ density n true true) atTop (𝓝 teeth) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ density n true false) atTop (𝓝 spine) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ density n false false) atTop (𝓝 interval) ∧
      teeth < spine ∧ spine < interval := by
  sorry

end Junge2025Activated

  sorry

title: Asymptotics of McKay numbers for S_n
problem_statement: In kane2007asymptotics.lean, prove either Kane2007Asymptotics.question_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Kane2007Asymptotics.question_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Asymptotics of McKay numbers for S_n

Author: Daniel M. Kane.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU
2005](https://sites.google.com/view/gallian-reu/additional-information/program-bibliography).
Reference: D. M. Kane, *Asymptotics of McKay numbers for S_n*, J. Number Theory **124** (2007),
200-228; doi:10.1016/j.jnt.2006.08.011.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Kane2007Asymptotics

open Finset

/-- The hook number: cells weakly right in the same row or weakly below in the same column,
with the cell itself counted once. -/
def hookLength (lambda : YoungDiagram) (c : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{d ∈ lambda.cells | (d.1 = c.1 ∧ c.2 ≤ d.2) ∨ (d.2 = c.2 ∧ c.1 ≤ d.1)}

/-- The hook product `H(lambda)` over every cell of the diagram. -/
def hookProduct (lambda : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  ∏ c ∈ lambda.cells, hookLength lambda c

/-- The signed difference `a_2(n)` of even- and odd-hook-valuation partition counts, that is,
the sum of `(-1) ^ a p_2(a; n)`. -/
def a2 (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ lambda : Nat.Partition n,
    (-1 : ℤ) ^ padicValNat 2 (hookProduct (YoungDiagram.ofPartition lambda))

/-- **Question 3** (with its expected-answer paragraph). The signed `a_2(n)` has order
`exp (√(c * n / log n))` for a fixed positive `c`.

"On the order of" is read as eventual two-sided positive multiplicative comparison with the
same `c`, without absolute value. -/
theorem question_3 :
    ∃ c A B : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧
      ∃ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∀ n ≥ N,
        A * Real.exp (√(c * (n : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ))) ≤ (a2 n : ℝ) ∧
        (a2 n : ℝ) ≤ B * Real.exp (√(c * (n : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ))) := by sorry

end Kane2007Asymptotics

  sorry

title: The Cross Number of Minimal Zero-sum Sequences in Finite Abelian Groups
problem_statement: In kim2015cross.lean, prove either Kim2015Cross.conjecture_23_primary_splitting_and_krause_zahlten_value or refute it by proving its logical negation Kim2015Cross.conjecture_23_primary_splitting_and_krause_zahlten_value_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Cross Number of Minimal Zero-sum Sequences in Finite Abelian Groups

Author: Bumsoo Kim.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: B. Kim, *The Cross Number of Minimal Zero-sum Sequences in Finite Abelian Groups*,
arXiv:1410.6867.
-/

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace Kim2015Cross

/-- A sequence is zero-sum free if no nonempty subsequence has sum zero. -/
def IsZeroSumFree {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (S : Multiset G) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : Multiset G, T ≤ S → T ≠ 0 → T.sum ≠ 0

/-- A sequence is minimal zero-sum when it is nonempty, zero-sum, and its only zero-sum
subsequences are the empty sequence and itself. -/
def IsMinimalZeroSum {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (S : Multiset G) : Prop :=
  S ≠ 0 ∧ S.sum = 0 ∧
    ∀ T : Multiset G, T ≤ S → T.sum = 0 → T = 0 ∨ T = S

/-- The cross number `k(S) = sum_g v_g(S) / ord(g)` of a sequence. -/
def crossNumber {G : Type*} [AddMonoid G] (S : Multiset G) : ℚ :=
  (S.map fun g : G ↦ (1 : ℚ) / (addOrderOf g : ℚ)).sum

/-- `q` is the cross number `K(G)`, the maximum cross number among minimal zero-sum
sequences over `G`. -/
def HasCrossNumber (G : Type*) [AddCommMonoid G] (q : ℚ) : Prop :=
  IsGreatest {r : ℚ | ∃ S : Multiset G, IsMinimalZeroSum S ∧ crossNumber S = r} q

/-- A cyclic prime-power decomposition `G ≃ ⨁ᵢ C_{pᵢ^{aᵢ}}`, as a product of cyclic groups. -/
structure CyclicPrimePowerDecomposition (G : Type u) [AddCommGroup G] where
  /-- The index type of the cyclic factors. -/
  ι : Type u
  fintype : Fintype ι
  /-- The prime `pᵢ` of each cyclic factor. -/
  prime : ι → ℕ
  /-- The exponent `aᵢ` of each cyclic factor. -/
  exponent : ι → ℕ
  prime_isPrime : ∀ i : ι, Nat.Prime (prime i)
  exponent_pos : ∀ i : ι, 0 < exponent i
  /-- The isomorphism of `G` with the product of the cyclic factors. -/
  equiv : G ≃+ (∀ i : ι, ZMod (prime i ^ exponent i))

namespace CyclicPrimePowerDecomposition

attribute [instance] fintype

/-- The little cross number `k⋆(G) = ∑ i, (1 - 1 / pᵢ ^ aᵢ)` of a cyclic prime-power
decomposition. -/
def kStar {G : Type u} [AddCommGroup G] (D : CyclicPrimePowerDecomposition G) : ℚ :=
  letI := D.fintype
  ∑ i : D.ι, ((1 : ℚ) - (1 : ℚ) / ((D.prime i ^ D.exponent i : ℕ) : ℚ))

end CyclicPrimePowerDecomposition

/-- **Conjecture 23**. Maximal minimal zero-sum sequences consist of one element and primary
zero-sum-free factors, with cross number `K*`; zero-sum-free sequences attaining `k*` likewise
split into primary factors. -/
theorem conjecture_23_primary_splitting_and_krause_zahlten_value
    {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]
    (D : CyclicPrimePowerDecomposition G) :
    (∀ U : Multiset G,
      IsMinimalZeroSum U → HasCrossNumber G (crossNumber U) →
        ∃ (g : G) (parts : {p : ℕ // p ∈ (AddMonoid.exponent G).primeFactors} → Multiset G),
          U = {g} + ∑ p, parts p ∧
            ∀ p, IsZeroSumFree (parts p) ∧
              ∀ x ∈ parts p, x ∈ AddCommGroup.primaryComponent G p.1) ∧
      HasCrossNumber G (D.kStar + (1 : ℚ) / (AddMonoid.exponent G : ℚ)) ∧
        ∀ S : Multiset G, IsZeroSumFree S → crossNumber S = D.kStar →
          ∃ parts : {p : ℕ // p ∈ (AddMonoid.exponent G).primeFactors} → Multiset G,
            S = ∑ p, parts p ∧
              ∀ p, IsZeroSumFree (parts p) ∧
                ∀ x ∈ parts p, x ∈ AddCommGroup.primaryComponent G p.1 := by
  sorry

end Kim2015Cross

  sorry

title: Solutions to the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation in Hyperbolic Space
problem_statement: In kleinhenz2014solutions.lean, prove either Kleinhenz2014Solutions.conjecture_1_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Kleinhenz2014Solutions.conjecture_1_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Solutions to the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation in Hyperbolic Space

Author: Peter Kleinhenz.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2014](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: P. Kleinhenz, *Solutions to the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation in Hyperbolic Space*,
SPUR final report (2014).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Kleinhenz2014Solutions

open MeasureTheory FourierTransform Filter
open scoped SchwartzMap LineDeriv Laplacian Topology ENNReal Real

/-- Radial hyperbolic energy data represented by the unitary conjugate
`w(r) = (sinh r / r) u(r)` and its genuine weak Euclidean derivatives. -/
structure RadialEnergy where
  /-- The radial conjugate function `w`. -/
  value : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))
  /-- The weak partial derivatives of `w`. -/
  gradient : Fin 3 → Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))
  weak_derivative : ∀ j, (gradient j : 𝓢'((EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), ℂ)) =
    ∂_{EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)} (value : 𝓢'((EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), ℂ))
  radial : ∀ A : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
    (fun x ↦ value (A x)) =ᵐ[volume] value

instance : TopologicalSpace RadialEnergy :=
  TopologicalSpace.induced (fun u : RadialEnergy ↦ (u.value, u.gradient)) inferInstance

/-- The hyperbolic focusing energy in unitary radial coordinates (source (1.2)). -/
def energy (u : RadialEnergy) : ℝ :=
  let ρ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ := fun x ↦
    if ‖x‖ = 0 then 1 else ‖x‖ / Real.sinh ‖x‖
  (‖u.value‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖u.gradient j‖ ^ 2) / 2 -
    (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), ρ x ^ 4 * ‖u.value x‖ ^ 6) / 6

/-- The Euclidean ground state (Theorem 1.2). -/
def groundState (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : ℝ :=
  (√(1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 3))⁻¹

/-- The linear hyperbolic Schrodinger flow after radial conjugation. It is defined on all of
`L2` by its exact spectral multiplier. -/
def linearFlow (t : ℝ) (f : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))) :
    Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) :=
  let phase : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℂ := fun ξ ↦
    Complex.exp (-Complex.I * (t : ℂ) *
      ((1 + (2 * π) ^ 2 * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))
  let hp : MemLp phase ∞ volume := by
    apply memLp_top_of_bound (μ := volume) (C := 1)
    · apply Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable
      dsimp [phase]
      fun_prop
    · filter_upwards [] with ξ
      simp only [phase, Complex.norm_exp, Complex.mul_re, Complex.neg_re,
        Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im, Complex.neg_im, Complex.ofReal_re,
        Complex.ofReal_im, mul_zero, sub_zero]
      norm_num
  𝓕⁻ ((hp.toLp phase) • (𝓕 f))

/-- **Conjecture 1.4**. Every radial hyperbolic energy datum below both Euclidean ground-state
thresholds has a global focusing solution scattering in both time directions.

The statement uses the unitary radial coordinates `w(r) = (sinh r / r) u(r)`. -/
theorem conjecture_1_4 (u₀ : RadialEnergy)
    (henergy : energy u₀ <
      (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), ‖fderiv ℝ groundState x‖ ^ 2) / 2 -
      (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), |groundState x| ^ 6) / 6)
    (hgradient : ‖u₀.value‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖u₀.gradient j‖ ^ 2 <
      ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), ‖fderiv ℝ groundState x‖ ^ 2) :
    let ρ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ := fun x ↦
      if ‖x‖ = 0 then 1 else ‖x‖ / Real.sinh ‖x‖
    ∃ u : C(ℝ, RadialEnergy), u 0 = u₀ ∧
      (∃ v : ℝ × (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) → ℂ,
        AEStronglyMeasurable v (volume.prod volume) ∧
        (∀ t : ℝ, (fun x ↦ v (t, x)) =ᵐ[volume] (u t).value) ∧
        ∀ a b : ℝ, a ≤ b →
          (∫⁻ t in Set.Icc a b, ∫⁻ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3),
            ENNReal.ofReal (ρ x ^ 8 * ‖v (t, x)‖ ^ 10)) < ∞) ∧
      (∀ (t : ℝ) (φ : 𝓢((EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), ℂ)),
        Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ↦
          (u t).value x * ((Δ φ) x - φ x) +
          (ρ x ^ 4 : ℂ) * (‖(u t).value x‖ ^ 4 : ℂ) *
            (u t).value x * φ x) volume ∧
        HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ ↦ ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), (u s).value x * φ x)
          (Complex.I * ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3),
            (u t).value x * ((Δ φ) x - φ x) +
            (ρ x ^ 4 : ℂ) * (‖(u t).value x‖ ^ 4 : ℂ) *
              (u t).value x * φ x) t) ∧
      ∃ uPlus uMinus : RadialEnergy,
        Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦
          ‖(u t).value - linearFlow t uPlus.value‖ ^ 2 +
          ∑ j, ‖(u t).gradient j - linearFlow t (uPlus.gradient j)‖ ^ 2)
          atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
        Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦
          ‖(u t).value - linearFlow t uMinus.value‖ ^ 2 +
          ∑ j, ‖(u t).gradient j - linearFlow t (uMinus.gradient j)‖ ^ 2)
          atBot (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

end Kleinhenz2014Solutions

title: On the Maximal Cross Number of Unique Factorization Indexed Multisets
problem_statement: In kriz2013maximal.lean, prove either Kriz2013Maximal.conjecture_maximal_ufim_splits_over_sylow_components or refute it by proving its logical negation Kriz2013Maximal.conjecture_maximal_ufim_splits_over_sylow_components_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the Maximal Cross Number of Unique Factorization Indexed Multisets

Author: Daniel Kriz.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2012](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: D. Kriz, *On the maximal cross number of unique factorization indexed multisets*,
J. Number Theory **133** (2013), 3033-3056; arXiv:1301.1401.
-/

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace Kriz2013Maximal

/-- An indexed multiset over `G`: a finite index type whose indices carry values in `G`. -/
structure IndexedMultiset (G : Type u) where
  /-- The finite index type. -/
  ι : Type u
  instFintype : Fintype ι
  /-- The value in `G` carried by each index. -/
  elem : ι → G

namespace IndexedMultiset

attribute [instance] instFintype

variable {G : Type u}

/-- The restriction of an indexed multiset to the submultiset on a finite set of indices. -/
def restrict (S : IndexedMultiset G) (I : Finset S.ι) : IndexedMultiset G where
  ι := {i : S.ι // i ∈ I}
  instFintype := inferInstance
  elem := fun i ↦ S.elem i.1

/-- `S(I)` is a minimal zero-sum indexed submultiset. -/
def IsMinimalZeroSumOn [AddCommMonoid G] (S : IndexedMultiset G)
    (I : Finset S.ι) : Prop :=
  I.Nonempty ∧ (∑ i ∈ I, S.elem i) = 0 ∧
    ∀ J : Finset S.ι, J ⊂ I → J.Nonempty → (∑ i ∈ J, S.elem i) ≠ 0

/-- An irreducible factorization of `S`: a finite set of minimal zero-sum index blocks that
partitions the indexing set. -/
def IsIrreducibleFactorization [AddCommMonoid G] (S : IndexedMultiset G)
    (F : Finset (Finset S.ι)) : Prop :=
  (∀ I ∈ F, S.IsMinimalZeroSumOn I) ∧
    ∀ i : S.ι, ∃! I : Finset S.ι, I ∈ F ∧ i ∈ I

/-- A unique factorization indexed multiset (UFIM): a zero-sum indexed multiset
over `G \ {0}` with exactly one irreducible factorization, up to reordering of
the factor blocks. -/
def IsUFIM [AddCommMonoid G] (S : IndexedMultiset G) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : S.ι, S.elem i ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ i : S.ι, S.elem i) = 0 ∧
    ∃ F : Finset (Finset S.ι), S.IsIrreducibleFactorization F ∧
      ∀ E : Finset (Finset S.ι), S.IsIrreducibleFactorization E → E = F

/-- The cross number `k(S) = sum_{i in indices} 1 / ord(g_i)`. -/
def crossNumber [AddMonoid G] (S : IndexedMultiset G) : ℚ :=
  ∑ i : S.ι, (1 : ℚ) / (addOrderOf (S.elem i) : ℚ)

end IndexedMultiset

/-- `q` is Kriz's `K_1(G)`, the maximal cross number among UFIMs over
`G \ {0}`. -/
def HasMaximalUFIMCrossNumber (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] (q : ℚ) : Prop :=
  IsGreatest {r : ℚ | ∃ S : IndexedMultiset G,
    S.IsUFIM ∧ S.crossNumber = r} q

/-- **Conjecture 43**. A maximal-cross-number UFIM over a finite abelian group is a disjoint
union of UFIMs supported on its Sylow components. -/
theorem conjecture_maximal_ufim_splits_over_sylow_components
    {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]
    (S : IndexedMultiset G) (hS : S.IsUFIM)
    (hmax : HasMaximalUFIMCrossNumber G (S.crossNumber)) :
    ∃ parts : {p : ℕ // p ∈ (Nat.card G).primeFactors} → Finset S.ι,
      (∀ x : S.ι, ∃! p, x ∈ parts p) ∧
        ∀ p, (S.restrict (parts p)).IsUFIM ∧
          ∀ x ∈ parts p, S.elem x ∈ AddCommGroup.primaryComponent G p.1 := by
  sorry

end Kriz2013Maximal

  sorry

title: Binomial edge ideals of crown graphs
problem_statement: In kumar2025binomial.lean, prove either Kumar2025Binomial.conjecture_5_6 or refute it by proving its logical negation Kumar2025Binomial.conjecture_5_6_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Binomial edge ideals of crown graphs

Authors: Arvind Kumar, Joshua Pomeroy, and Le Tran.
Origin: [New Mexico State University Summer Undergraduate Research Program
2024](https://math.nmsu.edu/research/summer-undergraduate-research-program/summer2024.html).
Reference: A. Kumar, J. Pomeroy, and L. Tran, *Binomial edge ideals of crown graphs*,
J. Algebraic Combin. **62** (2025), article 51; arXiv:2507.03889v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Kumar2025Binomial

open MvPolynomial

/-- The crown graph. Vertex labels are shifted from one-based to zero-based. -/
def crownGraph (n : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n)) where
  Adj u v := u.val % 2 ≠ v.val % 2 ∧ u.val / 2 ≠ v.val / 2
  symm := ⟨fun _ _ h ↦ And.intro (Ne.symm h.1) (Ne.symm h.2)⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun _ h ↦ h.1 rfl⟩

/-- The binomial edge ideal. The `x` variables are indexed by `false` and the `y` by `true`. -/
def binomialEdgeIdeal (K : Type*) [Field K] {N : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) :
    Ideal (MvPolynomial (Bool × Fin N) K) :=
  Ideal.span {p | ∃ i j, G.Adj i j ∧
    p = X (false, i) * X (true, j) - X (false, j) * X (true, i)}

/-- The collection `C(G)` of sets `T` such that deleting each member of `T` increases the
component count. -/
def cutPointSets {N : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : Set (Set (Fin N)) :=
  {T | ∀ v ∈ T,
    Nat.card (G.induce (T \ {v})ᶜ).ConnectedComponent <
      Nat.card (G.induce Tᶜ).ConnectedComponent}

/-- The prime `P_T(G)`, generated by the variables on `T` and the minors within each remaining
component. -/
def cutPointPrime (K : Type*) [Field K] {N : ℕ}
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) (T : Set (Fin N)) :
    Ideal (MvPolynomial (Bool × Fin N) K) :=
  Ideal.span
    ({p | ∃ i ∈ T, (p = X (false, i) ∨ p = X (true, i))} ∪
      {p | ∃ u v : {i : Fin N // i ∉ T},
        (G.induce Tᶜ).Reachable u v ∧
          p = X (false, u.val) * X (true, v.val) -
            X (false, v.val) * X (true, u.val)})

/-- **Conjecture 5.6**. Every cut-point prime of a crown graph with `n ≥ 4` has local
Vasconcelos number four, over any field.

The local Vasconcelos number is expressed as the least homogeneous witness degree. -/
theorem conjecture_5_6 (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n)
    (T : Set (Fin (2 * n))) (hT : T ∈ cutPointSets (crownGraph n)) :
    IsLeast {d : ℕ | ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Bool × Fin (2 * n)) K,
      f.IsHomogeneous d ∧
        (binomialEdgeIdeal K (crownGraph n)).colon {f} = cutPointPrime K (crownGraph n) T} 4 := by
  sorry

end Kumar2025Binomial

theorem Kumar2025Binomial.conjecture_5_6_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Kumar2025Binomial.conjecture_5_6.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Dedekind Sums with Even Denominators
problem_statement: In kural2019dedekind.lean, prove either Kural2019Dedekind.conjecture_4_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Kural2019Dedekind.conjecture_4_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Dedekind Sums with Even Denominators

Author: Michael Kural.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2017](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: M. Kural, *Dedekind sums with even denominators*, J. Number Theory **197** (2019),
106-120.
-/

namespace Kural2019Dedekind

/-- The sawtooth function, with value zero at integers (Definition 1.1). -/
def sawtooth (x : ℚ) : ℚ :=
  if Int.fract x = 0 then 0 else Int.fract x - 1 / 2

/-- The normalized Dedekind sum `S(a,b) = 12 s(a,b)` (Definition 1.1). -/
def normalizedDedekindSum (a : ℤ) (b : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  12 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 b, sawtooth ((j : ℚ) / b) * sawtooth ((a : ℚ) * j / b)

/-- The residue `h_q(x,y)` (Definition 4.2). The inverse of `y` is chosen by Bezout; off the
coprime domain the value is junk. -/
def h (q : ℕ) (x y : ℤ) : ZMod (q ^ 2 - 1) :=
  let t : ℕ := (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2).toNat
  let a : ℤ := x * Int.gcdA y (t : ℤ)
  (⌊(((q : ℚ) ^ 2 - 1) * a) / t - (q : ℚ) * normalizedDedekindSum (a * q) t⌋ : ℤ)

/-- **Conjecture 4.3**. Every positive-parameter one-variable family `h_q(x + rq, xrq - 1)`
exhausts the prescribed residue subgroup `Gamma_q`. -/
theorem conjecture_4_3 (q r : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    {z : ZMod (q ^ 2 - 1) | ∃ x : ℤ,
      Int.gcd (x + (r : ℤ) * q) (x * r * q - 1) = 1 ∧
      Int.gcd (x ^ 2 + 1) q = 1 ∧
      z = h q (x + (r : ℤ) * q) (x * r * q - 1)} =
    {z : ZMod (q ^ 2 - 1) | ∃ s : ZMod (q ^ 2 - 1),
      z = (if IsSquare q then 24 else 12) * s} := by
  sorry

end Kural2019Dedekind

  sorry

title: Fast Algorithms for Finding Pattern Avoiders and Counting Pattern Occurrences in Permutations
problem_statement: In kuszmaul2017fast.lean, prove either Kuszmaul2017Fast.detector_linear_batch_cost or refute it by proving its logical negation Kuszmaul2017Fast.detector_linear_batch_cost_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Fast Algorithms for Finding Pattern Avoiders and Counting Pattern Occurrences in Permutations

Author: William Kuszmaul.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU
2015](https://sites.google.com/view/gallian-reu/additional-information/program-bibliography).
Reference: W. Kuszmaul, *Fast algorithms for finding pattern avoiders and counting pattern
occurrences in permutations*, Math. Comp. **87** (2018), 987-1011; arXiv:1509.08216v4.
-/

namespace Kuszmaul2017Fast

open Finset

/-- Order standardization (Definition 2.2). Letters are zero-based. -/
def standardize (w : List ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  w.map fun a ↦ (w.filter fun b ↦ b < a).length

/-- All length-`n` classical pattern avoiders (Definitions 2.5 and 2.8). -/
def avoiders (pattern : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Finset (List ℕ) :=
  {w ∈ (List.range n).permutations.toFinset |
    !(w.sublists.any fun s ↦ standardize s == pattern)}

/-- Removal of the `j`-th largest letter followed by standardization (Definition 2.12). -/
def down (w : List ℕ) (j : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  standardize (w.filter fun a ↦ a != w.length - j)

/-- The `j` largest letters in their original order (Section 2). -/
def upfix (w : List ℕ) (j : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  w.filter fun a ↦ w.length - j ≤ a

/-- Algorithm 1 with the incremental upfix shortcut, returning the decision and one entry charge
plus the number of visited layers (pp. 10-11). Each layer checks deletion membership before
the upfix shortcut. -/
def detectAvoider (pattern : List ℕ) (H : Finset (List ℕ))
    (w : List ℕ) : Bool × ℕ :=
  if w = pattern then (false, 1) else
    let rec
      /-- Scan the given layers, returning the decision and the number of visited layers. -/
      loop : List ℕ → Bool × ℕ
      | [] => (true, 0)
      | j :: js =>
        if down w j ∉ H then (false, 1)
        else if j ≤ pattern.length ∧
            standardize (upfix w j) ≠ standardize (upfix pattern j) then (true, 1)
        else
          let result := loop js
          (result.1, result.2 + 1)
    let result := loop (List.range' 1 (min (pattern.length + 1) w.length))
    (result.1, result.2 + 1)

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Algorithm 5, pp. 10-11). The upfix-short-circuited
detector has uniformly constant amortized work on each full insertion layer.

Cost is the source's wide-word/dictionary model with prior membership, inverse and
pattern-upfix data supplied, not bit complexity; the uniform constant and interleaved shortcut
follow the contextual source reading. -/
theorem detector_linear_batch_cost :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      ∀ k > 0, ∀ pattern : Equiv.Perm (Fin k),
        ∀ n ≥ 2,
        let H := avoiders (List.ofFn fun i ↦ (pattern i).val) (n - 1)
        ((∑ w ∈ H.biUnion (fun u ↦ (Finset.range n).image fun i ↦ u.insertIdx i (n - 1)),
            (detectAvoider (List.ofFn fun i ↦ (pattern i).val) H w).2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
          C * (n : ℝ) * (#H : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Kuszmaul2017Fast

theorem Kuszmaul2017Fast.detector_linear_batch_cost_neg : ¬ type_of% @Kuszmaul2017Fast.detector_linear_batch_cost := by
  sorry

title: A Computer Implementation of Whitehead's Algorithm
problem_statement: In lau1997computer.lean, prove either Lau1997Computer.conjecture_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Lau1997Computer.conjecture_5_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A Computer Implementation of Whitehead's Algorithm

Author: Michael Lau.
Origin: [Oregon State University REU
1997](https://sites.science.oregonstate.edu/math_reu/reucv.html).
Reference: M. Lau, *A computer implementation of Whitehead's algorithm*, Oregon State University
REU report (1997; current PDF dated 2010).
-/

namespace Lau1997Computer

/-- CP equivalence: a signed-letter permutation preserving inversion, followed by a cyclic
rotation (Definitions 3.1-3.2). -/
def CPEquivalent (u v : List (Fin 3 × Bool)) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3 × Bool),
    (∀ x, σ (x.1, !x.2) = ((σ x).1, !(σ x).2)) ∧
      List.IsRotated (u.map σ) v

/-- Reduced CP form: automorphism-minimal length and lexicographic leastness in the CP class,
with letter order `a < b < c < a⁻¹ < b⁻¹ < c⁻¹` (Definition 3.3). -/
def InReducedCPForm (w : FreeGroup (Fin 3)) : Prop :=
  (∀ φ : FreeGroup (Fin 3) ≃* FreeGroup (Fin 3),
    w.norm ≤ (φ w).norm) ∧
  ∀ v : List (Fin 3 × Bool), CPEquivalent w.toWord v →
    ¬List.Lex (fun x y : Fin 3 × Bool ↦
      x.1.val + (if x.2 then 0 else 3) < y.1.val + (if y.2 then 0 else 3))
      v w.toWord

/-- **Conjecture 5.1** (printed p. 21). Prefixing inequivalent reduced CP words by the positive
generator `a` preserves reduced CP form and inequivalence.

The domain includes the identity and pairs of unequal length; CP leastness is not leastness in
the full automorphism orbit, and no post-prefix normalization is performed. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 (w v : FreeGroup (Fin 3))
    (hw : InReducedCPForm w) (hv : InReducedCPForm v)
    (hne : ¬∃ φ : FreeGroup (Fin 3) ≃* FreeGroup (Fin 3), φ w = v) :
    InReducedCPForm (FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 3) * w) ∧
      InReducedCPForm (FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 3) * v) ∧
      ¬∃ φ : FreeGroup (Fin 3) ≃* FreeGroup (Fin 3),
        φ (FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 3) * w) = FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 3) * v := by
  sorry

end Lau1997Computer

theorem Lau1997Computer.conjecture_5_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Lau1997Computer.conjecture_5_1 := by
  sorry

problem_statement: In le2023machine.lean, prove either Le2023Machine.nesterov_ode_pl_rate or refute it by proving its logical negation Le2023Machine.nesterov_ode_pl_rate_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Machine learning optimization algorithms related to gradient descent

Author: Minh Le.
Origin: [University of Massachusetts Amherst REU
2023](https://sites.google.com/umass.edu/math-stat-reu/reports-2023).
Reference: M. Le, *Machine learning optimization algorithms related to gradient descent*, UMass
Amherst REU report, August 18, 2023.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Le2023Machine

/-- **Open question** (Section 3, Future Work, p. 17; cf. p. 16). The Nesterov ODE has
inverse-quadratic objective-gap decay under the global Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition and a
globally Lipschitz gradient, without convexity.

The continuous-time reading follows equation (11) and its stated initial data; it is not a
discrete-rate transfer, a sharp exponent, or a uniform convex-case prefactor. Luo-Xiao's
related theorems (2023 Theorem 2.3, Proposition 3.2) assume extra global growth and radial
flatness. -/
theorem nesterov_ode_pl_rate
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ)
    (L μ : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (hμ : 0 < μ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (xstar x₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (hmin : ∀ z, f xstar ≤ f z)
    (hgrad : LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal L) (gradient f))
    (hPL : ∀ z, f z - f xstar ≤ ‖gradient f z‖ ^ 2 / (2 * μ))
    (X : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (hC1 : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 X (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)))
    (hC2 : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 X (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)))
    (hinit : X 0 = x₀)
    (hvelocity : HasDerivWithinAt X 0 (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0)
    (hODE : ∀ t > 0,
      deriv (deriv X) t + ((3 : ℝ) / t) • deriv X t +
        gradient f (X t) = 0) :
    ∃ C > 0, ∃ T > 0, ∀ t ≥ T, f (X t) - f xstar ≤ C / t ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Le2023Machine

theorem Le2023Machine.nesterov_ode_pl_rate_neg : ¬ type_of% @Le2023Machine.nesterov_ode_pl_rate := by
  sorry

title: Brill--Noether Theory of Maximally Symmetric Graphs
problem_statement: In leake2015brill.lean, prove either Leake2015Brill.conjecture_6_all_large_genus_maximally_symmetric_graphs_are_special or refute it by proving its logical negation Leake2015Brill.conjecture_6_all_large_genus_maximally_symmetric_graphs_are_special_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Brill--Noether Theory of Maximally Symmetric Graphs

Authors: Timothy Leake and Dhruv Ranganathan.
Origin: [Yale SUMRY](https://sumry.yale.edu/past-projects).
Reference: T. Leake and D. Ranganathan, *Brill--Noether Theory of Maximally Symmetric Graphs*,
arXiv:1307.7652.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Leake2015Brill

/-- A finite multigraph bundled with its vertex and edge types. -/
structure FiniteGraph where
  /-- The vertex type. -/
  V : Type
  /-- The edge type. -/
  E : Type
  /-- The multigraph on these vertex and edge types. -/
  graph : Graph V E
  vertexSet_eq : graph.vertexSet = Set.univ
  edgeSet_eq : graph.edgeSet = Set.univ
  [fintypeV : Fintype V]
  [decidableEqV : DecidableEq V]
  [fintypeE : Fintype E]
  [decidableEqE : DecidableEq E]

attribute [instance] FiniteGraph.fintypeV FiniteGraph.decidableEqV
attribute [instance] FiniteGraph.fintypeE FiniteGraph.decidableEqE

/-- The ordered endpoints labelling the two half-edges of each edge. The order is a choice,
and even a loop has two distinct half-edge labels. -/
def edgeEnds (G : FiniteGraph) (e : G.E) :
    {p : G.V × G.V // G.graph.IsLink e p.1 p.2} :=
  let h := G.graph.exists_isLink_of_mem_edgeSet
    (show e ∈ G.graph.edgeSet by rw [G.edgeSet_eq]; trivial)
  ⟨(h.choose, h.choose_spec.choose), h.choose_spec.choose_spec⟩

/-- The genus `|E| - |V| + 1`, with integer subtraction (Section 2.1). -/
def graphGenus (G : FiniteGraph) : ℤ :=
  (Fintype.card G.E : ℤ) - (Fintype.card G.V : ℤ) + 1

/-- Divisors: integer combinations of vertices (Section 2.1). -/
abbrev Divisor (G : FiniteGraph) := G.V →₀ ℤ

/-- The degree of a divisor, the sum of its coefficients (Section 2.1). -/
def divisorDegree (G : FiniteGraph) (D : Divisor G) : ℤ :=
  ∑ v : G.V, D v

/-- Effective divisors: nonnegative coefficients (Section 2.1). -/
def Effective (G : FiniteGraph) (D : Divisor G) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : G.V, 0 ≤ D v

open scoped Classical in
/-- The divisor of an integer chip-firing function. Parallel edges contribute separately and
loops contribute zero. -/
def principalDivisor (G : FiniteGraph) (f : G.V → ℤ) : Divisor G :=
  Finsupp.onFinset Finset.univ
    (fun v ↦ ∑ w : G.V, ∑ e : G.E,
      if G.graph.IsLink e v w then f w - f v else 0)
    (by simp)

/-- Linear equivalence generated by chip-firing (Definition 7). -/
def LinearEquivalent (G : FiniteGraph) (D D' : Divisor G) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : G.V → ℤ, D' = D + principalDivisor G f

/-- The Brill--Noether number `ρ(g, r, d) = g - (r + 1)(g - d + r)` (Section 2.2). -/
def brillNoetherNumber (g r d : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (g : ℤ) - ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * ((g : ℤ) - (d : ℤ) + (r : ℤ))

/-- The loop subdivision: insert one vertex in each loop and replace that loop by two edges
(Section 3.1). -/
def loopSubdivision (G : FiniteGraph) : FiniteGraph :=
  let L := {e : G.E // (edgeEnds G e).val.1 = (edgeEnds G e).val.2}
  let a : G.E ⊕ L → G.V ⊕ L
    | Sum.inl e => Sum.inl (edgeEnds G e).val.1
    | Sum.inr e => Sum.inr e
  let b : G.E ⊕ L → G.V ⊕ L
    | Sum.inl e =>
        if h : (edgeEnds G e).val.1 = (edgeEnds G e).val.2 then Sum.inr ⟨e, h⟩
        else Sum.inl (edgeEnds G e).val.2
    | Sum.inr e => Sum.inl (edgeEnds G e.val).val.2
  { V := G.V ⊕ L
    E := G.E ⊕ L
    graph :=
      { vertexSet := Set.univ
        edgeSet := Set.univ
        IsLink e v w := (a e = v ∧ b e = w) ∨ (a e = w ∧ b e = v)
        isLink_symm := by
          intro e he
          exact ⟨fun _ _ h ↦ h.symm⟩
        eq_or_eq_of_isLink_of_isLink := by
          intro e x y v w h h'
          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ <;>
            rcases h' with ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ | ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ <;> simp_all
        edge_mem_iff_exists_isLink := by
          intro e
          exact ⟨fun _ ↦ ⟨a e, b e, Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩, fun _ ↦ Set.mem_univ e⟩
        left_mem_of_isLink := by intros; trivial }
    vertexSet_eq := rfl
    edgeSet_eq := rfl }

/-- Brill--Noether generality: for every `r, d ≥ 0` with negative Brill--Noether number, the
graph has no divisor of degree `d` and rank at least `r` (Section 2.2). Divisors are extended
by zero to the loop subdivision, following Caporaso's loop convention. -/
def BrillNoetherGeneral (G : FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ r d : ℕ,
    brillNoetherNumber
        (Int.natAbs (graphGenus G)) r d < 0 →
      ¬∃ D : Divisor G, divisorDegree G D = (d : ℤ) ∧
        (∀ E : Divisor (loopSubdivision G),
          Effective (loopSubdivision G) E →
          divisorDegree (loopSubdivision G) E = (r : ℤ) →
          ∃ D' : Divisor (loopSubdivision G),
            LinearEquivalent (loopSubdivision G)
              ((Finsupp.embDomain (Function.Embedding.inl) D :
                  Divisor (loopSubdivision G)) - E) D' ∧
              Effective (loopSubdivision G) D')

/-- Automorphisms of the multigraph: vertex and edge permutations preserving endpoints, with a
reversal flag for the two half-edges of each edge. Loop flips, as in the source's hyperelliptic
involutions, therefore count as automorphisms. -/
structure MultigraphAut (G : FiniteGraph) where
  /-- The permutation of vertices. -/
  vertexEquiv : G.V ≃ G.V
  /-- The permutation of edges. -/
  edgeEquiv : G.E ≃ G.E
  /-- Whether each edge's two half-edges are swapped. -/
  reverse : G.E → Bool
  map_init : ∀ e : G.E,
    (edgeEnds G (edgeEquiv e)).val.1 =
      vertexEquiv (if reverse e then (edgeEnds G e).val.2 else (edgeEnds G e).val.1)
  map_term : ∀ e : G.E,
    (edgeEnds G (edgeEquiv e)).val.2 =
      vertexEquiv (if reverse e then (edgeEnds G e).val.1 else (edgeEnds G e).val.2)

open scoped Classical in
instance (G : FiniteGraph) : Fintype (MultigraphAut G) :=
  Fintype.ofInjective
    (fun f : MultigraphAut G ↦ (f.vertexEquiv, f.edgeEquiv, f.reverse))
    (by
      intro f h hpair
      cases f
      cases h
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hpair
      rcases hpair with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
      rfl)

/-- Maximal symmetry in a comparison class: the automorphism group is at least as large as that
of every graph in the class. -/
def MaximallySymmetricIn (G : FiniteGraph) (Family : FiniteGraph → Prop) : Prop :=
  Family G ∧ ∀ H : FiniteGraph, Family H →
    Fintype.card (MultigraphAut H) ≤ Fintype.card (MultigraphAut G)

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 6**. If the genus is sufficiently large, then every trivalent maximally
symmetric graph or multigraph, with or without loops, is not Brill--Noether general.

"Sufficiently large" is read as one uniform threshold `g₀` for all three comparison classes. -/
theorem conjecture_6_all_large_genus_maximally_symmetric_graphs_are_special :
    let family (g : ℕ) (G : FiniteGraph) :=
      G.graph.toSimpleGraph.Connected ∧ (∀ v : G.V,
          (∑ e : G.E,
            ((if G.graph.Inc e v then 1 else 0) +
              (if G.graph.IsLoopAt e v then 1 else 0))) = 3) ∧ graphGenus G = (g : ℤ)
    ∃ g₀ : ℕ, ∀ g ≥ g₀, ∀ G : FiniteGraph,
      (MaximallySymmetricIn G (family g) ∨
        MaximallySymmetricIn G
            (fun H ↦ family g H ∧ H.graph.Loopless) ∨
          MaximallySymmetricIn G
            (fun H ↦ family g H ∧ H.graph.Simple)) →
        ¬BrillNoetherGeneral G := by
  sorry

end Leake2015Brill

theorem Leake2015Brill.conjecture_6_all_large_genus_maximally_symmetric_graphs_are_special_neg : ¬ type_of% @Leake2015Brill.conjecture_6_all_large_genus_maximally_symmetric_graphs_are_special := by
  sorry

title: Isoperimetric regions in surfaces and in surfaces with density
problem_statement: In lee2006isoperimetric.lean, prove either Lee2006Isoperimetric.conjecture_7_10 or refute it by proving its logical negation Lee2006Isoperimetric.conjecture_7_10_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Isoperimetric regions in surfaces and in surfaces with density

Author: Michelle Lee.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/published.html).
Reference: M. Lee, *Isoperimetric regions in surfaces and in surfaces with density*, Rose-Hulman
Undergrad. Math. J. **7** (2006), no. 2, Article 15, 24 pp.;
https://scholar.rose-hulman.edu/rhumj/vol7/iss2/15/.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lee2006Isoperimetric

open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped ContDiff Real ENNReal

/-- The unit-radius circle times the Gaussian line (Section 7.1). It carries the intrinsic `L2`
product distance and circle period `2 * π`. -/
abbrev Cylinder := WithLp 2 (AddCircle (2 * π) × ℝ)

/-- Gaussian area on the quotient cylinder: circle arclength of total mass `2 * π` times the
normalized variance-one Gaussian measure. -/
def cylinderMeasure : Measure Cylinder :=
  letI : Fact (0 < 2 * π) := ⟨mul_pos (by norm_num) Real.pi_pos⟩
  ((volume : Measure (AddCircle (2 * π))).prod
    (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)).map (WithLp.toLp 2)

/-- The weighted BV perimeter on the boundaryless cylinder. Test fields have compact support on
the quotient, not on a cut strip or lift, and are differentiated before angular evaluation. -/
def cylinderPerimeter (E : Set Cylinder) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : Fact (0 < 2 * π) := ⟨mul_pos (by norm_num) Real.pi_pos⟩
  let q : WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ) → Cylinder := fun z ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 (((WithLp.ofLp z).1 : AddCircle (2 * π)), (WithLp.ofLp z).2)
  let σ : Cylinder → WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ) := fun z ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 ((AddCircle.equivIoc (2 * π) 0 (WithLp.ofLp z).1 : ℝ),
      (WithLp.ofLp z).2)
  ⨆ (F : ContinuousMap Cylinder (WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ))),
    ⨆ (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun z ↦ F (q z))),
    ⨆ (_ : HasCompactSupport F),
    ⨆ (_ : ∀ z, ‖F z‖ ≤ 1),
      ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z in E,
        LinearMap.trace ℝ (WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ))
          (fderiv ℝ (fun w ↦ F (q w)) (σ z)).toLinearMap -
        (WithLp.ofLp z).2 * (WithLp.ofLp (F z)).2 ∂cylinderMeasure)

/-- **Conjecture 7.10** (p. 23). On the unit-radius Gaussian cylinder, essential non-meridional
constant-weighted-curvature boundaries minimize near zero and total mass, and vertical pairs
minimize throughout a neighborhood of half mass.

The radius is fixed to one. Milman covers the middle neighborhood at `T = π`, but his
end-regime theorem requires `T > π`. -/
theorem conjecture_7_10 :
    let q : WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ) → Cylinder := fun z ↦
      WithLp.toLp 2 (((WithLp.ofLp z).1 : AddCircle (2 * π)), (WithLp.ofLp z).2)
    ∃ etaZero etaTotal etaHalf : ℝ,
      0 < etaZero ∧ 0 < etaTotal ∧ 0 < etaHalf ∧
      ∀ (A : ℝ) (_ : 0 < A) (_ : A < 2 * π),
        ((A < etaZero ∨ 2 * π - A < etaTotal) →
          ∃ (γ : ℝ → WithLp 2 (ℝ × ℝ)) (k : ℤ),
            ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ ∧
            (∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0) ∧
            (∀ t, γ (t + 1) = γ t +
              WithLp.toLp 2 ((k : ℝ) * (2 * π), (0 : ℝ))) ∧
            k ≠ 0 ∧
            InjOn (fun t ↦ q (γ t)) (Ico 0 1) ∧
            (∃ s t, (WithLp.ofLp (γ s)).2 ≠ (WithLp.ofLp (γ t)).2) ∧
            (∃ K : ℝ, ∀ t,
              let v := deriv γ t
              ((WithLp.ofLp v).1 * (WithLp.ofLp (deriv (deriv γ) t)).2 -
                (WithLp.ofLp v).2 * (WithLp.ofLp (deriv (deriv γ) t)).1) / ‖v‖ ^ 3 +
                (WithLp.ofLp (γ t)).2 * (WithLp.ofLp v).1 / ‖v‖ = K) ∧
            ∃ c : Cylinder, c ∉ range (fun t ↦ q (γ t)) ∧
              let E := connectedComponentIn (range (fun t ↦ q (γ t)))ᶜ c
              NullMeasurableSet E cylinderMeasure ∧
              cylinderMeasure E = ENNReal.ofReal A ∧
              cylinderPerimeter E < ⊤ ∧
              ∀ (F : Set Cylinder) (_ : NullMeasurableSet F cylinderMeasure),
                cylinderMeasure F = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                  cylinderPerimeter E ≤ cylinderPerimeter F) ∧
        ((|A - π| < etaHalf) →
          ∃ θ : AddCircle (2 * π),
            let E : Set Cylinder := {z | ∃ t : ℝ,
              0 < t ∧ t < A ∧ (WithLp.ofLp z).1 = θ + (t : AddCircle (2 * π))}
            NullMeasurableSet E cylinderMeasure ∧
            cylinderMeasure E = ENNReal.ofReal A ∧
            cylinderPerimeter E < ⊤ ∧
            ∀ (F : Set Cylinder) (_ : NullMeasurableSet F cylinderMeasure),
              cylinderMeasure F = ENNReal.ofReal A →
                cylinderPerimeter E ≤ cylinderPerimeter F) := by
  sorry

end Lee2006Isoperimetric

theorem Lee2006Isoperimetric.conjecture_7_10_neg : ¬ type_of% @Lee2006Isoperimetric.conjecture_7_10 := by
  sorry

title: The complexity class PDQP
problem_statement: In lee2013complexity.lean, prove either Lee2013Complexity.question_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Lee2013Complexity.question_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The complexity class PDQP

Author: Mitchell Lee.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2013](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/documents/2013Lee.pdf).
Reference: M. Lee, *The complexity class PDQP*, MIT SPUR final paper (2013); see also
S. Aaronson, A. Bouland, J. Fitzsimons, and M. Lee, *The space "just above" BQP*,
arXiv:1412.6507v1 (2014).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lee2013Complexity

open scoped ENNReal Polynomial

/-- The two single-qubit gates of the fixed finite gate basis (Section 8.2, p. 14). -/
inductive OneQubitGate
  /-- The real rotation `exp(i cos⁻¹(3/5) Y)`, with entries `4/5` and `±3/5`. -/
  | rotation
  /-- The phase gate `diag(1, i)`. -/
  | phase
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The unitary matrix of a single-qubit gate: the rotation with entries `4/5`, `±3/5`, or the
phase gate `diag(1, i)` (Section 8.2, p. 14). -/
def OneQubitGate.matrix : OneQubitGate → Matrix.unitaryGroup Bool ℂ
  | .rotation =>
      ⟨Matrix.of fun x y ↦ if x = y then 4 / 5 else if x then 3 / 5 else -3 / 5, by
        rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
        ext x y
        cases x <;> cases y <;>
          norm_num [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply,
            map_ofNat]⟩
  | .phase =>
      ⟨Matrix.diagonal fun b ↦ if b then Complex.I else 1, by
        rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
        ext x y
        cases x <;> cases y <;>
          simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]⟩

/-- A gate of a circuit on `n` wires: a single-qubit gate or a controlled-NOT (Sections 2.1
and 8.2). -/
inductive Gate (n : ℕ)
  /-- A single-qubit gate of the basis applied to one wire. -/
  | single (kind : OneQubitGate) (wire : Fin n)
  /-- A controlled-NOT gate with distinct control and target wires. -/
  | controlledNot (control target : Fin n) (different : control ≠ target)

/-- The unitary matrix of a gate acting on its wires (Section 2.1). -/
def Gate.matrix {n : ℕ} : Gate n → Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n → Bool) ℂ
  | .single kind wire =>
      let e := Equiv.funSplitAt wire Bool
      let u := Matrix.kronecker kind.matrix.val
        (1 : Matrix ({j : Fin n // j ≠ wire} → Bool) ({j : Fin n // j ≠ wire} → Bool) ℂ)
      have hu : u ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup _ ℂ :=
        Matrix.kronecker_mem_unitary kind.matrix.property (one_mem _)
      ⟨u.submatrix e e, by
        rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff'] at hu ⊢
        change u.conjTranspose * u = 1 at hu
        change (u.submatrix e e).conjTranspose * u.submatrix e e = 1
        rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_submatrix, Matrix.submatrix_mul_equiv _ _ e e e, hu,
          Matrix.submatrix_one_equiv]⟩
  | .controlledNot c t h =>
      let f : (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) := fun x ↦ Function.update x t (xor (x c) (x t))
      have hf : Function.Involutive f := by
        intro x
        funext i
        by_cases hi : i = t
        · subst i
          simp [f, h]
        · simp [f, hi]
      let e := hf.toPerm
      ⟨e.permMatrix ℂ, by
        rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff']
        change (e.permMatrix ℂ).conjTranspose * e.permMatrix ℂ = 1
        rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_permMatrix, ← Matrix.permMatrix_mul]
        simp⟩

/-- A query to `Q_P`: a circuit given by its width and its unitary blocks, each followed by a
measurement of a set of wires (Section 4). -/
structure Query where
  /-- The number of qubits. -/
  width : ℕ
  /-- The gate lists, each followed by the set of measured wires. -/
  blocks : List (List (Gate width) × Finset (Fin width))

/-- Parse a counted list of gate instructions. -/
private def Query.decodeGates (width : ℕ) :
    ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List (Gate width) × List ℕ)
  | 0, fields => some ([], fields)
  | n + 1, 0 :: wire :: 0 :: tail => do
      if h : wire < width then
        let (gs, rest) ← Query.decodeGates width n tail
        return (.single .rotation ⟨wire, h⟩ :: gs, rest)
      else none
  | n + 1, 1 :: wire :: 0 :: tail => do
      if h : wire < width then
        let (gs, rest) ← Query.decodeGates width n tail
        return (.single .phase ⟨wire, h⟩ :: gs, rest)
      else none
  | n + 1, 2 :: c :: t :: tail => do
      if hc : c < width then
        if ht : t < width then
          if hct : c ≠ t then
            let (gs, rest) ← Query.decodeGates width n tail
            return (.controlledNot ⟨c, hc⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩
              (fun h ↦ hct (congrArg Fin.val h)) :: gs, rest)
          else none
        else none
      else none
  | _, _ => none

/-- Parse a counted list of blocks, each a gate list with a set of measured wires. -/
private def Query.decodeBlocks (width : ℕ) :
    ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List (List (Gate width) × Finset (Fin width)) × List ℕ)
  | 0, fields => some ([], fields)
  | n + 1, gateCount :: fields => do
      let (gates, afterGates) ← Query.decodeGates width gateCount fields
      let count :: afterCount := afterGates | none
      if (afterCount.take count).length = count then
        let measured ← (afterCount.take count).mapM
          (fun k ↦ if h : k < width then some (⟨k, h⟩ : Fin width) else none)
        let (blocks, rest) ← Query.decodeBlocks width n (afterCount.drop count)
        return ((gates, measured.toFinset) :: blocks, rest)
      else none
  | _, _ => none

/-- The explicit finite-alphabet encoding of a query by unary fields for the width, the block
count, the gate tags and wires, and the measured wires.

Gates come from the fixed basis, so no amplitudes or succinct register descriptions occur. -/
def Query.encoding : Computability.Encoding Query (Option Bool) :=
  -- Self-delimited unary fields.
  let fieldEncoding : Computability.Encoding (List ℕ) (Option Bool) :=
    let encode : List ℕ → List (Option Bool) :=
      List.flatMap (fun n ↦ List.replicate n (some true) ++ [none])
    let step : Option Bool → Option (List ℕ) → Option (List ℕ)
      | none, rest => (List.cons 0) <$> rest
      | some true, rest => rest.bind (fun ns ↦ match ns with
          | n :: tail => some ((n + 1) :: tail)
          | _ => none)
      | some false, _ => none
    let decode : List (Option Bool) → Option (List ℕ) :=
      fun word ↦ word.foldr step (some [])
    have readPrefix (n : ℕ) (w : List (Option Bool)) :
        decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: w) =
          (List.cons n) <$> decode w := by
      induction n with
      | zero => rfl
      | succ n ih =>
        simp only [List.replicate_succ, List.cons_append]
        change step (some true)
          (decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: w)) = _
        rw [ih]
        cases decode w <;> rfl
    ⟨encode, decode, by
      intro ns
      induction ns with
      | nil => rfl
      | cons n ns ih =>
        change decode ((List.replicate n (some true) ++ [none]) ++ encode ns) = _
        rw [List.append_assoc]
        change decode (List.replicate n (some true) ++ none :: encode ns) = _
        rw [readPrefix, ih]
        rfl⟩
  let gateFields {n : ℕ} (g : Gate n) : List ℕ := match g with
    | .single .rotation wire => [0, wire.val, 0]
    | .single .phase wire => [1, wire.val, 0]
    | .controlledNot c t _ => [2, c.val, t.val]
  let blockFields {n : ℕ} (b : List (Gate n) × Finset (Fin n)) : List ℕ :=
    b.1.length :: b.1.flatMap gateFields ++
      b.2.card :: ((b.2.sort (· ≤ ·)).map Fin.val)
  let encode (q : Query) : List (Option Bool) :=
    fieldEncoding.encode (q.width :: q.blocks.length :: q.blocks.flatMap blockFields)
  let decode (word : List (Option Bool)) : Option Query := do
    let width :: count :: fields ← fieldEncoding.decode word | none
    let (blocks, rest) ← Query.decodeBlocks width count fields
    if rest = [] then return ⟨width, blocks⟩ else none
  have gates_roundtrip {n : ℕ} (gs : List (Gate n)) (rest : List ℕ) :
      Query.decodeGates n gs.length (gs.flatMap gateFields ++ rest) = some (gs, rest) := by
    induction gs with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons g gs ih =>
      cases g with
      | single kind wire =>
        cases kind <;> simp [gateFields, Query.decodeGates, wire.isLt, ih]
      | controlledNot c t different =>
        have hct : c.val ≠ t.val := fun h ↦ different (Fin.ext h)
        simp [gateFields, Query.decodeGates, c.isLt, t.isLt, hct, ih]
  have indices_roundtrip {n : ℕ} (xs : List (Fin n)) :
      (xs.map Fin.val).mapM
        (fun k ↦ if h : k < n then some (⟨k, h⟩ : Fin n) else none) = some xs := by
    induction xs with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons x xs ih => simp [x.isLt, ih]
  have blocks_roundtrip {n : ℕ} (bs : List (List (Gate n) × Finset (Fin n)))
      (rest : List ℕ) :
      Query.decodeBlocks n bs.length (bs.flatMap blockFields ++ rest) = some (bs, rest) := by
    induction bs with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons b bs ih =>
      rcases b with ⟨gs, measured⟩
      simp only [List.length_cons, List.flatMap_cons, blockFields, List.cons_append,
        List.append_assoc, Query.decodeBlocks]
      rw [gates_roundtrip]
      have hlen : ((measured.sort (· ≤ ·)).map Fin.val).length = measured.card := by simp
      simp only [← hlen, List.length_map]
      simp only [Finset.length_sort, List.length_take, inf_eq_left, Option.pure_def,
        Option.bind_eq_bind, Option.bind_some, List.length_append, hlen, List.length_flatMap,
        List.length_cons, List.length_map, List.sum_map_add, List.map_const', List.sum_replicate,
        smul_eq_mul, mul_one, le_add_iff_nonneg_right, zero_le, ↓reduceIte, List.take_left',
        indices_roundtrip, List.drop_left', Finset.sort_toFinset]
      change (Query.decodeBlocks n bs.length (bs.flatMap blockFields ++ rest)).bind _ = _
      rw [ih]
      rfl
  ⟨encode, decode, by
    rintro ⟨width, blocks⟩
    have hb := blocks_roundtrip blocks []
    simp only [List.append_nil] at hb
    simp [encode, decode, hb]⟩

/-- A pure state of a register of `width` qubits: a unit vector (Section 2.1). -/
def State (width : ℕ) : Type :=
  {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin width → Bool) // ‖ψ‖ = 1}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The computational-basis measurement of a set `S` of wires, returning the normalized
post-measurement state (Section 2.1).

Only outcomes of positive Born weight occur, so no state is chosen for zero-weight outcomes. -/
def collapse {width : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin width)) (ψ : State width) : PMF (State width) :=
  let project : (S → Bool) → EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin width → Bool) :=
    fun r ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun x ↦ if (fun i : S ↦ x i) = r then ψ.val x else 0)
  have hsum : ∑ r : S → Bool, ‖project r‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
    calc
      ∑ r : S → Bool, ‖project r‖ ^ 2 =
          ∑ r : S → Bool, ∑ x : Fin width → Bool,
            if (fun i : S ↦ x i) = r then ‖ψ.val x‖ ^ 2 else 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro r _
        simp [project, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, apply_ite]
      _ = ∑ x : Fin width → Bool, ‖ψ.val x‖ ^ 2 := by
        rw [Finset.sum_comm]
        simp
      _ = 1 := by
        rw [← EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, ψ.property]
        simp
  let outcomes : PMF (S → Bool) :=
    PMF.ofFintype (fun r ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (‖project r‖ ^ 2)) (by
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun r _ ↦ sq_nonneg ‖project r‖), hsum]
      simp)
  outcomes.bindOnSupport fun r hr ↦ PMF.pure
    ⟨(‖project r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) • project r, by
      have hp : 0 < ‖project r‖ ^ 2 := by
        have h := (outcomes.apply_pos_iff r).mpr hr
        change 0 < ENNReal.ofReal (‖project r‖ ^ 2) at h
        exact ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mp h
      have hn : ‖project r‖ ≠ 0 := by
        intro hz
        simp [hz] at hp
      rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (norm_nonneg (project r))),
        inv_mul_cancel₀ hn]⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- The non-collapsing history of a pure state under a list of unitary blocks, each followed by
a computational-basis measurement (Section 4).

Each step prepends a full-register sample without disturbing the state, and the next block acts
on the post-measurement state. -/
def qpFrom {width : ℕ}
    (blocks : List (Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin width → Bool) ℂ × Finset (Fin width)))
    (ψ : State width) : PMF (Fin (blocks.length + 1) → Fin width → Bool) :=
  let samples : PMF (Fin width → Bool) :=
    PMF.ofFintype (fun x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (‖ψ.val x‖ ^ 2)) (by
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun x _ ↦ sq_nonneg ‖ψ.val x‖),
        ← EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, ψ.property]
      simp)
  samples.bind fun sample ↦
    match blocks with
    | [] => PMF.pure (fun _ ↦ sample)
    | (U, S) :: rest =>
      let φ : State width :=
        ⟨(@Matrix.toEuclideanCLM ℂ (Fin width → Bool) _ _ _) U.val ψ.val,
          (Unitary.norm_map
            (Unitary.map (StarMonoidHom.ofClass
              (@Matrix.toEuclideanCLM ℂ (Fin width → Bool) _ _ _)) U)
            ψ.val).trans ψ.property⟩
      (collapse S φ).bind fun next ↦ (qpFrom rest next).map (Fin.cons sample)
termination_by blocks.length

/-- The oracle `Q_P` on a query: run the circuit from `|0…0⟩` and output all `T + 1`
whole-register samples, in time order and wire order (Section 4).

Within a block the first gate acts first. -/
def Query.qp (query : Query) : PMF (List Bool) :=
  let blocks := query.blocks.map fun block ↦
    (block.1.foldl (fun unitary gate ↦ gate.matrix * unitary) 1, block.2)
  (qpFrom blocks ⟨EuclideanSpace.single (fun _ ↦ false) 1, by simp⟩).map
    (fun samples ↦ (List.ofFn samples).flatMap List.ofFn)

/-- **Question 1** (Section 9, p. 15; ABFL Section 7, question 4). Every language in PDQP belongs
to PP: `PDQP ⊆ PP`.

PDQP is encoded by a polynomial-time query generator and postprocessor around one `Q_P` call
with success probability at least `2/3`, over the fixed gate basis and the explicit encoding
`Query.encoding`; PP by a polynomial-time machine with fair coins and success probability
greater than `1/2`. -/
theorem question_1 (language : Set (List Bool)) :
    let wordPair := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList Bool) (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    (∃ (generate : List Bool → Query)
        (answer : List Bool × List Bool → Bool)
        (generator : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime
          (Computability.encodingList Bool).encode Query.encoding.encode generate)
        (postprocessor : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime
          wordPair Computability.encodeBool answer),
      (∀ k, Finite (generator.tm.Γ k)) ∧
      (∀ k, Finite (postprocessor.tm.Γ k)) ∧
      ∃ resource : ℕ[X], ∀ input : List Bool,
        let query := generate input
        query.width + query.blocks.length +
            (query.blocks.map (fun block ↦ block.1.length)).sum +
            (Query.encoding.encode query).length +
            query.width * (query.blocks.length + 1) ≤ resource.eval input.length ∧
        (2 / 3 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ query.qp.toOuterMeasure
          {transcript | answer (input, transcript) = true ↔ input ∈ language}) →
    ∃ (answer : List Bool × List Bool → Bool) (coins : ℕ[X])
        (machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime
          wordPair Computability.encodeBool answer),
      (∀ k, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
      ∀ input : List Bool,
        (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) <
          (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (coins.eval input.length) → Bool)).toOuterMeasure
            {bits | answer (input, List.ofFn bits) = true ↔ input ∈ language} := by
  sorry

end Lee2013Complexity

theorem Lee2013Complexity.question_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Lee2013Complexity.question_1 := by
  sorry

title: The d-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves
problem_statement: In leitz2025d.lean, prove either Leitz2025D.conjecture_1_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Leitz2025D.conjecture_1_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The d-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves

Authors: Desmond Leitz, Ralph Morrison, Soren Newman-Taylor, and Vincent X. Wang.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU 2025](https://math.williams.edu/small/research-publications/).
Reference: D. Leitz, R. Morrison, S. Newman-Taylor, and V. X. Wang, *The d-gonal locus in the
moduli space of tropical plane curves*, arXiv:2511.20805v1 (2025), 43 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Leitz2025D

open WithLp
open Finset

/-- A two-variable min-tropical Laurent polynomial with finite support (Section 2.4). -/
abbrev TropicalPolynomial := AddMonoidAlgebra (MinTropical (WithTop ℝ)) (Fin 2 → ℤ)

/-- The Newton polygon, the convex hull of the finite exponents (Section 2.4). -/
def newtonPolygon (f : TropicalPolynomial) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  convexHull ℝ ((fun a : Fin 2 → ℤ ↦ toLp 2 fun i ↦ (a i : ℝ)) ''
    (f.coeff.support : Set (Fin 2 → ℤ)))

/-- The exponents on the lower face exposed by a point of the tropical plane (Section 2.4). -/
def lowerFace (f : TropicalPolynomial) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ) :=
  let h := fun a ↦ (MinTropical.untrop (f.coeff a)).untopD 0
  {a ∈ f.coeff.support | ∀ b ∈ f.coeff.support,
    h a + ∑ i, (a i : ℝ) * x i ≤ h b + ∑ i, (b i : ℝ) * x i}

/-- The tropical curve, the locus where at least two monomials minimize (Section 2.4). -/
def tropicalCurve (f : TropicalPolynomial) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  {x | 2 ≤ #(lowerFace f x)}

/-- Smoothness: complete lattice support and a unimodular lower triangulation (Section 2.4). -/
def IsSmooth (f : TropicalPolynomial) : Prop :=
  (interior (newtonPolygon f)).Nonempty ∧
    (∀ a : Fin 2 → ℤ, toLp 2 (fun i ↦ (a i : ℝ)) ∈ newtonPolygon f →
      a ∈ f.coeff.support) ∧
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      #(lowerFace f x) ≤ 3 ∧
      (#(lowerFace f x) = 3 → ∃ a b c : Fin 2 → ℤ,
        lowerFace f x = {a, b, c} ∧
        |(b 0 - a 0) * (c 1 - a 1) - (b 1 - a 1) * (c 0 - a 0)| = 1)

/-- The convex hull of the interior lattice points (Section 2.1). -/
def interiorPolygon (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  convexHull ℝ {x | ∃ a : Fin 2 → ℤ,
    x = toLp 2 (fun i ↦ (a i : ℝ)) ∧ x ∈ interior P}

/-- The lattice width, measured by primitive integral covectors (Section 2.1). -/
def latticeWidth (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ (u : Fin 2 → ℤ) (c : ℤ), Int.gcd (u 0) (u 1) = 1 ∧
    ∀ x ∈ P, (c : ℝ) ≤ ∑ i, (u i : ℝ) * x i ∧
      (∑ i, (u i : ℝ) * x i) ≤ (c : ℝ) + k}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The expected gonality, including the exceptional triangle `2 Upsilon` (Section 2.2). -/
def expectedGonality (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℕ :=
  let Q := interiorPolygon P
  if Q = ∅ then 1 else if interior Q = ∅ then 2 else
    if ∃ (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) (b : Fin 2 → ℤ),
      IsUnit A.det ∧
      P = (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) ↦
        toLp 2 fun i ↦ (∑ j, (A i j : ℝ) * x j) + (b i : ℝ)) ''
          convexHull ℝ ({toLp 2 ![-2, -2], toLp 2 ![2, 0], toLp 2 ![0, 2]} :
            Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    then 3 else latticeWidth Q + 2

/-- The outgoing edge germs, parametrized at primitive lattice speed (Section 2.3; Morrison,
Tropical geometry, Definition 5). -/
def outgoingDirections (Γ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : Set (Fin 2 → ℤ) :=
  {v | Int.gcd (v 0) (v 1) = 1 ∧ ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε, p + t • toLp 2 (fun i ↦ (v i : ℝ)) ∈ Γ}

/-- The divisor of a continuous function with local integral slopes along every incident edge
germ (Section 2.3; Gathmann-Kerber, Definition 1.4). -/
def IsPrincipalDivisor (Γ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    (D : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →₀ ℤ) : Prop :=
  (D.support : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) ⊆ Γ ∧
    ∃ f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ, ContinuousOn f Γ ∧
      ∀ p ∈ Γ, ∃ s : (Fin 2 → ℤ) →₀ ℤ,
        (s.support : Set (Fin 2 → ℤ)) ⊆ outgoingDirections Γ p ∧
        (∀ v ∈ outgoingDirections Γ p, ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
          ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε,
            f (p + t • toLp 2 (fun i ↦ (v i : ℝ))) = f p + t * (s v : ℝ)) ∧
        D p = s.sum (fun _ z ↦ z)

/-- The least degree of an effective positive-rank divisor on the entire metric graph
(Section 2.3). Principal divisors use lattice lengths, not vertex-only chip-firing. -/
def divisorialGonality (Γ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ d : ℕ, n = (d : ℕ∞) ∧
    ∃ D : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →₀ ℤ,
      (D.support : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) ⊆ Γ ∧
      (∀ p, 0 ≤ D p) ∧ D.sum (fun _ z ↦ z) = (d : ℤ) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ Γ, ∃ D' : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →₀ ℤ,
        (D'.support : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) ⊆ Γ ∧
        (∀ q, 0 ≤ D' q) ∧ IsPrincipalDivisor Γ (D - Finsupp.single p 1 - D')}

/-- **Conjecture 1.1**. Every smooth tropical plane curve has divisorial gonality equal to the
expected gonality of its Newton polygon.

Gonality is taken on a compact truncation retaining all finite vertices, which has the same
gonality as the skeleton, also in genus zero and one. -/
theorem conjecture_1_1 (f : TropicalPolynomial) (hf : IsSmooth f) :
    divisorialGonality (tropicalCurve f ∩ Metric.closedBall 0
        (1 + sSup {r : ℝ | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
          #(lowerFace f x) = 3 ∧ r = ‖x‖} : ℝ)) =
      (expectedGonality (newtonPolygon f) : ℕ∞) := by
  sorry

end Leitz2025D

theorem Leitz2025D.conjecture_1_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Leitz2025D.conjecture_1_1 := by
  sorry

/-!
# Modeling Random Walks to Infinity on Primes in Z[sqrt(2)]

Authors: Bencheng Li, Steven J. Miller, Tudor Popescu, Daniel Sarnecki, and
Nawapan Wattanawanichkul.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2020](https://ploynawapan.github.io/talks/2020-09-01-talk-4).

/-- **Conjecture 22** (preprint Conjecture 4.1). No bounded-step walk on primes of `ℤ[√2]` has

Primes are the irreducible elements of this UFD; no fixed start, quadrant, increasing-radius or

      (∀ n, Irreducible (w n)) ∧
      (∀ n, dist (point (w n)) (point (w (n + 1))) ≤ (k : ℝ)) ∧
      ¬Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range (fun n ↦ point (w n))) := by

end Li2022Modeling

title: Counting numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, multiplicity, and depth
problem_statement: In li2023counting.lean, prove either Li2023Counting.ratio_surmise or refute it by proving its logical negation Li2023Counting.ratio_surmise_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Counting numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, multiplicity, and depth

Author: Sean Li.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU
2022](https://sites.google.com/view/gallian-reu/additional-information/program-bibliography).
Reference: S. Li, *Counting numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, multiplicity, and depth*,
Combin. Theory **3** (2023), no. 3, Paper No. 6, 29 pp.; doi:10.5070/C63362789;
arXiv:2208.14587v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Li2023Counting

open scoped Topology

open scoped Classical in
/-- The number `Fr(f)` of numerical semigroups with Frobenius number `f`. -/
def frobeniusCount (f : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let semigroups : Set (AddSubmonoid ℕ) :=
    {S | (S : Set ℕ)ᶜ.Finite ∧ FrobeniusNumber f (S : Set ℕ)}
  have hfinite : semigroups.Finite := by
    apply Set.Finite.of_injOn (f := fun S : AddSubmonoid ℕ ↦ (S : Set ℕ)ᶜ)
      (t := (Set.Iic f).powerset)
    · intro S hS
      change (S : Set ℕ)ᶜ ⊆ Set.Iic f
      have hF : f ∉ S ∧ ∀ k > f, k ∈ S := by
        simpa only [frobeniusNumber_iff, AddSubmonoid.closure_eq] using hS.2
      intro n hn
      exact le_of_not_gt (fun h ↦ hn (hF.2 n h))
    · intro S _ T _ hST
      exact SetLike.coe_injective (compl_injective hST)
    · exact (Set.finite_Iic f).powerset
  hfinite.toFinset.card

/-- **Open question** (Section 6.1; arXiv v2, p. 20). The ratio of the
even Frobenius count to the preceding odd one converges to a value strictly less than one. -/
theorem ratio_surmise :
    ∃ L : ℝ, L < 1 ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun k : ℕ ↦ (frobeniusCount (2 * k) : ℝ) /
          (frobeniusCount (2 * k - 1) : ℝ))
        Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  sorry

end Li2023Counting

theorem Li2023Counting.ratio_surmise_neg : ¬ type_of% @Li2023Counting.ratio_surmise := by
  sorry

/-!
# Return Probabilities of Skip-Free Random Walks

Author: Andrew Lin.
Origin: [Caltech SURF 2021](https://web.stanford.edu/~lindrew/SURFreport.pdf).
Reference: A. Lin, *Return Probabilities of Skip-Free Random Walks*, SURF report, 2021.

namespace Lin2021Return

/-- **Problem 4**. For the infinite-line skip-free random walk with allowed jumps
`-1, 0, …, k - 1`, if `p_1, …, p_k ≤ 1 / (k + 1)`, then `p_{k+1}` is at most one of the first
`k` return probabilities. -/
theorem problem_4_infinite_line_skip_free_return_probability
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (a : Fin (k + 1) → ℝ)
    (ha_nonneg : ∀ j, 0 ≤ a j) (ha_sum : ∑ j, a j = 1) :

      ∑ path : Fin n → Fin (k + 1),
        if (∑ t, ((path t : ℤ) - 1)) = 0 then ∏ t, a (path t) else 0
    (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, p i ≤ 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) →
      ∃ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, p (k + 1) ≤ p m := by sorry

end Lin2021Return

title: Effect of Transaction Tax on Optimal Portfolio Liquidation and Predatory Trading
problem_statement: In lkhagvajav2014effect.lean, prove either Lkhagvajav2014Effect.smooth_tax_equilibrium_exists or refute it by proving its logical negation Lkhagvajav2014Effect.smooth_tax_equilibrium_exists_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Effect of Transaction Tax on Optimal Portfolio Liquidation and Predatory Trading

Author: Enkhjargal Lkhagvajav.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2014](https://prod.lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/math-document/reu-documents/Lkhagvajav%20REU%202014.pdf).
Reference: E. Lkhagvajav, *Effect of Transaction Tax on Optimal Portfolio Liquidation and
Predatory Trading*, University of Michigan REU report (August 1, 2014), 14 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lkhagvajav2014Effect

open MeasureTheory

/-- Deterministic admissible strategies on the liquidation interval (Section 2.1). -/
def Admissible (x T : ℝ) (X : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  X 0 = x ∧ X T = 0 ∧ AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval X 0 T ∧
    MemLp (deriv X) 2 (volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 T)) ∧
      ∃ c ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 T, |X t| ≤ c

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (abstract and Introduction). With a smooth tax, every admissible
finite-agent market has a deterministic mean-variance Nash equilibrium.

The objective uses the deterministic form (15)-(16), with the printed path and index slips of
(14)-(15) corrected to the deviating path `Y`, opponents other than `i` and risk aversion
`alpha i`; nonnegative tax and positive horizon are contextual conventions, `n = 0` is the empty
market, and `c` is the source's `λ`. -/
theorem smooth_tax_equilibrium_exists
    {n : ℕ} (x α : Fin n → ℝ) (T S₀ σ γ c μ ε : ℝ)
    (b : ℝ → ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) (hα : ∀ i, 0 ≤ α i)
    (hσ : 0 ≤ σ) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hb : ContinuousOn b (Set.Icc 0 T)) :
    let utility := fun (X : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (i : Fin n) (Y : ℝ → ℝ) ↦
      x i * S₀ - γ / 2 * (x i) ^ 2 + μ * ε * T +
        ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T,
          Y t * (b t + γ * ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, deriv (X j) t) -
            α i * σ ^ 2 / 2 * (Y t) ^ 2 -
            c * deriv Y t *
              ((∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, deriv (X j) t) + deriv Y t) -
            μ * √((deriv Y t) ^ 2 + ε ^ 2)
    ∃ X : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ,
      (∀ i, Admissible (x i) T (X i)) ∧
        ∀ (i : Fin n) (Y : ℝ → ℝ), Admissible (x i) T Y →
          utility X i Y ≤ utility X i (X i) := by
  sorry

end Lkhagvajav2014Effect

title: Short Zero-Sum Sequences Over Abelian p-Groups of Large Exponent
problem_statement: In luo2017short.lean, prove either Luo2017Short.conjecture_5_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Luo2017Short.conjecture_5_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Short Zero-Sum Sequences Over Abelian p-Groups of Large Exponent

Author: Sammy Luo.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU
2016](https://sites.google.com/view/gallian-reu/additional-information/program-bibliography).
Reference: S. Luo, *Short zero-sum sequences over abelian p-groups of large exponent*, J. Number
Theory **177** (2017), 28-36; arXiv:1608.05157v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Luo2017Short

open scoped Classical in
/-- The least positive length forcing a nonempty zero-sum subsequence (Section 1). -/
def davenportConstant (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [Finite G] : ℕ :=
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite G
  Nat.find (show ∃ d > 0,
      ∀ S : Multiset G, d ≤ S.card →
        ∃ T : Multiset G, T ≤ S ∧ 0 < T.card ∧ T.sum = 0 from by
    have hn : 0 < AddMonoid.exponent G :=
      AddMonoid.ExponentExists.of_finite.exponent_pos
    refine ⟨Fintype.card G * AddMonoid.exponent G + 1, Nat.succ_pos _, ?_⟩
    intro S hS
    have hcount : ∃ g : G, AddMonoid.exponent G ≤ S.count g := by
      by_contra h
      have hlt : ∀ g : G, S.count g < AddMonoid.exponent G := by
        intro g
        exact Nat.lt_of_not_ge (fun hg ↦ h ⟨g, hg⟩)
      have hbound : S.card ≤ Fintype.card G * AddMonoid.exponent G := by
        calc
          S.card = ∑ g : G, S.count g := by
            symm
            exact Multiset.sum_count_eq_card (fun _ _ ↦ Finset.mem_univ _)
          _ ≤ ∑ _g : G, AddMonoid.exponent G :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum (fun g _ ↦ Nat.le_of_lt (hlt g))
          _ = Fintype.card G * AddMonoid.exponent G := by simp
      exact (Nat.not_lt_of_ge hbound) (lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self _) hS)
    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hcount
    refine ⟨Multiset.replicate (AddMonoid.exponent G) g,
      Multiset.le_count_iff_replicate_le.mp hg, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa using hn
    · rw [Multiset.sum_replicate, AddMonoid.exponent_nsmul_eq_zero])

/-- **Conjecture 5.4** (arXiv v1, pp. 7-8). Every sufficiently long sequence has an
exponent-length zero-sum subsequence or a twice-exponent zero-sum block containing a zero-sum
subsequence in the specified inclusive length interval.

The bounds are rearranged to avoid truncated natural subtraction; repetitions, zero entries,
`p = 2` and the trivial-group convention `n = D = 1` are retained. -/
theorem conjecture_5_4 (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p (Multiplicative G)) :
    let n := AddMonoid.exponent G
    let D := davenportConstant G
    ∀ (hD : D + 1 ≤ 2 * n),
      ∀ ell ≥ 1, ∀ (hell_upper : ell + n ≤ D + 1)
        (S : Multiset G) (hS : D + n + ell ≤ S.card + 2),
      (∃ B : Multiset G, B ≤ S ∧ B.card = n ∧ B.sum = 0) ∨
      (∃ B : Multiset G, B ≤ S ∧ B.card = 2 * n ∧ B.sum = 0 ∧
        ∃ C : Multiset G, C ≤ B ∧ C.sum = 0 ∧
          2 * n + ell ≤ C.card + D + 1 ∧ C.card + 1 ≤ n) := by
  sorry

end Luo2017Short

theorem Luo2017Short.conjecture_5_4_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Luo2017Short.conjecture_5_4.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Numerical integration for fractal measures
problem_statement: In malmquist2018numerical.lean, prove either Malmquist2018Numerical.discrepancy_one_midpoint or refute it by proving its logical negation Malmquist2018Numerical.discrepancy_one_midpoint_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Numerical integration for fractal measures

Authors: Jens Malmquist and Robert S. Strichartz.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~jensmalmquist/).
Reference: J. Malmquist and R. S. Strichartz, *Numerical integration for fractal measures*,
J. Fractal Geom.; doi:10.4171/JFG/60; arXiv:1606.02773v3 (2018), 50 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Malmquist2018Numerical

/-- The ordered equilateral boundary vertices `q0, q1, q2`. -/
def boundary (i : Fin 3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if i = 0 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0]
  else if i = 1 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0]
  else WithLp.toLp 2 ![(1 : ℝ) / 2, √3 / 2]

/-- The contraction `F_i(x) = (x + q_i) / 2`. -/
def contraction (i : Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (x + boundary i)

/-- The cell map `F_w`, with the first letter outermost. -/
def cellMap (w : List (Fin 3)) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  w.foldr contraction x

/-- The vertex sets `V_m`. -/
def vertices : ℕ → Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  | 0 => Finset.univ.image boundary
  | m + 1 => Finset.univ.biUnion fun i ↦ (vertices m).image (contraction i)

/-- The standard gasket, the closure of all finite-level vertices. -/
def gasket : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  closure (⋃ m : ℕ, (vertices m : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))

/-- The level-`m` graph: distinct corners of the same level-`m` cell are adjacent. -/
def levelGraph (m : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ ∃ w : List (Fin 3), w.length = m ∧
    ∃ i k : Fin 3, x = cellMap w (boundary i) ∧ y = cellMap w (boundary k)
  symm := ⟨by
    rintro x y ⟨hne, w, hw, i, k, hx, hy⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, w, hw, k, i, hy, hx⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro x hx; exact hx.1 rfl⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Example 3.2** (p. 15). The Dirichlet Green potential for the three boundary vertices and
one first-level midpoint has global maximum `11 / 225`.

The potential is characterized pointwise through the full uniform graph limit away from the four
pinned points, with the standard symmetric measure and Kigami normalization. -/
theorem discrepancy_one_midpoint
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (hu : ContinuousOn u gasket)
    (hboundary : ∀ i : Fin 3, u (boundary i) = 0)
    (hpinned : u (contraction 0 (boundary 1)) = 0)
    (hpoisson : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ M,
      ∀ x ∈ vertices m, x ∉ vertices 0 → x ≠ contraction 0 (boundary 1) →
        |(3 / 2 : ℝ) * (5 : ℝ) ^ m *
          ∑ y ∈ vertices m with (levelGraph m).Adj x y, (u y - u x) + 1| < ε) :
    IsGreatest (u '' gasket) (11 / 225 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Malmquist2018Numerical

theorem Malmquist2018Numerical.discrepancy_one_midpoint_neg : ¬ type_of% @Malmquist2018Numerical.discrepancy_one_midpoint := by
  sorry

/-!
# Edge disjoint caterpillar realizations

Authors: Istvan Miklos, Geneva Schlafly, Yuheng Wang, and Zhangyang Wei.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: I. Miklos, G. Schlafly, Y. Wang, and Z. Wei, *Edge disjoint caterpillar
realizations*, Discrete Appl. Math. **289** (2021), 327-344; doi:10.1016/j.dam.2020.11.006.

namespace Miklos2021Edge

/-- A tree degree sequence: positive entries summing to `2n - 2` (Definition 1). -/
def IsTreeDegreeSequence {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, 0 < d v) ∧ (∑ v, d v) + 2 = 2 * n

open scoped Classical in
/-- A caterpillar: a tree whose non-leaf vertices induce a path (Definition 1). The two-vertex
tree has the empty backbone. -/
def IsCaterpillar {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  G.IsTree ∧
    ∃ m : ℕ, Nonempty ((G.induce {v | G.degree v ≠ 1}) ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph m)

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 1**. Every tree degree matrix with each vertex a leaf in at most one row admits
pairwise edge-disjoint caterpillar realizations of all its rows.

The distinct-row condition follows the introduction and Section 6, where Definition 2 omits
the restriction on its row indices. -/
theorem conjecture_1 {k n : ℕ} (D : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin n) ℕ)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsTreeDegreeSequence (D i))
    (hleaves : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ v, D i v = 1 → D j v ≠ 1) :
    ∃ T : Fin k → SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (∀ i, IsCaterpillar (T i)) ∧
      (∀ i v, (T i).degree v = D i v) ∧
      Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (T i).edgeSet (T j).edgeSet) := by

title: Superpolynomial period lengths of the winning positions in the subtraction game
problem_statement: In miklos2024superpolynomial.lean, prove either Miklos2024Superpolynomial.conjecture_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Miklos2024Superpolynomial.conjecture_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Superpolynomial period lengths of the winning positions in the subtraction game

Authors: István Miklós and Logan Post.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics 2022](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: I. Miklós and L. Post, *Superpolynomial period lengths of the winning positions in the
subtraction game*, Internat. J. Game Theory **53** (2024), 1275-1313;
doi:10.1007/s00182-024-00911-5; arXiv:2312.02426v1.
-/

namespace Miklos2024Superpolynomial

/-- The window transition `F` for the moves `{a, b, c}`, appending the outcome of the next
position, with `true` meaning winning (Equations (1)-(2) and Definition 3).

The printed shift coordinates of Equation (3) are read consistently with Equations (1)-(2). -/
def nextState (a b c : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hbc : b < c)
    (v : Fin c → Bool) : Fin c → Bool :=
  fun i ↦
    if h : i.val + 1 < c then v ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩
    else !(v ⟨c - a, by omega⟩ && v ⟨c - b, by omega⟩ && v ⟨0, by omega⟩)

/-- The outcome sequence of the game with seed `S` (Definition 3).

`S i` is the seed value at position `i - c`, and the outcome at `n` is the last window entry
after `n + 1` transitions. -/
def winningSequence (a b c : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hbc : b < c)
    (S : Fin c → Bool) (n : ℕ) : Bool :=
  ((nextState a b c ha hab hbc)^[n + 1] S) ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩

/-- **Conjecture 4** (Section 7, p. 35). For moves `a < b < c` with `gcd(a, b, c) = 1`, every
seed yields an eventually periodic outcome sequence with period less than `c ^ 2`.

The least period is encoded as the existence of a positive eventual period below the bound, with
no restriction on the preperiod. -/
theorem conjecture_4 (a b c : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hbc : b < c)
    (hcoprime : (a.gcd b).gcd c = 1) (S : Fin c → Bool) :
    ∃ p > 0, p < c ^ 2 ∧ ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N,
      winningSequence a b c ha hab hbc S (n + p) = winningSequence a b c ha hab hbc S n := by
  sorry

end Miklos2024Superpolynomial
