title: Smith invariants of UD and DU linear operators in differential posets
problem_statement: In miller2006smith.lean, prove either Miller2006Smith.conjecture_11 or refute it by proving its logical negation Miller2006Smith.conjecture_11_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Smith invariants of UD and DU linear operators in differential posets

Author: Alexander Miller.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2006](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: A. Miller, *Smith invariants of UD and DU linear operators in differential posets*,
REU report (2006), 13 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Miller2006Smith

/-- The two differential conditions on the cover relation (Definition 1). The graded, minimum
and local/rank-finiteness conditions are ambient assumptions. -/
def IsDifferential (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x y : P, x ≠ y →
    Nat.card {z : P // z ⋖ x ∧ z ⋖ y} =
      Nat.card {z : P // x ⋖ z ∧ y ⋖ z}) ∧
  (∀ x : P, Nat.card {y : P // x ⋖ y} =
    Nat.card {y : P // y ⋖ x} + r)

/-- The rank fiber `P_n`, with its inherited labels. -/
abbrev Rank (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] [GradeOrder ℕ P] (n : ℕ) :=
  {x : P // grade ℕ x = n}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The integral up-incidence matrix in the poset bases (Definition 2). -/
def up (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] [GradeOrder ℕ P] (n : ℕ) :
    Matrix (Rank P (n + 1)) (Rank P n) ℤ :=
  fun y x ↦ if x.val ⋖ y.val then 1 else 0

/-- **Conjecture 11**. The complete integral Smith factors of every DU operator are the products
of its successive distinct-eigenvalue layers (Definition 7).

Theorem 12 supplies the rank-difference spectrum; the rank-minus-one size is zero. -/
theorem conjecture_11 (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] [OrderBot P]
    [GradeMinOrder ℕ P] [LocallyFiniteOrder P]
    (hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ, Finite (Rank P n))
    (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hP : IsDifferential P r) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : ∀ m : ℕ, Fintype (Rank P m) := fun m ↦ @Fintype.ofFinite _ (hfinite m)
    let p : ℕ → ℕ := fun m ↦ Fintype.card (Rank P m)
    let δ : ℕ → ℤ := fun m ↦ (p m : ℤ) -
      (if m = 0 then 0 else (p (m - 1) : ℤ))
    let d : Fin (p n) → ℤ := fun j ↦
      ∏ i ∈ {i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) | ((p n - j.val : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ δ (n - i)},
        (r : ℤ) * (i + 1)
    ∃ L R : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin (p n)) ℤ,
      (L : Matrix (Fin (p n)) (Fin (p n)) ℤ) *
          Matrix.of (fun i j ↦ ((up P n).transpose * up P n)
            ((Fintype.equivFin (Rank P n)).symm i) ((Fintype.equivFin (Rank P n)).symm j)) *
        (R : Matrix (Fin (p n)) (Fin (p n)) ℤ) = Matrix.diagonal d := by
  sorry

end Miller2006Smith

  sorry

title: The Fibonacci Quilt Game
problem_statement: In miller2020fibonacci.lean, prove either Miller2020Fibonacci.conjecture_1_10_random_game_lengths_converge_to_gaussian or refute it by proving its logical negation Miller2020Fibonacci.conjecture_1_10_random_game_lengths_converge_to_gaussian_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Fibonacci Quilt Game

Authors: Steven J. Miller and Alexandra Newlon.
Origin: [Williams College SMALL REU
2019](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/sjmiller/public_html/math/talks/small2019/Fibonacci_Quilt_Game_Umass_Slides.pdf).
Reference: S. J. Miller and A. Newlon, *The Fibonacci Quilt Game*, arXiv:1909.01938, 2019.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Miller2020Fibonacci

open scoped Topology Real

section Setup

attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

/-- A game state: the finite multiset of Fibonacci Quilt terms, as the count function
`i ↦` number of copies of `q_i`. Source indices start at `1`; valid states exclude `0`. -/
abbrev GameState : Type := ℕ →₀ ℕ

/-- The elementary moves (Definition 1.7). -/
inductive MoveKind where
  | consecutive (i : ℕ) : MoveKind
  | distanceFour (i : ℕ) : MoveKind
  | duplicateToSingle (i : ℕ) : MoveKind
  | duplicateThree : MoveKind
  | duplicateFourToOneSix : MoveKind
  | duplicateFourToThreeFive : MoveKind
  | duplicateFive : MoveKind
  | duplicateSixToTwoEight : MoveKind
  | duplicateSixToThreeSeven : MoveKind
  | duplicateLarge (i : ℕ) : MoveKind
  | distanceThree (i : ℕ) : MoveKind
  | oneAndThree : MoveKind

/-- Number of copies of `q_j` consumed by a move. -/
def moveConsumes : MoveKind → ℕ → ℕ
  | MoveKind.consecutive i, j => (if j = i then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 1 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.distanceFour i, j => (if j = i then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 4 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateToSingle i, j => if j = i then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateThree, j => if j = 3 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToOneSix, j => if j = 4 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToThreeFive, j => if j = 4 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFive, j => if j = 5 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToTwoEight, j => if j = 6 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToThreeSeven, j => if j = 6 then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateLarge i, j => if j = i then 2 else 0
  | MoveKind.distanceThree i, j => (if j = i then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 3 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.oneAndThree, j => (if j = 1 then 1 else 0) + if j = 3 then 1 else 0

/-- Number of copies of `q_j` produced by a move. -/
def moveProduces : MoveKind → ℕ → ℕ
  | MoveKind.consecutive i, j =>
      if i = 1 then if j = 3 then 1 else 0
      else if 2 ≤ i then if j = i + 3 then 1 else 0
      else 0
  | MoveKind.distanceFour i, j =>
      if i = 1 then (if j = 2 then 1 else 0) + if j = 4 then 1 else 0
      else if 2 ≤ i then if j = i + 5 then 1 else 0
      else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateToSingle i, j =>
      if i = 1 then if j = 2 then 1 else 0
      else if i = 2 then if j = 4 then 1 else 0
      else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateThree, j => (if j = 2 then 1 else 0) + if j = 4 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToOneSix, j => (if j = 1 then 1 else 0) + if j = 6 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToThreeFive, j => (if j = 3 then 1 else 0) + if j = 5 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateFive, j => (if j = 1 then 1 else 0) + if j = 7 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToTwoEight, j => (if j = 2 then 1 else 0) + if j = 8 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToThreeSeven, j => (if j = 3 then 1 else 0) + if j = 7 then 1 else 0
  | MoveKind.duplicateLarge i, j =>
      if 7 ≤ i then (if j = i - 5 then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 2 then 1 else 0 else 0
  | MoveKind.distanceThree i, j =>
      if i = 1 ∨ i = 2 then if j = i + 4 then 1 else 0
      else if i = 3 then (if j = 1 then 1 else 0) + if j = 7 then 1 else 0
      else if i = 4 ∨ i = 5 then (if j = 1 then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 4 then 1 else 0
      else if i = 6 then (if j = 2 then 1 else 0) + if j = 10 then 1 else 0
      else if 7 ≤ i then (if j = i - 5 then 1 else 0) + if j = i + 4 then 1 else 0
      else 0
  | MoveKind.oneAndThree, j => if j = 4 then 1 else 0

/-- Applicability side conditions for all move kinds except the special side condition on
Rule (2a), `q_1 ∧ q_5 → q_2 ∧ q_4`. -/
def MoveKind.ApplicableExceptRuleTwoA (mv : MoveKind) : Prop :=
  match mv with
  | MoveKind.consecutive i => i = 1 ∨ 2 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.distanceFour i => 2 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.duplicateToSingle i => i = 1 ∨ i = 2
  | MoveKind.duplicateThree => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToOneSix => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToThreeFive => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFive => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToTwoEight => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToThreeSeven => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateLarge i => 7 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.distanceThree i => 1 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.oneAndThree => True

/-- A move other than Rule (2a) is legally available from `st`. -/
def HasLegalMoveExceptRuleTwoA (st : GameState) : Prop :=
  ∃ (mv : MoveKind) (next : GameState),
    st 0 = 0 ∧ MoveKind.ApplicableExceptRuleTwoA mv ∧
      (∀ j : ℕ, moveConsumes mv j ≤ st j) ∧
        (∀ j : ℕ, next j = st j - moveConsumes mv j + moveProduces mv j) ∧
          next 0 = 0

/-- Applicability side conditions for the moves, where Rule (2a), `q_1 ∧ q_5 → q_2 ∧ q_4`, may
be used only when no other move is possible (Definition 1.7). -/
def MoveKind.Applicable (mv : MoveKind) (st : GameState) : Prop :=
  match mv with
  | MoveKind.consecutive i => i = 1 ∨ 2 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.distanceFour i =>
      (i = 1 ∧ 0 < st 1 ∧ 0 < st 5 ∧ ¬HasLegalMoveExceptRuleTwoA st) ∨ 2 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.duplicateToSingle i => i = 1 ∨ i = 2
  | MoveKind.duplicateThree => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToOneSix => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFourToThreeFive => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateFive => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToTwoEight => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateSixToThreeSeven => True
  | MoveKind.duplicateLarge i => 7 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.distanceThree i => 1 ≤ i
  | MoveKind.oneAndThree => True

/-- Legal Fibonacci Quilt Game moves (Definition 1.7). -/
def LegalMove (st : GameState) (mv : MoveKind) (next : GameState) : Prop :=
  st 0 = 0 ∧ MoveKind.Applicable mv st ∧
    (∀ j : ℕ, moveConsumes mv j ≤ st j) ∧
      (∀ j : ℕ, next j = st j - moveConsumes mv j + moveProduces mv j) ∧
        next 0 = 0

/-- One recorded move in a finite Fibonacci Quilt game. -/
structure PlayedMove where
  /-- The kind of move played. -/
  kind : MoveKind
  /-- The game state after the move. -/
  stateAfter : GameState

/-- A finite play whose consecutive states are related by legal Fibonacci Quilt moves. -/
def IsLegalPlayFrom : GameState → List PlayedMove → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | st, step :: rest =>
      LegalMove st step.kind step.stateAfter ∧ IsLegalPlayFrom step.stateAfter rest

end Setup

/-- **Conjecture 1.10**. Standardized lengths of the Quilt game of Definition 1.7 converge to a
standard Gaussian under uniform legal-move choices.

The game stops when no listed move remains, without terminal-value conditioning, and Section 2.2
supplies the moment normalization. The literal rules are kept although Rule (3f),
`2q6 → q3 + q7`, changes value 14 to 12, contrary to the source's conservation description. -/
theorem conjecture_1_10_random_game_lengths_converge_to_gaussian
    (μ : ℕ → List PlayedMove → ℝ)
    (hlaw : ∀ N : ℕ,
      (∀ play, 0 ≤ μ N play) ∧
      (∀ play, μ N play ≠ 0 →
        IsLegalPlayFrom (Finsupp.single 1 N) play ∧
          ¬∃ mv next,
            LegalMove ((play.map PlayedMove.stateAfter).getLastD (Finsupp.single 1 N)) mv next) ∧
      (Function.support (μ N)).Finite ∧
      (∑' play, μ N play) = 1 ∧
      (∀ pref : List PlayedMove,
        IsLegalPlayFrom (Finsupp.single 1 N) pref →
        let st := (pref.map PlayedMove.stateAfter).getLastD (Finsupp.single 1 N)
        (∃ mv next, LegalMove st mv next) →
        ∃ choices : Finset (MoveKind × GameState),
          (∀ choice, choice ∈ choices ↔ LegalMove st choice.1 choice.2) ∧
          choices.Nonempty ∧
          ∀ choice₁ ∈ choices, ∀ choice₂ ∈ choices,
            (∑' tail : List PlayedMove,
              μ N (pref ++
                ({ kind := choice₁.1, stateAfter := choice₁.2 } : PlayedMove) :: tail)) =
            (∑' tail : List PlayedMove,
              μ N (pref ++
                ({ kind := choice₂.1, stateAfter := choice₂.2 } : PlayedMove) :: tail)))) :
    let mean : ℕ → ℝ := fun N ↦ ∑' play, μ N play * (play.length : ℝ)
    let variance : ℕ → ℝ := fun N ↦
      ∑' play, μ N play * ((play.length : ℝ) - mean N) ^ 2
    ∀ a b : ℝ, a < b →
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ ↦ ∑' play : List PlayedMove,
          if a ≤ ((play.length : ℝ) - mean N) / √(variance N) ∧
              ((play.length : ℝ) - mean N) / √(variance N) ≤ b then
            μ N play
          else 0)
        Filter.atTop
        (𝓝 (∫ x in a..b, (√(2 * π))⁻¹ * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2) / 2))) := by
  sorry

end Miller2020Fibonacci

/-!
# Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences

Authors: Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar,
Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, and the Polymath REU Walking to Infinity Group.
Origin: Polymath Jr. 2020.
Reference: S. J. Miller, F. Peng, T. Popescu, J. M. Siktar, N. Wattanawanichkul, and the
Polymath REU Walking to Infinity Group, *Walking to infinity along some number theory
sequences*, arXiv:2010.14932.
-/

namespace Miller2020Walking

/-- A single right-append step in base `b`, appending a block of exactly `d` digits.
The appended block may have leading zeroes, so its value is some `r < b ^ d`. -/
def IsRightDigitAppend (b : ℕ) (d : ℕ) (n m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < d ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, r < b ^ d ∧ m = n * b ^ d + r

/-- A walk to infinity along primes in base `b`, appending between one and `maxDigits` digits
at each step. `StrictMono w` is implied by the positive append lengths and prime terms. -/
def IsInfinitePrimeWalk (b maxDigits : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  1 < b ∧ 0 < maxDigits ∧ StrictMono w ∧ (∀ i, Nat.Prime (w i)) ∧
    ∀ i, ∃ d > 0, d ≤ maxDigits ∧ IsRightDigitAppend b d (w i) (w (i + 1))

/-- **Conjecture from the conclusion**. There is no walk to infinity along the primes by
appending one digit at a time to the right in base ten. -/
theorem conjecture_no_base_ten_one_digit_prime_walk :
    ¬∃ w : ℕ → ℕ, IsInfinitePrimeWalk 10 1 w := by
  sorry

end Miller2020Walking

/-!
# Congruences of Concave Composition Functions

Authors: Keenan Monks and Lynnelle Ye.
Origin: [Emory University REU in Number Theory
2012](https://uva.theopenscholar.com/ken-ono/reus-archive-2012).
Reference: K. Monks and L. Ye, *Congruences of concave composition functions*, INTEGERS **13**
(2013), A61.
-/

namespace Monks2014Congruences

open Finset

/-- Concave compositions of odd length of type 1 of `n`:
`a₁ + ... + aₘ₊₁ + b₁ + ... + bₘ`, with
`a₁ > ... > aₘ₊₁ < bₘ < ... < b₁` and `aₘ₊₁ ≥ 0`. For `m = 0` the right list is empty, so
`([0], [])` contributes the constant term. -/
def concaveOdd1 (n : ℕ) : Set (List ℕ × List ℕ) :=
  {ab |
    ab.1.length = ab.2.length + 1 ∧
    ab.1.IsChain (· > ·) ∧
    ab.2.IsChain (· > ·) ∧
    ((∃ x : ℕ, ab.1.getLast? = some x ∧ ab.2 = []) ∨
      ∃ x y : ℕ, ab.1.getLast? = some x ∧ ab.2.getLast? = some y ∧ x < y) ∧
    ab.1.sum + ab.2.sum = n}

open scoped Classical in
/-- `co₁(n)`, the number of odd type-1 concave compositions of `n`. -/
noncomputable def co1 (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let lists := (Finset.range (n + 1)).powerset.image (fun s ↦ s.sort (· ≥ ·));
  #{ab ∈ lists.product lists | ab ∈ concaveOdd1 n}

/-- The strict-endpoint count `E_f(r,a;X)`. The natural ceiling gives exactly the indices below
the real endpoint, including when `X ≤ 0`. -/
noncomputable def E (f : ℕ → ℕ) (r a : ℕ) (X : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  #{n ∈ Finset.range ⌈X⌉₊ | f n % a = r}

open Filter Asymptotics

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Theorem 1.2, displayed type-1 statement). The residue counts
of odd type-1 concave compositions have uniform linear asymptotics except for odd residues
modulo an even modulus, which have square-root asymptotics. -/
theorem conjecture (a r : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hr : r < a) :
    (Odd a → (fun X : ℝ ↦ (E co1 r a X : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun X : ℝ ↦ X / a)) ∧
    (Even a → Even r → (fun X : ℝ ↦ (E co1 r a X : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun X : ℝ ↦ 2 * X / a)) ∧
    (Even a → Odd r → (fun X : ℝ ↦ (E co1 r a X : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun X : ℝ ↦ 2 * √(2 * X) / a)) := by
  sorry

end Monks2014Congruences

  sorry

title: Polychromatic Ramsey Properties of Ideals
problem_statement: In nan2021polychromatic.lean, prove either Nan2021Polychromatic.conjecture_4_2 or refute it by proving its logical negation Nan2021Polychromatic.conjecture_4_2_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Polychromatic Ramsey Properties of Ideals

Author: Jonah Nan.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2021](https://lsa.umich.edu/math/undergraduates/research-and-career-opportunities/research/research-experience-for-undergraduates--reu%2D/recent-reu-projects.html).
Reference: J. Nan, *Polychromatic Ramsey properties of ideals*, Michigan REU report
(August 2021), 21 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Nan2021Polychromatic

open Finset

/-- The type coloring: the least coordinate where an unordered pair differs (Definition 2.1). -/
def typeColor (m : ℕ) (e : {e : Sym2 (Fin m → ℕ) // ¬e.IsDiag}) : Fin m :=
  let t : Sym2 (Fin m → ℕ) → WithTop (Fin m) :=
    Sym2.lift ⟨fun x y ↦ ({i | x i ≠ y i} : Finset (Fin m)).min,
      fun x y ↦ by simp only [ne_comm]⟩
  (t e.val).untop <| by
    rcases e with ⟨e, he⟩
    induction e using Sym2.inductionOn with
    | hf x y =>
      change ({i | x i ≠ y i} : Finset (Fin m)).min ≠ ⊤
      intro h
      have hempty := Finset.min_eq_top.mp h
      apply he
      apply funext
      intro i
      by_contra hne
      have hi : i ∈ ({j | x j ≠ y j} : Finset (Fin m)) := by simp [hne]
      rw [hempty] at hi
      exact Finset.notMem_empty i hi

/-- The colors on unordered pairs from a set use at most `n` values (Definition 1.2). -/
def NChromatic {V C : Type*} (c : {e : Sym2 V // ¬e.IsDiag} → C)
    (n : ℕ) (A : Set V) : Prop :=
  ∃ colors : Finset C, #colors ≤ n ∧
    ∀ e, e.val ∈ A.sym2 → c e ∈ colors

/-- The ideal generated by the `n`-chromatic sets of the type coloring (Definition 2.2). -/
def edIdeal (m n : ℕ) : Order.Ideal (Set (Fin m → ℕ)) :=
  sInf {I | ∀ A, NChromatic (typeColor m) n A → A ∈ I}

/-- **Conjecture 4.2**. Every positive input contains a positive subset using at most `n + 1`
colors under any finite pair-coloring.

The natural-number domain retains `n = 0`, where Definition 2.2 gives the finite-set ideal; no
tallness or wedge assumption is imposed. -/
theorem conjecture_4_2 {m : ℕ} (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (hnm : n < m)
    (c : {e : Sym2 (Fin m → ℕ) // ¬e.IsDiag} → Fin k)
    (B : Set (Fin m → ℕ)) (hB : B ∉ edIdeal m n) :
    ∃ A : Set (Fin m → ℕ), A ⊆ B ∧ A ∉ edIdeal m n ∧
      NChromatic c (n + 1) A := by
  sorry

end Nan2021Polychromatic

theorem Nan2021Polychromatic.conjecture_4_2_neg : ¬ type_of% @Nan2021Polychromatic.conjecture_4_2 := by
  sorry

title: Circular Trace Reconstruction
problem_statement: In narayanan2020circular.lean, prove either Narayanan2020Circular.open_problem_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Narayanan2020Circular.open_problem_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Circular Trace Reconstruction

Authors: Shyam Narayanan and Michael Ren.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU
2020](https://sites.google.com/view/gallian-reu/additional-information/program-bibliography).
Reference: S. Narayanan and M. Ren, *Circular Trace Reconstruction*, in ITCS 2021, LIPIcs
**185** (2021), 18:1-18:18; arXiv:2009.01346v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Narayanan2020Circular

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- **Open problem 3** (Section 6, arXiv v2 p. 16). Average-case circular trace reconstruction
succeeds with probability tending to one from a subpolynomial number of traces.

The uniformly random word is uniformly rotated, and each trace rotates it uniformly before
independent deletions with probability `q`; the rule is a deterministic function of the trace
tuple, and success means recovering the word up to rotation. -/
theorem open_problem_3 (q : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hq₁ : q < 1) :
    ∃ (T : ℕ → ℕ)
      (D : (n : ℕ) → List.Vector {trace : List Bool // trace.length ≤ n + 1} (T n) →
        Fin (n + 1) → Bool),
      (∀ n, 0 < T n) ∧
      (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, (T n : ℝ) ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ε) ∧
      Tendsto
        (fun n ↦
          let experiment : PMF ((Fin (n + 1) → Bool) × (Fin (n + 1) → Bool)) :=
            (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1) → Bool)).bind fun bits ↦
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1))).bind fun initialRotation ↦
                let x : Fin (n + 1) → Bool := fun i ↦ bits (finCycle initialRotation i)
                let traceLaw : PMF {trace : List Bool // trace.length ≤ n + 1} :=
                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1))).bind fun rotation ↦
                    PMF.map (fun deleted : List.Vector Bool (n + 1) ↦
                      Subtype.mk
                        (((List.finRange (n + 1)).filter fun i ↦ !deleted.get i).map
                          fun i ↦ x (finCycle rotation i))
                        (by
                          simp only [List.length_map]
                          exact (List.length_filter_le _ _).trans_eq List.length_finRange))
                      (List.Vector.mOfFn fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦
                        (ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure true false
                          ⟨q, hq.le, hq₁.le⟩).toPMF)
                PMF.map (fun traces ↦ (x, D n traces))
                  (List.Vector.mOfFn fun _ : Fin (T n) ↦ traceLaw)
          (experiment.toOuterMeasure
            {result | List.IsRotated (List.ofFn result.2) (List.ofFn result.1)}).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Narayanan2020Circular

  sorry

title: Calculus on the Sierpinski gasket I: polynomials, exponentials and power series
problem_statement: In needleman2004calculus.lean, prove either Needleman2004Calculus.monomial_positive_away_from_q0 or refute it by proving its logical negation Needleman2004Calculus.monomial_positive_away_from_q0_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Calculus on the Sierpinski gasket I: polynomials, exponentials and power series

Authors: Jonathan Needleman, Robert S. Strichartz, Alexander Teplyaev, and Po-Lam Yung.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU
2002](https://math.cornell.edu/history-reu-and-spur-programs-department-mathematics).
Reference: J. Needleman, R. S. Strichartz, A. Teplyaev, and P.-L. Yung, *Calculus on the
Sierpinski gasket I: polynomials, exponentials and power series*, J. Funct. Anal. **215**
(2004), 290-340; arXiv:math/0312027.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Needleman2004Calculus

open scoped Topology

/-- The ordered equilateral boundary vertices `q0, q1, q2`. -/
def boundary (i : Fin 3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if i = 0 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0]
  else if i = 1 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0]
  else WithLp.toLp 2 ![(1 : ℝ) / 2, √3 / 2]

/-- The contraction `F_i(x) = (x + q_i) / 2`. -/
def contraction (i : Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (x + boundary i)

/-- The cell map `F_w`, with the first letter outermost. -/
def cellMap (w : List (Fin 3)) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  w.foldr contraction x

/-- The vertex sets `V_m`. -/
def vertices : ℕ → Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  | 0 => Finset.univ.image boundary
  | m + 1 => Finset.univ.biUnion fun i ↦ (vertices m).image (contraction i)

/-- The standard gasket, the closure of all finite-level vertices. -/
def gasket : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  closure (⋃ m : ℕ, (vertices m : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))

/-- The level-`m` graph: distinct corners of the same level-`m` cell are adjacent. -/
def levelGraph (m : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ ∃ w : List (Fin 3), w.length = m ∧
    ∃ i k : Fin 3, x = cellMap w (boundary i) ∧ y = cellMap w (boundary k)
  symm := ⟨by
    rintro x y ⟨hne, w, hw, i, k, hx, hy⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, w, hw, k, i, hy, hx⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro x hx; exact hx.1 rfl⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- The graph Laplacian over finite-level neighbors (1.1). -/
def graphLaplacian (m : ℕ) (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ y ∈ vertices m with (levelGraph m).Adj x y, (u y - u x)

/-- The Kigami Laplacian relation, as a uniform limit of graph Laplacians (1.2). -/
def HasLaplacian (u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u gasket ∧ ContinuousOn v gasket ∧
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ M,
      ∀ x ∈ vertices m, x ∉ vertices 0 →
        |(3 / 2 : ℝ) * (5 : ℝ) ^ m * graphLaplacian m u x - v x| < ε

/-- **Conjecture 2.10** ((2.36), p. 22). Every first-family monomial based at `q0` is strictly
positive at every other gasket point.

Monomials are characterized as in Definition 2.1 by the Laplacian tower and boundary jets. -/
theorem monomial_positive_away_from_q0 {j : ℕ}
    (u : Fin (j + 2) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (hlap : ∀ r : Fin (j + 1), HasLaplacian (u r.castSucc) (u r.succ))
    (hzero : ∀ x ∈ gasket, u (Fin.last (j + 1)) x = 0)
    (hjets : ∀ r : Fin (j + 1),
      u r.castSucc (boundary 0) = (if r.val = j then 1 else 0) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (5 / 3 : ℝ) ^ m *
        (2 * u r.castSucc (boundary 0) -
          u r.castSucc ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 1)) -
          u r.castSucc ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 2))))
        Filter.atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (5 : ℝ) ^ m *
        (u r.castSucc ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 1)) -
          u r.castSucc ((contraction 0)^[m] (boundary 2))))
        Filter.atTop (𝓝 0))
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (hx : x ∈ gasket) (hx₀ : x ≠ boundary 0) :
    0 < u ⟨0, by omega⟩ x := by sorry

end Needleman2004Calculus

  sorry

title: Sampling on the Sierpinski Gasket
problem_statement: In oberlin2003sampling.lean, prove either Oberlin2003Sampling.sampling_exponential_decay or refute it by proving its logical negation Oberlin2003Sampling.sampling_exponential_decay_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Sampling on the Sierpinski Gasket

Authors: Richard Oberlin, Brian Street, and Robert S. Strichartz.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU](https://math.cornell.edu/history-reu-and-spur-programs-department-mathematics).
Reference: R. Oberlin, B. Street, and R. S. Strichartz, *Sampling on the Sierpinski Gasket*,
Experiment. Math. **12** (2003), no. 4, 403-418; doi:10.1080/10586458.2003.10504509.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Oberlin2003Sampling

open Finset

/-- The ordered equilateral boundary vertices `q0, q1, q2`. -/
def boundary (i : Fin 3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if i = 0 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0]
  else if i = 1 then WithLp.toLp 2 ![1, 0]
  else WithLp.toLp 2 ![(1 : ℝ) / 2, √3 / 2]

/-- The contraction `F_i(x) = (x + q_i) / 2`. -/
def contraction (i : Fin 3) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (x + boundary i)

/-- The cell map `F_w`, with the first letter outermost. -/
def cellMap (w : List (Fin 3)) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  w.foldr contraction x

/-- The vertex sets `V_m`. -/
def vertices : ℕ → Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  | 0 => Finset.univ.image boundary
  | m + 1 => Finset.univ.biUnion fun i ↦ (vertices m).image (contraction i)

/-- The standard gasket, the closure of all finite-level vertices. -/
def gasket : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  closure (⋃ m : ℕ, (vertices m : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))

/-- The level-`m` graph: distinct corners of the same level-`m` cell are adjacent. -/
def levelGraph (m : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ ∃ w : List (Fin 3), w.length = m ∧
    ∃ i k : Fin 3, x = cellMap w (boundary i) ∧ y = cellMap w (boundary k)
  symm := ⟨by
    rintro x y ⟨hne, w, hw, i, k, hx, hy⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, w, hw, k, i, hy, hx⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro x hx; exact hx.1 rfl⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- The graph Laplacian over finite-level neighbors (1-11). -/
def graphLaplacian (m : ℕ) (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ y ∈ vertices m with (levelGraph m).Adj x y, (u y - u x)

/-- The Kigami Laplacian relation, as a uniform limit of graph Laplacians (1-10). -/
def HasLaplacian (u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u gasket ∧ ContinuousOn v gasket ∧
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ M,
      ∀ x ∈ vertices m, x ∉ vertices 0 →
        |(3 / 2 : ℝ) * (5 : ℝ) ^ m * graphLaplacian m u x - v x| < ε

/-- The Dirichlet eigenspace `E_λ` for `-Δ`. Functions are extended by zero outside `SG`. -/
def dirichletEigenspace (μ : ℝ) :
    Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) :=
  Submodule.span ℝ {u | HasLaplacian u (fun x ↦ -μ * u x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ vertices 0, u x = 0) ∧ (∀ x ∉ gasket, u x = 0)}

/-- The space `B_m` of the lowest `card (V_m \ V_0)` Dirichlet eigenfunctions. Eigenspace
multiplicities are counted through cardinal rank. -/
def bandlimited (m : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ) :=
  Submodule.span ℝ {u | ∃ μ > (0 : ℝ),
    u ∈ dirichletEigenspace μ ∧
    Module.rank ℝ ((⨆ t : {a : ℝ // 0 < a ∧ a ≤ μ},
      dirichletEigenspace t.val) :
        Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)) ≤
      (#(vertices m \ vertices 0) : Cardinal)}

/-- The level-`m` cells, adjacent exactly when two distinct closed cells meet. -/
def cellGraph (m : ℕ) : SimpleGraph {w : List (Fin 3) // w.length = m} where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧
    ((cellMap v.val '' gasket) ∩ (cellMap w.val '' gasket)).Nonempty
  symm := ⟨by
    rintro v w ⟨hne, x, hv, hw⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, x, hw, hv⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro w hw; exact hw.1 rfl⟩

/-- `d_m(x,y)`, the least number of level-`m` cells in a chain joining the points. -/
def cellDistance (m : ℕ) (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ v w : {w : List (Fin 3) // w.length = m},
    x ∈ cellMap v.val '' gasket ∧ y ∈ cellMap w.val '' gasket ∧
    ∃ p : (cellGraph m).Walk v w, n = p.length + 1}

/-- **Conjecture 3.1** ((3-1), p. 409). The canonical Dirichlet sampling functions have a
uniform exponential bound in level-cell distance.

Positive decay constants are the contextual convention; the spectral cutoff follows p. 406,
correcting p. 405's dimension typo, and the sampling function is characterized existentially,
being unique by the source's interpolation result. -/
theorem sampling_exponential_decay :
    ∃ c α : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧
      ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ y ∈ vertices m, y ∉ vertices 0 →
        ∃ ψ ∈ bandlimited m,
          (∀ z ∈ vertices m, z ∉ vertices 0 →
            ψ z = if z = y then 1 else 0) ∧
          ∀ x ∈ gasket, |ψ x| ≤ c * α ^ cellDistance m x y := by sorry

end Oberlin2003Sampling

title: On Optimal Point Sets Determining Distinct Triangles

/-!
# On Optimal Point Sets Determining Distinct Triangles

Authors: Eyvindur A. Palsson and Edward Yu.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2023](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu).
Reference: E. A. Palsson and E. Yu, *On Optimal Point Sets Determining Distinct Triangles*,
arXiv:2308.13107.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Palsson2024Optimal

open Finset
open scoped Real

/-- The Euclidean plane, with the Euclidean norm. -/
abbrev Point2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- The distinct-triangle count: unordered side-length multisets of triples of distinct points,
including collinear triples (Introduction). Squared distances are used, which identifies the
same congruence classes. -/
def distinctTriangleCount (P : Finset Point2) : ℕ :=
  #({abc ∈ (P.product P).product P |
      abc.1.1 ≠ abc.1.2 ∧ abc.1.1 ≠ abc.2 ∧ abc.1.2 ≠ abc.2}.image fun abc ↦
    ([(dist abc.1.1 abc.1.2 ^ 2), (dist abc.1.1 abc.2 ^ 2),
      (dist abc.1.2 abc.2 ^ 2)] : Multiset ℝ))

/-- The regular polygon, realized on the Euclidean unit circle. -/
def regularPolygon (n : ℕ) : Finset Point2 :=
  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin n ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 ![Real.cos (2 * π * (j : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)),
      Real.sin (2 * π * (j : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))]

/-- **Conjecture 4.1** (Section 4). The maximum number of points in the plane spanning four
distinct triangles is seven, achieved only by the regular heptagon. -/
theorem conjecture_4_1 :
    (#(regularPolygon 7) = 7 ∧ distinctTriangleCount (regularPolygon 7) = 4) ∧
      ∀ P : Finset Point2, distinctTriangleCount P = 4 →
        #P ≤ 7 ∧ (#P = 7 →
          (∃ scale > (0 : ℝ), ∃ e : Point2 ≃ᵢ Point2,
            (regularPolygon 7).image (fun p ↦ e (scale • p)) = P)) := by
  sorry

end Palsson2024Optimal

  sorry

title: An intermediate case of exponential multivalued forbidden matrix configurations
problem_statement: In peaslee2026intermediate.lean, prove either Peaslee2026Intermediate.conjecture_6_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Peaslee2026Intermediate.conjecture_6_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# An intermediate case of exponential multivalued forbidden matrix configurations

Authors: Wallace Peaslee, Attila Sali, and Jun Yan.
Origin: [Budapest Semesters in Mathematics 2020](https://www.bsmath.hu/articles.html).
Reference: W. Peaslee, A. Sali, and J. Yan, *An intermediate case of exponential multivalued
forbidden matrix configurations*, Art Discrete Appl. Math. (2026), accepted manuscript;
doi:10.26493/2590-9770.1898.8b5; arXiv:2312.11446 (2023).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Peaslee2026Intermediate

open Filter
open scoped Topology
open Finset

/-- The choices of a triangular choice multigraph on `V`: each unordered triple chooses one of
its three pairs (Definition 1.3). Values off triples are ignored, and distinct triples may
choose the same pair. -/
def IsTriangularChoice {m : ℕ} (V : Finset (Fin m))
    (choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∀ t ∈ V.powersetCard 3, choose t ∈ t.powersetCard 2

/-- Recursive realizations of a TCM by splitting into two nonempty parts, where every mixed
triple chooses the pair in its two-vertex part (Definition 1.3). -/
inductive IsTwoRecursive {m : ℕ} (choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m)) :
    Finset (Fin m) → Prop
  | base {V : Finset (Fin m)} (hV : #V = 1 ∨ #V = 2) :
      IsTwoRecursive choose V
  | split {V₁ V₂ : Finset (Fin m)}
      (h₁ : V₁.Nonempty) (h₂ : V₂.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint V₁ V₂)
      (hcard : 3 ≤ #(V₁ ∪ V₂))
      (r₁ : IsTwoRecursive choose V₁) (r₂ : IsTwoRecursive choose V₂)
      (mixed : ∀ t ∈ (V₁ ∪ V₂).powersetCard 3, ¬t ⊆ V₁ → ¬t ⊆ V₂ →
        choose t = if #(t ∩ V₁) = 2 then t ∩ V₁ else t ∩ V₂) :
      IsTwoRecursive choose (V₁ ∪ V₂)

/-- The number `m_G(e)` of triples that choose the unordered pair `e` (Question 1.4). -/
def multiplicity {m : ℕ} (V : Finset (Fin m))
    (choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m)) (e : Finset (Fin m)) : ℕ :=
  #{t ∈ V.powersetCard 3 | choose t = e}

/-- The weight `w(G, α)`, a sum over all unordered pairs (Question 1.4). Pairs of multiplicity
zero are included and contribute `α ^ 0 = 1`. -/
def weight {m : ℕ} (V : Finset (Fin m))
    (choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m)) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ V.powersetCard 2, α ^ multiplicity V choose e

/-- The maximum weight `H(m, α)` over all TCM realizations on `m` vertices (Question 1.4).
The set of choices is finite, so the supremum is a maximum. -/
def H (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {w : ℝ | ∃ choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m),
    IsTriangularChoice Finset.univ choose ∧ weight Finset.univ choose α = w}

/-- The maximum weight `H₂(m, α)` over recursively realized TCMs (Question 1.4). -/
def H₂ (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {w : ℝ | ∃ choose : Finset (Fin m) → Finset (Fin m),
    IsTriangularChoice Finset.univ choose ∧ IsTwoRecursive choose Finset.univ ∧
      weight Finset.univ choose α = w}

/-- The series `λ(α)` (before Theorem 1.8; Section 5.1). The source index `j ≥ 1` is shifted
to `j + 1`. -/
def lambda (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' j : ℕ, (2 : ℝ) ^ j / α ^ (2 ^ (j + 1))

/-- **Conjecture 6.3**. For every `α ≥ 2`, all TCMs and 2-recursive TCMs have the same maximum
weight for every `m ≥ 3`, and both normalized maxima converge to `λ(α)`.

The recursive class is that of Definition 1.3, not the exceptional-split formula of
Theorem 6.2. -/
theorem conjecture_6_3 (α : ℝ) (hα : 2 ≤ α) :
    (∀ m ≥ 3, H m α = H₂ m α) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ 2 * H m α / ((m : ℝ) * α ^ m)) atTop (𝓝 (lambda α)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ 2 * H₂ m α / ((m : ℝ) * α ^ m)) atTop (𝓝 (lambda α)) := by
  sorry

end Peaslee2026Intermediate

theorem Peaslee2026Intermediate.conjecture_6_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Peaslee2026Intermediate.conjecture_6_3 := by
  sorry

/-!
# Counting Shellings of Complete Bipartite Graphs and Trees

Author: Junyao Peng.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2018](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: J. Peng, *Counting shellings of complete bipartite graphs and trees*, MIT SPUR final
paper, August 1, 2018.

namespace Peng2021Counting

/-- The number of edge orderings in which each edge after the first meets an earlier edge
(Definitions 1.2-1.3). -/
noncomputable def shellingNumber {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {s : Fin (Nat.card G.edgeSet) ≃ G.edgeSet //
    ∀ i, 0 < i.val → ∃ j, j < i ∧ ∃ v ∈ (s i).val, v ∈ (s j).val}

/-- The complete tree, in which the root has `k` children and other nonleaves have `k - 1`
children (Conjecture 4.1, Figure 7). Vertices carry breadth-first labels. -/
def completeTree (k m : ℕ) :
    SimpleGraph (Fin ((k * (k - 1) ^ m - 2) / (k - 2))) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b ↦ b.val ≠ 0 ∧ a.val = (b.val - 2) / (k - 1)

/-- **Conjecture 4.1** (pp. 20-21). The complete depth-`m` tree maximizes the shelling number
among trees of the specified order and maximum degree at most `k`. -/
theorem conjecture_4_1 (k m : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hm : 0 < m)
    (T : SimpleGraph (Fin ((k * (k - 1) ^ m - 2) / (k - 2))))
    (hT : T.IsTree) (hdegree : ∀ v, (T.neighborSet v).ncard ≤ k) :
    shellingNumber T ≤ shellingNumber (completeTree k m) := by
  sorry

end Peng2021Counting

title: Toward Fair and Strategyproof Tournament Rules for Tournaments with Partially Transferable Utilities
problem_statement: In pennock2025toward.lean, prove either Pennock2025Toward.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Pennock2025Toward.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Toward Fair and Strategyproof Tournament Rules for Tournaments with Partially Transferable Utilities

Authors: David Pennock, Ariel Schvartzman, and Eric Xue.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2021](https://archive.reu.dimacs.rutgers.edu/2021/ex20/public_html/).
Reference: D. Pennock, A. Schvartzman, and E. Xue, *Toward fair and strategyproof tournament
rules for tournaments with partially transferable utilities*, arXiv:2408.10346v1 (2024), 25 pp.
-/

namespace Pennock2025Toward

/-- A tournament: a complete asymmetric digraph (Definition 1). An edge points from winner to
loser. -/
def Tournament (n : ℕ) :=
  { G : Digraph (Fin n) //
    (∀ i j, G.Adj i j → ¬G.Adj j i) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → G.Adj i j ∨ G.Adj j i) }

/-- A tournament rule: randomized winner-selection rules, one for each positive size
(Definition 2). -/
abbrev TournamentRule :=
  (n : PNat) → Tournament (n : ℕ) → PMF (Fin (n : ℕ))

/-- `S`-adjacency: only matches with both endpoints in the coalition change (Definition 7). -/
def SAdjacent {n : ℕ} (S : Set (Fin n)) (T T' : Tournament n) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b, a ≠ b → ¬(a ∈ S ∧ b ∈ S) →
    (T.val.Adj a b ↔ T'.val.Adj a b)

/-- **Conjecture 1**. A monotone, Condorcet-consistent, 2-NM_1 rule exists for every positive
size.

Adjacency follows the mutual-match reading of Definition 7's prose rather than its inconsistent
displayed complement condition; probability differences are taken in the reals, and no anonymity
condition is imposed. -/
theorem conjecture_1 :
    ∃ r : TournamentRule,
      (∀ (n : PNat) (T T' : Tournament (n : ℕ)) (i j : Fin (n : ℕ))
          (_ : i ≠ j) (_ : T ≠ T')
          (_ : SAdjacent {i, j} T T') (_ : T.val.Adj i j),
          (r n T' i).toReal ≤ (r n T i).toReal) ∧
      (∀ (n : PNat) (T : Tournament (n : ℕ)) (i : Fin (n : ℕ))
          (_ : ∀ j : Fin (n : ℕ), j ≠ i → T.val.Adj i j),
          r n T i = 1) ∧
      (∀ (n : PNat) (T T' : Tournament (n : ℕ)) (i j : Fin (n : ℕ))
          (_ : i ≠ j) (_ : T ≠ T') (_ : SAdjacent {i, j} T T'),
          (r n T' i).toReal + (r n T' j).toReal ≤
            (r n T i).toReal + (r n T j).toReal +
              max ((r n T i).toReal - (r n T' i).toReal)
                ((r n T j).toReal - (r n T' j).toReal)) := by
  sorry

end Pennock2025Toward

theorem Pennock2025Toward.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Pennock2025Toward.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

title: Simple reductions to circuit minimization: DIMACS REU Report
problem_statement: In ramesh2021simple.lean, prove either Ramesh2021Simple.conjecture_3_6 or refute it by proving its logical negation Ramesh2021Simple.conjecture_3_6_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Simple reductions to circuit minimization: DIMACS REU Report

Authors: Vishal Ramesh, Sasha Sami, and Noah Singer.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2021](https://archive.reu.dimacs.rutgers.edu/2021/vr342/public_html/).
Reference: V. Ramesh, S. Sami, and N. Singer, *Simple reductions to circuit minimization: DIMACS
REU Report* (July 2021), 10 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Ramesh2021Simple

/-- An internal De Morgan gate, whose predecessors are variables, free constants or earlier
internal gates. -/
inductive Gate (m previous : ℕ)
  | neg : ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin previous) → Gate m previous
  | conj : ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin previous) →
      ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin previous) → Gate m previous
  | disj : ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin previous) →
      ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin previous) → Gate m previous

/-- A finite acyclic single-output circuit, counting only its internal gates. -/
structure Circuit (m : ℕ) where
  /-- The number of internal gates. -/
  gates : ℕ
  /-- Each gate, whose inputs are variables, constants or earlier gates. -/
  gate : (i : Fin gates) → Gate m i.val
  /-- The output: a variable, a Boolean constant or a gate. -/
  output : (Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin gates

/-- The value of an internal gate, recursively evaluating its earlier predecessors. -/
def Circuit.gateValue {m : ℕ} (C : Circuit m) (x : Fin m → Bool)
    (i : Fin C.gates) : Bool :=
  let value : ((Fin m ⊕ Bool) ⊕ Fin i.val) → Bool := fun w ↦
    match w with
    | .inl (.inl j) => x j
    | .inl (.inr b) => b
    | .inr j => C.gateValue x ⟨j.val, Nat.lt_trans j.isLt i.isLt⟩
  match C.gate i with
  | .neg a => !(value a)
  | .conj a b => value a && value b
  | .disj a b => value a || value b
termination_by i.val

/-- The Boolean function computed by the circuit, with zero-cost output selection. -/
def Circuit.eval {m : ℕ} (C : Circuit m) (x : Fin m → Bool) : Bool :=
  match C.output with
  | .inl (.inl j) => x j
  | .inl (.inr b) => b
  | .inr j => C.gateValue x j

/-- The minimum internal-gate count `size(f)` among circuits computing `f` (Section 1). -/
def circuitSize {m : ℕ} (f : (Fin m → Bool) → Bool) : ℕ :=
  sInf {s : ℕ | ∃ C : Circuit m, C.gates = s ∧ C.eval = f}

/-- **Conjecture 3.6**. For all sufficiently large truth tables, the expected minimum circuit
size is nondecreasing throughout the stated bias interval.

Size is the De Morgan gate count with free constant inputs, the contextual GII/MW/Wegener
reading; the report does not specify constant costs. -/
theorem conjecture_3_6 :
    ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ m₀,
      ∀ p q : ℝ, 1 / 50 ≤ p → p < q → q ≤ 1 / 2 →
        (∑ f : ((Fin m → Bool) → Bool),
          (circuitSize f : ℝ) *
            ∏ x : (Fin m → Bool), if f x then p else 1 - p) ≤
        (∑ f : ((Fin m → Bool) → Bool),
          (circuitSize f : ℝ) *
            ∏ x : (Fin m → Bool), if f x then q else 1 - q) := by
  sorry

end Ramesh2021Simple

theorem Ramesh2021Simple.conjecture_3_6_neg : ¬ type_of% @Ramesh2021Simple.conjecture_3_6 := by
  sorry

title: Filtering cohomology of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannians
problem_statement: In reiner2022filtering.lean, prove either Reiner2022Filtering.h_basis_conjecture or refute it by proving its logical negation Reiner2022Filtering.h_basis_conjecture_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Filtering cohomology of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannians

Authors: The 2020 Polymath Jr. q-binomials and the Grassmannian group.
Origin: [Polymath Jr. 2020](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/polymathreu).
Reference: The 2020 Polymath Jr. q-binomials and the Grassmannian group, *Filtering cohomology
of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannians*, Involve **15** (2022), 271-288;
doi:10.2140/involve.2022.15.271.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Reiner2022Filtering

open Finset

/-- A Young diagram fits in a `rows` by `cols` rectangle. -/
def FitsInRectangle (rows cols : ℕ) (lambda : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ lambda, c.1 < rows ∧ c.2 < cols

/-- A partition is `k`-bounded when its first part is at most `k`. -/
def IsKBoundedPartition (k : ℕ) (lambda : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  lambda.rowLen 0 ≤ k

/-- The hook length of a cell in a Young diagram. -/
def hookLength (lambda : YoungDiagram) (c : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{d ∈ lambda.cells | (d.1 = c.1 ∧ c.2 ≤ d.2) ∨ (d.2 = c.2 ∧ c.1 ≤ d.1)}

/-- A `(k + 1)`-core, as used for `k`-conjugation: no cell has hook length exactly `k + 1`. -/
def IsKPlusOneCore (k : ℕ) (lambda : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ lambda.cells, hookLength lambda c ≠ k + 1

/-- The projection `p` from `(k + 1)`-cores to `k`-bounded partitions: remove all cells of hook
length greater than `k` and left-justify the remaining cells row-wise. The result is specified
relationally. -/
def IsCoreProjection (k : ℕ) (core lambda : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  IsKPlusOneCore k core ∧ lambda.rowLens = List.ofFn (fun r : Fin (core.colLen 0) ↦
    #{c ∈ core.cells | c.1 = (r : ℕ) ∧ hookLength core c ≤ k})

/-- The `k`-conjugation relation: apply `p⁻¹` to a `k`-bounded partition, transpose the
resulting `(k + 1)`-core, and apply `p` again. -/
def IsKConjugate (k : ℕ) (lambda μ : YoungDiagram) : Prop :=
  IsKBoundedPartition k lambda ∧ IsKBoundedPartition k μ ∧
    ∃ core : YoungDiagram, IsCoreProjection k core lambda ∧
      IsCoreProjection k core.transpose μ

/-- Variables for the Borel presentation of the ordinary Grassmannian cohomology ring: the
elementary generators `e_1, …, e_ell` and complete homogeneous generators `h_1, …, h_k`. -/
inductive GrassmannianVar (ell k : ℕ) where
  | e : Fin ell → GrassmannianVar ell k
  | h : Fin k → GrassmannianVar ell k

/-- The variable `e_r` in the Borel presentation, with `e_0 = 1` and `e_r = 0` outside
`0 ≤ r ≤ ell`. -/
def grassmannianE (ell k r : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (GrassmannianVar ell k) ℚ :=
  if h₀ : r = 0 then 1
  else if hr : r ≤ ell then MvPolynomial.X (GrassmannianVar.e ⟨r - 1, by omega⟩)
  else 0

/-- The variable `h_r` in the Borel presentation, with `h_0 = 1` and `h_r = 0` outside
`0 ≤ r ≤ k`. -/
def grassmannianH (ell k r : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (GrassmannianVar ell k) ℚ :=
  if h₀ : r = 0 then 1
  else if hr : r ≤ k then MvPolynomial.X (GrassmannianVar.h ⟨r - 1, by omega⟩)
  else 0

/-- The Borel ideal for the ordinary Grassmannian cohomology ring. -/
def grassmannianIdeal (ell k : ℕ) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (GrassmannianVar ell k) ℚ) :=
  Ideal.span {p : MvPolynomial (GrassmannianVar ell k) ℚ |
    ∃ d ≥ 1, d ≤ k + ell ∧ p =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (d + 1),
        MvPolynomial.C ((-1 : ℚ) ^ i) * grassmannianE ell k i * grassmannianH ell k (d - i)}

/-- The rational cohomology ring `R^{ell,k} = H^*(Gr(ell, ℂ^{k+ell}), ℚ)` in the Borel
presentation. -/
abbrev GrassmannianCohomology (ell k : ℕ) :=
  MvPolynomial (GrassmannianVar ell k) ℚ ⧸ grassmannianIdeal ell k

/-- The subalgebra `R^{ell,k,m}` of `R^{ell,k}` generated by homogeneous elements of halved
degree at most `m`. -/
def grassmannianFilteredSubalgebra (ell k m : ℕ) :
    Subalgebra ℚ (GrassmannianCohomology ell k) :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℚ
    {x : GrassmannianCohomology ell k |
      ∃ d ≤ m, ∃ p ∈ MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodule ℚ
          (fun y : GrassmannianVar ell k ↦
            match y with
            | GrassmannianVar.e i => (i : ℕ) + 1
            | GrassmannianVar.h j => (j : ℕ) + 1) d,
        x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (grassmannianIdeal ell k) p}

/-- The class `h_lambda` in `R^{ell,k}`, the product of the complete homogeneous generators
indexed by the parts of `lambda`. -/
def completeHomogeneousClass (ell k : ℕ) (lambda : YoungDiagram) : GrassmannianCohomology ell k :=
  Ideal.Quotient.mk (grassmannianIdeal ell k) ((lambda.rowLens.map (grassmannianH ell k)).prod)

/-- **Conjecture 1.2**. The complete homogeneous classes indexed by partitions `lambda` with
`lambda_1 ≤ m` and `lambda^{omega(k)} ⊆ (k^ell)` form a rational basis of the filtered
subalgebra `R^{ell,k,m}`. -/
theorem h_basis_conjecture
    (ell k m : ℕ)
    (hm : 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ min ell k) :
    LinearIndependent ℚ
        (fun lambda : {lambda : YoungDiagram // lambda.rowLen 0 ≤ m ∧ ∃ μ : YoungDiagram,
            IsKConjugate k lambda μ ∧ FitsInRectangle ell k μ} ↦
          completeHomogeneousClass ell k lambda.1) ∧
      Submodule.span ℚ
          (Set.range fun lambda : {lambda : YoungDiagram // lambda.rowLen 0 ≤ m ∧
              ∃ μ : YoungDiagram, IsKConjugate k lambda μ ∧ FitsInRectangle ell k μ} ↦
            completeHomogeneousClass ell k lambda.1) =
        (grassmannianFilteredSubalgebra ell k m).toSubmodule := by sorry

end Reiner2022Filtering

theorem Reiner2022Filtering.h_basis_conjecture_neg : ¬ type_of% @Reiner2022Filtering.h_basis_conjecture := by
  sorry

title: On the classification of Stanley sequences
problem_statement: In rolnick2017classification.lean, prove either Rolnick2017Classification.conjecture_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Rolnick2017Classification.conjecture_5_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# On the classification of Stanley sequences

Author: David Rolnick.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2011](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: D. Rolnick, *On the classification of Stanley sequences*, European J. Combin. **59**
(2017), 51-70; arXiv:1408.1940v1.
-/

namespace Rolnick2017Classification

/-- The Stanley sequence generated by `A`: increasing, 3-free, with exactly the prescribed
initial segment, and covering every omitted larger integer by two earlier terms (Section 2). -/
def IsStanleySequence (A : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  A.Nonempty ∧ StrictMono a ∧ ThreeAPFree (Set.range a) ∧
    (∀ x ≤ A.sup id, x ∈ Set.range a ↔ x ∈ A) ∧
    ∀ x : ℕ, A.sup id < x → x ∉ Set.range a →
      ∃ i j : ℕ, a i < a j ∧ a j < x ∧ a i + x = 2 * a j

/-- An independent root-position Stanley sequence with character `μ` (Section 2.1). -/
def IsIndependent (a : ℕ → ℕ) (μ : ℤ) : Prop :=
  a 0 = 0 ∧ (∃ A : Finset ℕ, IsStanleySequence A a) ∧
    ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ K,
      (∀ i < 2 ^ k, a (2 ^ k + i) = a (2 ^ k) + a i) ∧
        (a (2 ^ k) : ℤ) = 2 * (a (2 ^ k - 1) : ℤ) - μ + 1

/-- Regularity, with an independent core of the same character (Section 2.2). Shifted indices
are required to be positive before conversion to naturals. -/
def IsRegular (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  a 0 = 0 ∧ (∃ A : Finset ℕ, IsStanleySequence A a) ∧
    ∃ μ σ : ℤ, ∃ core : ℕ → ℕ, IsIndependent core μ ∧
      ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ K,
        let start : ℤ := (2 : ℤ) ^ k - σ
        0 < start ∧
          (∀ i < 2 ^ k, a (start.toNat + i) = a start.toNat + core i) ∧
            (a start.toNat : ℤ) = 2 * (a (start.toNat - 1) : ℤ) - μ + 1

/-- **Conjecture 5.1**. Every finite 3-free set, in the source's standing root-position
convention, has an end-extension generating a regular Stanley sequence. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 (A : Finset ℕ) (hroot : 0 ∈ A)
    (hA : ThreeAPFree (A : Set ℕ)) :
    ∃ B : Finset ℕ, ThreeAPFree (B : Set ℕ) ∧
      (∀ x ≤ A.sup id, x ∈ B ↔ x ∈ A) ∧
      ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsStanleySequence B a ∧ IsRegular a := by
  sorry

end Rolnick2017Classification

theorem Rolnick2017Classification.conjecture_5_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Rolnick2017Classification.conjecture_5_1 := by
  sorry

title: Bijections of Strictly Convex Sets and Closed Convex Projective Surfaces that Preserve Complete Geodesics
source_label: Unnumbered conjecture (Introduction, p. 2; specified in Section 4)
problem_statement: In roy2022bijections.lean, prove either Roy2022Bijections.complete_geodesic_bijection_preserves_hilbert_distance or refute it by proving its logical negation Roy2022Bijections.complete_geodesic_bijection_preserves_hilbert_distance_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Bijections of Strictly Convex Sets and Closed Convex Projective Surfaces that Preserve Complete Geodesics

Author: Drimik Roy Chowdhury.
Origin: [University of Michigan REU
2021](https://prod.lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/math-document/reu-documents/ugradreu/2021/D-Chowdhury_REU21-FINAL.pdf).
Reference: D. R. Chowdhury, *Bijections on strictly convex sets and closed convex projective
surfaces that preserve complete geodesics*, preprint (2022); arXiv:2209.04896v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Roy2022Bijections

open Set
open scoped MatrixGroups Pointwise

local notation "E" => EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
local notation "RP2" => Projectivization ℝ (Fin 3 → ℝ)

/-- The standard affine chart `x ↦ [1 : x_0 : x_1]` in the real projective plane. -/
def affineChart (x : E) : RP2 :=
  Projectivization.mk ℝ ![1, x 0, x 1] (by
    intro h
    have h₀ := congrFun h 0
    norm_num at h₀)

/-- The quotient topology on the real projective plane. -/
scoped instance projectiveTopology : TopologicalSpace RP2 := by
  unfold Projectivization
  infer_instance

/-- The quotient topology `GL(3, ℝ) / Z(GL(3, ℝ))` on `PGL(3, ℝ)`. -/
scoped instance projectiveGroupTopology : TopologicalSpace PGL(3, ℝ) := by
  unfold Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup
  infer_instance

/-- The Hilbert distance, with the source's log-cross-ratio normalization (Definition 2.2). The
boundary endpoints are located as an infimum and a supremum over the chord. -/
def hilbertDistance (Ω : Set E) (x y : E) : ℝ :=
  if x = y then 0 else
    let T : Set ℝ := {t | x + t • (y - x) ∈ Ω}
    let a := x + sInf T • (y - x)
    let b := x + sSup T • (y - x)
    Real.log (dist a y * dist b x / (dist a x * dist b y))

/-- The orbit quotient of the projective domain by the given subgroup (Definition 4.1). -/
abbrev Surface (Ω : Set E)
    (Γ : Subgroup (MulAction.stabilizer PGL(3, ℝ) (affineChart '' Ω))) :=
  Quotient (MulAction.orbitRel Γ (affineChart '' Ω))

/-- The quotient projection, with affine points represented in the projective chart. -/
def projection (Ω : Set E)
    (Γ : Subgroup (MulAction.stabilizer PGL(3, ℝ) (affineChart '' Ω)))
    (x : Ω) : Surface Ω Γ :=
  Quotient.mk (MulAction.orbitRel Γ (affineChart '' Ω))
    ⟨affineChart x, ⟨x, x.property, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The induced Hilbert distance on the quotient, as the infimum over all lifts. By projective
invariance this equals the source's infimum over deck translates of one lift. -/
def quotientHilbertDistance (Ω : Set E)
    (Γ : Subgroup (MulAction.stabilizer PGL(3, ℝ) (affineChart '' Ω)))
    (p q : Surface Ω Γ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ x y : Ω, projection Ω Γ x = p ∧
    projection Ω Γ y = q ∧ r = hilbertDistance Ω x y}

/-- A complete geodesic, as the projection of the intersection of the domain with a line. -/
def completeGeodesic (Ω : Set E)
    (Γ : Subgroup (MulAction.stabilizer PGL(3, ℝ) (affineChart '' Ω)))
    (L : AffineSubspace ℝ E) : Set (Surface Ω Γ) :=
  projection Ω Γ '' {x : Ω | (x : E) ∈ L}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Introduction, p. 2; specified in Section 4). Every bijection of
the surface carrying each complete geodesic onto a complete geodesic preserves the quotient
Hilbert distance.

No continuity, orientability or surjectivity on the geodesic family is assumed. -/
theorem complete_geodesic_bijection_preserves_hilbert_distance
    (Ω : Set E) (hNonempty : Ω.Nonempty) (hOpen : IsOpen Ω)
    (hBounded : Bornology.IsBounded Ω) (hConvex : Convex ℝ Ω)
    (hStrict : ∀ a ∈ frontier Ω, ∀ b ∈ frontier Ω,
      segment ℝ a b ⊆ frontier Ω → a = b)
    (Γ : Subgroup (MulAction.stabilizer PGL(3, ℝ) (affineChart '' Ω)))
    [DiscreteTopology Γ]
    (hFree : ∀ (g : Γ) (x : affineChart '' Ω), g • x = x → g = 1)
    [ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul Γ (affineChart '' Ω)]
    [CompactSpace (Surface Ω Γ)]
    (f : Surface Ω Γ → Surface Ω Γ) (hf : Function.Bijective f)
    (hGeodesics : ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ E, Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
      (∃ x : Ω, (x : E) ∈ L) →
      ∃ L' : AffineSubspace ℝ E, Module.finrank ℝ L'.direction = 1 ∧
        (∃ x : Ω, (x : E) ∈ L') ∧
        f '' completeGeodesic Ω Γ L = completeGeodesic Ω Γ L')
    (p q : Surface Ω Γ) :
    quotientHilbertDistance Ω Γ (f p) (f q) = quotientHilbertDistance Ω Γ p q := by
  sorry

end Roy2022Bijections

  sorry

title: Some conjectures on the maximal height of divisors of x^n - 1
problem_statement: In ryan2010conjectures.lean, prove either Ryan2010Conjectures.conjecture_4_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Ryan2010Conjectures.conjecture_4_1_neg.

/-!
# Some conjectures on the maximal height of divisors of x^n - 1

Authors: Nathan C. Ryan, Bryan C. Ward, and Ryan Ward.
Origin: [Bucknell Undergraduate Research Group
2008-2009](https://www.eg.bucknell.edu/~theburg/projects/2008.html).
Reference: N. C. Ryan, B. C. Ward, and R. Ward, *Some conjectures on the maximal height of
divisors of x^n - 1*, Involve **3** (2010), no. 4, 451-457.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Ryan2010Conjectures

/-- The height of an integral polynomial: its largest absolute coefficient (Section 1). -/
def height (f : Polynomial ℤ) : ℕ :=
  f.support.sup fun k ↦ (f.coeff k).natAbs

/-- The maximal height over integral polynomial divisors of `X ^ n - 1` (Section 1). -/
def maximalDivisorHeight (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {h | ∃ f : Polynomial ℤ, f ∣ Polynomial.X ^ n - 1 ∧ h = height f}

/-- **Conjecture 4.1** (preprint Conjecture 3.3). For every two distinct primes, the maximal
divisor height at their squared product is attained by one of the two specified cyclotomic
products. -/
theorem conjecture_4_1 (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) :
    maximalDivisorHeight (p ^ 2 * q ^ 2) =
      max (height (Polynomial.cyclotomic p ℤ * Polynomial.cyclotomic q ℤ *
        Polynomial.cyclotomic (p ^ 2 * q) ℤ * Polynomial.cyclotomic (p * q ^ 2) ℤ))
        (height (Polynomial.cyclotomic p ℤ * Polynomial.cyclotomic q ℤ *
          Polynomial.cyclotomic (p ^ 2) ℤ * Polynomial.cyclotomic (q ^ 2) ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end Ryan2010Conjectures

  sorry

title: Time Complexity of Computation and Construction in the Chemical Reaction Network-Controlled Tile Assembly Model
problem_statement: In schiefer2016time.lean, prove either Schiefer2016Time.conjecture_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Schiefer2016Time.conjecture_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Time Complexity of Computation and Construction in the Chemical Reaction Network-Controlled Tile Assembly Model

Authors: Nicholas Schiefer and Erik Winfree.
Origin: [Caltech SURF 2015-2016](https://www.dna.caltech.edu/DNApeople-past-members.html).
Reference: N. Schiefer and E. Winfree, *Time Complexity of Computation and Construction in the
Chemical Reaction Network-Controlled Tile Assembly Model*, DNA 2016, LNCS **9818** (2016),
165-182; doi:10.1007/978-3-319-43994-5_11.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Schiefer2016Time

open Finset

/-- A physical tile: its four oriented label-strength bonds (Definition 1). -/
structure Tile (Label : Type) where
  /-- The label and strength of the north bond. -/
  north : Label × ℕ
  /-- The label and strength of the east bond. -/
  east : Label × ℕ
  /-- The label and strength of the south bond. -/
  south : Label × ℕ
  /-- The label and strength of the west bond. -/
  west : Label × ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A tile system: finite species and tile sets, removal map and temperature (Definition 3).
Tiles are a set of four-tuples, so identical tiles are not distinguished by IDs. -/
structure TileSystem (Label Signal : Type) where
  /-- The finite set of signal species. -/
  signals : Finset Signal
  /-- The finite set of physical tiles. -/
  tiles : Finset (Tile Label)
  /-- The optional signal associated with removing each tile. -/
  removal : tiles → Option signals
  /-- The binding temperature. -/
  temperature : ℕ

variable {Label Signal : Type}

/-- A finite, oriented lattice map of tiles (Definition 2). -/
abbrev Placement (K : TileSystem Label Signal) :=
  Finmap (fun _ : ℤ × ℤ ↦ K.tiles)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The total local binding strength at an occupied site (Definition 2). -/
def bindingStrength (K : TileSystem Label Signal) (A : Placement K)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) : ℕ :=
  A.keys.sum (fun q ↦
    match A.lookup p, A.lookup q with
    | some a, some b =>
        let matching (x y : Label × ℕ) := if x = y then x.2 else 0
        if q = (p.1 + 1, p.2) then matching a.val.east b.val.west
        else if q = (p.1 - 1, p.2) then matching a.val.west b.val.east
        else if q = (p.1, p.2 + 1) then matching a.val.north b.val.south
        else if q = (p.1, p.2 - 1) then matching a.val.south b.val.north
        else 0
    | _, _ => 0)

/-- An assembly: grid connectivity, origin seed and local binding (Definition 2). The activated
singleton is the only binding exception, and assemblies are determined by their placement. -/
@[ext] structure Assembly (K : TileSystem Label Signal) where
  /-- The tiles placed at the occupied grid positions. -/
  placement : Placement K
  origin : (0, 0) ∈ placement.keys
  connected : (SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun p q : placement.keys ↦
    q.val = (p.val.1 + 1, p.val.2) ∨
    q.val = (p.val.1 - 1, p.val.2) ∨
    q.val = (p.val.1, p.val.2 + 1) ∨
    q.val = (p.val.1, p.val.2 - 1))).Connected
  binding : placement.keys = {(0, 0)} ∨
    ∀ p ∈ placement.keys, K.temperature ≤ bindingStrength K placement p

/-- The activated singleton seed of the last two reaction types (Definition 3). -/
def seedAssembly (K : TileSystem Label Signal) (t : K.tiles) : Assembly K where
  placement := Finmap.singleton (0, 0) t
  origin := by simp
  connected := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable]
    refine ⟨⟨(0, 0), by simp⟩, ?_⟩
    intro w
    have hw : w.val = (0, 0) := by simpa using w.property
    have heq : w = ⟨(0, 0), by simp⟩ := Subtype.ext hw
    subst w
    exact SimpleGraph.Reachable.rfl
  binding := Or.inl (Finmap.keys_singleton _ _)

/-- Species: free signals, free tiles and activated assemblies (Definition 6). -/
inductive Species (K : TileSystem Label Signal)
  | signal : K.signals → Species K
  | tile : K.tiles → Species K
  | assembly : Assembly K → Species K

/-- A state: a finite multiset of species, as natural multiplicities (Definition 6). -/
abbrev State (K : TileSystem Label Signal) := Species K →₀ ℕ

/-- The epsilon notation for an optional signal (Definition 3). Absence contributes no signal
molecule. -/
def signalTerm (K : TileSystem Label Signal) (s : Option K.signals) :
    Multiset (Species K) :=
  (s.toList.map Species.signal : List (Species K))

/-- A reaction: reactant and product multisets and a nonnegative rational rate. Equality
identifies permutations, not separate syntactic reaction IDs. -/
structure Reaction (K : TileSystem Label Signal) where
  /-- The multiset of reactant species. -/
  reactants : Multiset (Species K)
  /-- The multiset of product species. -/
  products : Multiset (Species K)
  /-- The nonnegative rational rate constant. -/
  rate : NNRat

/-- The six explicit reaction types, with both permitted product forms for creation
(Definition 3). Null signals are omitted rather than treated as an inexhaustible species. -/
def ExplicitReaction {K : TileSystem Label Signal} (r : Reaction K) : Prop :=
  (∃ a b c d : Option K.signals,
    r.reactants = signalTerm K a + signalTerm K b ∧
    r.products = signalTerm K c + signalTerm K d) ∨
  (∃ (a c d : Option K.signals) (t : K.tiles),
    r.reactants = signalTerm K a + {Species.tile t} ∧
    r.products = signalTerm K c + signalTerm K d) ∨
  (∃ a b : Option K.signals,
    r.reactants = signalTerm K a + signalTerm K b ∧
    ((∃ (t : K.tiles) (c : Option K.signals),
      r.products = {Species.tile t} + signalTerm K c) ∨
     (∃ t u : K.tiles, r.products = {Species.tile t} + {Species.tile u}))) ∨
  (∃ (a b : Option K.signals) (t u : K.tiles),
    r.reactants = signalTerm K a + {Species.tile t} ∧
    r.products = signalTerm K b + {Species.tile u}) ∨
  (∃ (a : Option K.signals) (t : K.tiles),
    r.reactants = signalTerm K a + {Species.tile t} ∧
    r.products = {Species.assembly (seedAssembly K t)} + signalTerm K (K.removal t)) ∨
  (∃ (a : Option K.signals) (t : K.tiles),
    r.reactants = {Species.assembly (seedAssembly K t)} + signalTerm K (K.removal t) ∧
    r.products = signalTerm K a + {Species.tile t})

/-- The implicit unit-rate additions and removals between valid assemblies (Definition 5).
Only a nonorigin site changes, and removal requires exactly temperature and a signal. -/
def ImplicitReaction {K : TileSystem Label Signal} (r : Reaction K) : Prop :=
  ∃ (A B : Assembly K) (p : ℤ × ℤ) (t : K.tiles),
    p ≠ (0, 0) ∧ A.placement.lookup p = none ∧
    B.placement = A.placement.insert p t ∧ r.rate = 1 ∧
    ((r.reactants = {Species.assembly A} + {Species.tile t} ∧
      r.products = {Species.assembly B} + signalTerm K (K.removal t)) ∨
     (K.removal t ≠ none ∧ bindingStrength K B.placement p = K.temperature ∧
      r.reactants = {Species.assembly B} + signalTerm K (K.removal t) ∧
      r.products = {Species.assembly A} + {Species.tile t}))

/-- A finite program, with only free signals and tiles initially present (Definition 3). -/
structure Program (Label Signal : Type) where
  /-- The underlying tile system. -/
  system : TileSystem Label Signal
  /-- The finite set of explicit reactions. -/
  reactions : Finset (Reaction system)
  explicit : ∀ r ∈ reactions, ExplicitReaction r
  /-- The initial counts of free signals and tiles. -/
  initial : system.signals ⊕ system.tiles →₀ ℕ

/-- The initial state embeds free supplies without any prebuilt assembly. -/
def Program.initialState (P : Program Label Signal) : State P.system :=
  P.initial.mapDomain (fun x ↦ match x with
    | Sum.inl s => Species.signal s
    | Sum.inr t => Species.tile t)

/-- Possible reactions, with full multiset feasibility including repeated reactants
(Definition 7). Positive null-reactant templates remain possible, with unspecified kinetics. -/
def Program.Possible (P : Program Label Signal) (L : State P.system)
    (r : Reaction P.system) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact (r ∈ P.reactions ∨ ImplicitReaction r) ∧
    r.rate ≠ 0 ∧ r.reactants.toFinsupp ≤ L

/-- A directed edge: stoichiometric consumption and production (Definition 8). Identity events
are retained. -/
def Program.Step (P : Program Label Signal) (L M : State P.system) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact ∃ r : Reaction P.system, P.Possible L r ∧
    M = L - r.reactants.toFinsupp + r.products.toFinsupp

/-- Finite-path reachability (Definition 8). Finiteness of the reachable set is a separate
source condition. -/
def Program.Reachable (P : Program Label Signal) (L : State P.system) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen P.Step P.initialState L

/-- The mass: signals and free tiles weigh one; assemblies weigh all their tiles
(Definition 10). -/
def State.mass {K : TileSystem Label Signal} (L : State K) : ℕ :=
  L.sum (fun species count ↦ count * match species with
    | Species.signal _ => 1
    | Species.tile _ => 1
    | Species.assembly A => #A.placement.keys)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The partial propensity for one or two reactants, with no factor `1 / 2` (Definition 11).
Inactive events give `0`, null-reactant, higher-arity and zero-volume binary events give `none`,
and the volume is an input. -/
def Reaction.propensity {K : TileSystem Label Signal} (r : Reaction K)
    (L : State K) (volume : NNRat) : Option NNRat :=
  if r.rate = 0 ∨ ¬r.reactants.toFinsupp ≤ L then some 0
    else if 1 ≤ r.reactants.card ∧ r.reactants.card ≤ 2 ∧
        (r.reactants.card = 1 ∨ volume ≠ 0) then
      some (r.rate * r.reactants.toFinsupp.prod
        (fun s n ↦ ((L s).descFactorial n : NNRat)) /
        volume ^ (r.reactants.card - 1))
    else none

/-- The assembly encodes a binary word: a start tile followed by its decoded symbols
(Definition 16). The word runs along the positive horizontal axis from a start tile that need
not be the origin seed. -/
def Assembly.Encodes {K : TileSystem Label Signal} (A : Assembly K)
    (start : K.tiles) (decode : K.tiles → Option Bool) {n : ℕ}
    (word : Fin n → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ offset : ℤ, A.placement.lookup (offset, 0) = some start ∧
    (∀ p : ℤ × ℤ, p ∈ A.placement.keys ↔
      p.2 = 0 ∧ offset ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 ≤ offset + (n : ℤ)) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ tile : K.tiles,
      A.placement.lookup (offset + (i.val : ℤ) + 1, 0) = some tile ∧
      decode tile = some (word i)

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Conjecture 1**. No zero-error CRN-TAM family constructs every length-`n` binary word in
polynomial expected time.

Determinism means terminal coverage and time means expected global event absorption, given by
finite mean-time equations; the singleton-seed and event-stopping conventions are contextual
readings. -/
theorem conjecture_1 :
    ¬∃ (program : ℕ → Program ℕ ℕ) (C : ℝ) (d n₀ : ℕ),
      0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
      let P := program n
      ∃ (start : P.system.tiles) (decode : P.system.tiles → Option Bool)
        (states : Finset (State P.system))
        (events : Finset (Reaction P.system))
        (rate : State P.system → Reaction P.system → NNRat)
        (time : State P.system → ℝ),
        (∀ L, L ∈ states ↔ P.Reachable L) ∧
        (∀ r, r ∈ events ↔ ∃ L ∈ states, P.Possible L r) ∧
        (∀ L ∈ states, ∃ M,
          Relation.ReflTransGen P.Step L M ∧ ¬∃ r, P.Possible M r) ∧
        (∀ L ∈ states, ∀ r ∈ events,
          P.Possible L r →
            r.propensity L ((states.sup State.mass : ℕ) : NNRat) = some (rate L r) ∧
            0 < rate L r) ∧
        (∀ L ∈ states, 0 ≤ time L) ∧
        (∀ L ∈ states, (¬∃ r, P.Possible L r) →
          time L = 0 ∧ ∀ word : Fin n → Bool,
            ∃ A : Assembly P.system,
              0 < L (Species.assembly A) ∧ A.Encodes start decode word) ∧
        (∀ L ∈ states, (∃ r, P.Possible L r) →
          (∑ r ∈ events, if P.Possible L r then
            (rate L r : ℝ) *
              (time L - time (L - r.reactants.toFinsupp + r.products.toFinsupp))
            else 0) = 1) ∧
        (n₀ ≤ n → time P.initialState ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ d) := by sorry

end Schiefer2016Time

theorem Schiefer2016Time.conjecture_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Schiefer2016Time.conjecture_1 := by
  sorry

Authors: Nathan S. Sheffield and Zoe Xi.

title: A Generalization of an Action of the Braid Group on Upper-Triangular Matrices
problem_statement: In shin2012generalization.lean, prove either Shin2012Generalization.conjecture_20 or refute it by proving its logical negation Shin2012Generalization.conjecture_20_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# A Generalization of an Action of the Braid Group on Upper-Triangular Matrices

Author: Minseon Shin.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2011](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: M. Shin, *A Generalization of an Action of the Braid Group on Upper-Triangular
Matrices*, Harvard College Math. Rev. **4** (Spring 2012), 4-16.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Shin2012Generalization

/-- The ring `k[X,Y]`, with one `X` variable for each strict upper-triangular position and `m`
auxiliary `Y` variables (pp. 5 and 8). -/
abbrev SourcePolynomial (n m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommRing K] :=
  MvPolynomial ({p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2} ⊕ Fin m) K

/-- The polynomial `P_[n]` on the enlarged coefficient-variable ring (Definition 14; before
Lemma 19). -/
def P {n m : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommRing K]
    (f : Fin n → SourcePolynomial n m K) : SourcePolynomial n m K :=
  (∑ i, f i ^ 2) +
    ∑ p : {p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2},
      MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl p) * f p.val.1 * f p.val.2

/-- The map `T_l`: negate the other coordinates and update coordinate `l` (Definition 16).
The source's `X_jl` for `j ≠ l` uses the unordered-pair index convention. -/
def T {n m : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommRing K] (l : Fin n)
    (f : Fin n → SourcePolynomial n m K) : Fin n → SourcePolynomial n m K :=
  fun i ↦ if i = l then f l +
    (∑ j : {j : Fin n // j < l},
      MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl ⟨(j.val, l), j.property⟩) * f j.val) +
    (∑ j : {j : Fin n // l < j},
      MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl ⟨(l, j.val), j.property⟩) * f j.val)
  else -f i

/-- **Conjecture 20** (p. 8). Every polynomial solution of `P_[n](f) = 1` reduces by a finite
sequence of maps `T_l` to a signed coordinate vector.

Positive dimension, empty auxiliary variables and an empty word use the standard finite
conventions; no matrix-column, degree or rational-coefficient restriction is imposed. -/
theorem conjecture_20 (K : Type*) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K]
    {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (f : Fin n → SourcePolynomial n m K)
    (hf : P f = 1) :
    ∃ word : List (Fin n), ∃ j : Fin n,
      word.foldr T f = (fun i ↦ if i = j then 1 else 0) ∨
      word.foldr T f = (fun i ↦ if i = j then -1 else 0) := by sorry

end Shin2012Generalization

theorem Shin2012Generalization.conjecture_20_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Shin2012Generalization.conjecture_20.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Families with no perfect matchings
problem_statement: In singhal2021families.lean, prove either Singhal2021Families.conjecture_7_4 or refute it by proving its logical negation Singhal2021Families.conjecture_7_4_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Families with no perfect matchings

Author: Mihir Singhal.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2020](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: M. Singhal, *Families with no perfect matchings*, Combin. Theory **1** (2021);
doi:10.5070/C61055359; arXiv:2008.08792v2 (2020).
-/

namespace Singhal2021Families

open Finset

/-- A matching: a subfamily of pairwise disjoint sets. -/
def IsMatching (F M : Finset (Finset ℕ)) : Prop :=
  M ⊆ F ∧ (M : Set (Finset ℕ)).PairwiseDisjoint id

/-- A blocking set: at most `s` vertices, not coverable by a matching of exactly its own
cardinality. -/
def IsBlocking (n s : ℕ) (F : Finset (Finset ℕ)) (B : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ #B ≤ s ∧
    ¬∃ M : Finset (Finset ℕ), IsMatching F M ∧
      #M = #B ∧ B ⊆ M.biUnion id

/-- The disjoint blocks `E_1, …, E_(b-1)` of Example 1.3, chosen as successive intervals
outside `[b]`. The index `i` is zero-based. -/
def block (k b i : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  Finset.Ico (b + 1 + i * (k - 1)) (b + 1 + (i + 1) * (k - 1))

/-- The family `E(k,n,b)` built from the canonical disjoint blocks (Example 1.3). The last
distinguished vertex has no exceptional edge of its own. -/
def extremalFamily (k n b : ℕ) : Finset (Finset ℕ) :=
  (Finset.Icc (b + 1) n).powersetCard k ∪
    (Finset.range b).biUnion (fun i ↦
      (if i + 1 < b then {insert (i + 1) (block k b i)} else ∅) ∪
      ({S ∈ (Finset.Icc (b + 1) n).powersetCard (k - 1) |
        ¬Disjoint S ((Finset.range i).biUnion (block k b))}).image
          (insert (i + 1)))

/-- **Conjecture 7.4**. The extremal bound holds for all `k ≥ 4` after a threshold depending
only on `b`.

The threshold is at least `2 * b`, which ensures Example 1.3's domain `n ≥ b * k + b`. -/
theorem conjecture_7_4 :
    ∃ s₀ : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ b, 2 * b ≤ s₀ b) ∧
      ∀ (k b s : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hs : s₀ b ≤ s)
        (F : Finset (Finset ℕ))
        (hF : ∀ A ∈ F, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 (k * s) ∧ #A = k)
        (hperfect : ¬∃ M : Finset (Finset ℕ),
          IsMatching F M ∧ M.biUnion id = Finset.Icc 1 (k * s))
        (hblocking : ∀ B : Finset ℕ, #B < b → ¬IsBlocking (k * s) s F B),
        #F ≤ #(extremalFamily k (k * s) b) := by
  sorry

end Singhal2021Families

theorem Singhal2021Families.conjecture_7_4_neg : ¬ type_of% @Singhal2021Families.conjecture_7_4 := by
  sorry

title: High-dimensional envy-free partitions
problem_statement: In soberon2023high.lean, prove either Soberon2023High.simultaneous_envy_free_convex_partition or refute it by proving its logical negation Soberon2023High.simultaneous_envy_free_convex_partition_neg.

/-!
# High-dimensional envy-free partitions

Authors: Pablo Soberon and Christina Yu.
Origin: [NYC Discrete Math REU 2023](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/home/previous-years).
Reference: P. Soberon and C. Yu, *High-dimensional envy-free partitions*, arXiv:2311.09905v1
(2023), 14 pp.
-/

namespace Soberon2023High

open MeasureTheory

/-- A convex partition: closed convex pieces covering the space with pairwise disjoint
interiors (p. 2). -/
def IsConvexPartition {d n : ℕ} (C : Fin n → Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, IsClosed (C i) ∧ Convex ℝ (C i)) ∧
    (⋃ i, C i) = Set.univ ∧
    Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (interior (C i)) (interior (C j)))

/-- An envy-free partition: a bijective allocation gives each measure a piece of maximal value
among all pieces (p. 2). -/
def IsEnvyFree {d n : ℕ} (C : Fin n → Set (Fin d → ℝ))
    (μ : Fin n → Measure (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i j, μ i (C j) ≤ μ i (C (π i))

/-- **Conjecture 5.1** (p. 12). Any `d` groups of `n` absolutely continuous probability measures
on real `d`-space admit one convex partition that is envy-free for every group. -/
theorem simultaneous_envy_free_convex_partition {d n : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hn : 0 < n)
    (μ : Fin d → Fin n → Measure (Fin d → ℝ))
    (hprob : ∀ r i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ r i))
    (hac : ∀ r i, μ r i ≪ volume) :
    ∃ C : Fin n → Set (Fin d → ℝ), IsConvexPartition C ∧
      ∀ r, IsEnvyFree C (μ r) := by
  sorry

end Soberon2023High

title: Variations of Helly's theorem for convex splinters
problem_statement: In soberon2026variations.lean, prove either Soberon2026Variations.dual_vc_dimension_linear_partitions or refute it by proving its logical negation Soberon2026Variations.dual_vc_dimension_linear_partitions_neg.

/-!
# Variations of Helly's theorem for convex splinters

Authors: Pablo Soberon and Iris Ye.
Origin: [NYC Discrete Math REU 2024](https://geometrynyc.wixsite.com/home/previous-years).
Reference: P. Soberon and I. Ye, *Variations of Helly's theorem for convex splinters*,
arXiv:2606.23437v1 (2026), 12 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Soberon2026Variations

/-- A linear partition: a finite union of affine spaces for which every choice of affinely
independent subsets has affinely independent union (Definition 4.1). -/
def IsLinearPartition {d : ℕ} (C : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : ℕ) (A : Fin s → AffineSubspace ℝ (Fin d → ℝ)),
    C = ⋃ i, (A i : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ U : Fin s → Set (Fin d → ℝ),
      (∀ i, U i ⊆ (A i : Set (Fin d → ℝ))) →
      (∀ i, AffineIndependent ℝ (fun x : U i ↦ (x : Fin d → ℝ))) →
      AffineIndependent ℝ (fun x : (⋃ i, U i) ↦ (x : Fin d → ℝ))

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (after Theorem 4.4, p. 8). The dual VC dimension of linear
partitions in positive-dimensional real affine space is `d + 1`.

The dual VC dimension is expressed as an attained maximum of the sizes of fully realized
membership patterns. -/
theorem dual_vc_dimension_linear_partitions (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) :
    IsGreatest {m : ℕ | ∃ C : Fin m → Set (Fin d → ℝ),
      (∀ i, IsLinearPartition (C i)) ∧
      let traces : Set (Finset (Fin m)) :=
        {t | ∃ x : Fin d → ℝ, ∀ i, x ∈ C i ↔ i ∈ t}
      (Set.toFinite traces).toFinset.Shatters Finset.univ} (d + 1) := by
  sorry

end Soberon2026Variations
