title: An Efficient Way of Understanding the Maximum Number of Steady-State Solutions for Chemical Reaction Networks
problem_statement: In sofia2019efficient.lean, prove either Sofia2019Efficient.conjecture_9 or refute it by proving its logical negation Sofia2019Efficient.conjecture_9_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# An Efficient Way of Understanding the Maximum Number of Steady-State Solutions for Chemical Reaction Networks
for Chemical Reaction Networks

Author: Dilruba Sofia.
Origin: [Texas A&M University REU
2019](https://artsci.tamu.edu/mathematics/_files/_docs/reu/results/2019/sofia-report.pdf).
Reference: D. Sofia, *An Efficient Way of Understanding the Maximum Number of Steady-State
Solutions for Chemical Reaction Networks*, Texas A&M REU report (July 25, 2019).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Sofia2019Efficient

open scoped Pointwise
open Finset

/-- A reaction network: finite distinct complexes and distinct directed reactions between them,
with no diagonal reactions. -/
structure Network (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The finite set of complexes. -/
  complexes : Finset (Fin n →₀ ℕ)
  /-- The directed reactions between complexes. -/
  reactions : Finset (complexes × complexes)
  noLoops : ∀ e ∈ reactions, e.1 ≠ e.2

open scoped Classical in
/-- Full reversibilization: every missing reverse reaction is added on the same species and
complexes. -/
def Network.fullyReversible {n : ℕ} (G : Network n) : Network n where
  complexes := G.complexes
  reactions := G.reactions ∪ G.reactions.image Prod.swap
  noLoops := by
    intro e he
    rcases Finset.mem_union.mp he with he | he
    · exact G.noLoops e he
    · rcases Finset.mem_image.mp he with ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
      exact Ne.symm (G.noLoops f hf)

/-- The real stoichiometric subspace spanned by the complete reaction vectors. -/
def Network.stoichiometric {n : ℕ} (G : Network n) :
    Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
  Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun e : G.reactions ↦
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i ↦ (e.val.2.val i : ℝ) - (e.val.1.val i : ℝ)))

open scoped Classical in
/-- The mass-action species polynomials. The coefficient ring may hold actual rates or
unspecialized rate parameters. -/
def Network.massAction {n : ℕ} (G : Network n) {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (rates : G.reactions → R) (i : Fin n) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R :=
  ∑ e : G.reactions,
    MvPolynomial.monomial e.val.1.val
      (rates e * ((e.val.2.val i : R) - (e.val.1.val i : R)))

open scoped Classical in
/-- The conservation-augmented system. Rates and totals are symbolic coefficient variables and
species are the outer variables. -/
def Network.augmentedSystem {n d : ℕ} (G : Network n)
    (W : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin n) ℝ) (pivot : OrderEmbedding (Fin d) (Fin n))
    (i : Fin n) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (G.reactions ⊕ Fin d) ℝ) :=
  if h : ∃ r, pivot r = i then
    (∑ j : Fin n,
      MvPolynomial.C (MvPolynomial.C (W (Classical.choose h) j)) *
        MvPolynomial.X j) -
      MvPolynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr (Classical.choose h)))
  else G.massAction (fun e ↦ MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl e)) i

open scoped Classical in
/-- The BKK mixed volume of the generic augmented supports (equation (7)). This polarization
has no division by the factorial of the dimension. -/
def Network.mixedVolume {n d : ℕ} (G : Network n)
    (W : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin n) ℝ) (pivot : OrderEmbedding (Fin d) (Fin n)) :
    ℝ :=
  let P : Fin n → TopologicalSpace.Compacts (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
    fun i ↦
      { carrier := convexHull ℝ
          ((fun a : Fin n →₀ ℕ ↦
            WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j ↦ (a j : ℝ))) ''
              ((G.augmentedSystem W pivot i).support : Set (Fin n →₀ ℕ)))
        isCompact' :=
          (((G.augmentedSystem W pivot i).support.finite_toSet).image
            (fun a ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j ↦ (a j : ℝ)))).isCompact_convexHull ℝ }
  let partialSum : Finset (Fin n) →
      TopologicalSpace.Compacts (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) := fun J ↦
    { carrier := ∑ i ∈ J, (P i : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
      isCompact' := by
        induction J using Finset.induction_on with
        | empty =>
          change IsCompact ({0} : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
          exact isCompact_singleton
        | @insert i J hi ih =>
          simpa [Finset.sum_insert hi] using (P i).isCompact.add ih }
  ∑ J ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powerset,
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - #J) *
      (MeasureTheory.volume
        (partialSum J : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))).toReal

/-- Equatoriality: the mixed volume equals the attained greatest finite count of distinct
positive states, over all positive rates and nonempty classes. -/
def Network.Equatorial {n d : ℕ} (G : Network n)
    (W : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin n) ℝ) (pivot : OrderEmbedding (Fin d) (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  let counts : Set ℕ := {k | ∃ rates : G.reactions → ℝ,
    (∀ e, 0 < rates e) ∧ ∃ c : Fin d → ℝ,
      (∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) ∧ W.mulVec x = c) ∧
      ({x : Fin n → ℝ | (∀ i, 0 < x i) ∧ W.mulVec x = c ∧
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (G.massAction rates i) = 0}.encard = k)}
  ∃ k : ℕ, IsGreatest counts k ∧ G.mixedVolume W pivot = (k : ℝ)

/-- **Conjecture 9** (p. 9). A strongly connected equatorial network remains equatorial after
full reversibilization.

The row-reduced convention is read as RREF in the species order, with the same conservation
matrix; no nondegeneracy or generic-rate condition restricts the positive-state maximum. -/
theorem conjecture_9 {n d : ℕ} (G : Network n)
    (W : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin n) ℝ) (pivot : OrderEmbedding (Fin d) (Fin n))
    (hRREF : W.IsReducedRowEchelon)
    (hrows : LinearIndependent ℝ (fun r ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (W r)))
    (hspan : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun r ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (W r)) =
      G.stoichiometric.orthogonal)
    (hpivot : ∀ r, W.IsLeadingEntry r (pivot r))
    (hconnected : ∀ a b : G.complexes,
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b ↦ (a, b) ∈ G.reactions) a b)
    (hequatorial : G.Equatorial W pivot) :
    G.fullyReversible.Equatorial W pivot := by
  sorry

end Sofia2019Efficient

theorem Sofia2019Efficient.conjecture_9_neg : ¬ type_of% @Sofia2019Efficient.conjecture_9 := by
  sorry

title: Laplacians on Julia Sets III: Cubic Julia Sets and Formal Matings
problem_statement: In spicer2013laplacians.lean, prove either Spicer2013Laplacians.conjecture_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Spicer2013Laplacians.conjecture_5_1_neg.

/-!
# Laplacians on Julia Sets III: Cubic Julia Sets and Formal Matings

Authors: Calum Spicer, Robert S. Strichartz, and Emad Totari.
Origin: [Cornell Mathematics REU 2011](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~etota001/).
Reference: C. Spicer, R. S. Strichartz, and E. Totari, *Laplacians on Julia Sets III: Cubic
Julia Sets and Formal Matings*, arXiv:1206.2301v1 (2012), 24 pp.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Spicer2013Laplacians

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped Topology

/-- The itinerary for the left-open, right-closed three-arc partition. -/
def kneading (k : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) (j : ℕ) : Fin 3 :=
  let θ : ℝ := 1 / (3 * ((3 : ℝ) ^ k - 1))
  let x : ℝ := AddCircle.equivIoc (1 : ℝ) θ ((3 ^ j : ℕ) • t)
  if x ≤ θ + 1 / 3 then 0 else if x ≤ θ + 2 / 3 then 1 else 2

/-- The angle vertices of the level-`m` circle graph, before identifications. -/
def vertex {k : ℕ} (m : ℕ) (ell : Fin (3 ^ m)) (a : Fin k) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ) :=
  (((3 : ℝ) ^ a.val + ell.val * ((3 : ℝ) ^ k - 1)) /
    ((3 : ℝ) ^ m * ((3 : ℝ) ^ k - 1)) : ℝ)

/-- The oriented length of a type-`a` interval, including the wraparound edge. -/
def edgeLength {k : ℕ} (m : ℕ) (a : Fin k) : ℝ :=
  2 * (3 : ℝ) ^ a.val / ((3 : ℝ) ^ m * ((3 : ℝ) ^ k - 1))

/-- The renormalized finite bilinear energy over every cyclic edge. Weights are `b_a = r ^ a`,
as forced by (2.5) rather than the printed powers after (2.6), and parallel edges and loops are
kept. -/
def graphEnergy (k m : ℕ) : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ C(AddCircle (1 : ℝ), ℝ) :=
  let r : ℝ := (3 : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / k)
  ∑ ell : Fin (3 ^ m), ∑ a : Fin k,
    let x := vertex m ell a
    let y := x + (edgeLength m a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))
    let d := (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ) y).toLinearMap -
      (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ) x).toLinearMap
    ((r ^ m)⁻¹ * r ^ a.val / edgeLength m a) •
      LinearMap.BilinForm.linMulLin d d

/-- The domain `dom(E)`: continuous pullbacks respecting the primary kneading identification,
with bounded renormalized graph energies at every positive level. -/
def energyDomain (k : ℕ) : Submodule ℝ C(AddCircle (1 : ℝ), ℝ) where
  carrier := {u | (∀ x y, kneading k x = kneading k y → u x = u y) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ m : ℕ, graphEnergy k (m + 1) u u ≤ C}
  zero_mem' := by
    refine ⟨by simp, 0, ?_⟩
    intro m
    simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u v hu hv
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x y h
      change u x + v x = u y + v y
      rw [hu.1 x y h, hv.1 x y h]
    · obtain ⟨Cu, huC⟩ := hu.2
      obtain ⟨Cv, hvC⟩ := hv.2
      refine ⟨2 * (Cu + Cv), fun m ↦ ?_⟩
      have hsum : graphEnergy k (m + 1) (u + v) (u + v) ≤
          2 * (graphEnergy k (m + 1) u u + graphEnergy k (m + 1) v v) := by
        simp only [graphEnergy, LinearMap.sum_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply,
          LinearMap.BilinForm.linMulLin_apply, smul_eq_mul]
        simp only [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro ell _
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro a _
        have hD : 0 ≤ (3 : ℝ) ^ k - 1 := sub_nonneg.mpr (one_le_pow₀ (by norm_num))
        have hL : 0 ≤ edgeLength (m + 1) a := by
          unfold edgeLength
          positivity
        have hc : 0 ≤ (((3 : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / k)) ^ (m + 1))⁻¹ *
            ((3 : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / k)) ^ a.val / edgeLength (m + 1) a := by
          positivity
        simp only [map_add]
        nlinarith [mul_nonneg hc (sq_nonneg
          (((ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
            (vertex (m + 1) ell a + (edgeLength (m + 1) a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).toLinearMap -
            (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ) (vertex (m + 1) ell a)).toLinearMap) u -
           ((ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ)
            (vertex (m + 1) ell a + (edgeLength (m + 1) a : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))).toLinearMap -
            (ContinuousMap.evalCLM ℝ (M := ℝ) (vertex (m + 1) ell a)).toLinearMap) v))]
      exact hsum.trans (by linarith [huC m, hvC m])
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x y h
      change c * u x = c * u y
      rw [hu.1 x y h]
    · obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hu.2
      refine ⟨c ^ 2 * C, fun m ↦ ?_⟩
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hC m) (sq_nonneg c)
      simpa only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, pow_two, mul_assoc] using h

/-- The real weak eigenspace of the nonnegative limiting Laplacian. Members satisfy the energy
limit against every function in `dom(E)`, not just finite graph tests. -/
def weakEigenspace (k : ℕ) (μ : ℝ) : Submodule ℝ C(AddCircle (1 : ℝ), ℝ) where
  carrier := {u | u ∈ energyDomain k ∧ ∀ v ∈ energyDomain k,
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ graphEnergy k (m + 1) u v) atTop
      (𝓝 (μ * ∫ t : AddCircle (1 : ℝ), u t * v t))}
  zero_mem' := by
    refine ⟨(energyDomain k).zero_mem, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro u w hu hw
    refine ⟨(energyDomain k).add_mem hu.1 hw.1, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    have hiu : Integrable (fun t : AddCircle (1 : ℝ) ↦ u t * v t) :=
      (u.continuous.mul v.continuous).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
        (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
    have hiw : Integrable (fun t : AddCircle (1 : ℝ) ↦ w t * v t) :=
      (w.continuous.mul v.continuous).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
        (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _)
    simpa only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, ContinuousMap.add_apply, add_mul,
      integral_add hiu hiw, mul_add] using (hu.2 v hv).add (hw.2 v hv)
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    refine ⟨(energyDomain k).smul_mem c hu.1, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    simpa only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, ContinuousMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
      mul_assoc, integral_const_mul, mul_left_comm μ c] using (hu.2 v hv).const_mul c

/-- The multiplicity recurrence of Conjecture 5.1: `multiplicity k 0 = 2`, and step `j + 1`
maps `m` to `3 (m - 2) + 2` when `k ∣ j + 1` and to `3 (m - 1) + 1` otherwise. -/
def multiplicity (k : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 2
  | j + 1 =>
    if k ∣ j + 1 then 3 * (multiplicity k j - 2) + 2 else 3 * (multiplicity k j - 1) + 1

/-- **Conjecture 5.1**. For every cubic-family parameter and nonzero eigenvalue, the full
multiplicity is the prescribed recurrence at its primitive order.

Identifications use the primary same-kneading definition on p. 4, not its conflicting grouped
display, and weights follow (2.5), not the displayed powers on pp. 6-7; no no-coincidences
principle is assumed. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (μ : ℝ) (hμ : μ ≠ 0)
    (heigen : weakEigenspace k μ ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ j : ℕ, weakEigenspace k (μ / ((3 : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) + 1) / k)) ^ j) ≠ ⊥ ∧
      weakEigenspace k (μ / ((3 : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) + 1) / k)) ^ (j + 1)) = ⊥ ∧
      Module.rank ℝ (weakEigenspace k μ) = (multiplicity k j : Cardinal) := by
  sorry

end Spicer2013Laplacians

theorem Spicer2013Laplacians.conjecture_5_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Spicer2013Laplacians.conjecture_5_1 := by
  sorry

title: Line Complexity Asymptotics of Polynomial Cellular Automata
problem_statement: In stone2018line.lean, prove either Stone2018Line.section_9_recurrence_conjecture or refute it by proving its logical negation Stone2018Line.section_9_recurrence_conjecture_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Line Complexity Asymptotics of Polynomial Cellular Automata

Author: Bertrand Stone.
Origin: [MIT UROP+ 2015](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/urop-plus/papers.html).
Reference: B. Stone, *Line Complexity Asymptotics of Polynomial Cellular Automata*,
arXiv:1604.02753v2.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Stone2018Line

open Polynomial

/-- The number of distinct length-`k` blocks occurring in any row of the integer-indexed
automaton with initial state `1` and transition rule `T` (Sections 1-2). -/
def lineComplexity (T : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card { b : Fin k → ZMod 2 //
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∃ j : ℤ,
      ∀ i : Fin k, b i = (T ^ t).toLaurent.coeff (j + (i.val : ℤ)) }

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 9, p. 30). The rule `1 + x + x ^ 3 + x ^ 4` satisfies
both order-four line-complexity recursions of Theorem 5 with a common constant. -/
theorem section_9_recurrence_conjecture :
    let a := fun k : ℕ ↦
      (lineComplexity (1 + X + X ^ 3 + X ^ 4 : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) k : ℤ)
    ∃ C : ℤ, ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      a (2 * k) = 2 * a k + 2 * a (k + 2) + C ∧
      a (2 * k + 1) = a k + a (k + 1) + a (k + 2) + a (k + 3) + C := by
  sorry

end Stone2018Line

  sorry

problem_statement: In strichartz1995densities.lean, prove either Strichartz1995Densities.lipschitz_uniqueness or refute it by proving its logical negation Strichartz1995Densities.lipschitz_uniqueness_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Densities of Self-Similar Measures on the Line

Authors: Robert S. Strichartz, Arthur Taylor, and Tong Zhang.
Origin: [NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates Program](https://www.maths.tcd.ie/EMIS/journals/EM/restricted/4/4.2/strich.ps).
Reference: R. S. Strichartz, A. Taylor, and T. Zhang, *Densities of Self-Similar Measures on the
Line*, Experiment. Math. **4** (1995), no. 2, 101-128.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Strichartz1995Densities

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (following Problem 3.3, p. 111). Under Hypotheses 3.1, positive
Lipschitz projective weights determine at most one probability eigensolution of (3.3).

Interval weights cover the source's attractor-weight convention by positive Lipschitz extension;
the maps need only have uniformly shrinking composition mesh, and `c` is the source's scaling
constant `λ`. -/
theorem lipschitz_uniqueness
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m)
    (S : Fin m → C(unitInterval, unitInterval))
    (hinj : ∀ j, Function.Injective (S j))
    (hdisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
      Disjoint
        (interior (Set.range (fun x : unitInterval ↦ ((S i x : unitInterval) : ℝ))))
        (interior (Set.range (fun x : unitInterval ↦ ((S j x : unitInterval) : ℝ)))))
    (hmesh : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ N : ℕ,
      ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ w : Fin n → Fin m,
        ∀ x y : unitInterval,
          dist ((List.ofFn w).foldr (fun j f ↦ (S j) ∘ f) id x)
            ((List.ofFn w).foldr (fun j f ↦ (S j) ∘ f) id y) < ε)
    (q : Fin m → unitInterval → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ j x, 0 < q j x)
    (hlip : ∀ j, ∃ L : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith L (q j))
    (μ ν : ProbabilityMeasure unitInterval)
    (c η : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hη : 0 < η)
    (hμ : ENNReal.ofReal c • (μ : Measure unitInterval) =
      ∑ j,
        ((μ : Measure unitInterval).withDensity (fun x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (q j x))).map
          (S j))
    (hν : ENNReal.ofReal η • (ν : Measure unitInterval) =
      ∑ j,
        ((ν : Measure unitInterval).withDensity (fun x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (q j x))).map
          (S j)) :
    μ = ν := by
  sorry

end Strichartz1995Densities

  sorry

title: Generalizing Rules of Three
problem_statement: In tang2017generalizing.lean, prove either Tang2017Generalizing.conjecture_3_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Tang2017Generalizing.conjecture_3_1_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Generalizing Rules of Three

Author: Ewin Tang.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Twin Cities REU
2017](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~reiner/REU/REU.html).
Reference: E. Tang, *Generalizing Rules of Three*, University of Minnesota REU report, 2017.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Tang2017Generalizing

/-- The one-row Schur Q-function with hook reading: decreasing elementary factors followed by
increasing complete-homogeneous factors (Section 3.1). -/
def schurQ {R : Type*} [Ring R] {N : ℕ} (x : Fin N → R)
    (S : Finset (Fin N)) (k : ℕ) : R :=
  PowerSeries.coeff k
    (((S.sort (· ≥ ·)).map (fun i ↦
      (1 : PowerSeries R) + PowerSeries.C (x i) * PowerSeries.X)).prod *
     ((S.sort (· ≤ ·)).map (fun i ↦
      PowerSeries.invOfUnit
        ((1 : PowerSeries R) - PowerSeries.C (x i) * PowerSeries.X) 1)).prod)

/-- **Conjecture 3.1**. All hook-reading Q-functions of two alphabets commute on every common
subalphabet exactly when the degree-one commutations hold. -/
theorem conjecture_3_1 {R : Type*} [Ring R] {N : ℕ} (x y : Fin N → R) :
    (∀ (S : Finset (Fin N)) (k l : ℕ), Commute (schurQ x S k) (schurQ y S l)) ↔
      (∀ (S : Finset (Fin N)) (k l : ℕ), k = 1 ∨ l = 1 →
        Commute (schurQ x S k) (schurQ y S l)) := by
  sorry

end Tang2017Generalizing

theorem Tang2017Generalizing.conjecture_3_1_neg.{u0} : ¬ type_of% @Tang2017Generalizing.conjecture_3_1.{u0} := by
  sorry

title: Conditions for discrete equidecomposability of polygons
problem_statement: In turner2014conditions.lean, prove either Turner2014Conditions.conjecture_1_3_facet_decidability or refute it by proving its logical negation Turner2014Conditions.conjecture_1_3_facet_decidability_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Conditions for discrete equidecomposability of polygons

Authors: Paxton Turner and Yuhuai (Tony) Wu.
Origin: [Summer@ICERM 2014](https://icerm.brown.edu/summerug/2014/).
Reference: P. Turner and Y. Wu, *Conditions for discrete equidecomposability of polygons*,
arXiv:1412.0191v1, 2014.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Turner2014Conditions

open Finset

/-- Finite rational boundary coordinates, each stored as an integer numerator and a natural
denominator minus one. -/
abbrev PolygonCode := List ((ℤ × ℕ) × (ℤ × ℕ))

/-- The cyclically ordered boundary vertices of a finite input code. -/
def polygon (c : PolygonCode) : Polygon (Fin 2 → ℝ) c.length where
  vertices i := ![((c.get i).1.1 : ℝ) / ((c.get i).1.2 + 1),
    ((c.get i).2.1 : ℝ) / ((c.get i).2.2 + 1)]

/-- The closed polygonal region bounded by a valid code: the boundary and the bounded components
of its complement. -/
def polygonRegion (c : PolygonCode) : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ) :=
  (polygon c).boundary ℝ ∪
    {x | x ∉ (polygon c).boundary ℝ ∧
      Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn ((polygon c).boundary ℝ)ᶜ x)}

/-- A finite rational triangulation, as a Mathlib simplicial complex (Section 3.1). -/
structure RationalTriangulation (P : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) extends
    Geometry.SimplicialComplex ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ) where
  finite_faces : faces.Finite
  rational_vertices : ∀ x ∈ toSimplicialComplex.vertices, ∀ i,
    ∃ q : ℚ, (q : ℝ) = x i
  triangular_facets : ∀ s ∈ toSimplicialComplex.facets, #s = 3
  covers : toSimplicialComplex.space = P

/-- A facet map: a bijection of open triangular facets, with one integral affine-unimodular map
on each facet (Definition 3.1). Edges and vertices are ignored. -/
structure FacetMap {P Q : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)}
    (T : RationalTriangulation P) (U : RationalTriangulation Q) where
  /-- The bijection between the facets of the two triangulations. -/
  matching : T.toSimplicialComplex.facets ≃ U.toSimplicialComplex.facets
  /-- The unimodular linear part of the affine map on each facet. -/
  linear : T.toSimplicialComplex.facets → Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℤ
  /-- The integral translation part of the affine map on each facet. -/
  translation : T.toSimplicialComplex.facets → Fin 2 → ℤ
  maps_facets : ∀ s : T.toSimplicialComplex.facets,
    (fun x : Fin 2 → ℝ ↦
      Matrix.mulVec ((linear s).val.map (Int.castRingHom ℝ)) x +
        fun i ↦ (translation s i : ℝ)) ''
      interior (convexHull ℝ (s.val : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ))) =
        interior (convexHull ℝ ((matching s).val : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)))

/-- **Conjecture 1.3** (first assertion). One total computable procedure decides rational
facet-map existence.

This uses Definition 3.1 and the existential refinement criterion of Proposition 3.15 and
Theorem 3.17, not the inconsistent all-multiples summary or the stronger single-base proposal
of Section 5(1). -/
theorem conjecture_1_3_facet_decidability :
    ∃ f : PolygonCode × PolygonCode → Bool, Computable f ∧
      ∀ (p q : PolygonCode)
        (hp : 3 ≤ p.length ∧ Function.Injective (polygon p).vertices ∧
          ∀ i j : Fin p.length, i ≠ j →
            (polygon p).edgeSet ℝ i ∩ (polygon p).edgeSet ℝ j =
              convexHull ℝ
                (({polygon p i, polygon p (finRotate p.length i)} : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∩
                  {polygon p j, polygon p (finRotate p.length j)}))
        (hq : 3 ≤ q.length ∧ Function.Injective (polygon q).vertices ∧
          ∀ i j : Fin q.length, i ≠ j →
            (polygon q).edgeSet ℝ i ∩ (polygon q).edgeSet ℝ j =
              convexHull ℝ
                (({polygon q i, polygon q (finRotate q.length i)} : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∩
                  {polygon q j, polygon q (finRotate q.length j)})),
        f (p, q) = true ↔
          ∃ (T : RationalTriangulation (polygonRegion p))
            (U : RationalTriangulation (polygonRegion q)), Nonempty (FacetMap T U) := by
  sorry

end Turner2014Conditions

theorem Turner2014Conditions.conjecture_1_3_facet_decidability_neg : ¬ type_of% @Turner2014Conditions.conjecture_1_3_facet_decidability := by
  sorry

title: Maximizing Truth Learning in a Social Network is NP-hard
problem_statement: In uradnik2025maximizing.lean, prove either Uradnik2025Maximizing.bayesian_network_learning_not_in_np or refute it by proving its logical negation Uradnik2025Maximizing.bayesian_network_learning_not_in_np_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Maximizing Truth Learning in a Social Network is NP-hard

Authors: Filip Uradnik, Amanda Wang, and Jie Gao.
Origin: [DIMACS REU 2024](https://dimacs.rutgers.edu/reu-participant-details/uradnik-filip-2024).
Reference: F. Uradnik, A. Wang, and J. Gao, *Maximizing Truth Learning in a Social Network is
NP-hard*, Proc. AAMAS 2025 (2025), 2078-2086; arXiv:2502.12704v1.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Uradnik2025Maximizing

/-- A directed network with a common truth prior and private-signal accuracy (Definition 2.1).
The source's parameter domain is enforced by the decoder `readProblem`. -/
structure SocialNetwork where
  /-- The number of agents. -/
  size : ℕ
  /-- The directed network on the agents. -/
  graph : Digraph (Fin size)
  /-- The common prior probability of the truth state. -/
  prior : ℚ
  /-- The probability that each private signal matches the truth. -/
  accuracy : ℚ

open scoped Classical in
/-- The expected fraction of correct announcements in a fixed time-to-vertex ordering, with
fresh fair ties (Definition 2.2; Bayesian rule, p. 2080). The recursion stores unannounced
coordinates as `false` padding. -/
def learningRate (N : SocialNetwork) (order : Equiv.Perm (Fin N.size)) : ℚ :=
  let rec
    /-- The joint probability of the truth, the signals and the padded announcements
    after the first `t` turns. -/
    joint : ℕ → Bool → (Fin N.size → Bool) → (Fin N.size → Bool) → ℚ
    | 0 => fun b s a ↦
      if a = (fun _ ↦ false) then
        (if b then N.prior else 1 - N.prior) *
          ∏ u, if s u = b then N.accuracy else 1 - N.accuracy
      else 0
    | t + 1 =>
      let previous := joint t
      if h : t < N.size then
        let v := order ⟨t, h⟩
        fun b s a ↦
          let weight := fun truth : Bool ↦
            ∑ signals : Fin N.size → Bool, ∑ actions : Fin N.size → Bool,
              if signals v = s v ∧
                  (∀ u : Fin N.size, N.graph.Adj u v →
                    (order.symm u).val < t → actions u = a u) then
                previous truth signals actions
              else 0
          previous b s (Function.update a v false) *
            (if weight false < weight true then (if a v then 1 else 0)
             else if weight true < weight false then (if a v then 0 else 1)
             else (1 / 2 : ℚ))
      else previous
  (∑ b : Bool, ∑ s : Fin N.size → Bool, ∑ a : Fin N.size → Bool,
    joint N.size b s a * ∑ v : Fin N.size, (if a v = b then 1 else 0 : ℚ)) /
      (N.size : ℚ)

/-- The canonical binary input: seven escaped binary-natural fields (size, then
numerator/denominator for prior, accuracy and error tolerance), followed by the row-major
adjacency bits. A digit is `true` then the digit and `false` ends a field; noncanonical,
malformed and out-of-domain inputs are rejected. -/
def readProblem (word : List Bool) : Option (SocialNetwork × ℚ) := do
  let rec
    /-- Read one escaped binary word, returning its digits and the remaining input. -/
    field : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
    | false :: rest => some ([], rest)
    | true :: bit :: rest => do
      let (bits, tail) ← field rest
      pure (bit :: bits, tail)
    | _ => none
  let readNat := fun input ↦ do
    let (bits, rest) ← field input
    let value := Computability.decodeNat bits
    if Computability.encodeNat value = bits then some (value, rest) else none
  let (n, rest) ← readNat word
  let (qn, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (qd, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (pn, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (pd, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (en, rest) ← readNat rest
  let (ed, edges) ← readNat rest
  let q : ℚ := (qn : ℚ) / (qd : ℚ)
  let p : ℚ := (pn : ℚ) / (pd : ℚ)
  let ε : ℚ := (en : ℚ) / (ed : ℚ)
  if 0 < n ∧ edges.length = n * n ∧
      0 < qd ∧ 0 < pd ∧ 0 < ed ∧
      Nat.Coprime qn qd ∧ Nat.Coprime pn pd ∧ Nat.Coprime en ed ∧
      0 < q ∧ q < 1 ∧ (1 / 2 : ℚ) < p ∧ p < 1 ∧
      0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 then
    some (⟨n, Digraph.mk' (fun u v ↦ edges.getD (u.val * n + v.val) false),
      q, p⟩, ε)
  else none

/-- Network learning for the fixed Bayesian rule: some ordering chosen before any random draws
attains the inclusive average-learning threshold (Definition 2.5). -/
def networkLearning : Set (List Bool) :=
  {word | ∃ (N : SocialNetwork) (ε : ℚ),
    readProblem word = some (N, ε) ∧
      ∃ order : Equiv.Perm (Fin N.size), 1 - ε ≤ learningRate N order}

/-- **Unnumbered conjecture** (Section 6, Future Work, p. 2085). Bayesian Network Learning is
not in NP.

The rule, implicit in the paragraph, is taken as the Bayesian variant of Definition 2.5 with
rational binary inputs; Definition 2.5 controls the threshold despite the reduction's
epsilon-complement mismatch. -/

    let pairCode := (Computability.encodingProd
      (Computability.encodingList Bool) (Computability.encodingList Bool)).encode
    ¬(∃ verifier : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool,
      ∃ machine : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime pairCode
          Computability.encodeBool verifier,
        (∀ k : machine.tm.K, Finite (machine.tm.Γ k)) ∧
        ∃ bound : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ input : List Bool,

title: Domination in Direct Products of Complete Graphs
problem_statement: In vemuri2020domination.lean, prove either Vemuri2020Domination.conjecture_1_11 or refute it by proving its logical negation Vemuri2020Domination.conjecture_1_11_neg.

/-!
# Domination in Direct Products of Complete Graphs

Author: Harish Vemuri.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2019](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: H. Vemuri, *Domination in direct products of complete graphs*, Discrete Appl. Math.
**285** (2020), 473-482; arXiv:1908.02445v1.
-/

namespace Vemuri2020Domination

open Finset

/-- The total domination number: the least size of a finite set whose open neighborhoods cover
the graph (Section 1). The target graphs are finite without isolates. -/
noncomputable def totalDominationNumber {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ D : Finset V, #D = k ∧
    ∀ v : V, ∃ w ∈ D, G.Adj v w}

/-- The Jacobsthal function `g(n)`: the least positive interval length forcing an integer
coprime to `n` in every interval of positive integers (Section 1). -/
noncomputable def jacobsthal (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ ∀ a > 0,
    ∃ i : ℕ, i < m ∧ Nat.Coprime (a + i) n}

/-- **Conjecture 1.11** (p. 4). Every positive gap from Jacobsthal's function to total
domination occurs for integers with arbitrarily many distinct prime factors. -/
theorem conjecture_1_11 (j : ℕ) (hj : 0 < j) (K : ℕ) :
    ∃ n ≥ 2, K ≤ #n.primeFactors ∧
      totalDominationNumber (SimpleGraph.addCayley {x : ZMod n | IsUnit x}) + j ≤
        jacobsthal n := by
  sorry

end Vemuri2020Domination

theorem Vemuri2020Domination.conjecture_1_11_neg : ¬ type_of% @Vemuri2020Domination.conjecture_1_11 := by
  sorry

title: Toward explicit Hilbert series of quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic p and q-deformed quasi-invariants
problem_statement: In wang2022toward.lean, prove either Wang2022Toward.conjecture_5_7 or refute it by proving its logical negation Wang2022Toward.conjecture_5_7_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Toward explicit Hilbert series of quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic p and q-deformed quasi-invariants

Author: Frank Wang.
Origin: [MIT SPUR 2021](https://math.mit.edu/research/undergraduate/spur/past-projects.html).
Reference: F. Wang, *Toward explicit Hilbert series of quasi-invariant polynomials in
characteristic p and q-deformed quasi-invariants*, arXiv:2201.06111v2 (2022).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Wang2022Toward

open MvPolynomial

/-- The space of `q`-deformed `m`-quasi-invariants (Definition 5.1). -/
def quasiInvariants (n m : ℕ) (q : ℂ) :
    Submodule ℂ (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) where
  carrier := {P | ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j →
    (∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc (-(m : ℤ)) (m : ℤ),
      (X i - C (q ^ k) * X j)) ∣ P - rename (Equiv.swap i j) P}
  zero_mem' := by simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro P Q hP hQ i j hij
    simpa only [map_add, add_sub_add_comm] using dvd_add (hP i j hij) (hQ i j hij)
  smul_mem' := by
    intro a P hP i j hij
    simpa only [smul_eq_C_mul, map_mul, rename_C, mul_sub] using
      dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hP i j hij) (C a)

/-- The Hilbert series of the graded spaces of Definition 5.1 (Definition 2.3). -/
def hilbertSeries (n m : ℕ) (q : ℂ) : PowerSeries ℕ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d ↦ Module.finrank ℂ
    ↥(quasiInvariants n m q ⊓ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) ℂ d)

/-- **Conjecture 5.7**. A change in the Hilbert series forces the stated root order. -/
theorem conjecture_5_7 (n m : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (q : ℂ) (hq : q ≠ 0)
    (h : hilbertSeries n m q ≠ hilbertSeries n m 1) :
    ∃ p > 0, IsPrimitiveRoot q p ∧
      ((m : ℚ) * n * ((n : ℚ) - 2) + (n.choose 2 : ℚ)) /
        ((n.choose 2 : ℚ) - 1) ≤ (p : ℚ) ∧ p ≤ m * n := by sorry

end Wang2022Toward

theorem Wang2022Toward.conjecture_5_7_neg : ¬ type_of% @Wang2022Toward.conjecture_5_7 := by
  sorry

title: Permutations with Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_id,w(q) = 1 + q^h
problem_statement: In woo2009permutations.lean, prove either Woo2009Permutations.conjecture_a5_one or refute it by proving its logical negation Woo2009Permutations.conjecture_a5_one_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Permutations with Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_id,w(q) = 1 + q^h

Authors: Alexander Woo; appendix by Sara Billey and Jonathan Weed.
Origin: [University of Washington REU 2008](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~reu/papers/2008/).
Reference: A. Woo, with an appendix by S. Billey and J. Weed, *Permutations with
Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_id,w(q) = 1 + q^h*, Electron. J. Combin. **16** (2009), no. 2,
Research Paper 10, 32 pp.; doi:10.37236/76.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Woo2009Permutations

open Finset Polynomial

/-- The rank matrix (Section 2.1). Both indices are shifted from one to zero. -/
def rank {n : ℕ} (w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (p q : Fin n) : ℕ :=
  #{i | i ≤ p ∧ w i ≤ q}

/-- Bruhat order: reverse componentwise comparison of ranks (Section 2.1). -/
def Bruhat {n : ℕ} (u w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : Fin n, rank w p q ≤ rank u p q

instance {n : ℕ} (u w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Decidable (Bruhat u w) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ p q : Fin n, rank w p q ≤ rank u p q))

/-- Coxeter length, the number of inversions (Section 2.1). -/
def length {n : ℕ} (w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  #{ij : Fin n × Fin n | ij.1 < ij.2 ∧ w ij.2 < w ij.1}

/-- The adjacent transposition swapping positions `i` and `i + 1` (Section 2.1). -/
def simple {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n - 1)) : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) :=
  Equiv.swap ⟨i.val, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩
    ⟨i.val + 1, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩

/-- The type-A Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial, by right-descent recursion (Billey-Warrington,
arXiv:math/0102168v1, equation (12.1)). The correction coefficient is zero unless the relevant
length difference is odd. -/
def kl {n : ℕ} (u w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Polynomial ℤ :=
  if u = w then 1
  else if Bruhat u w then
    let descents := ({i | length (w * simple i) < length w} : Finset (Fin (n - 1)))
    if hd : descents.Nonempty then
      let i := descents.min' hd
      let s := simple i
      let v := w * s
      have hv : length v < length w := (mem_filter.mp (descents.min'_mem hd)).2
      let c : ℕ := if length (u * s) < length u then 1 else 0
      X ^ c * kl u v + X ^ (1 - c) * kl (u * s) v -
        ∑ z : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
          if hz : Bruhat u z ∧ Bruhat z v ∧ length z < length v ∧
              length (z * s) < length z ∧ (length v - length z) % 2 = 1 then
            C ((kl z v).coeff ((length v - length z - 1) / 2)) *
              X ^ ((length w - length z) / 2) * kl u z
          else 0
    else 0
  else 0
termination_by length w
decreasing_by
  all_goals first | exact hv | exact Nat.lt_trans hz.2.2.1 hv

/-- The permutations indexing the irreducible singular components (Appendix A). They are
encoded as the Bruhat-maximal `u ≤ w` with `P_u,w` not identically one. -/
def maxsing {n : ℕ} (w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :=
  {u | Bruhat u w ∧ kl u w ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ v : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), Bruhat v w → kl v w ≠ 1 → Bruhat u v → v = u}

/-- **Conjecture A.5(1)**. If `P_id,w(1) ≤ 3`, the maximal singular locus has at most three
elements.

Only type A and this first numbered assertion are formalized. -/
theorem conjecture_a5_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (w : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (h : (kl 1 w).eval 1 ≤ 3) : #(maxsing w) ≤ 3 := by
  sorry

end Woo2009Permutations

theorem Woo2009Permutations.conjecture_a5_one_neg : ¬ type_of% @Woo2009Permutations.conjecture_a5_one := by
  sorry

title: C-(k,l)-Sum-Free Sets
problem_statement: In zhang2020c.lean, prove either Zhang2020C.conjecture_5_1 or refute it by proving its logical negation Zhang2020C.conjecture_5_1_neg.
challenge:

/-!
# C-(k,l)-Sum-Free Sets

Author: Rachel Zhang.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2019](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: R. Zhang, *C-(k,l)-Sum-Free Sets*, arXiv:2001.00327v3.
-/

namespace Zhang2020C

open scoped Pointwise

/-- The maximum cardinality `mu^C_{k,l}` of a noisy sum-free set (Section 1). -/
def noisySumFreeMaximum (n : ℕ+) (C : Finset (ZMod (n : ℕ))) (k l : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ({A | Disjoint (k • A + (k - 1) • C) (l • A + (l - 1) • C)} :
    Finset (Finset (ZMod (n : ℕ)))).sup Finset.card

/-- **Conjecture 5.1**. Interval noise has the conjectured exact maximum sum-free cardinality for
every modulus and pair of summand counts. -/
theorem conjecture_5_1 (n : ℕ+) (k l c : ℕ) (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hkl : l < k)
    (hc : 2 ≤ c) :
    let C : Finset (ZMod (n : ℕ)) := (Finset.range c).image fun i : ℕ ↦ (i : ZMod (n : ℕ))
    let χ : ℤ := ((n : ℤ) + 2 * ((c : ℤ) - 2)) / ((k : ℤ) + l) - ((c : ℤ) - 2)
    let r : ℤ := (-(k : ℤ) * χ - ((k : ℤ) - 1) * ((c : ℤ) - 2)) %
      (Nat.gcd (n : ℕ) (k - l) : ℤ)
    (noisySumFreeMaximum n C k l : ℤ) =
      max 0 (((n : ℤ) + 2 * ((c : ℤ) - 2) - r) / ((k : ℤ) + l) - ((c : ℤ) - 2)) := by
  sorry

end Zhang2020C

theorem Zhang2020C.conjecture_5_1_neg : ¬ type_of% @Zhang2020C.conjecture_5_1 := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture 1** (arXiv v1, p. 9). The sum of a homogeneous polynomial with zero spherical
mean over the integer points in a ball has error exponent at most its degree plus one, with any
positive loss.

The polynomial summand omitted on the MIT report's p. 9 is included, as in the arXiv version;

theorem conjecture_1 (degree : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ)

    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),

title: Coloring Bipartite Graphs with Semi-small List Size
problem_statement: In zhu2023coloring.lean, prove either Zhu2023Coloring.conjecture_1_11 or refute it by proving its logical negation Zhu2023Coloring.conjecture_1_11_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Coloring Bipartite Graphs with Semi-small List Size

Author: Daniel G. Zhu.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2020](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: D. G. Zhu, *Coloring bipartite graphs with semi-small list size*, Ann. Comb. **27**
(2023), 469-491; doi:10.1007/s00026-022-00633-z.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Zhu2023Coloring

open scoped Topology
open Finset

/-- Asymmetric list choosability for the specified ordered vertex parts. -/
def Choosable {a b : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin a ⊕ Fin b)) (kA kB : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : (Fin a ⊕ Fin b) → Finset ℕ,
    (∀ v : Fin a, #(L (Sum.inl v)) = kA) →
    (∀ v : Fin b, #(L (Sum.inr v)) = kB) →
    ∃ c : G.Coloring ℕ, ∀ v, c v ∈ L v

/-- The invariant `xi`, with natural logarithm and partwise maximum degrees (Definition 2.7). -/
def xi (deltaA deltaB kA kB : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (deltaB : ℝ) * Real.log (deltaA : ℝ) ^ (kA - 1) / (kB : ℝ) ^ kA

open scoped Classical in
/-- The infimum of `xi` over all non-choosable ordered bipartite graphs (Definition 6.1). -/
def xiG (kA : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ (a b : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin a ⊕ Fin b))
    (kB : ℕ), 0 < kB ∧ G ≤ completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b) ∧
    ¬Choosable G kA kB ∧
    x = xi (Finset.univ.sup (fun v : Fin a ↦ G.degree (Sum.inl v)))
      (Finset.univ.sup (fun v : Fin b ↦ G.degree (Sum.inr v))) kA kB}

/-- **Conjecture 1.11**. All optimal general-bipartite thresholds are positive, and their
logarithms divided by the first list size have a finite limit. -/
theorem conjecture_1_11 :
    (∀ kA > 0, 0 < xiG kA) ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto (fun kA : ℕ ↦ Real.log (xiG kA) / (kA : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 c) := by
  sorry

end Zhu2023Coloring

theorem Zhu2023Coloring.conjecture_1_11_neg : ¬ type_of% @Zhu2023Coloring.conjecture_1_11 := by
  sorry

title: Sub-Fibonacci behavior in numerical semigroup enumeration
problem_statement: In zhu2023sub.lean, prove either Zhu2023Sub.conjecture_7_3 or refute it by proving its logical negation Zhu2023Sub.conjecture_7_3_neg.
challenge:
import Mathlib

/-!
# Sub-Fibonacci behavior in numerical semigroup enumeration

Author: Daniel G. Zhu.
Origin: [University of Minnesota Duluth REU 2020](https://www.d.umn.edu/~jgallian/progbib.html).
Reference: D. G. Zhu, *Sub-Fibonacci behavior in numerical semigroup enumeration*,
arXiv:2202.05755v3, 2023.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Zhu2023Sub

open scoped Topology

/-- Kunz words: positive integer words satisfying both one-indexed Kunz inequalities
(Definition 3.2). -/
def IsKunz (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ a ∈ w, 0 < a) ∧
  ∀ i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ w.length → 1 ≤ j → j ≤ w.length →
    (i + j ≤ w.length →
      w.getD (i + j - 1) 0 ≤ w.getD (i - 1) 0 + w.getD (j - 1) 0) ∧
    (w.length + 1 < i + j →
      w.getD (i + j - w.length - 2) 0 ≤ w.getD (i - 1) 0 + w.getD (j - 1) 0 + 1)

/-- **Conjecture 7.3(a)-(c)**. Deep numerical semigroups and stressed Kunz words have the
proposed exponential rate, successive-count ratio, and polynomial correction. -/
theorem conjecture_7_3 (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hroot : ρ ^ 6 - ρ ^ 3 - 2 * ρ ^ 2 - 2 * ρ - 1 = 0) :
    let counts : Bool → ℕ → ℕ := fun stressed g ↦
      {w : List ℕ | IsKunz w ∧ w.sum = g ∧
        if stressed then (∀ a ∈ w, a ≤ 3) ∧ w.getLast? = some 3
        else ∃ a ∈ w, 4 ≤ a}.ncard
    (∀ stressed : Bool, Filter.Tendsto
      (fun g : ℕ ↦ (counts stressed g : ℝ) ^ (1 / (g : ℝ)))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 ρ)) ∧
    (∀ stressed : Bool, Filter.Tendsto
      (fun g : ℕ ↦ (counts stressed (g + 1) : ℝ) / (counts stressed g : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 ρ)) ∧
    (∀ stressed : Bool, ∃ α : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto
      (fun g : ℕ ↦ (Real.log (counts stressed g) - (g : ℝ) * Real.log ρ) /
        Real.log g) Filter.atTop (𝓝 α)) := by
  sorry

end Zhu2023Sub

theorem Zhu2023Sub.conjecture_7_3_neg : ¬ type_of% @Zhu2023Sub.conjecture_7_3 := by
  sorry
